title: 修学基礎Ｂ
subtitle: Basic Style for Study B
courseType: Student and Study Skills Courses ProgramStudent and Study Skills CoursesStudent and Study Skills
educationalGoal:
The aim of this course is to improve further the skills learned in Basic Style for Study A (and other courses) from the first semester in KIT.
After completing this course, you will be able to develop critical and logical thinking skills that enable you to put yourself into a social context and see yourself from the perspective of a third person, which is necessary to continue on the path to a meaningful and successful career.
advice:
1. “Weekly report”: Making good use of KIT’s academic support system to practice self-management.
2. “Newspaper portfolio”: Raising interest in social issues in terms of career management.
3. Special lecture on career management: Considering career management in the context of career development.
4. Group discussion and presentation: Becoming familiar with specialized courses for better career development.
5. Academic planning: Comprehending KIT’s educational curriculum and system in detail
(such as prerequisites for course registration, graduation requirements, etc.) in terms of career management.
6. Short essay: Improving academic writing skills (including critical and logical thinking skills)
by writing a Short essay.
7. Self-reflection: Group discussion and interview with the academic adviser to review the first year.

*The submission date for each assignments must be strictly observed.
*Access the “Student Portal”, “e-syllabus”, and other systems frequently to get the latest information
*When submitting research papers and/or assignments, strictly adhere to the designated forms and instructions.
books: None
requiredKnowledge:
1. Willpower to understand and observe “KIT IDEALS.”
2. Willpower to understand and observe the “Student pledge.”
3. Willpower to acquire KIT human skills.
4. Motivation to develop language competence (in your native language).
5. Motivation to develop academic writing skills.

activityGoals.body: Be able to express your achievements and goals through weekly report and self-evaluation of achievement report.
Be able to organize the contents of special lectures accurately and express them in speech and writing.
Be able to find out problems in group discussions and express your opinions in speech and writing.
Be able to express your opinions of a social issue in academic writing (a short paper).
Be able to clarify in writing the academic planning of your course curriculum and future prospects in life.
Be able to develop and implement the skills necessary for students.

title: 技術者と持続可能社会
subtitle: Engineer and Sustainable Society
courseType: Student and Study Skills Courses ProgramCharacter Building CoursesCharacter Building
educationalGoal: Maintaining an interest in social trends, understanding market conditions and customer needs, and societal expectations of companies operating within society, students will appreciate quality, cost, delivery, and safety as essential engineering skills and be able to research and analyze corporate activities using a scientific approach. Students will also understand innovation and connect it to their own career design to help realize a sustainable society.
advice:
The students considered their future career direction in the "Basic Style for Study" in the first year. Based on this, in this course, students will learn the following items needed to do a good job at a company.

(1) Understand the trends of sustainable society such as SDGs, the role of companies, and the responsibilities and rewards of engineers working there.
(2) Learn basic management knowledge and matters related to the work of engineers, such as R & D and production processes.
(3) Understand that there is a wide variety of industries in society, and engineers are active in various occupations in a wide range of fields.
(4) Deepen understanding of the work of engineers by exchanging opinions on items investigated by themselves through group discussions and presentations.
(5) Learn examples of innovation to play an active role in a developing society.

(3) Understand that there is a wide variety of industries in society, and engineers are active in various occupations in a wide range of fields.
(4) Deepen understanding of the work of engineers by exchanging opinions on items investigated by themselves through group discussions and presentations.

title: 日本学（日本と日本人）Ａ
subtitle: Japanology (Japan and Japanese)A
courseType: Student and Study Skills Courses ProgramCharacter Building CoursesCharacter Building
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn about the life of the founders of Japan and how to live and think.
(2) Understand the characteristics and national character of Japan.
(3) Learn about various world and Japanese founding myths.
(4) Understand that there are various ways of thinking about the world.
(5) Improve their basic reading, listening, thinking, and writing skills.
advice:
This course will teach the Japanese way of life and thinking by covering the following:
1. Japanese way of life and thinking
2. Japanese national character
3. Japanese mythology
4. Various myths around the world
5. Japanese founding myth

Students are required to participate actively in class.
Students are expected to bring their textbooks, handouts, and other necessary materials to every class.
Students must read and prepare to discuss the designated text pages.
Students are required to understand the content of the lectures and to write using appropriate Japanese terminology.
Students are expected to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class.
books: Textbooks： Reference books：The Story of Japan, Vols. I-III (Seisei kikaku) Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge:
Ability to read preparatory text correctly.
Ability to prepare and have a comprehensive understanding of the lecture content.
Ability to think about the instructed theme and write about the results using appropriate Japanese terminology.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the Japanese way of life and thinking using appropriate Japanese term.
Be able to explain the Japanese national character using appropriate Japanese term.
Be able to read about the characteristics of Japanese myths and explain them using appropriate Japanese term.
Be able to explain the founding of Japan using appropriate Japanese term.
Be able to self-assess one’s own goals in this class.

title: 実践ウェルビーイング
subtitle: Practical Wellbeing
courseType: Student and Study Skills Courses ProgramCharacter Building CoursesCharacter Building
educationalGoal: In this course, students will look at their own life from a positive perspective in order to find meaningful purpose. There will be many positive psychology exercises which include building interpersonal communication skills. Students are expected to actively participate in the exercises. Activities are intended to help students become aware of their psychological wellbeing, find meaning in life, and learn more about their place in this diverse world.
advice:
Students will receive either a “pass” or “fail” grade for this course.
There will be many psychological exercises and group activities in the course.
Students will utilize their non-cognitive skills such as empathy and compassion more than their cognitive skills which are usually required for academic courses.
Students will be asked to actively participate in experiential learning activities such as psychological exercises and group work (workshops).
Students will complete homework activities and discuss the content during in-class activities.
books: None required
requiredKnowledge:
Ability to observe things objectively - (e.g., Not only find negative, but also positive things in your life.)
Perseverance - (e.g., Attending every class.)
Diligence - (e.g., Complete homework according to the given instructions.)
Ability to plan appropriately - (e.g., 1) Conduct group work with an awareness of the time. 2) Be aware of deadlines in order to complete homework on time.)
 Positive attitude - (e.g., Actively participate in the positive psychology activities.)

activityGoals.body: Realize and appreciate your own character strengths.
Notice and appreciate the positive things in your daily life.
Listen to others actively and constructively.
When necessary, be assertive in expressing your opinions to others.
Imagine your ideal future self.
Thoughtfully consider the pathways to your ideal future self.

title: 健康・体力づくり
subtitle: Introduction to Fitness and Health Promotion
courseType: Student and Study Skills Courses ProgramCharacter Building CoursesLifelong Sports
educationalGoal:
To lead a healthy and fulfilling life throughout their own lifetime, students will learn the following:
(1) Knowledge about fitness and health promotion and lifestyle-related diseases, (2) Procedures for measuring and analyzing personal health and physical fitness characteristics, (3) How to develop a personal exercise prescription (training program), (4) How to understand and practice health and fitness self-care, (5) Various risks in student/social life, and (6) How to cooperate, lead, and observe rules
advice:
Students will learn knowledge and procedures for health promotion through measurement and diagnosis in health and physical fitness, the development of safe and effective individual exercise prescription/training programs, lifestyle-related diseases, and health care procedures. Specifically, students will learn the following: 1.Methods for warm-up exercises, 2.Measurement and diagnosis procedures in physical fitness, 3.Methods for strength, endurance, and shape-up training, 4.Exercise prescription procedures, 5.Knowledge about lifestyle-related diseases and health care procedures, 6.Self-management of diet, sleeping, and exercise habits for health promotion, and 7.Risks in student/social life.
 Classes will be held once per week (100 minutes).
In practical classes, students should wear appropriate clothing such as sportswear, T-shirts, shorts, and indoor shoes.
 Students should aim to attend all classes highly motivated to learn.
 Students should pay attention to their own health condition.
 Students should understand the knowledge and procedures necessary for health promotion, and practice them in student life and throughout their lifetime.
 Practice classes will take place in the gymnasium (Building 13 or Building 20), and lectures will take place in the lecture hall shown on the class schedule.
requiredKnowledge:
Taking an interest in various types of news and information about health and physical fitness.
Preparing for physical activities and understanding safety management in sports activities.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the procedures of exercise prescription and design effective training programs.
Be able to understand express the importance of health promotion throughout their lifetime.
Be able to understand and practice fundamental social skills such as cooperation and leadership.
Be able to understand the importance of self-management of lifestyle habits and to lead a healthy life.
Be able to study actively while paying careful attention to one's own health and fitness characteristics.
Be able to understand various health-related problems and explain these coping behaviors.

              授業科目の学習・教育目標

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Warm-up
2.Measurement and diagnosis in physical
3.Exercise prescription
4.Lifestyle-related diseases
5.Self-management

              To lead a healthy and fulfilling life throughout their own lifetime, students will learn the following:
(1) Knowledge about fitness and health promotion and lifestyle-related diseases, (2) Procedures for measuring and analyzing personal health and physical fitness characteristics, (3) How to develop a personal exercise prescription (training program), (4) How to understand and practice health and fitness self-care, (5) Various risks in student/social life, and (6) How to cooperate, lead, and observe rules

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

               Students will learn knowledge and procedures for health promotion through measurement and diagnosis in health and physical fitness, the development of safe and effective individual exercise prescription/training programs, lifestyle-related diseases, and health care procedures. Specifically, students will learn the following: 1.Methods for warm-up exercises, 2.Measurement and diagnosis procedures in physical fitness, 3.Methods for strength, endurance, and shape-up training, 4.Exercise prescription procedures, 5.Knowledge about lifestyle-related diseases and health care procedures, 6.Self-management of diet, sleeping, and exercise habits for health promotion, and 7.Risks in student/social life.
 Classes will be held once per week (100 minutes).
In practical classes, students should wear appropriate clothing such as sportswear, T-shirts, shorts, and indoor shoes.
 Students should aim to attend all classes highly motivated to learn.
 Students should pay attention to their own health condition.
 Students should understand the knowledge and procedures necessary for health promotion, and practice them in student life and throughout their lifetime.
 Practice classes will take place in the gymnasium (Building 13 or Building 20), and lectures will take place in the lecture hall shown on the class schedule.

  (1) Characteristics of tennis equipment (racket and ball) (2) Skills: strokes (3) Skills: volleys (4) Skills: serve and overhead smash

  Classes will be held once per week (100 minutes). In practical classes, students should wear appropriate clothing such as sportswear, T-shirts, shorts, and outdoor shoes. educationalGoal:

advice:
This class aims to achieve the above-mentioned learning objectives through mountain climbing:
1. Lecture format
The format will be practice-intensive, held over 1 nights and 2 days at Hakusan after the end of the previous semester.
2. Summary of class
1) Basic mountain climbing knowledge
2) Basic mountain climbing skills
3) Safety management in the mountainous region
3. Equipment
The following equipment is required for safe climbing (plan Hakusan): rucksack, hat, gloves, climbing trousers, trekking shoes (or climbing shoes), socks, rain gear (poncho) sweater, underwear, other winter clothes, toiletries, water bottle, flashlight, sunglasses, medicine, camera, shoelaces, writing utensils, and health certificate.
In particular, a rucksack appropriate for the amount of supplies, rain gear, and trekking shoes are essential. Also, if you bring a stove or tableware for each small group, the activity will be more comfortable.

educationalGoal: Through learning activities for Athletic club activities, students will:　1．Understand the pleasure derived from sports.　2．Acquire the knowledge and ability to practice various sports activities voluntarily through the PDCA cycle.　3．Learn the things that are needed for social/college life, such as observation of the rules, discipline, respect, a competitive spirit, leadership/followership abilities, responsibility, safety awareness, and communication skills.
advice:
In this course, students aim to achieve the above learning and educational objectives through participation in the “100-km Walk” program.
1. Course Format and Implementation: This course will be conducted in an intensive format and will take place during the 2026 Koudaisai (university festival) period. The walk will start from the Anamizu to the KIT Ogigaoka campus. Participants will walk a total distance of approximately 100 km over two days. Including rest breaks, the total walking time will be approximately 29 hours.
2. Course Overview (1) Basic knowledge of walking: In order to understand appropriate clothing for walking (including in rainy conditions), the fundamentals of walking, and walking pace, students are required to practice long-distance walking prior to the event. Students will learn how to balance walking pace and rest periods, and will also understand that paying attention to the natural environment is effective in reducing mental fatigue. (2) Safety measures for walking: As the walk is conducted on public roads, students must obey traffic rules at all times and wear safety lights, reflective bands, and similar equipment while walking. (3) Planning to complete the walk: The sense of achievement gained by overcoming physical and mental difficulties will become a valuable asset in the future. Therefore, students are expected to repeatedly practice long-distance walking in advance and develop both physical and mental endurance. 3. Evaluation Criteria
(1) Credit certification: Students who do not complete the full 100-km walk will not be awarded course credit.

title: イングリッシュトピックス３
subtitle: English Topics 3
educationalGoal: In English Topics 3, students will acquire English communication skills by studying various topics, English expressions, sentence structures, and vocabulary. They will gain confidence in speaking, listening and reading and improve their fluency and accuracy.
advice:
Students will practice speaking, listening, and reading English using daily topics from the textbook. The targeted achievement level is CEFR A2+ to B1. Students will improve their English proficiency by balancing input and output activities.

Before class, students have to study the materials from the textbook using the pre-class assignments. In class, students will ask questions to their teacher and engage in pair work and group work to further deepen their skills and knowledge. They need to look up the words that they do not know in the textbook and assignments beforehand.
Message to students: On Week 1, please bring the textbook and your PC. If possible, please bring either a paper or electronic dictionary.
books: Live Escalate Book 2: Trekking [Seibido Publishing]
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of basic English grammar and vocabulary is necessary (Please refer to Royal English Grammar or Sogo Eigo Forest).

activityGoals.body: Students can use expressions and vocabulary about given topics to carry out a conversation or dicussion.
Students can carry out conversations and discussions about given topics.
Students will comprehend a short story or a conversation about given topics.
Students will comprehend multi-paragraph texts utilizing knowledge of vocabulary and grammar.

title: ビジネスコミュニケーション
subtitle: Business Communication
educationalGoal: In this course, students will engage with English in simulated business situations. Students will employ English vocabulary and phrases to complete business tasks effectively. Students will participate in group activities including discussions, interviews, role plays, and presentations to develop both their understanding of the business environment as well as the four language skills of speaking, listening, reading, and writing.
advice:
1. In order to develop English communication skills for business situations, the majority of class will be conducted through group work. When completing projects, it will be necessary to work cooperatively with group members.

2. Group work includes activities such as presentations and discussions. English will be used for these activities.

3. While conducting group work, each student must actively participate and contribute to the completion of the activities.
books: None
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of basic English grammar is necessary.

activityGoals.body: Learn vocabulary and phrases used in the workplace and use them appropriately in business settings.
Learn how to do business tasks such as market research, presentations, and advertisement making.
Understand the differences between Japanese and foreign business cultures and appropriately apply them.
Learn the foundations of digital literacy and appropriately apply them.

title: アカデミックリーディング１
subtitle: Academic Reading 1
educationalGoal: Improve reading skills and develop a diverse perspective by reading academic level articles about global events and cultures. Be able to read texts, discuss content, and express personal opinions logically.
advice:
Reading is a core component of listening, speaking, and writing skills. The objective of this course is to improve all 4 skills through reading passages at an appropriate speed to understand the content.

The following topics will be covered: Unit 5: Finding Wonders.   Unit 6: Reef Encounters.   Unit 7: Dollars and Scents.   Unit 8: Great Explorers.   Extra readings will be distributed in class.

Active learning in English class includes presentations, Q&A sessions, pair-work, group work, and worksheets.

Preview: Read the story, check the content, pronunciation, vocabulary, and answer all of the questions in the textbook.

In class: Ask questions and solve any problems you have encountered during the preview.
Review: Check the content and pronunciation of the words in the story and memorize the vocabulary.
Use office hours to ask extra questions.

Plan and prepare for group presentations.
Make study plans throughout the semester.
books: Reading Explorer 2 Third Edition
requiredKnowledge:
Students must have a basic knowledge of grammar and vocabulary.
There will be daily quizzes.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the topic of the story in each unit.
Be able to understand the structure of paragraphs and stories.
Be able to read, listen, pronounce, and write the words in the story in each unit.
Be able to find specific information about each story using various reading skills at an appropriate speed.
Be able to understand the story and exchange opinions with other students.
Be able to give a presentation on the topic taught in each unit.

advice:

(3) Constructing an essay
(4) Mechanics
(5) Formatting

Students are required to actively participate in the class.

In this subject you will acquire presentation skills in English. The learning goals are as follows

(1) Learn the format and structure of the academic presentation.
(2) Learn linguistic expressions used in presentations (eg, descriptions of figures, tables, graphs, data, etc.).
(3) Learn how to create presentation materials and manuscripts.
advice:
This course is a presentation skills course. We will cover the following materials:

1. English Presentation Basics.
2. Structure and Flow of Academic English Presentation.
3. Digital Presentation.

Students are required to actively participate in the class.
requiredKnowledge:
Computer literacy skills such as presentation software.
It is recommended that prospective graduate students and Boeing Externship students take this course.

title: ＳＴＥＭイングリッシュ
subtitle: STEM English
educationalGoal: In this course, students will acquire four skills (reading, writing, speaking, and listening) using English in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM). The aim is to acquire the ability to find and solve problems in STEM fields. Find out more about the issues covered and gain the ability to communicate your opinions and ideas in English through discussions and presentations.
advice:
In this course, students will gain content knowledge and apply what they have learned to solve a range of different STEM related problems. An outline of the activities is as follows.
1. Science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) centered course
2. Content language integrated learning (CLIL) approach
3. Learn about and apply the scientific method to a range of topics
4. Plan and conduct investigations
5. Collect and analyze data from experiments
6. Report the findings from a range of STEM investigations
Be sure to check e-syllabus before each class. Use English videos and related articles for teaching materials.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of basic English grammar is required.

activityGoals.body: Can describe STEM issues and research methods in English.
Can analyze the issues in English.
Explain collected data and analysis results in English using graphs and diagrams.
Understand your role during activities and work on issues in teams.
Effectively report the results of activities using presentation software and present solutions.

・ Be able to read, write, speak, and listen properly using English in the fields of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics).

・ Discover and solve issues in STEM fields.

・ Be able to investigate the issues and issues taken up in detail, make presentations, and convey opinions and ideas appropriately in English.

・ Read, write, speak, and listen in English in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics).

・ Discover issues in the STEM field and solve them to some extent.

subtitle: TOEIC Intermediate
educationalGoal: This class is for students who started from English Topics 5 (intermediate class) or for students who want to further improve their TOIEC scores for job hunting or going to graduate school. Students will learn the test taking techniques nessesary to improve each part of the TOEIC test. Students will learn skills for listening, grammar, and reading comprehention.
advice:
Students will have to attend every class from Monday to Friday. They must have the motivation to give all their time and effort to improve their TOEIC scores during the 3 intensive weeks of study.

Students will have to take the pre- and post-course IP tests.

Students are strongly encouraged to take the official TOEIC test right after finishing this course.

This class is dedicated to improving the TOEIC scores by learning test-taking strategies for listening, grammar, and reading comprehension. This class does not focus on communicative skills or grammar. Students must improve those skills on their own during this course.

Active learning includes presentations, Q & A, pair work, and group work.

Students will learn and practice basic grammar patterns through group work, pair work, short writing assignments, and presentations. Students will also learn effective techniques for studying English at the college level.
advice:

Classes will consist of active learning activities that practice reading, writing, speaking, and listening, as well as extensive group and pair work.
Before each class, students must complete homework assignments on Moodle.

Japanese culture topics include: everyday life of a college student in Japan, daily activities, special occasions (festivals, special holidays, etc.), working in Japan, Kanazawa architecture, and religion in Japan.

Course work consists of in-class activities and independent inquiry activities.

educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) functions and their graphs.
(2) equations and inverse functions.
(3) exponential functions and logarithmic functions.
(4) trigonometric functions and inverse trigonometric functions.
advice:
This is a basic course in mathematics and science for engineer. We will cover the following topics:

1. Functions, their graphs, displacement of graphs, and the limit value.
2. Equations and inverse functions.
3. Exponential functions and logarithmic functions.
4. Trigonometric functions and inverse trigonometric functions.

Extra classes may be held depending the comprehension level of students.
Students are required to review and preview each class. As a matter of particular emphasis, students are required to attempt the exercises after each class.
Extra materials may be distributed if necessary.
Students are required to show their procedure for solution/calculation logically and clearly in each assignment.
Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the instructor.

(1) Learn basic probabilities, conditional probabilities, and Bayes' theorem.
(2) Learn basic data organization and statistics.

title: データサイエンス物理
subtitle: Physics with Data Science
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
term:
2026年度

                2nd year 1st semester2nd year 2nd semester1st year 2nd semester
educationalGoal: In this course, students learn the fundamentals of physics, including description of motion, the three laws of motion, work and energy, momentum and collisions, and rotation and oscillation, using knowledge of vectors, derivatives, and integrals. The goal is also to apply the knowledge learned and to develop insight into the physics behind natural phenomena through logical thinking and data analysis.
advice:
Logical thinking and data analysis are conducted based on actual measurement data, and the ability to gain insight into the physics behind natural phenomena is nurtured. We will cover the following topics:

1. Dimension and units.
2. Motion in one dimension.
3. Motion in two dimensions.
4. Newton's laws of motion.
5. Energy of a system.
6. Conservation of energy.
7. Rotational motion.
8. Oscillatory motion.

Students are required to have a knowledge of vectors, differentiation, and integration.
Students will learn a number of formulas related to the laws of physics. Students will not only be expected to memorize the formulas but also be required to understand the meaning of these formulas.
books:
Textbooks：Serway Principles of Physics (mechanics) [Tokyo Kagaku Dougin]
Reference books：Basics of Physics 5th Edition [Gakujutsu Tosho Shuppan-sha Co., Ltd.], Dynamics to Understand Lecture [Shokabo Co., Ltd.]
Reserved books：Basics of Physics (mechanics) [Gakujutsu Tosho Shuppan-sha Co., Ltd.]
requiredKnowledge: Background knowledge: Basic knowledge of elementary mathematics such as trigonometric ratios, vectors, differentiation, integration, etc. Skills: Trigonometric ratios, vectors, differentiation, integration, etc., elementary mathematics calculation skills

activityGoals.body: Basic knowledge of mechanics such as speed, acceleration, and force.
Ability to evaluate the motion of an object by deriving and solving Newton’s equations of motion.
Ability to calculate potential energy using integral calculus and a knowledge of work and energy.
Ability to understand mechanical energy, conservation of momentum, and conservation of angular momentum.
Ability to perform data analysis using measured data and interpret the data based on logical thinking.
Ability to understand the content of the lesson by completing the homework and paticipating in group activities.

courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Engineering problems are often expressed as two-variable functions or multivariable functions. In this course, students will learn how to:
(1) derive partial derivatives.
(2) find the extreme values of two-variable functions.
(3) calculate a double integral using the iterated integral approach.
(4) calculate a double integral using the change of variables approach.
advice:
This is an advanced course following single-variable calculus and includes:

1. Multivariable functions, their limits and continuity, and partial derivatives.
2. Tangent plane and total differential for a multivariable function.
3. The chain rule in several variables.
4. Higher order partial derivatives and Taylor expansion of two-variable functions.
5. Maxima and minima of two-variable functions.
6. Iterated integration and reversing the order of integration.
7. Change of variables in a double integral.

Students are required to actively participate in class and to engage in the review and preview in every class.
Students are required to work on exercises after class and are expected to understand the contents of each class.
Students are required to explain carefully and logically the solution procedure in their homework and report.

Students should actively use the teachers' office hours and the Math. and Science Education Research Center.
books: Textbook: Advanced Mathematics A (Partial Derivative & Double Integral) [Kanazawa Institute of Technology]

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the concepts of multivariable functions and the calculation of partial derivatives.
Be able to find partial derivatives by applying the chain rule.
Be able to find the extreme values of two-variable functions.
Be able to understand the concept of multiple integration and perform it by iterated integration.
Be able to find the value of a double integral by variable transformation, especially polar transformation.
Attend every class, make a strong effort to understand the course contents and English mathematical expressions.

title: アドバンスト数理Ｂ
subtitle: Advanced Mathematics B
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
keywords: 1st order ODEs and properties of their solutions
Mathematical models for phenomena and analyses of their solutions
educationalGoal: Various issues in engineering, science and social science are often described by differential equations. Students will learn how to solve 1st order ordinary differential equations (ODEs), 2nd order constant-coefficient linear ODEs and systems of simultaneous linear ODEs, and will understand (1) how to construct mathematical models of phenomena, (2) solution method and geometrical concept and (3) how to analyze solution properties and characteristics. Students will learn the fundamentals of programming to develop the generic ability to analyze physical phenomena.
advice:
In the class, the students will learn differential equations (ODEs): (1) 1st order ODEs, (2) 2nd order constant-coefficient linear ODEs (homogeneous and inhomogeneous ODEs), and (3) systems of 1st order simultaneous linear ODEs. The students will learn the following analytical methods:
(I) How to express physical and social phenomena with ODEs (construction of mathematical models).
(II) How to solve specific types of ODEs and how to think geometrically about phenomena by means of solution curves and direction fields.
(III) Analytical methods in which students will analyze obtained solutions and acquire information pertinent to the activities of engineers such as the pattern and the speed of changes in various phenomena.
After the student learn the main themes of ODEs, the students will apply the above knowledge (I), (II), and (III) to computing projects by using formula manipulation system, and submit a report of their results.
In the class, the students will use MATLAB in the following activities:
1) Visualizing the solutions for ODEs and thinking geometrically.
2) Setting and evaluating the parameters of ODEs.
3) Modeling physical phenomena and deriving and analyzing their solutions.
Therefore, the students should install MATLAB on individual notebook computer, and should master basic usage of MATLAB beforehand.

              授業科目の学習・教育目標

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.1st order ODEs and properties of their solutions
2.2nd order homogeneous linear ODEs
3.2nd order inhomogeneous linear ODEs
4.Simultaneous systems of linear ODEs
5.Mathematical models for phenomena and analyses of their solutions

              Various issues in engineering, science and social science are often described by differential equations. Students will learn how to solve 1st order ordinary differential equations (ODEs), 2nd order constant-coefficient linear ODEs and systems of simultaneous linear ODEs, and will understand (1) how to construct mathematical models of phenomena, (2) solution method and geometrical concept and (3) how to analyze solution properties and characteristics. Students will learn the fundamentals of programming to develop the generic ability to analyze physical phenomena.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In the class, the students will learn differential equations (ODEs): (1) 1st order ODEs, (2) 2nd order constant-coefficient linear ODEs (homogeneous and inhomogeneous ODEs), and (3) systems of 1st order simultaneous linear ODEs. The students will learn the following analytical methods:
(I) How to express physical and social phenomena with ODEs (construction of mathematical models).
(II) How to solve specific types of ODEs and how to think geometrically about phenomena by means of solution curves and direction fields.
(III) Analytical methods in which students will analyze obtained solutions and acquire information pertinent to the activities of engineers such as the pattern and the speed of changes in various phenomena.
After the student learn the main themes of ODEs, the students will apply the above knowledge (I), (II), and (III) to computing projects by using formula manipulation system, and submit a report of their results.
In the class, the students will use MATLAB in the following activities:
1) Visualizing the solutions for ODEs and thinking geometrically.
2) Setting and evaluating the parameters of ODEs.
3) Modeling physical phenomena and deriving and analyzing their solutions.
Therefore, the students should install MATLAB on individual notebook computer, and should master basic usage of MATLAB beforehand.

title: 環境系数理
subtitle: Math and Science for Environmental Engineering
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Students will
(1) acquire the necessary mathematical knowledge of functions, calculus, and statistics for structural, soil, and fluid mechanics, materials, surveying, and environmental engineering.
(2) understand the importance of fundamental mathematics for solving problems in civil engineering.
(3) apply mathematical knowledge to various problems.
advice:
This is a course on the fundamental mathematics used in structural mechanics, soil mechanics, fluid mechanics, materials technology, surveying, and environmental engineering.
Students will apply the learned mathematics to analyze various phenomena related to environmental civil engineering.

Students are expected to
(1) deepen their mathematical understanding of exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, and tackle real problems requiring the application of this knowledge.
(2) deepen their mathematical understanding of differentiation and integration, and tackle real problems requiring the application of this knowledge.
(3) understand basic operations and graph drawings and data analysis by using Excel.
(4) learn statistical data processing methods and analyze data generated in experiments.
(5) utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center and the teachers of the  environmental civil engineering.

This course should make it possible for students to apply their knowledge of fundamental mathematics to solve  environmental civil engineering problems.
books: Textbook: "Math and Science for Environmental Engineering",  KIT
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of mathematics learned in Mathematics and Science for Engineer I, II.

activityGoals.body: Ability to apply knowledge of fundamental functions to environmental problems.
Ability to apply knowledge of calculus to environmental problems.
Ability to make graphs of fundamental functions and data analysis using Excel.
Ability to analyze environmental experimental data and understand statistical processing.
Ability to understand the meanings of fundamental English words for mathematics and environmental engineering.
Ability to understand the contents of the class, complete all reports, attend every class, etc.

subtitle: Linear Algebra I
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) vector operations.
(2) matrix operations.
(3) solving linear systems using “row reduction.”
(4) representing linear transformations of a plane or a space.
advice:
This is a basic course in linear algebra. We will cover the following topics:

1. Vectors
1.1 Vectors and their operations
1.2 Dot products and cross products of vectors
1.3 The equation of a plane or a line
2. Matrices and linear maps
2.1 Matrices and their operations
2.2 Linear systems and row reduction
2.3 Linear maps and linear transformation

Classes include exercises and quizzes; a final examination will be given at the end of the semester.
Daily preparation and review are important. Students are required to complete the designated tasks.
Students should prepare reports and study research topics in a planned manner, and strictly avoid plagiarism.
Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the teacher.
books:
Textbook: Linear Algebra I (KIT Math and Science Academic Foundations Programs)
Reference book: A First Course in Linear Algebra (Open Textbook Library)[Lyryx]
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of mathematics, especially trigonometric functions.

activityGoals.body: Understand the concept of vectors and be able to properly perform vector operations.
Understand the concept of matrices and be able to properly perform matrix operations.
Be able to find solutions to linear systems by using row reduction.
Understand the concept of a linear transforms and be able to represent them in matrix form.
Understand the meanings of fundamental english words for mathematics.
Understand the contents of the course and be able to complete the required tasks by the announced deadlines.

2.2 Eigenvalues and eigenvectors

Students should prepare reports and study research topics in a planned manner, and strictly avoid plagiarism.

              Students will learn:
(1) the properties of a determinant and a method to calculate determinants.
(2) the properties of cofactors.
(3) the concept of a vector space and a basis.
(4) eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is a basic course in linear algebra, continued from “Linea Algebra I.” We will cover the following topics:

1. Determinants
1.1 Definition of determinant.
1.2 Properties of the determinant and calculation method
1.3 Cofactors and their applications
2. Vector spaces and Eigenvalue
2.1 Vector spaces
2.2 Eigenvalues and eigenvectors

Classes include exercises and quizzes; a final examination will be given at the end of the semester.
Daily preparation and review are important. Students are required to complete the designated tasks.
Students should prepare reports and study research topics in a planned manner, and strictly avoid plagiarism.

courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) limit value and continuity of functions.
(2) exponential functions, logarithmic functions, trigonometric functions, and inverse trigonometric functions.
(3) differentiation and its applications.
(4) functions expressing the motion of an object.
advice:
This is a basic course in integrated mathematics and science for engineering. We will cover the following topics:

1. Functions, their graphs, displacement of graphs, and the limit value and continuity of functions.
2. Equations and inverse functions.
3. Differentiation of various functions.
4. Applications of differentiation.

Extra classes may be held depending the comprehension level of students.
Students are required to review and preview each class. As a matter of particular emphasis, students are required to attempt the exercises after each class.
Extra materials may be distributed if necessary.
Students are required to show their solution/calculation procedure logically and clearly in each assignment.
Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the teacher.

activityGoals.body: Understand the theory, limits, and continuity of functions and draw graphs of functions.
Understand the theory of differentiation and find the derivatives of basic functions.
Understand the theory of power series expansion and find the approximate expressions of functions.
Understand the function of motion and apply to the differentiation.
Understand the meanings of fundamental english words for mathematics.
Be able to demonstrate an understanding of all topics, attend every class, and do the required work.

title: 工学のための数理工Ⅱ（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Integrated Math and Science for Engineering II
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) definite and indefinite integrals, integration by parts and integration by substitution.
(2) equations of motion as an application of integrals.
(3) line integrals and energy.
(4) moments of force, center of gravity, and moments of inertia.
advice:
This is a basic course in integrated mathematics and science for engineering. We will cover the following topics:
1. Sum of sequences and their limit, definite and indefinite integrals, integration by parts and integration by substitution.
2. 1st-order differential equations, 2nd-order linear differential equations, equations of motion and mechanics.
3. Line integral, work and energy, motion of a system of particles.
4. Areas between two curves, multiple integrals, volume of a solid, center of gravity, rotational motion and moments of inertia.
Extra classes may be held depending the comprehension level of students.
Students are required to review and preview each class. As a matter of particular emphasis, students are required to attempt the exercises after each class.
Extra materials may be distributed if necessary.
Students are required to show their procedure for solution/calculation logically and clearly in each assignment.
Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the instructor.
books:
Textbook:             Integrated Math and Science for Engineering II
Reference books:  Integrated Math and Science for Engineering I
Calculus Volume 1, 2, 3 (OpenStax) https://openstax.org/details/books/calculus-volume-1,
https://openstax.org/details/books/calculus-volume-2, https://openstax.org/details/books/calculus-volume-3
requiredKnowledge:
Skills and knowledge from the Integrated Math and Science for Engineering I.
Knowledge of exponential functions, logarithmic functions, and trigonometric functions.
Basic calculation skills for differentiation.

activityGoals.body: Evaluate the integrals of various functions and integration by parts and integration by substitution.
Solve separable, 1st-order linear and 2nd-order, linear, homogeneous differential equations.
Understand the concept of line integrals, and explain the energy of a system.
Evaluate the areas, the volumes of a solid, moments of inertia, and the center of gravity for a solid.
Understand the meanings of fundamental English words for mathematics.
Be able to demonstrate an understanding of all topics, attend every class, and do the required works.

title: 環境・建築系数理（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Math and Science for Environmental Engineering and Architecture
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Students will
(1) acquire the necessary mathematical knowledge of functions, calculus, and statistics for structural, soil, and fluid mechanics, materials, surveying, and environmental engineering.
(2) understand the importance of fundamental mathematics for solving problems in architecture and civil engineering.
(3) apply mathematical knowledge to various problems.
advice:
This is a course on the fundamental mathematics used in structural mechanics, soil mechanics, fluid mechanics, materials technology, surveying, and environmental engineering.
Students will apply the learned mathematics to analyze various phenomena related to architecture and environmental civil engineering.

Students are expected to
(1) deepen their mathematical understanding of exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, and tackle real problems requiring the application of this knowledge.
(2) deepen their mathematical understanding of differentiation and integration, and tackle real problems requiring the application of this knowledge.
(3) understand basic operations and graph drawings and data analysis by using Excel.
(4) learn statistical data processing methods and analyze data generated in experiments.
(5) utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center and the teachers of the architecture and the civil engineering.

This course should make it possible for students to apply their knowledge of fundamental mathematics to solve architecture and environmental civil engineering problems.

subtitle: Mathematics for Informatics
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn how to express n-base and floating point numbers (IEEE754).
(2) apply the concept of sets to logical algebra and learn the basics of how to represent logic in a computer. Learn how to configure logic circuits to implement logic in a computer.
(3) learn basic probabilities, conditional probabilities, and Bayes' theorem. Learn basic data organization and statistics using Excel.
advice:
This is a basic course in mathematics, logic, and statistics. We will cover the following topics:

1. n-base: binary system, octal system, hexadecimal system.
2. Representation of numbers in computers: Floating point number (IEEE754).
3. Sets and Logic: basic set theory, propositional logic, truth table, logical circuit.
4. Basic probabilities: Permutations and combinations, probabilities, conditional probabilities and Bayes' theorem.
5: A data analysis method using statistics: Frequency distribution table, histogram, correlation diagram, mean/variance, covariance/correlation coefficient.

Students are expected to understand above materials.
Students are expected to process data using Excel (computer spreadsheet software).
Students are expected to complete the exercises on their own without consulting/copying others.
Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the teacher.

title: 基礎化学（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Fundamental Chemistry
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the chemical foundations necessary for science and engineering.
(2) learn how to apply attitude and chemistry knowledge to science and engineering.
(3) establish a style of study using a preview and review approach.
(4) develop an autonomous and consecutive self-directed study ability.
advice:
This is a course in chemical foundations. We will cover the following:

1. Atomic Structure, Electron Configuration, Periodic Table, Ionization Energy, and Electron Affinity.
2. Chemical Bond, Hybrid Orbital, Electronegativity, and Polarity of Molecules.
3. Calculation of Unknown Molecular Weights Using the “Ideal Gas Law” from Given Conditions.
4. Expressions for Various Concentrations of Solutions, Molarity, and Molar Fractions.
5. Expressions for Reaction Rate and the Temperature Dependence of Reaction Rate.
6. Chemical Equilibrium, Ionization Equilibrium of Electrolyte Solution, and Calculation of pH.
7. Reaction of Acid and Base, Oxidation-reduction Reaction, and Organic Compounds.

(1) The class will follow the order of the contents in the textbook according to this syllabus.
(2) Students are expected to do the homework, previews, and reviews for every class.
(3) Students are expected to ask the teacher questions and use the Math. and Science Education Research Center.
(4) Students are expected not to be late, as the accumulation of learning is important.
(5) Students are expected to approach exams and quizzes with sufficient preparation.
(6) Some details of the course may be changed as the course progresses.
books:
Textbooks：John Kenkel, “Basic Chemistry Concepts and Exercises”, CRC Press
Reference books：John Mcmarry, “Organic Chemistry”, Brooks/Cole Pub Co
Peter Atkins, De Paula, Julio, James Keeler, “Atkins' Physical Chemistry”, Oxford Univ Pr
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge:
(1) High school chemistry is not a prerequisite. However, students will need to work hard in the course and make sufficient effort to master the topics.
(2) Students are expected to read the textbook, complete the homework, and engage in the previews and reviews.

activityGoals.body: Understand the periodic law of elements and explain basic orbital properties.
Explain basic chemical bonds, the mechanism of hybrid orbitals, and electronegativity.
Calculate an unknown molecular weight and amount of substance using the ideal gas law.
Understand the concentration of solutions and chemical equilibrium, explain it, and calculate pH.
Understand and explain the mechanism of oxidation-reduction reaction, etc.
Attendance at every class and acquisition of  English explanations and consecutive self-directed study ability.

title: 基礎生物（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Fundamental Biology
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal: During the long evolutionary history of life on Earth, organisms have been modified in many different ways. The human organism is included in this process. The driving force of evolution is diversity. In this course, we will learn about life, the environment and relationships among organisms.
advice:
The 21st century has been called the Century of Life Science. Biology is a complex study in a new frame, whether taught by liberal arts faculty or by physical science faculty. We will develop the power to think about the subject rather than place an overemphasis on detailed content knowledge. Elements of the class will include:

(1) Structure and functions of life
(2) The continuity of life
(3) Response and regulation in organisms
(4) Organisms and their environment
(5) Life-science technology and society

Classes will be conducted using various methods: lectures, seminars, video viewing or a combination of these.
books: Textbooks：Ya-Sa-Shi-I Biological Science (English version) YODOSHA:ISBN978-4-7581-2070-8
requiredKnowledge: To gain more insight, the student should be interested in TV and news coverage.

              During the long evolutionary history of life on Earth, organisms have been modified in many different ways. The human organism is included in this process.               The 21st century has been called the Century of Life Science. Biology is a complex study in a new frame, whether taught by liberal arts faculty or by physical science faculty. (5) Life-science technology and society

books:

courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Utilization of data is indispensable for realizing the smart society Society 5.0, and it will be indispensable in the future to acquire a background in data science.
In this lecture, you will learn the two most basic methods of data analysis, which occupy a very large part of data science, 1) various methods of data aggregation and 2) regression analysis through lectures and exercises. It aims to.
advice:
In this class, you will learn the introductory contents of data analysis, which is important in data science, through lectures and exercises.
First, we will learn about "aggregation" for understanding the characteristics of data sets for various types of data. Preceding subject "Data Science"
In addition to the simple tabulation learned in "Introduction to Su", to understand the procedure for stratified tabulation and cross tabulation, and to visualize the data set.
You will also learn about graph drawing. Learn about the correlation between the following data sets. Furthermore, it is widely used in various fields.
Learn about (linear) regression analysis.
In each case, not only lectures by classroom lectures, but also exercises to actually move hands and perform analysis will be conducted.
The mathematical explanation of the mathematical background is kept to the minimum for understanding the method, practical exercises are performed, and the concrete operation method and analysis of the tool are performed.
Try to devote time to explaining the findings that can be expected from the results.
books:
Do not use textbooks.
References will be given as appropriate in class.
requiredKnowledge:
It is essential to take the preceding course "Introduction to Data Science" and acquire the basic operations and data literacy of Microsoft Excel.
Furthermore, it is strongly recommended to take "Statistics for Engineers" to learn the basics of statistics.
Since Microsoft Excel will be used in each class, bring a laptop PC with Microsoft Excel installed.

subtitle: Design Project / Introduction
courseType: Design Project ProgramDesign Project CoursesDesign Project
educationalGoal:
-To gain the basic skills needed in processes from finding problems to solutions.
-To understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively.
-To be able to find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objectives, and events.
-To be able to deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly.
-To gain various basic skills to proceed smoothly with verification activities.
-To be able to have a picture of technology fields and engineers of discipline.
advice:
In this course, students will learn the basic skills required for the validation process and problem-solving process in order to achieve the above-mentioned learning and education goals. In addition, this course focuses on the characteristic experiments of the department.One is to learn the basics of “data handling skills” required to collect, organize, analyze, hypothesis test, visualize, and report data. The other is to learn the basic skills of “Science and Engineering PBL”, which includes the basic elements of the process from problem discovery to solution and verification activities. Students learn "data handling skills" and "science and technology PBL" through experiments on basic laws related to electrical and electronic engineering.In “Data Handling Skills”, students acquire and establish knowledge essential for planning, designing, executing, and operating various projects, and learn how to use various measuring instruments. “Science and Engineering PBL (Project Based Learning)” cultivates problem discovery and resolution skills through project issues. The following six project themes will be dealt with, focusing on "Direct Current".
(1) Ohm's Law, (2) Power Supplies, (3) Electric Line of Force & Equipotential Lines, (4) Resistors in Series & in Parallel, (5) Kirchhoff's Laws & Superposition Theorem, (6) Joule's Law
In order to secure the necessary experiment time, the class will be conducted on the premise of preparation. Always be aware of “safety” during the experiment. In each project, the first week is centered on the acquisition of knowledge and skills necessary for the experiment, and the second week is to tackle the missions using the knowledge and techniques acquired by the team in the first week.
books: Design Project / Introduction of 2026 (Experiment) (Department of Electrical Energy Systems Engineering, Department of Electronics and Information Systems Engineering), Kanazawa Institute of Technology
requiredKnowledge: Each project covers the basic laws and phenomena handled in classes such as "Electric Circuit I" and "Electromagnetics I / II". Challenge the experiment with awareness of the "connection" with these subjects. When collecting information, it is good to use information that suits the purpose of the experiment, such as a Library Center or the Internet. In addition, since reports and posters are created on a personal computer, it is necessary to quickly learn how to use the personal computer and how to use the campus printer.

Students learn "data handling skills" and "science and technology PBL" through experiments on basic laws related to electrical and electronic engineering.In “Data Handling Skills”, students acquire and establish knowledge essential for planning, designing, executing, and operating various projects, and learn how to use various measuring instruments. “Science and Engineering PBL (Project Based Learning)” cultivates problem discovery and resolution skills through project issues. The following six project themes will be dealt with, focusing on "Direct Current".
(1) Ohm's Law, (2) Power Supplies, (3) Electric Line of Force & Equipotential Lines, (4) Resistors in Series & in Parallel, (5) Kirchhoff's Laws & Superposition Theorem, (6) Joule's Law
In order to secure the necessary experiment time, the class will be conducted on the premise of preparation. Always be aware of “safety” during the experiment. In each project, the first week is centered on the acquisition of knowledge and skills necessary for the experiment, and the second week is to tackle the missions using the knowledge and techniques acquired by the team in the first week.

-To gain various basic skills to proceed smoothly with verification activities.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, to achieve the above educational goals, the students will learn basic skills required for verification and problem-solving processes.
This course will deal with characteristic things of corresponding department.
One is that the students will learn basics of “data-handling skills” needed for collection → organization → analysis→ hypothesis → visualization → report.
One is that the students will learn basic skills of “PBL for science and technology” including basic elements of processes from problem-finding to solution and verification activities.
By the experiment of the field of building structure, students perform the strength examination of the paper
structure which students made by a team. Students put the structure which students made between the fulcrums of 40cm in a structure object similar to a bridge, and loading does a weight at the center. Students compete
with weight before a structure collapsing for durability time. Students make the structure from the design
characteristics of the shape and a structural mechanics-like viewpoint using paper material.
Students make an insulation material of 15cm *15cm at thickness 3cm every team and, by the experiment of the field of building environment, measure the insulation performance. The insulation performance measures a heat flux level or surface temperature and calculates it using the data. The material to use for an insulation material concentrates an idea every team and devises composition of the material.

educationalGoal:
You will experience the activities of solving familiar problems of the actual world.
You will develop fundamental skills, such as information gathering of market trend and customer's demand, idea creation, and shaping of the idea.
You will also improve your communication skills in English.
advice:
By experiencing the process of solving familiar problems of the actual world, you will understand the key feature of the problem that people are concerned about, which enables you to realize the necessity for learning of various fields. Through the project-based learning, you will have the opportunity to learn about the engineering design process, which includes
‐discovering the problems of the community and daily life problems in a team
‐combining the collected information
‐creating multiple proposals (or ideas) which will lead to the possible solutions to the problem
‐proposing the technique to put the best solution into shape.
You are required to do a lot of homework assignments, such as information collection of market trend and custom-er's demand, idea creation, shaping of the idea and preparation for presentation.
You will be graded by your reports, presentations and portfolios; ratio of 50% each from team and indivisual is taken to give a total grade.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅡ
subtitle: Design Project II
courseType: Design Project ProgramDesign Project CoursesDesign Project
educationalGoal:
You will be able to gain experience, knowledge, and skills to: Perform activities
based on logical thinking; Perform activities to solve an open-ended problem; Gather and utilize individual knowledge to solve problems; and Explore and creatively discover new problems.
advice:
- Project teams will work to gather new and previously gained knowledge, information, and experience towards solving real world problems of others.

- The Main Theme will be presented by the instructor in class.

- Through the project design activities, students are expected to be able to perform ‘activities based on logical thinking’, and their activities focus on: (a) Understanding required resources (information and experience), and making and evaluating decisions made logically based on data, facts, and truth; (b) Realizing characteristics of problems involved in human activities and needs of accumulating learning experiences of different fields of study; (c) Realizing the importance of finding Project Themes in a suited area defined by abilities; (d) Paying attention on problems and situations existing in the real world; (e) Ways to proceed activities (works) in a team (organization), and ways to find roles as a team member as simulation of OJT; (f) Ways to interact with others of different social positions; and (g) Realizing individual abilities by using basic knowledge through problem-solving process.
books: None
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge and experience learned and gained prior to the beginning of the course.

activityGoals.body: To be able to make and evaluate the decision made logically based on data, facts, and truth.
To be able to understand and gain resources (information and experience, etc.) required for project activities.
To be able to find a Project Theme appropriate for needs, abilities, and compensations from the Main Theme.
To be able to realize existing problems and develop awareness of problem-finding in the real world.
To be able to proceed effective project activities efficiently as a team (organization).
To be able to self-evaluate abilities objectively.

              学習・教育目標

              1.Problem solving skills

              You will be able to gain experience, knowledge, and skills to: Perform activities
based on logical thinking; Perform activities to solve an open-ended problem; Gather and utilize individual knowledge to solve problems; and Explore and creatively discover new problems.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              - Project teams will work to gather new and previously gained knowledge, information, and experience towards solving real world problems of others.

- The Main Theme will be presented by the instructor in class.

- Through the project design activities, students are expected to be able to perform ‘activities based on logical thinking’, and their activities focus on: (a) Understanding required resources (information and experience), and making and evaluating decisions made logically based on data, facts, and truth; (b) Realizing characteristics of problems involved in human activities and needs of accumulating learning experiences of different fields of study; (c) Realizing the importance of finding Project Themes in a suited area defined by abilities; (d) Paying attention on problems and situations existing in the real world; (e) Ways to proceed activities (works) in a team (organization), and ways to find roles as a team member as simulation of OJT; (f) Ways to interact with others of different social positions; and (g) Realizing individual abilities by using basic knowledge through problem-solving process.

educationalGoal:
In this course, students gather the knowledge, experience, and information needed
to solve others’ problems in real-world settings, integrate them individually or
in teams, and carry out organized project activities as a team. Students build on
the basic skills learned in the prerequisite course Project Design I. Through thes
e activities, they explore problems with diverse possible answers and develop the
ability to solve them logically and creatively.
advice:
Teams conduct organized project activities using a main theme provided by the instructor, targeting the resoluti
on of problems faced by communities, companies, and other real-world stakeholders. Students collect not only pre
viously acquired knowledge and experience but also practical data and information necessary to advance the proje
ct, acquire new insights through research and hands-on experience, and integrate these into activities grounded
in logical thinking.
Students aim to carry out deeper project work efficiently by building on the fundamental skills acquired in the
prerequisite course Project Design I.
When conducting activities, pay attention to the following points:
- Monitor real-world conditions and problems, and identify project themes within a scope appropriate to each ind
ividual’s or team’s capabilities.
- Obtain data from reliable information sources.
- Collect a sufficient amount of information worthy of analysis and use appropriate tools for that analysis.
- Consider how to carry out work within the team (organization) and how to behave as a team member.
- Be considerate when dealing with stakeholders who hold different perspectives.
- Through thorough inquiry, assess your own level and recognize the importance of foundational knowledge.

title: プロジェクトデザイン実践（実験）(機械工学科)
subtitle: Design Project / Implementing and Operating
courseType: Design Project ProgramDesign Project CoursesDesign Project
educationalGoal:
-To gain skills to verify hypotheses or solution concept with logical approaches.
-To understand phenomena, objects and events quantitatively with high credibility based on data science.
-To reliably find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objects, events.
-To deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly.
-To gain basic skills to credibly and smoothly conduct verification activities.
-To have an image of the technology fields and engineers in the discipline.
advice:
-Learn how to proceed with the hypothesis testing process. Learn the process of verifying the effectiveness/acceptability of methods aimed at solving problems.
-Learn "data processing skills" necessary for data collection, organization, analysis, hypothesis, visualization, and reporting.
-Students will learn "skills to advance the verification process" and "basic skills of verification activities" from hypothesis planning to verification based on data science.
-The Department of Mechanical Engineering has the theme of "heat sink," which is a heat dissipation mechanism for engines, etc., as the basis of thermal engineering.
-Performance has been verified with experimental tests and evidence-based prototypes.
-Based on this validation, you will learn data collection skills, validation process progress skills, and validation factor solution proposals.
[Activity report]
Regardless of the effectiveness of the solution proposal, the results of the project activities are compiled into a project report and presented in a poster session or verbally.
requiredKnowledge:
Comprehensive experience in "investigation of information", "how to put out ideas", "experimental methods", and "problem discovery / problem solving / team activity / logical verification activity" acquired in Project Design Introduction I/II. In order to make use of these, it is necessary to review these items.
At the same time, students must pay attention to the utilization and improvement of learning CAD skills in mechanical drawing.
This course uses Yumekobo machine tools, so be sure to obtain a license.

activityGoals.body: To be able to proceed with activities from finding problems to solutions.
To be able to understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively.
To be able to find characteristics, features, and laws of phenomena, objects, and events.
To be able to deliver acquired information to a third person intelligibly.
To be able to utilize various basic skills needed to proceed smoothly with verification activities.
To be able to have a picture of the technology fields and engineers in the discipline.

courseType: Design Project ProgramDesign Project CoursesDesign Project
keywords: Credibility PBL for science and technology
educationalGoal:

advice:
This is a basic skills course for driving engineering projects. We will cover the following materials:

1. Understand the basic skills for measurements, analysis, verification, and report of the data while learning how to use measuring equipment and its theory.
2. Understand basic skills for improving the authenticity of the measured data through verification processes.

The above skills will be obtained through the following basic projects:
A. Measurements of AC waveforms using an oscilloscope
B. Characteristics of circuit elements under AC waveform supply
C. Characteristics of resonance circuits
D. Measurements of AC power
E. Design of a logic circuit using Digital ICs
F. Measurements of static characteristics of a semiconductor device

This course also includes an applied project in order to understand how to drive engineering projects by using the obtained basic skills.

              This is a basic skills course for driving engineering projects. We will cover the following materials:

F. Measurements of static characteristics of a semiconductor device

This course also includes an applied project in order to understand how to drive engineering projects by using the obtained basic skills.

title: プロジェクトデザイン実践（実験）(建築)
subtitle: Design Project / Implementing and Operating
courseType: Design Project ProgramDesign Project CoursesDesign Project
educationalGoal: Students will:(1) learn a skill of inspection process of a hypothesis or the solution to the problem concept,(2) understand a phenomenon, an object, a phenomenon quantitatively and qualitatively,(3) tell information to a third party clearly,(4) learn various skills required for pushing forward inspection activity smoothly,(5) imagine a technical area and an engineer image to learn in architecture.
advice: Students learn how to lead processes to inspect a hypothesis or learn how to lead processes to inspect effectiveness / acceptance characteristics of the specific part among the characteristics of a concept aiming at a solution to the problem or the concept.In part students learn "a building design skill" to need data in collection → rearranging → analysis → hypothesis → visualization → report. In part "a structure design skill" to lead to the inspection, "an environmental design skill" and "an element skill of the inspection activity" are learned by the drafting of the hypothesis.(1) Building design skill: Students announce the design of a house that an individual designed in a group and narrow it down to one basic design plan based on exchange of opinions. (2) Environmental design skill: Based on basic design plan, students perform the examination of the environmental characteristic (insulation characteristics, sound, illumination, air conditioning, ventilation) while using analysis tools. (3) Structure design skill: Based on basic design plan, students examine construction and how to structure and the method of construction. Students examine examination and the transformation of the material of the Class basic axis and perform the loading experiment with the model. (4) Inspection activity skill: Students summarize result provided by a series of design activity in a project report and announce the team by a poster session and plan communalization of the knowledge in the whole class.
books: None
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable to have the experience that worked on design of a house in individuals as a design problem. It is desirable to learn the basics of how to write building plan. It is desirable to review the common rule including how to write dimensions, a building term and the drawing symbol that the design is a team and will wrestle.

Be able to tell the information that oneself got to a third party clearly
Be able to utilize various basic skills to need if students push forward inspection activity smoothly
Be able to imagine a technical area and an engineer image to learn in architecture

educationalGoal: Understand the mechanics of personal computers and their capabilities and possibilities. On top of that, students will acquire the basic ability to utilize personal computers as students and members of society for purposes such as education, research, and technological development. In particular, students will acquire the ability to create documents and presentation materials.
advice:
In this course, you will learn the following basics of using your personal computer (laptop computer) for study and student life.
1. Basic PC skills: Learn basic operations such as using Windows and software installation.
2. Networks: Learn how to set up connections to on-campus and off-campus networks, how to view on-campus and off-campus web pages, how to use the on-campus web systems, learn about network security and anti-virus software, and learn the proper behaviors when using networks.
3. MS Office software: Learn basic skills in document creation and presentation material creation.

The 1st and 2nd class sessions will be held during the orientation period. Guidance will be provided during the  3rd class session. From the 4th to the 8th class sessions, quizzes using video materials and the e-syllabus will be available. Students who complete the quiz (scoring full marks) by the day before the class session will be exempt from attending the face-to-face class for that session only.
There are 8 class sessions. Missing 3 or more sessions will result in failure (due to poor attendance).
Pass/fail is determined by the final report. Only students who pass all quizzes from sessions 4 through 8 will be permitted to begin work on the final report.
books: Introduction to ICT/Introduction to Data Sciense 2026(Kanazawa Institute of Technology)

              In this course, you will learn the following basic knowledge as an introduction to data science.

1. Basic operations of Excel: Learn the basic operations of the spreadsheet software Excel, which is an introductory tool for handling data.
2. Aggregation/analysis of experimental data: Use Excel to aggregate/analyze experimental data.
3. Questionnaire data aggregation/analysis: Use Excel to aggregate/analyze questionnaire data.
4. Aggregation/analysis of open data: Use Excel to aggregate/analyze open data.

Each class session includes a quiz using video materials and the e-syllabus. Students who complete the quiz (scoring full marks) by the day before the class session are exempt from attending the in-person session for that particular session only.
There are seven class sessions. Missing three or more sessions will result in failure (due to poor attendance).
Pass/fail is determined by the final report. Only students who have passed all quizzes from the 1st to 7th class session will be permitted to begin the final report.

subtitle: Web Design
educationalGoal:
This course is for an educational goal of the Dept. of Management Systems to acquire "Information design basic ability". Students will:
(1)acquire the basic ability to utilize IT including mark-up language and the Internet,
(2)learn the fundamental theory of WWW (World Wide Web) site,
(3)learn how to create, manage and operate web pages.
advice:
To create, manage and operate a WWW site, the following 3 abilities are required:
(1)	The ability to understand the WWW site production process,
(a)	Planning a WWW site,
(b)	Design and implement a WWW site,
(c)	Manage and Operate a WWW site.
(2)	The ability to understand and apply HTML (Hyper-Text Mark-up Language) and CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) to produce a WWW site,
(3)	The ability to produce a web site that considers effective expression of information, ease of use, and availability to anyone.

Students will acquire abilities 1 and 2 mainly through lectures and exercises in the first half of the course; they will acquire ability 3 in the second half of the course.
