title: データアナリティクス入門
subtitle: Data Analytics Basic
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will:
(1) acquire a basic knowledge of data analytics.
(2) learn how to collect, aggregate, and visualize data based on questionnaire surveys.
(3) learn how to use statistical methods of sampling.
advice:
To analyze data properly, the following four abilities are required:
  1. The ability to collect data according to purpose and hypothesized issues.
  2. The ability to aggregate data in a table according to the data format.
  3. The ability to display data visually using graphs.
  4. The ability to verify hypotheses with statistical methods.

Students will acquire abilities 1 to 3 mainly through the questionnaire survey exercises in the first half of the course; ability 4 will be learned through exercises using sample data in the second half of the course.

Be able to create and improve a questionnaire sheet.
Be able to use simple/cross-tabulation to analyze questionnaire results.

title: ＩＴシステム基礎
subtitle: Information Technology Basic
educationalGoal:
This course is designed to achieve the learning and education goal of the information design fundamentals in the Department of Management Information.
Its purpose is to train students who have a fundamental level of knowledge and skills in information technology on the user side. The topics are essentially those covered on the IT passport test, as indicated by the keywords shown here.
advice:
This course is designed to achieve the Department of Management Information Systems’ learning and educational objective of developing foundational competencies in Information Design.
The course aims to cultivate students who possess fundamental knowledge and skills related to AI, Digital Transformation (DX), and Data Science. Among the learning components of the Mathematics, Data Science, and AI Education Program, students will primarily study the content indicated by key terms while also deepening their understanding of the specialized fields within the Department of Management Information Systems.
As foundational knowledge of AI, students will learn the definition of AI, societal changes brought about by AI, the utilization of data in society, and application domains of AI.
Regarding Data and AI technologies, students will study methods of data utilization, ethics related to data, and security issues concerning data and AI.
In addition, students will learn the fundamentals of statistics and mathematics, algorithms, programming, and practical data utilization.
Students are required to prepare a report on applications of AI.
books: 改定新版　はじめてのAIリテラシー、技術評論社
requiredKnowledge: Students should enroll in this course only after thoroughly understanding the content of the first-year spring semester courses Introduction to Data Science and Data Analytics Basic

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course is designed to achieve the Department of Management Information Systems’ learning and educational objective of developing foundational competencies in Information Design.
The course aims to cultivate students who possess fundamental knowledge and skills related to AI, Digital Transformation (DX), and Data Science. Among the learning components of the Mathematics, Data Science, and AI Education Program, students will primarily study the content indicated by key terms while also deepening their understanding of the specialized fields within the Department of Management Information Systems.
As foundational knowledge of AI, students will learn the definition of AI, societal changes brought about by AI, the utilization of data in society, and application domains of AI.
Regarding Data and AI technologies, students will study methods of data utilization, ethics related to data, and security issues concerning data and AI.
In addition, students will learn the fundamentals of statistics and mathematics, algorithms, programming, and practical data utilization.

title: 経営分析とＥＳＧ
subtitle: Business Analysis and ESG
educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Financial Ability” learning/education goal of the Faculty of Management Information. In order for managers to fulfill their duties in the future, analytical information on management activities is required. In this course, students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary for management analysis and develop the ability to make comprehensive judgments on the results of management analysis from a multifaceted perspective.
advice:
In the first part of the course, students will review their knowledge of preparing financial statements
(such as bookkeeping).
In the second part, students will learn the key points of financial analysis and analytical indicators. And then, students will practice financial analysis of specific companies using the analytical indicators they have learned.
 Finally, students will prepare and give a presentation on the results of their financial analysis.
When doing the assigned exercises, it is important that students pay attention to economic news and company information and study in depth their target company and industry.
books:
Textbook: 経営分析入門 : データから企業を読み解く[同文舘出版]
Reference book: 合格テキスト日商簿記3級　第15版(Ver.15.0)[TAC株式会社出版事業部]
Reserved Book: Not specified
requiredKnowledge: Students will need to thoroughly review what they learned in Basics of Corporate Accounting before taking this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand that financial analysis information is useful for making decisions.
Be able to collect and organize corporate information through EDINET, HP, and other media.
Be able to understand the indicators of financial analysis and use them in exercises.
Be able to describe the findings from the financial analysis, considering the corporate environment.
Be able to understand how to prepare and the characteristics of various financial statements.

achievementLevels.ideal:
・ Be able to recognize that financial analysis information is useful for managers and interested parties, and understand what information users are looking for.
・ Be able to use EDINET and HP to collect company and industry information and analyze characteristics of specific industries and companies.
・ Be able to analyze the financial status of specific companies using accounting-related knowledge and financial analysis formulas.
・ Be able to summarize the results of financial analysis in reports, and create materials.
・　Be able to explain the methods for preparing and characteristics of various financial statements.
achievementLevels.standard:
・ Be able to understand that financial analysis results are useful for managers and interested parties.
・ Be able to use EDINET and HP to collect company and industry information.
・ Be able to calculate indicators of financial analysis for specific companies.
・ Be able to summarize the results of financial analysis in reports and give appropriate presentations.
・　Be able to understand how to prepare and the characteristics of various financial statements.

title: 戦略会計入門
subtitle: Management Accounting Basic
educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Financial Accounting Basic Ability” learning/education goal of the Department of Management Information. It aims to cultivate in the students various skills related to the creation of profit plans and cash plans, using exercises relating accounting information and the financial management of companies from a profit management and money management perspective.
advice:
This course consists of three parts:
In the first part, students will learn about variable income statements, CVP analysis, and profit charts.
In the second part, students will learn to create profit plans, focusing on relevant exercises.
In the third part, we will cover topics from profit planning to financial planning, focusing on exercises.

Since there are numbers of exercises to prepare, it is important that students take an active approach to the class.
books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Students should review the contents of Basic Accounting, a course that must be taken prior to this course.
It is also important for students to understand that the contents learned in this course will be needed for　"Strategic Accounting Application".

activityGoals.body: Be able to create a variable income statement and perform a CVP analysis.
Be able to create a profit plan master plan following the profit plan creation procedure.
Be able to create an estimated income statement.
Be able to understand the importance of cash flow management.
Be able to create an estimated balance sheet / estimated cash flow statement.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course consists of three parts:
In the first part, students will learn about variable income statements, CVP analysis, and profit charts.
In the second part, students will learn to create profit plans, focusing on relevant exercises.
In the third part, we will cover topics from profit planning to financial planning, focusing on exercises.

Since there are numbers of exercises to prepare, it is important that students take an active approach to the class.

subtitle: Logical Thinking
educationalGoal:
This course deals with the way of logical thinking, especially for business purpose.
Students will learn:
(1) what are the basic concepts and the way of logical thinking.
(2) how to make decisions or solve problems based on the logical thinking through many kinds of simple exercise.

We will cover the following topics:
1) Basics of formal logic and reasoning.

title: データベースマネジメント
subtitle: Database Management
educationalGoal:
This course is for an educational goal of the Dept. of Management Systems to acquire "Information design basic ability". Students will:
(1) acquire the basic ability to utilize IT.
(2) learn the fundamental theory of relational databases.
(3) learn how to design a database, use SQL, and operate a database.
advice:
To use a database, the following three abilities are required:
  1. The ability to use SQL, a language for managing data held in a database.
  2. The ability to maintain data integrity using normalization, primary/foreign key, and so on.
  3. The ability to design application systems using a database.

Students will acquire abilities 1 and 2 mainly through lectures and exercises in the first half of the course; they will acquire ability 3 in the second half of the course.
books: The Manga Guide to Database by Mana Takahashi, Shoko Azuma, and Trend-Pro Co., Ltd., No Starch Press; ISBN: 978-1-59327-190-9
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of computers such as the basic operation of a PC, Web design, IT systems, etc.

Be able to explain a relational database.
Be able to design an E-R diagram.
Be able to convert an entity to third normal form.
Be able to use the SQL’s “SELECT” statement.
Be able to design a database.

title: システムモデリング
subtitle: Systems Modeling
educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) how to grasp complex systems correctly.
(2) how to describe conceptual models using UML diagrams.
(3) how to improve the system using the model.
advice:
To grasp complex systems correctly, the following three abilities are required :
  1. The ability to view the system in two levels (concept level and implementation level).
  2. The ability to view the system from three aspects (static, functional, and dynamic).
  3. The ability to visualize the structure and behavior of the system with appropriate expressions.

In the first half of the class, students will learn 1 and 2 through lectures and quizzes, and in the second half, they will learn 3 through exercises.

In 3, students use PC to draw UML diagrams.
As the drawing software, astah* will be used. The installing will be instructed in the class.
books: Textbook : The Introduction to UML Modeling, Nikkei-BP (Japanese book)
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of any model diagram (Not required)

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain "class" and "instance".
Be able to explain "three facets" and associate UML diagrams.
Be able to draw UML diagrams of a simple system.
Be able to design specific requirements and draw the concept model.
Be able to understand system behavior from UML diagrams.
Be able to pick up problems and improve systems.

educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Financial Ability” learning and educational goal of the Department of Management Systems. The goal is to cultivate in students the ability to properly use accounting information for business and structural decisions made by corporate managers.
advice:
In corporate activities, decision-making is required in a variety of situations.
In the first half of this course, students will learn how to make decisions in their daily work; in the second half of the course, students will learn how to make long-term decisions such as those involving capital investment.

title: 会計情報とビジネス法規
subtitle: Accounting Information and Business Regulations
educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Financial Ability” learning and educational goal of the Department of Management Systems. The goal is for the student to understand important accounting standards to understand what accounting information conveys and to understand the basic part of legal knowledge such as tax system, corporate law, civil law, etc. as peripheral knowledge so that they can understand the contents of securities report, which is a general disclosure document of a company.
advice:
This course covers a wide range of subjects such as accounting standards, taxation, and legal knowledge related to corporate law.
First of all, since this course will be conducted on the premise that you understand the matters learned in the "Accounting basic", it is necessary to review the "Accounting basic".
In addition, new terms and ideas will appear frequently, so enthusiastic class participation and constant efforts are required.
books: None
requiredKnowledge: Since this course teaches the theoretical part of accounting, it is necessary to have a solid understanding of what was learned in "Accounting Basic" in order to understand the content of the lesson.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the concept of important accounting standards.
Be able to understand what accounting information conveys by understanding accounting standards.
Be able to understand the overall mechanism of the tax system centered on corporate tax and income tax.
Be able to use your tax knowledge for business and life by understanding the overall mechanism of the tax system
Be able to recognize the importance of legal knowledge in conducting corporate management.
Be able to understand the minimum required legal knowledge about corporate management.

subtitle: Business Statistics II
educationalGoal:
This course deals with statistical and quantitative analysis from a management  techniques perspective. Students will learn to:
(1)learn the techniques to select, process, and extract necessary information from various information sources.
(2)understand statistical data analysis methods.
advice:
This is an introductory course in statistical analysis. Participants will learn various theoretical foundations of statistical analysis, and acquire practical business skills in processing, filtering, and extracting information using Microsoft Excel.
We will cover the following topics:
1)Hypothesis testing
2)Population intercept ,population slope
3)Estimated regression relationship
Students are required to bring their laptop computer, with Microsoft Excel installed, to every class.

title: 流体力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Fluid Mechanics II
educationalGoal: In this course, students will first understand the characteristics of viscous fluid and learn about flow in a pipe and flow around an object in the fluid. Then, students will learn about the mechanisms of drag and lift generation. With an emphasis on viscous fluid dynamics, which is the basis of actual fluid motion, students will focus on grasping the engineering and physical meanings while solving exercises on fluid flow concepts. Develop the ability to evaluate the validity of CFD and expriment results.
advice:
This is a basic course in fluid mechanics. We will cover the following topics:
1. Outline of fluid dynamics
2. Outline of viscous fluid flow, laminar flow, transition, turbulent flow, and boundary layer
3. Analysis of viscous fluid flow, laminar flow in a circular pipe, and turbulent flow in a circular pipe
4. Flow in pipes, Bernoulli's equation considering loss, friction loss of pipe flow, losses of pipes, problems of piping systems
5. Force acting on a body, momentum theorem and drag, force, pressure resistance and frictional resistance acting on boundary layer and flat plate, flow and drag around cylinders and spheres, vortices, drag of objects with various shapes, fluid forces related to vortexes, and related vibration and safety design
6. Vortex and circulation, lift, and flow around a wing
7. Comprehensive problems: Report discussion and study meetings on specific issues (including regional contributions) in fluid dynamics. Express your understanding, ideas, and questions.
On-demand materials are prepared and should be used for preparation and review.

title: 機械加工学
subtitle: Machining Engineering
educationalGoal:
(1) Learn the basic theory of removal machining.
(2) Learn methods to measure cutting force and cutting edge temperature.
(3) Learn the types of tool damage and their causes.
(4) Learn how to manufacture cutting tools using powder metallurgy and surface
    coating techniques.
(5) Learn how to select cutting tool materials and cutting conditions.
advice:
This class will cover the following topics:
 1.  Classification of processing methods
 2.  Chip formation mechanism (Classification and formation mechanism of chips, Built-up edge, Generation
     conditions, and Methods to prevent built-up edge)
 3.  Cutting theory (Theoretical calculation of cutting force and Theoretical calculation of cutting
     temperature)
 4.  Measurement of cutting specifications (Cutting force, Cutting temperature, Chip thickness, and Contact
     length between chip and rake face)
 5.  Cutting tool wear and wear factors
 6.  Cutting tool material (Type and Classification)
 7.  Powder metallurgy technology and coating technology
 8.  Finished surface quality and control
 9.  Machinability of difficult-to-cut materials

Students should be aware of the teacher’s instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests, and reports may change as the class progresses.
books:
Textbooks：
Reference books：None
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge:
Students are expected to watch the machining videos that supplement the lecture content.
In addition, it is important to have the experiences of touring machining facilities and attending a machine industry fair.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the basics of cutting theory.
Be able to understand the measurement methods for cutting specifications.
Be able to understand the form and factors of tool damage.
Be able to understand the types of cutting tool materials and their effective use.
Be able to understand the types of difficult-to-cut materials and their machinability.
Be able to select optimum cutting conditions and machine tools.

title: 熱力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Thermodynamics II
keywords: Vapor power cycles, Refrigeration cycles and Air Conditioning
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn basic knowledge of the irreversibility in the nature world
(2) Learn how to convert energy and obtain work from heat
(3) Acquire design skills for energy conversion in mechanical engineering
advice:
This is an advanced course in thermodynamics that follows Thermodynamics I.
We will cover the following topics:

1. Carnot cycle
2. The 2nd law of thermodynamics
3. Entropy, Exergy
4. Thermal characteristics of real gas
5. Vapor power cycles, Refrigeration cycles and Air Conditioning

Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and formulas.
Students are expected to solve exercises independently.
Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests, and reports may change as the class progresses.
Students should not be absent from class, as they may not receive the handouts.

Detailed schedules and content of the course are explained in the first class.
books:
Textbooks : (1) JSME Text Series, Thermodynamics (Maruzen)
Reference book : (1) Arai, Furuhata, English-Japanese Bilingual Textbook Series, Thermodynamics, Morikita (2) JSME Text Series, Problems in Thermodynamics (Maruzen)
Reserved books : N/A
requiredKnowledge:
Have sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential and integral calculations).
Know how to use a calculator.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the Carnot cycle and apply it to problems
Be able to explain the 2nd law of thermodynamics and apply it to problems
Be able to explain entropy and apply it to problems
Be able to explain the characteristics of a real gas with phase change and apply it to problems
Be able to explain vapor power and refrigeration cycles, and apply the knowledge to probrems

title: マイクロ・ナノ加工
subtitle: Micro-Nano Processing
educationalGoal: Currently, technologies for realizing ultrafine parts and mechanisms are required for manufacturing, and these technologies are applied to pressure sensors, the heads of inkjet printers, MEMS such as gyroscopes, manufacture of Si-IC and LED substrates, and micro-machines. In addition, processing methods include not only top-down types that refine existing elements but bottom-up types that build up atoms according to the purpose. In this course, students will learn the basics of processing methods to obtain such ultrafine parts and mechanisms.
advice:
We will cover various leading-edge processes that can fabricate micro- to nanoscale parts. The outline of this class is shown below:
1. Relationship between the processing method and scale concepts expressed as micro, meso, and nano
2. Latest top-down micro-processing methods
3. Micro-processing using lasers
4. Planarization processing of Si wafers
5. Planarization processing using chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) methods
6. Outline of surface modification methods
7. Outline of MEMS
8. Summary
To deepen your understanding of the content of this course, exercise questions will be presented and explained appropriately. Students will need to bring a scientific calculator to class. In addition, special classes will be held for outside lecturers as needed.

title: 材料力学Ⅲ
subtitle: Strength of Materials III
educationalGoal: Based on the fundamental knowledge of the relationship between force and deformation in materials studied in the Strength of Materials I and II, students will study the application knowledge required for the design of structures, such as triaxial stresses, strain energy, buckling of column, and so on.
advice:
This is a course on strength of materials. We will cover the following topics:

1. Stress-strain relationship under triaxial stress
2. Combination of torsion, bending, and axial forces
3. Strain energy
4. Castigliano's theorem
5. Failure criteria of materials
6. Short column subjected to eccentric load
7. Buckling of long column

All of these topics are based on the content learned in "Strength of Materials I": stress, strain, Hook's law, frame structure, thermal stress, stress concentration, thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure, a beam and its supporting condition, and shearing force and bending moment of a beam. Students will also need the knowledge learned in "Strength of Materials II": bending stress and deflection in a beam, torsion, principal stress and principal shearing stress, Mohr’s stress circle, and combined stress problems.

Lecture and exercise explanations will be provided on demand as needed.

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Triaxial stress
2.Strain energy
3.Failure criteria
4.Buckling

              Based on the fundamental knowledge of the relationship between force and deformation in materials studied in the Strength of Materials I and II, students will study the application knowledge required for the design of structures, such as triaxial stresses, strain energy, buckling of column, and so on.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is a course on strength of materials. We will cover the following topics:

1. Stress-strain relationship under triaxial stress
2. Combination of torsion, bending, and axial forces
3. Strain energy
4. Castigliano's theorem
5. Failure criteria of materials
6. Short column subjected to eccentric load
7. Buckling of long column

All of these topics are based on the content learned in "Strength of Materials I": stress, strain, Hook's law, frame structure, thermal stress, stress concentration, thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure, a beam and its supporting condition, and shearing force and bending moment of a beam. Students will also need the knowledge learned in "Strength of Materials II": bending stress and deflection in a beam, torsion, principal stress and principal shearing stress, Mohr’s stress circle, and combined stress problems.

Lecture and exercise explanations will be provided on demand as needed.

              Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: Basics of Strength of Materials, Baifukan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reserved books: Unspecified

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              Students should have a good understanding of the content learned in "Strength of Materials I" and "Strength of Materials II. In addition, it is recommended that students understand differential and integral calculation methods, especially for a good understanding of the buckling of a long column.

title: 材料科学Ⅲ
subtitle: Materials Science III
educationalGoal: In the design and manufacture of machines and structures, it is necessary to select appropriate materials based on an understanding of their properties. Based on the basic knowledge of the structure and properties of materials acquired in Materials Science I and II, students learn corrosion and fracture mechanisms, which are defects of materials, and understand the structure and properties of nonferrous metals, resins, ceramics, and composite materials. Furthermore, students discuss some cases of material selection and it helps deeper understanding of materials.
advice:
The following items are studied.
-Corrosion and corrosion protection techniques
-Fracture mechanics
-Stainless steel and alloyed steel
-Aluminum and aluminum alloys
-Copper and copper alloys
-Plastics
-Ceramics
-Composite materials

Some case studies of material selection based on Ishikawa area are discussed in order to understand materials knowledge deeper.

Lectures are conducted by face-to-face teaching, also can be took place by remote class depending on a situation.
books:
Textbooks：None
Reference books：None
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge: This lecture requires the understanding of Materials Science I and Materials Science II. Students should understand the relationship between microstructure and material properties in Materials Science I,and also understand the relationship between microstructure formation and properties of steel in Materials Science Ⅱ. Knowledge of thermodynamics is also required to understand corrosion mechanisms.

activityGoals.body: Abilities to understand the basic mechanisms of corrosion, typical corrosion forms and corrosion control methods
Abilities to understand the failure mechanisms of materials.
Abilities to understand the properties of stainless steel and alloyed steels.
Abilities to understand the properties of non-ferrous metals, ceramics, resigns, composite materials.
Abilities to select appropriate materials according to engineering needs.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1) Abilities to understand the basic principle of corrosion and typical corrosion forms, and to select appropriate corrosion protection methods.
2) Abilities to be able to explain the failure mechanism of materials.
3) Abilities to understand the characteristics of alloyed steels and stainless steels.
4)Abilities to be able to explain the relationship between the structure and the properties of non-ferrous metals, ceramics, resins and composite materials.
5)Abilities to be able to select appropriate materials using the knowledge acquired in this course.
achievementLevels.standard:
1) Abilities to understand that corrosion progresses by the anode reaction and cathode reaction and to explain the principle of cathodic protection.
2) Abilities to be able to explain the meaning of the plane strain fracture toughness value (KIC).
3)Abilities to be able to explain the characteristics of advanced materials such as alloy steel and stainless steels.
4) Abilities to be able to explain the characteristics of typical aluminum and copper alloys, ceramics, resins and composite materials.
5) Abilities to be able to point out the hazards of materials in the environment in which they are used.

title: 自動車工学
subtitle: Automobile Engineering
educationalGoal:
The automobile is a product of mechanical engineering and electrical engineering.
Students will:
(1)	acquire the ability to determine basic vehicle performance.
(2)	acquire the ability to understand  basic powertrain output characteristics.
advice:
This is a basic course of in automotive engineering. We will cover the following topics.
(1) History and role of automobile.
(2)	Automotive internal combustion engine
(3)	Powertrain
(4)	Automotive braking system
(5) Driving performance
(6)	Production technology
(7)	Recycling technology
books: No textbook
requiredKnowledge: Students must have a basic understanding of mathematics, mechanics, and thermodynamics.

activityGoals.body: Be able to calculate simple vehicle performance parameters.
Be able to explain simple structures and mechanisms.
Be able to explain the theoretical cycle and operating principles of an internal combustion engine.
Be able to explain the driving, turning, and stopping of cars in mechanical terms.
Be able to establish a simple equation of motion for cars.

title: ３Ｄモデリング
subtitle: Computer Aided Design and Modeling
educationalGoal: Students will learn about machine designs, including functional and performance designs, and manufacturing processes. Students also create design plans and drawings that meet the required specifications. In this course, students will create a design for strength and reliability that follows the engineering drawing, a manufacturing design that considers the manufacturing method and cost, and a draft that represents the mechanism and overall configuration utilizing the three-dimensional computer aided design (3D-CAD) system.
advice:
The main mechanism studied in this course is a three-axis two-stage helical gear reducer. We will use it to acquire the ability to systematically design machines through designing function, performance, accuracy, strength, and reliability. utilizing 3D-CAD system for embodiment of machine elements.
Basically, lectures and exercises are held weekly. However, the design and drafting of assigned tasks will not be completed in the practice time during the lecture, so preparation and review as homework will be necessary. In addition, students will use the basics of 3D-CAD software that were taught in “Mechanical Elements Design”, “Mechanical Drawing I” and “Mechanical Drawing II” that they attended before taking this course.
It is assumed that you have mastered the operating and reference methods of the JIS drawing textbook, so please check this material carefully before taking this course.
The topics covered in this course are as follows:
(1) Mechanical design and design process improvement; (2) Design problems, design concepts, and basic design; (3) Design problem strength, reliability of design, and detailed design; (4) 3D-CAD mechanical drawing; (5) Inspection of mechanical design problem drawings; and (6) Self-inspection and third-party evaluation of mechanical design problems.
books:
Textbooks: New JIS Mechanical Drawing (6th edition), Morikita Publishing (in Japanese),   Mechanical Drawing, Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese),   Helical Reducer Design, Power-sha Publishing (in Japanese),   Mechanical Design of Helical Reducer (Exercise), Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese)
Reference books: None
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
This course is intended as a design and drafting course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering in accordance with the courses of Mechanical Principles/Exercises, Mechanical Drawing I, Mechanical Drawing II, and Mechanical Element Design. Therefore, to participate in this course, the design and CAD drawing abilities acquired in these courses are required.
Before attending this course, it is recommended that you review the content acquired in previous courses. Persistent effort is necessary.

title: ３Ｄシミュレーション
subtitle: Computer Aided Design and Simulation
educationalGoal: CAE (Computer Aided Engineering) system is a technology for the design optimization/enhancement by utilizing FEM (Finite Element Method) based on CAD (Computer Aided Design). In this course, students will understand the FEM theory/overview and specific methods for application to mechanical design. Then, students will study the design/analysis approaches of mechanical structures through stress and deformation analysis by FEM. Furthermore, students will deepen their knowledge by understanding CAE problems in actual companies.
advice:
Design and manufacturing are important fundamental technologies supporting Japanese economic power. They can be roughly classified into the hardware manufacturing technology, where high-precision components are efficiently processed and assembled into products, the software technology, which efficiently supports the complicated and wide-ranging design/manufacturing activities.
This course will focus on the CAE system, which efficiently supports various activities of engineers from design to manufacturing. Students will study their functions and applications. Classes will consist of lectures on system functions/structures and computer-aided practices. In addition, students will understand the practical usage of CAE at the actual design section and its role.

              1.CAE

              CAE (Computer Aided Engineering) system is a technology for the design optimization/enhancement by utilizing FEM (Finite Element Method) based on CAD (Computer Aided Design). In this course, students will understand the FEM theory/overview and specific methods for application to mechanical design. Then, students will study the design/analysis approaches of mechanical structures through stress and deformation analysis by FEM. Furthermore, students will deepen their knowledge by understanding CAE problems in actual companies.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Design and manufacturing are important fundamental technologies supporting Japanese economic power. They can be roughly classified into the hardware manufacturing technology, where high-precision components are efficiently processed and assembled into products, the software technology, which efficiently supports the complicated and wide-ranging design/manufacturing activities.
This course will focus on the CAE system, which efficiently supports various activities of engineers from design to manufacturing. Students will study their functions and applications. Classes will consist of lectures on system functions/structures and computer-aided practices. In addition, students will understand the practical usage of CAE at the actual design section and its role.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（高野則之研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Takano Noriyuki)
educationalGoal: Students will (1) learn technical mechanisms and new mechanisms required to research, develop, design, and manufacture socially useful and high-quality products using the basic academic ability acquired by studies in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, (2) scquire the ability to identify and solve problems in mechanical engineering-related fields, (3) learn about the importance of collaboration, particularly with local communities.
advice:
This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. To realize the educational objectives of the Department, this course focuses on the following topics:
Students will acquire the ability to model phenomena accurately and analyze the models.
Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to evaluate solutions using the obtained results.
In practice, students should reconfirm their project theme, which was determined in Preparatory Seminar, with the supervisors of individual laboratories. (The theme should be revised as necessary.)
Students are expected to pursue the identification and solution of problems in accordance with the engineering process.

Our laboratory promotes projects with the following content:
(1) materials assositaed with hydrogen energy (2) biomedical engineering ( matrials and treatments) (3) techniques for material design

Students will learns theory, experimental procedure and computer simulation in thees projects.
requiredKnowledge:
It is essential to acquire knowledge and improve the skills necessary for safe research activities.
It is desirable to obtain a machining license from the KIT Dream works (Yumekobo).

Be able to act independently to solve the issues presented separately.

              Students will (1) acquire the ability to identify and solve problems to research, develop, design, and manufacture socially useful and high-quality products using the basic knowledge learned in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, (2) learn what technologies or new mechanisms are needed for that purpose, (3) learn about the importance of collaboration with society (particularly local communities).

              This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. educationalGoal:
This course is for an educational goal of the Dept. of Environmental Design and Innovation to acquire "Information design basic ability". Students will:
(1)acquire the basic ability to utilize IT including mark-up language and the Internet,
(2)learn the fundamental theory of WWW (World Wide Web) site,
(3)learn how to create, manage and operate web pages.
advice:

(1)	The ability to understand the WWW site production process,
(a)	Planning a WWW site,
(b)	Design and implement a WWW site,
(c)	Manage and Operate a WWW site.
(2)	The ability to understand and apply HTML (Hyper-Text Mark-up Language) and CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) to produce a WWW site,
(3)	The ability to produce a web site that considers effective expression of information, ease of use, and availability to anyone.

Students will acquire abilities 1 and 2 mainly through lectures and exercises in the first half of the course; they will acquire ability 3 in the second half of the course.

title: データアナリティクス入門
subtitle: Introduction to Data Analytics
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will:
(1) acquire a basic knowledge of data analytics.
(2) learn how to collect, aggregate, and visualize data based on questionnaire surveys.
(3) learn how to use statistical methods of sampling.
advice:
To analyze data properly, the following four abilities are required:
  1. The ability to collect data according to purpose and hypothesized issues.
  2. The ability to aggregate data in a table according to the data format.
  3. The ability to display data visually using graphs.
  4. The ability to verify hypotheses with statistical methods.

Students will acquire abilities 1 to 3 mainly through the questionnaire survey exercises in the first half of the course; ability 4 will be learned through exercises using sample data in the second half of the course.
books: Textbook : 統計学〈1〉データ分析の基礎 オフィシャルスタディノート 改定第2版(Japanese book)
requiredKnowledge: Understanding the meaning of the average, variance, and standard deviation formulas, scatter plots, and correlation coefficients learned in high school mathematics.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the concept of data analytics.
Be able to plan a questionnaire survey.
Be able to create and improve a questionnaire sheet.
Be able to use simple/cross-tabulation to analyze questionnaire results.
Be able to be to produce pie, bar, and scatter charts using Excel.
Be able to test a hypothesis using confidence intervals and various hypothesis testing methods.

              In this course, students will:

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              To analyze data properly, the following four abilities are required:
  1. The ability to collect data according to purpose and hypothesized issues.
  2. The ability to aggregate data in a table according to the data format.
  3. The ability to display data visually using graphs.

Students will acquire abilities 1 to 3 mainly through the questionnaire survey exercises in the first half of the course; ability 4 will be learned through exercises using sample data in the second half of the course.

title: グローバル開発論
subtitle: Global Development Theory
educationalGoal: Recently, there are variety of approaches for international cooperation, even in people's daily life. In this course, students will learn that people are able to participate in supporting developing countries and the poor in many ways. Students are expected to understand such current situation. Upon completing this course, students will be able to think by themselves how to contribute to international cooperation.
advice:
(Outline of the course)
   Students will learn activities of global development through development assistance cooperation, international organizations, or NGO to support other people living inside and outside of their countries through learning international affairs. The goal of the students is to achieve the basic knowledge of international cooperation and its background so that they can practice such activities in their future.
   Students will learn the concept of global development/international cooperation and its practice. By the end of the course, students will learn K (Kindness of Heart), I (Intellectual Curiosity), T (Team Sprits), So that they can acquire skills and knowledges that they can practice in future.
(Advice and comments)
1)Students will learn to open up their eyes to watch the world, to take interests in social issues, and keep their minds on such issues.
2)The international and social issues which will be discussed in these classes will be the issues that students may have to tackle in future.
3)The program of the course may change depending on the number of students and circumstances of classes.
4)A lecturer of one class will be a guest lecturer from outside, so there may be some changes in the program.
5)The lecturer of this course used to work for JBIC and JICA, as well as served as a JOCV, and as a director of an NGO.
books:
1)David, Hulme, 2016, Should Rich Nations Help the Poor?, Polity press
2)Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), every year, White Paper on Development Cooperation / Japan's ODA White Paper, MOFA: https://www.mofa.go.jp/policy/oda/page_000017.html
3)Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), every year, JICA Annual Report, JICA: https://www.jica.go.jp/english/about/disc/report/index.html
requiredKnowledge: No specific requirements to take this course. It is desirable that students have interests in daily international issues. Some English materials will be used.

activityGoals.body: Discuss and argue whether and why the aspect of global development is necessary.
Comprehend and explain the roles and needs of Official Development Assistance (ODA) .
Understand approaches for global development by government level, grass-root level, and private sector level.
Analyze the trends of global development at global level in relation with global society.
Plan his/her own roles/actions to contribute to global development.
Express his/her own critical view about global development and/or ODA.

title: コミュニケーション・デザイン入門
subtitle: Introduction to Communication Design
educationalGoal: This course cultivates the ability to design effective questions that elicit feasible information and create meaningful dialogue. Students will reconstruct ideas from collected data and enhance them through collaboration. They will also develop fundamental skills to clearly communicate ideas to others. Additionally, the course covers methods for creating communication spaces that support smooth observation, as well as techniques for refining and verifying hypotheses derived from observations through lectures and practical exercises.
advice:
In this course, students will engage in a project-based learning experience focused on both tangible and intangible creation. The course is structured around four key processes: "Questioning," "Dialogue," "Collaboration," and "Communication." Through these processes, students will design communication spaces within each stage of the project.
By doing so, they will come to understand the importance of fundamental communication skills necessary for comprehending and solving social issues.
1) Designing Questions: students will learn how to prepare and structure effective questions that facilitate meaningful discussions when investigating latent needs from stakeholders.
2) Designing Dialogue: students will explore how to create an environment that fosters effective dialogue during field investigations or in simulated settings.
3) Designing Collaboration: students will learn how to define problems as a team based on research findings, formulate hypotheses, and design a collaborative environment to develop concrete solutions.
4) Designing Communication: students will examine how to effectively communicate their project outcomes to stakeholders and design appropriate methods and settings for presentation.
Advice for Learning: It is recommended to consciously observe aspects of daily life, such as "easy-to-use objects" and "people in a relaxed state." Additionally, considering the reasons and factors behind these observations is also beneficial for learning in this course.
books:
Textbooks："The Art of Discussion" by Jun Nakahara, published by PHP Institute, 2022.
Reference books："Designing of Questions" by Yuki Anzai and Takayuki Shiose, published by Gakugei Publishing, 2020.
Reserved books：None specified
requiredKnowledge: No prior preparation is required. However, there are many excellent books on communication that cover a wide range of topics, from improving individual skills to facilitating team activities. Reading such books as reference materials is recommended. Additional recommended readings will be introduced during the lectures as needed.

Facilitate effective dialogues to promote discussions on the problem.
Design collaborative environments that enhance communication and teamwork in projects.
Effectively communicate project outcomes to stakeholders.
Engage in effective communication in collaborative and cooperative settings.

title: コミュニケーション・デザイン実践
subtitle: Practical Communication Design
educationalGoal: Communication can be defined as the process by which human beings convey and mutually understand intentions, emotions, and thoughts through interpersonal relationships. This course focuses specifically on logic, which plays a crucial role in the transmission and understanding of thought. By examining everyday language from the perspective of elementary logic, students will refine their logical skills and acquire the ability to understand others' reasoning accurately and to communicate their own claims clearly and effectively.
advice:
Communication refers to the process by which human beings convey and mutually understand intentions, emotions, and thoughts through interpersonal relationships.This definition indicates that communication encompasses a wide variety of interactive processes of transmission and understanding. Naturally, it is not possible for this course to cover all such aspects.

Accordingly, this course focuses on logic as a key perspective for understanding and conveying thought. From the standpoint of logic, students will learn fundamental concepts and skills necessary for accurately understanding others' reasoning and for expressing their own arguments in a precise manner.

To achieve these aims, the course uses Shigeki Noya's 『まったくゼロからの論理学』 as the main textbook. This book consists of two major parts: Part I, Logic in Everyday Language, and Part II, Constructing a Symbolic Language for Logic. Following the approach recommended in the textbook’s introduction, this course primarily works through Part II while incorporating relevant content from Part I as appropriate. Through reexamining everyday language from the viewpoint of elementary logic, students will aim to refine their logical competence.
books: 野矢茂樹（2020）『まったくゼロからの論理学』、岩波書店

title: 経営分析とＥＳＧ
subtitle: Business Analysis and ESG
educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Basic ability to expand on the current situation and foresee the future” learning/education goal of the Faculty of Environmental design and innovation. In order for managers to fulfill their duties in the future, analytical information on management activities is required. In this course, students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary for management analysis and develop the ability to make comprehensive judgments on the results of management analysis from a multifaceted perspective.
advice:
In the first part of the course, students will learn the knowledge of preparing financial statements
(such as bookkeeping).
In the second part, students will learn the key points of financial analysis and analytical indicators. And then, students will practice financial analysis of specific companies using the analytical indicators they have learned.
 Finally, students will prepare and give a presentation on the results of their financial analysis.
When doing the assigned exercises, it is important that students pay attention to economic news and company information and study in depth their target company and industry.

title: ウェルビーイングシティ政策デザイン
subtitle: Well-being City Policy Design
educationalGoal: The objective of this course is to learn methods for exploring how to propose a future where we genuinely want to live and continue to engage as a "related population" (Kankeijinko). This is achieved by personalizing regional revitalization, extracting appropriate leverage points in regional design based on objective data, and utilizing generative AI.
advice:
In this course, we will learn how to use our own power to create cities that realize well-being, leaving no one behind.
To prevent urban design from relying solely on loud voices or a few individuals in power, it is crucial to conduct regional design using objective evidence. On the other hand, to view urban design not as someone else's problem but as a personal matter, it must be combined with initiatives that you are deeply passionate about. Unless everyone views urban design as a personal matter, citizen-participatory urban design will not be realized, and consequently, a comfortable environment for each individual cannot be achieved.
Against this background, this course will use Nonoichi City and Kaga City as research fields. Students will learn to analyze their "Oshi", conduct regional analysis using data, and create proposals to approach the extracted leverage points. Rather than simply being dissatisfied with society, we hope that through this course, you will acquire the motivation and methods necessary to design comfortable environments with your own hands.
Please note that as this is the first year this course is being offered, there may be changes to some of the content or procedures in the future. Therefore, the course procedures will be reconfirmed at the start of the first class, and that confirmation will serve as the official syllabus.

              The objective of this course is to learn methods for exploring how to propose a future where we genuinely want to live and continue to engage as a "related population" (Kankeijinko). This is achieved by personalizing regional revitalization, extracting appropriate leverage points in regional design based on objective data, and utilizing generative AI.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, we will learn how to use our own power to create cities that realize well-being, leaving no one behind.
To prevent urban design from relying solely on loud voices or a few individuals in power, it is crucial to conduct regional design using objective evidence. On the other hand, to view urban design not as someone else's problem but as a personal matter, it must be combined with initiatives that you are deeply passionate about. Unless everyone views urban design as a personal matter, citizen-participatory urban design will not be realized, and consequently, a comfortable environment for each individual cannot be achieved.
Against this background, this course will use Nonoichi City and Kaga City as research fields. Students will learn to analyze their "Oshi", conduct regional analysis using data, and create proposals to approach the extracted leverage points. Rather than simply being dissatisfied with society, we hope that through this course, you will acquire the motivation and methods necessary to design comfortable environments with your own hands.
Please note that as this is the first year this course is being offered, there may be changes to some of the content or procedures in the future. Therefore, the course procedures will be reconfirmed at the start of the first class, and that confirmation will serve as the official syllabus.

title: 共生社会デザイン概論
subtitle: Introduction to Designs for a Co-existing Society
educationalGoal:
The goal of this course is for students to understand the concept and realities of a co-existing society and to act toward its realization. The course will primarily focus on persons with disabilities as a representative case.
Students will study the philosophy and systems of disability welfare. Through this course, students are expected to: understand the importance of respecting minorities, learn about human rights,reflect upon these themes, and be able to explain them clearly.
advice:
(Course Overview)
1)Introduction, 2)Target groups in a co-existing society
3)Basic knowledge about persons with disabilities(PWD)
4)History of PWD, 5)Laws and systems supporting PWD
6)Living environments of PWD, 7)Key actors in disability welfare
8)Social work, 9)Disability and Development, 10)Disability welfare by local government
11)Various co-existing societies (gender, LGBTQ, children)
12)Various co-existing societies (people in poverty, single-parent households, elderly persons living alone, urban and rural disparities, homelessness)
13)Various co-existing societies (Zainichi foreign residents, migrants, refugees, indigenous peoples)
14)Special lecture by an external guest speaker
15)Course reflection
(Advice for Students)
Pay attention to daily life, newspapers, and news to deepen interest in co-existing society issues.
A special lecture by external practitioners/persons concerned is scheduled (some changes may occur).
books:
1)Oliver Michael, Sapey Bob, Thomas Pam：Social work with disabled people (4th edition). Bloomsbury Publishing, (2012).
2)Schein Edgar H.：Helping: How to Offer, Give, and Receive Help. Berrett-Koehler, (2011).
3)Kallen Evelyn：Social inequality and social injustice: A human rights perspective. Palgrave Macmillan Basingstoke, UK, (2004).
requiredKnowledge:
No specific prior knowledge or skills are required.
However, students are expected to have an interest in current affairs and social issues in daily life. Some English-language materials may occasionally be used for reference purposes; however, it is sufficient if students can grasp the general atmosphere and meaning.

activityGoals.body: Acquire and be able to explain basic information about a co-existing society and persons with disabilities.
Understand issues concerning a co-existing society and persons with disabilities as issues affecting society.
Develop the ability to think and act without discrimination between majority and minority groups, and others.
Acquire the ability to gather knowledge and information and solve problems faced by international society.
Understand knowledge and structures concerning humans, society, and nature; from regional to global level.
Identify issues in local communities and society and develop plans to address diverse social challenges

title: 異文化理解・コミュニケーション
subtitle: Intercultural Understanding and Communication
educationalGoal: This course is designed to achieve the educational goal of the Department of Environmental Design Creation: “fundamental abilities for collaborative work through communication.” Communication in a global society refers not only to language skills but also to the ability to build trust by understanding the cultures and values of others. This course aims to cultivate individuals who can transform potential cultural and value differences in a global society into mutual understanding rather than friction.
advice: This course explores various forms of cross-cultural understanding and communication based on business administration and international affairs, addressing questions such as “What is a global society?” and “What constitutes a different culture?” (This is not a foreign language course like English). Subsequently, it aims to impart knowledge and practice communication patterns in business situations based on cultural differences between countries. This focuses on the communication skills necessary to effectively utilize an organization as a member of a global team, with the goal of mastering these techniques. Furthermore, students will examine how to effectively utilize their communication skills within the organizations they are involved in and share these insights with other participants.
books: Culture Map, Erin Maylor
requiredKnowledge: Different cultures exist in every aspect of daily life. While this is especially true in environments where people come from different countries, even individuals of the same nationality inevitably have differences in their ways of thinking and values based on the regions and environments where they grew up. It is desirable to maintain an interest and awareness of what is happening in the world and in Japan today through the daily habit of reading newspapers and watching the news.

              学習・教育目標

              1.Intercultural Understanding
2.Intercultural Communication
3.Multicultural Coexistence
4.Global Society
5.Religion and History

              This course is designed to achieve the educational goal of the Department of Environmental Design Creation: “fundamental abilities for collaborative work through communication.” Communication in a global society refers not only to language skills but also to the ability to build trust by understanding the cultures and values of others. This course aims to cultivate individuals who can transform potential cultural and value differences in a global society into mutual understanding rather than friction.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course explores various forms of cross-cultural understanding and communication based on business administration and international affairs, addressing questions such as “What is a global society?” and “What constitutes a different culture?” (This is not a foreign language course like English). Subsequently, it aims to impart knowledge and practice communication patterns in business situations based on cultural differences between countries. This focuses on the communication skills necessary to effectively utilize an organization as a member of a global team, with the goal of mastering these techniques. Furthermore, students will examine how to effectively utilize their communication skills within the organizations they are involved in and share these insights with other participants.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Culture Map, Erin Maylor

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              Different cultures exist in every aspect of daily life. While this is especially true in environments where people come from different countries, even individuals of the same nationality inevitably have differences in their ways of thinking and values based on the regions and environments where they grew up. It is desirable to maintain an interest and awareness of what is happening in the world and in Japan today through the daily habit of reading newspapers and watching the news.

title: 思考のトレーニング
subtitle: Training of Thought
educationalGoal:
Through learning to summarize arguments, grasp their structure, and evaluate
their validity and soundness, students will develop the ability to create and
sustain spaces for constructive discussion on their own.

The course begins with careful understanding of others’ spoken statements and
written texts, and ultimately aims to enable students to develop and present
their own original arguments.
advice:
First, this course introduces key concepts and methods for structurally understanding and analyzing Japanese texts and spoken discourse. Specifically, students will learn to identify the basic components of sentences-such as negation, conjunction, disjunction, and conditionals-as well as various connective expressions that link sentences and arguments, including interpretation, justification, addition, and contrast. Through this process, students will develop the ability to grasp the structure of arguments. In addition, the course aims to cultivate the ability to evaluate arguments whose structure has been clarified in this way. Particular emphasis is placed
on assessing whether an argument is valid. By developing these skills, students will also acquire the ability to raise precise and constructive questions about specific arguments. Ultimately, through analyzing and evaluating the structure of arguments on a given topic, students will learn to construct their own well-reasoned arguments on that topic.
books: 野矢茂樹（2006）．『新版　論理トレーニング』、産業図書．
requiredKnowledge: None

advice:

2. urban problems in the modern era, theories and measures to deal with them, and present trends of urbanism
3. basic framework of city planning in Japan
4. details of local development activities
5. practical examples of local development and their methods

title: 社会シミュレーション
subtitle: Social Simulation
educationalGoal: In this course, students learn about mathematical modeling of social systems and simulation techniques. Students understand system dynamics and multi-agent models—representative mathematical models that incorporate interactions among people or between humans and the natural environment. Students also understand to acquire insights into the macroscopic characteristics and global behavior of economic, social, and environmental systems through simulations using these models.
advice:
In this course, students study "systems thinking", which means an approach that focuses on the interactions among components of a system considered as a whole system. Students learn the basics of mathematical modeling and perform simulations using these models.
Students break down a complex system into its components, analyze causal relationships, and use these relationships to understand changes in outcomes based on different parameter settings via simulation.
Through simulation, students grasp real-world social phenomena and trends, forecast future conditions, and clarify what actions are necessary for building a better society.
Advice for Students is as follows:
1. Maintain a habit of considering relationships among various things in daily life.
2. If you cannot understand something at once, ask questions and review the material.
3. Engage in hands-on simulation practice, and reflect critically on the results, for example, "Does this match what I expected?", "How should I interpret this result?”

requiredKnowledge:
This course is designed so that no special prior knowledge is required.
However, familiarity with computers is desirable.
Basic mathematical knowledge, such as differential equations and linear algebra, will deepen your understanding of mathematical models and simulation techniques.
Reference materials for mathematics will be introduced during class as needed.

activityGoals.body: Understand mathematical models involving population and competition dynamics .
Implement simple mathematical models as simulation models.
Understand and perform simulations using system dynamics and multi-agent approaches.
Execute simulations, organize results, and create visualizations.
Interpret simulation results appropriately.
Consider methods for verifying simulation results.

5.System Dynamics

              In this course, students learn about mathematical modeling of social systems and simulation techniques. Students understand system dynamics and multi-agent models—representative mathematical models that incorporate interactions among people or between humans and the natural environment. Students also understand to acquire insights into the macroscopic characteristics and global behavior of economic, social, and environmental systems through simulations using these models.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, students study "systems thinking", which means an approach that focuses on the interactions among components of a system considered as a whole system. Students learn the basics of mathematical modeling and perform simulations using these models.
Students break down a complex system into its components, analyze causal relationships, and use these relationships to understand changes in outcomes based on different parameter settings via simulation.
Through simulation, students grasp real-world social phenomena and trends, forecast future conditions, and clarify what actions are necessary for building a better society.
Advice for Students is as follows:
1. Maintain a habit of considering relationships among various things in daily life.
2. If you cannot understand something at once, ask questions and review the material.
3. Engage in hands-on simulation practice, and reflect critically on the results, for example, "Does this match what I expected?", "How should I interpret this result?”

educationalGoal:
As represented by FBW aircraft, flight control is an essential technology for modern aircraft.
In Aircraft Control Engineering, students will learn control technology and learn the basics of flight control law design/analysis.
advice:
Students will begin by learning the Laplace transform, transfer functions, block diagrams, etc., which are indispensable for control technology.
Next, students will learn pole/zero placement, frequency response, and transient response, which are indispensable for understanding control characteristics.
Finally, students will learn about actual flight control systems through examples.

Be able to draw board diagrams and vector trajectories and also determine whether the system is stable or not.
Be able to determine the transfer function with feedback and draw outlines of the root locus

title: 航空流体力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Aerodynamics I
educationalGoal: Fluid dynamics is one of the major subjects in the machine and aeronautical fields. Students will learn the method of theoretical analysis of fluids using the governing equation. The goal of this subject is to understand the aerodynamic characteristics of the wings of aircraft, and to learn how to analyze the fluid around objects in irrotational ideal flow.
advice:
We will learn the two-dimensional flow of incompressible, inviscid and irrotational fluids, and how to apply the theory to airplane wings. We will cover the following materials:

1. Governing equation of fluid flow
2. Velocity potential
3. Flow around a cylinder
4. Kutta-Joukowski theorem
4. Conformal transformation
5. Flow around an airfoil and thin airfoil theory
6. Aerodynamic characteristics of two-dimensional wings
7. Aerodynamic characteristics of three-dimensional wings

Students must take and review notes because not everything is in the textbook.
books: Introduction to aerodynamics, Maruzen publishing, in Japanese
requiredKnowledge:
Acquisition of fluid mechanics.
Sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential and integral calculations).

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the governing equation of fluid flow.
Be able to analyze simple irrotational flow.
Be able to explain the mechanism of wing lift generation.
Be able to estimate the aerodynamic characteristics of a two-dimensional wing.
Be able to explain the aerodynamic characteristics of a three-dimensional wing.

title: 航空材料
subtitle: Materials for Aircraft Structure
educationalGoal: Aerospace vehicle are required to emphasize earth-friendly aspects and pursue high performance and high functioning at the same time. The various materials that compose aerospace vehicle have been steadily improving to satisfy these requirements. Students will learn the basic characteristic and applications of various materials such as aluminum, and fiber-reinforced composite materials for aerospace vehicle and other industrial products. Students will also use generative AI to explore the potential for entry into the local aerospace industry.
advice:
The outline is as follows.

1. Overview of materials for machinery
 1.1 Metallic materials, organic materials, inorganic materials, composite materials
 1.2 Characteristics and evaluation tests of materials
 1.3 Force and deformation, yield strength, tensile strength, Young’s modulus, Poisson’s ratio
2. Metallic materials
 2.1 Crystal structure and dislocation
 2.2 Deformation and fracture, elastic deformation and plastic deformation
 2.3 Equilibrium diagram
 2.4 Structure and heat treatment
 2.5 Phase transformation and toughening of metal and steel
 2.6 Aluminum, titanium
3. Composite materials
 3.1 Fiber and resin
 3.2 Molding methods and characteristics evaluation technology
requiredKnowledge: As a prerequisite, it is necessary to fully understand Strength of Materials. This is the first step to understanding the content of the course so the students can utilize reference book etc. on their own.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain practical materials such as steel materials, non-ferrous metal materials, and composites etc.
Be able to explain which materials are used in which areas of an aircraft.
Be able to explain basic evaluation test methods and features of metallic materials and composite materials.
Be able to explain how heat treatment affects properties of materials.

title: 宇宙推進工学
subtitle: Space Propulsion
educationalGoal:
Learn how thermal energy systems, mainly liquid rocket engines, are formed and utilized in the aerospace industry, in relation to energy and environmental issues.
In addition, students will learn the basics of rocket and rocket engines and deepen understanding of dreamy space technology.
advice:
Space projects such as the launch of artificial satellites, space travel business by the private sector, and exploration of the moon, Mars, and the solar system by each country government are increasing year by year, and the Age of Discovery of space is expected to arrive in the near future. In space transportation it is necessary to carry the spacecraft including heavy fuel and oxidizer to distant space against gravity. Therefore, in order to expand space development fast, it is essential to develop the ultimate effective use of thermal energy, to significantly reduce transportation costs.
Against this background, in this course, a liquid rocket engine is mainly described as an example to learn how thermal energy systems are useful in aviation and space, and what principles, structures, and design ideas are used to form them. This course is roughly divided into the following contents.
1. General remarks on space engineering
2. Rocket fundamentals
3. Liquid rocket engine design and performance
4. Overview of solid / hybrid rocket, electric propulsion, and ramjet
5. Summary, future technology trends of aerospace engines
By systematically studying the above, students will deepen understanding of dreamy space technology.
books:
Textbooks：Yoshiro Nakamura and Koichi Suzuki, “Rocket Engine”, Morikita shuppan
Reference books：Koichi Suzuki, “Introduction to Space Engineering”, Morikita shuppan
                 George P. Sutton, “Rocket propulsion elements 9th edition”, Wiley
requiredKnowledge:
"thermodynamics I" in the undergraduate course program.
Computational ability based on high school level knowledge of calculus and physics is essential.

activityGoals.body: Understand the rocket fundamentals, staging, and how to obtain the final speed.
Understand the utilization of liquid / electric propulsion.
Understand the effects of nozzle and atmosphere on the performance of rocket engines.
Understand the outline of the basic design of a liquid rocket engine.

(3) Be able to properly explain the characteristics and utilization of various rockets such as electric propulsion and hybrid rockets.
(4) Be able to calculate electric propulsion performance and explain the difference from the chemical rocket performance and the reason appropriately.

title: 航空原動機

keywords: Cycle Performance of Gas Turbine and Jet Engine
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)learn the basic principles and system components of gas turbines and jet engines
(2)learn the cycle calculations and how to evaluate performances of gas turbines
(3)learn the performance of components such as compressor, combustor, turbine
(4)learn the technical trend of the jet engines and environmental measures
(5)research the status of Aeroengines technologies using a database
advice:
This is a basic course of the aeroengines (aircraft gas turbines and jet engines) technology. The following subjects will be covered:

1. History, basic principle, and technology development of gas turbines and jet engines
2. Gas turbine cycles and thermodynamic analysis
3. Major performance parameters such as specific thrust, specific fuel consumption, thermal efficiency, propulsive efficiency, and overall efficiency
4. Cycle performance calculation of a turbojet engine
5. Gas turbine engine core components such as compressor, turbine, and combustor
6. Technical trend and environmental measures of jet engines

Students will be expected to understand the meaning of technical terms and formulas.
Students will be expected to solve the exercises by themselves.
Students should be aware of the teacher’s instructions in the class because the schedules of quizzes, tests, and reports may be changed as the class progresses.
Students should not be absent from the classes as the handouts may not be received.

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Cycle Performance of Gas Turbine and Jet Engine
2.Compressor
3.Combustor
4.Turbine
5.Utilization of database

              Students will:
(1)learn the basic principles and system components of gas turbines and jet engines
(2)learn the cycle calculations and how to evaluate performances of gas turbines
(3)learn the performance of components such as compressor, combustor, turbine
(4)learn the technical trend of the jet engines and environmental measures
(5)research the status of Aeroengines technologies using a database

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is a basic course of the aeroengines (aircraft gas turbines and jet engines) technology. The following subjects will be covered:

1. History, basic principle, and technology development of gas turbines and jet engines
2. Gas turbine cycles and thermodynamic analysis
3. Major performance parameters such as specific thrust, specific fuel consumption, thermal efficiency, propulsive efficiency, and overall efficiency
4. Cycle performance calculation of a turbojet engine
5. Gas turbine engine core components such as compressor, turbine, and combustor
6. Technical trend and environmental measures of jet engines

Students will be expected to understand the meaning of technical terms and formulas.
Students will be expected to solve the exercises by themselves.
Students should be aware of the teacher’s instructions in the class because the schedules of quizzes, tests, and reports may be changed as the class progresses.
Students should not be absent from the classes as the handouts may not be received.

Reference books: Jet engine, Morikita syuppan
Reference books: Wakariyasui Gasturbine, Kyouritsu syuppan
Reserved books: None

              High school level mathematics (especially differential/integral and vector calculations).
Basic knowledge of thermodynamics, fluid-dynamics, and heat transfer

2. Sonic speed and Mach number

5. Aerodynamic characteristics of high-speed airfoils

title: 航空システム専門実験・演習Ａ
subtitle: Aeronautics Major Lab/Exercises A
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)learn the method and theory of a selected basic subject, and perform
   experiment and practice on selected subject.
(2)acquire deeper understanding and ability to apply engineering subjects.
(3)learn how to write the experimental method in an experiment report.
(4)learn how to create presentations on experiments and their results.
advice:
Students will carry out the following experiments in Exercise A. Details on the experiments can be confirmed in the textbook.
① Molding and evaluation of CFRPs (carbon fiber reinforced plastics)
② Strength evaluation of the thin sheet structure with stiffeners (Semi-monocoque structure)
③ Flight dynamics
Students attending the lecture will be divided into three groups (A, B, and C). Group A will carry out experiment ① for five weeks and then theme ② for the next five weeks and finally theme ③ for another five weeks. Group B will follow the order of ②→③→① and group C the order of ③→①→②. In addition, class details are distributed at the time of the start of each experiment theme.
It is also important to utilize AI and open data as assistance to own learning.
books: Textbook "Aerospace Major Lab/Exercises AB" published by Kanazawa Institute of Technology
requiredKnowledge: Student should read the textbook and handout before an experiment and understand what kind of experiment they will be carrying out. In addition, students should make a lesson report before a class as preparation, if necessary for that class.

activityGoals.body: Be able to plan an experiment and carry it out independently based on knowledge learned.
Be able to carry out tests safely based on an understanding of the principle of an experiment and the measuremen
Be able to arrange test data using computers and explain the key and problem appropriately.
Be able to reliably interpret the results of an experiment and evaluate the validity of the test data.
Be able to explain the obtained test data reasonably by comparing it with an analytical solution.
Be able to summarize the experimental results in a report, submit it before a deadline, and explain them.
