achievementLevels.ideal:
①	Students understand the basics of carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRPs) and design CFRPs laminated plates. Students understand the details of the experiments and carry out molding of laminated plates, cutting of specimens, and bending tests, and also carry out recording, analysis and consideration of test results.
②	Students properly conduct tests of three characteristic buckling types for semi-monocoque structures b evaluate the validity of obtained data by comparing it with theoretical or numerical analysis results.
③	Students can properly explain the generation of lift and the principle of stability, the difference between test models and actual aircraft, and record test data.
achievementLevels.standard:
①	Students understand features of the mechanical properties of carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRPs). Students understand experiments and carry out molding of laminated plates, cutting of specimens, and bending tests, and also carry out recording and analysis of test results. Students prepare reports and presentations as scheduled.
②	Students conduct the buckling experiments and give a general explanation of the buckling phenomena in a presentation.
③	Students can roughly explain the generation of lift and the principle of stability, the difference between test models and actual aircraft, and record test data.

lessons.content:
Students understand the learning objectives,
outline, and target abilities of this course
based on the distributed syllabus.
In particular, students understand which role
this course assumes within the learning
objectives of the department of aeronautics
and a rough concrete level of achievement.
①Guidance on outline and manner of operation
of molding and evaluation of CFRPs (carbon
fiber reinforced plastics). Students research
design of laminated CFRPs using a prepreg
sheet with given properties. Students start
to prepare lamination.
lessons.assignments:
Students understand the
relationship between the
learning objectives of
the department of
aeronautics and this
course.
①Students research the
application, molding
method and strength
properties of CFRPs,
and hand in the
research report the
following week.

lessons.content:
Students laminate prepreg sheets based on a
defined design in the first week and make
laminated plates by hot press molding.
lessons.assignments:
Students research evaluation
method of strength properties
of CFRPs based on the JIS
standards given in the first
week.

lessons.content:
Students cut out specimens from the molded
plates by diamond-cutter and measure the
dimensions.
Students understand the handling of the
universal testing machine. Teaching
assistants conduct bending tests and
obtain load-deflection curve.
lessons.assignments:
Student research strength
properties and the
calculation method of the
strength of the molded plates
by load-deflection curve.

lessons.content:
Students evaluate the bending properties of the
molded plates from the experimental results in
the third week, and examine these results and
compare them with designed values.
Students begin preparation of report and
presentation.
lessons.assignments:
Students prepare result
report, PowerPoint material
and presentation.

lessons.content:
Students hand in result report and deliver
presentation and discussion. Students need
to research literature before presentation
for proper question and answer.
Students self-check the content of the
experiments, reports, presentation and
attendance.
lessons.assignments:
Students rehearse group
presentation and prepare
presentation by researching
literature for question and
answer.

lessons.content:
Strength evaluation of Semi-monocoque
structure
Orientation: It is explained
that the aircraftstructure consists
of thin sheet metal; therefore,
buckling strength becomes
a problem for structural design.
The experimental method and general
background of the buckling
experiment,including the calculation
method of the buckling load, are
explained. In addition, actual
examples of aircraft structures,
T-3 and OH-6D, are shown
as the teaching materials.
lessons.operation:
Lecture and meeting
Confirmation of
experimental procedure and
 task allocation
in the experiments.
lessons.assignments:
Students should review
the three types of
buckling typical
for semi-monocoque structures
from a textbook
of structural mechanics.
Students should also
read p. 5 of the textbook
and understand
the purpose of the
experiment.

lessons.content:
Snap buckling test
Students can understand the typical failure mode
 of shell structures though
a comparison between a theoretical and
experimental buckling load obtained
from the snap buckling tests using
an aluminum can they prepare.
Self-check of lecture content
and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments:
Students review failure
behavior of the shell
structure and predict the
expected failure
load and the buckling mode
through the textbook pp. 6 to
7.

lessons.content:
Shear buckling test
Students observe the shear buckling
process, such as the shear buckling
wrinkle and load resistant capability,
under a tension field through the shear
buckling test. Students learn the shear
load resistant capability of the shear
load members of the aircraft, including
spar-webs and rib-webs through
a comparison between the experimental
value and the expected failure load.
Self-check of lecture content and
current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments:
Students should learn tension
field theory and predict the
expected buckling
load and the buckling
mode. Students should
also read pp. 7 to
10 of the textbook
and understand the
calculation method of
the shear buckling load
of the test specimen.

lessons.content:
Compression buckling test
A thin sheet has little load-resistant
capability after compression buckling.
However, reinforcement with thin stiffeners
shows an enhanced load-resistant capability
even in a post-buckling situation.
Students observe the above state by
experiment. At the same time,
students also confirm by sight
the situation of the structure
which caused compression buckling.
In addition, students estimate
the effective width based on
the experimental results and also
understand the grounds of the enhancement
of strength for the stiffened panel.
 Self-check of lecture content
and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments:
Students learn the theory of
the compression buckling
and predict the expected
buckling load and the
buckling mode. Students
read pp. 10 to 12 of the
textbook and understand
the calculation method
of the local buckling
load of the test
specimen.

lessons.content:
Oral presentation and report submission
Students perform an oral presentation
on three kinds of buckling experiments.
Using experimental data and a comparison
between test results and the theoretical
predicted value, students investigate
the load resistance capability of
the stiffened panels. In the oral
presentation, students can
appropriately cope with various
questions by having researched
the reference documents.
Self-check of current progress is
conducted.
lessons.assignments:
Students should perform
preparations for their
oral presentation and
the submitted report.
Students should
understand the style
of the submitted report
by reading pp. 13 to 14
of the textbook and
also prepare for questions
in the oral presentation
by reviewing the related
documents for the concept
of stiffened panels.

lessons.content:
Flight dynamics
Equipment: Flight demonstration wind tunnel
Flight dynamics test (1): aerodynamic properties
Investigation of lift characteristics of the
aircraft model as the angle of attack is varied.
Comparison between experimental data and
theoretical analysis.
Self-check the content of the lecture,
experiments and theory.
lessons.assignments:
Read textbook pp. 21-35
Create 1st report

lessons.content:
Flight dynamics test (2): trim and neutral
points
Investigation of static stability and neutral
points of the aircraft model as the center of
gravity moves.
Comparison between experimental data and
theoretical analysis.
Self-check the content of the lecture,
experiments and theory.
lessons.assignments:
Read textbook pp. 36 to 45
Create 2nd report

lessons.content:
Flight dynamics test (3): short period
oscillation and phugoid oscillation
Investigation of dynamic stability of the
aircraft model as free flight varies.
Comparison between experimental data and
theoretical analysis.
Self-check the content of the lecture,
experiments and theory.
lessons.assignments:
Read textbook pp. 46 to 51
Create 3rd report

lessons.content:
Flight dynamics test
(4): stalling
Investigation of stall characteristics of
aircraft model using flow visualization.
Self-check the content of the lecture,
experiments and theory.
lessons.assignments: Read textbook pp. 52 to 56

lessons.content:
Oral presentation and integrated learning
Review and self-evaluation
lessons.assignments:
Prepare to submit second
report and oral presentation.
Self-evaluation on
achievement in this course.

On the basis of knowledge learned in subjects such as ‘Strength of Materials' and ‘Strength of Materials for Aircraft Structures’, student will learn the advanced mechanics for aircraft structures.

title: 航空構造力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Mechanics of Aircraft Structures II
educationalGoal:
Students will learn
(1) Thin-walled cross section bar under torsional moment
(2) Aircraft structural design under static loads
(3) Aircraft structural design under fatigue loads"
advice:
On the basis of knowledge learned in subjects such as'Strength of Materials for Aircraft structure' and 'Mechanics of Aircraft Structures I', student will learn the advanced topics in mechanics of aircraft structures.
We will cover the following materials:
(1) Thin-walled cross section bar under torsional moment
(2) Basic concepts of structural design methods under static loads
    (Strength ratio, Margin of safety)
(3) Basic concepts of structural design methods under fatigue loads
    (Safe life design, Damage tolerance design)

Students should thoroughly review what they have learned in
'Strength of Materials for Aircraft structure' and
'Mechanics of Aircraft Structures I'
before taking this course.
books: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials -Second Edition, Kyoritsu Syuppan, 2013
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of Mechanics of Materials and Mechanics of Aircraft Structure.

activityGoals.body: Be able to calculate torsional stiffness and shear stress of bars with circular cross sections
Be able to explain the meanings of 'limit load' and 'ultimate load'
Be able to evaluate the static strength of aircraft structure using strength ratio or margin of safety
Be able to analyze fatigue strength in aircraft structures through fatigue life calculation
Be able to analyze fatigue strength in aircraft structures through damage progression calculation

title: 構造解析演習
subtitle: Structural Analysis Exercises
educationalGoal:
Students will learn basic knowledge of the finite element method,
acquire skills to perform structural analysis using the finite
element analysis software, and develop the ability to appropriately
utilize these knowledge and skills in aircraft structural design.
advice:
In this course, students will learn how to properly conduct numerical structural analyses
by using the finite element analysis (FEA) software.
In the first half of the course, students will analyze the stress concentration of
a flat plate with semicircular notches.
In the second half of the course, students will analyze the deformation and stress
of the boxbeam which is a simplified model of an aircraft wing structure.
Through the exercises, students will learn the basic knowledge of the finite element method,
acquire the skills to perform structural analysis using the FEA software,
and develop the ability to appropriately utilize these knowledge and skills in aircraft
structural design.
books: Keishiro Yoshida, 'Structural Analysis Exercises', Kanazawa Institute of Technology (2022).
requiredKnowledge: It is recommended that students have already taken the subject of 'Strength of Materials'.

activityGoals.body: Be able to evaluate the effect of elements division on the analysis results
Be able to adjust the density of elements division to conduct an accurate analysis
Be able to calculate the deformation and stress of boxbeam
Be able to evaluate the analysis results based on knowledge of strength of materials
Be able to design the thickness of skin panels of the boxbeam

educationalGoal:
With the rapid development of computers, numerical simulations for aerodynamic analysis are essential in the aircraft design process.
In this practical training course, students will learn how to properly use numerical simulation for fluid dynamics in the aircraft design process. Students will also learn how to utilize numerical simulation to solve actual engineering problems that occur in their local community.
advice:
In this course, students will learn numerical analysis through the use of numerical analysis software.
We will cover the following materials:
1 Introduction to numerical simulation
2 Aerodynamic analysis
Geometry modelling, Meshing, Computational method, Initial and boundary conditions, Execution of analysis, Evaluation of results, Comparison with experimental results
books: Required materials will be specified in the first lesson.
requiredKnowledge:
It is recommended that students have already taken the following courses: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics, 3D-CAD, Aerodynamics for Aircraft I, and Mathematical Modeling and Programming.
The textbook will be handed out during the class.

              1.Numerical simulation

3.Computational Fluid Dynamics
4.Finite volume method
5.Local collaboration

              With the rapid development of computers, numerical simulations for aerodynamic analysis are essential in the aircraft design process.
In this practical training course, students will learn how to properly use numerical simulation for fluid dynamics in the aircraft design process. Students will also learn how to utilize numerical simulation to solve actual engineering problems that occur in their local community.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, students will learn numerical analysis through the use of numerical analysis software.
We will cover the following materials:
1 Introduction to numerical simulation
2 Aerodynamic analysis
Geometry modelling, Meshing, Computational method, Initial and boundary conditions, Execution of analysis, Evaluation of results, Comparison with experimental results

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)propose a problem for Design Project III.
(2)study a procedure to solve the problem.

Students will:

-rules and the administration methods in the laboratory

-other conventions of lab use.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（小栗和幸研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Oguri Kazuyuki)
educationalGoal:
On the basis of the design and fabrication technology of the basics of aerospace engineering learned so far, the basic ability to design, fabricate and propose feasible ideas on transportation machines by applying aerospace engineering theory will be obtained.
At the same time, students will learn the importance of cooperation with local community to advance their ideas.
Generative AI will also be effectively utilized in research.
advice:
Design Project III is the subject of the collected studies in the final stage of the curriculum. Examples of research subjects at Oguri Lab include the following.

-Surface treatment of composite materials
 Modification and analysis of surfaces by atmospheric pressure and plasma, and fine particle shot blast to obtain better adhesion of bond and paint.
-Surface treatment of metallic materials
 Modification and analysis of surface by fine particle shot peening to obtain better fatigue and anti-corrosion properties, also photocatalytic properties.
-Surface treatment of aircraft materials
 Various surface microfabrications and analysis to obtain electromagnetic shielding and stealth properties.

A detailed project theme is determined through discussion. Students will discover their own problems and solve them. Students will also understand the targets of this subject, the overview of the course and the objectives. In particular, students will understand which part of the learning objectives of this department this subject carries and a detailed level of their achievement.
books: Not specified.
requiredKnowledge: Because Design Project III is based on the lectures, experiments, and practice of quarters 1 to 6 in the department of aeronautics, students should review them appropriately as needed. In particular, a review of Materials for Aerospace Vehicle Structure and Strength of Materials is needed.

activityGoals.body: Be able to establish a project theme and put it into action based on an engineering design process.
Be able to finalize the results students obtained as documents and conduct a presentation with discussion.
Be able to perform design, drafting, manufacturing (production) and simulation.

educationalGoal:
Based on the fundamental knowledge of aeronautics and astronautics and the fundamental skills for designing and manufacturing aircrafts/spacecrafts and their components, students will develop their ability to design actual aircrafts/spacecrafts and their components.
Students will conduct numerical simulations and/or experiments on mechanical properties of aerospace composite structures.
advice:
The Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics aims to educate students to become engineers who can support the development of transportation machines such as aircrafts and spacecrafts by using their knowledge of aeronautics/astronautics and their skills on mechanical design and manufacturing. Design Project III is a culmination subject in the final stage of the curriculum.
The targets of this subject are the following:
-to develop the ability to design actual aircrafts/spacecrafts and their components
-to develop the ability to apply theories in aeronautics and astronautics to solve real technical problems of aircraft and spacecraft
-to develop the ability to evaluate the phenomena that occur in real aircraft and spacecraft based on aeronautics and astronautics

In this laboratory, students conduct research on technical issues on composite materials used for aerospace structures. A detailed project theme is decided through discussion with the supervisor. Students will discover their own problems and solve them. Students must also understand the targets of this subject and the content of this course based on the syllabus.

              学習・教育目標

              Based on the fundamental knowledge of aeronautics and astronautics and the fundamental skills for designing and manufacturing aircrafts/spacecrafts and their components, students will develop their ability to design actual aircrafts/spacecrafts and their components.
Students will conduct numerical simulations and/or experiments on mechanical properties of aerospace composite structures.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              The Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics aims to educate students to become engineers who can support the development of transportation machines such as aircrafts and spacecrafts by using their knowledge of aeronautics/astronautics and their skills on mechanical design and manufacturing. Design Project III is a culmination subject in the final stage of the curriculum.
The targets of this subject are the following:
-to develop the ability to design actual aircrafts/spacecrafts and their components
-to develop the ability to apply theories in aeronautics and astronautics to solve real technical problems of aircraft and spacecraft
-to develop the ability to evaluate the phenomena that occur in real aircraft and spacecraft based on aeronautics and astronautics

In this laboratory, students conduct research on technical issues on composite materials used for aerospace structures. A detailed project theme is decided through discussion with the supervisor. Students will discover their own problems and solve them. Students must also understand the targets of this subject and the content of this course based on the syllabus.

advice:

Design Project III is the subject of the collected studies in the final stage of the curriculum. The targets of this subject are the following:
-to develop the abilities of design and analysis through the designing of actual transport machines such as aircraft, applying theories of mainly aeronautics, and evaluating actual phenomena relating to the transportation machines such as aircraft.
-to develop the ability to estimate the obtained results from the aeronautical engineering viewpoint.
A detailed project theme is decided through discussion with the teacher. Students will discover their own problems and solve them. The example of the themes are described as follows:
 (1) Research and development of combustor technology for high power, high efficiency, and low pollution.
 (2) Experimental study on engine noise reduction structure.
 (3) Development of combustor concept design tools using optimization techniques and machine learning.
 (4) Research and development of other phenomena and systems in aerospace engineering

title: ロボット応用力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Dynamics of Machine Systems II
educationalGoal:
Acquire basic knowledge about machinery vibration problems.
Understand the basics of vibration and apply it to machine design.
Model and analyze basic vibration phenomena.
advice:
In recent years, high speed and high precision have been achieved to improve productivity, but vibrations generated in various machines cause problems. In this course, it is necessary to understand how to derive and solve the equations for expressing the motion of various vibration models. Therefore, students must not only understand the lectures but also work on exercises and reports the help them acquire the ability to solve vibration problems.
The following topics are covered:
1.Basics of mechanical vibration: equations of motion, simple vibration, harmonic vibration, vectors, and complex representation of vibration
2.Free vibration of a one-degree-of-freedom system without damping
3.Free vibration of a one-degree-of-freedom system with damping
4.Forced vibration of a one-degree-of-freedom system
5.Basics of vibration of a two-degree-of-freedom system
books: Textbook: Basic Vibration Engineering (3rd Edition) [Kyoritsu, in Japanese]
requiredKnowledge: Review Robot Basic Mechanics I & II and Robot Applied Dynamics I in addition to mathematics such as trigonometric functions and differential equations.

activityGoals.body: Model vibration phenomena and derive equations of motion.
Solve equations of motion (differential equations).
Understand and explain the characteristics of the free vibration system with and without damping.
Understand and explain the characteristics of the forced vibration system with and without damping.
Understand and explain the characteristics of a two-degree-of-freedom vibration system using eigenvalue analysis

title: 熱流体工学
subtitle: Thermal and Fluid Science
educationalGoal:
(1) Learn static and dynamic fluid properties.
(2) Learn Bernoulli's principle.
(3) Learn the relation between heat and material properties.
(4) Learn heat conduction and heat convection.
advice:
This is the introduction to thermal and fluid science.
We will cover the following topics:
1. Physical properties of fluids.
2. Static characteristics and dynamic characteristics of fluids.
3. Basic governing equations of fluids.
4. Bernoulli's principle.
5. Relation between heat and phase change of materials.
6. Heat conduction and heat convection.
Students will also learn about advanced issues such as radiation.
Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and formulas.
Students are expected to complete advanced exercises independently.
Students are required to review each unit with on-demand learning materials.
Student should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of lectures, quizzes, tests and reports may change as the class progresses.

title: 制御工学Ⅱ
subtitle: Control Engineering II
educationalGoal:
(1)	Learn the stability and control performance of dynamic systems and learn proportional integral derivative (PID) control.
(2)	Learn the state space representation, state transition matrix, and behavior of dynamic systems.
(3)	Acquire basic knowledge for state feedback control.
(4)	Acquire basic knowledge and skills for control system design and analysis.
advice:
This is another basic course in control engineering that follows completion of Control Engineering I.

Students are expected to actively participate in class reviews of basic mathematics (e.g., differential equations and linear algebra).

Students are expected to complete exercises independently and to identify their own abilities.

Students will acquire basic knowledge and skills to control robotic and mechatronic systems.
requiredKnowledge:
Completion of Mathematics for Robotics I and Control Engineering I.
Sufficient mathematical skill (differentials, integrals, differential equations, and linear algebra).

activityGoals.body: Apply knowledge of differential equations and linear algebra to the design and analysis of dynamic systems.
Calculate gain and phase margins, and determine the stability of systems.
Understand PID control and apply this control method to systems.
Understand state space representation and obtain a mathematical model using this representation.
Understand the behavior of dynamic systems and perform design and analysis to control objects.

title: メカトロニクス
subtitle: Mechatronics
educationalGoal:
Understand mechatronics, a multidisciplinary field of mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, and computer engineering.
Learn sensor technology, principles of motors, and electrical and electronic circuits for sensors and motors.
advice:
Course Content

1.Sensor Selection and Circuit Design
Students will learn how to interpret data sheets for various sensors and develop a deeper understanding of sensor circuits that interface with microcontrollers.

2.DC Servo Motors and Control Circuits
The course will cover the characteristics and selection methods of DC servo motors, which serve as representative actuators in robotic systems, along with an in-depth study of motor control circuits.

3.Mechanical Transmission and Motor Selection
Students will learn how to mathematically model mechanical transmission mechanisms and apply these models to select appropriate DC motors for specific applications.
books:

Reference books: None
Reserved books: None

title: アドバンストロボティクス
subtitle: Advanced Robotics
keywords: Model Learning and Learning Based Control
educationalGoal: Acquire the necessary knowledge of machine learning in robotics. Students will understand how to learn the motion of a robot in space from data and be able to use it for model learning and learning-based control. Students will learn linear regression and classification, polynomial regression, Gaussian kernel regression, and other kernel methods, as well as support vector machines and Gaussian process regression, and be able to use these methods in Python. Students will also acquire knowledge and skills for model learning and learning-based control.
advice: The student should understand the fundamentals of linear algebra and probability. It is also necessary to understand the fundamentals of system control (control engineering). Preparation for the next lecture will be given in class, and students are expected to check the contents of the lecture in advance. For review, solve the exercise reports (using Python) given in the class by yourself, and clarify any unclear points by the next class.
requiredKnowledge: The student should have an understanding of the fundamentals of linear algebra and probability. The student should also have an understanding of the fundamentals of system control (control engineering).

Can perform machine learning using the kernel method of polynomial regression and Gaussian kernel regression.
Can perform machine learning with support vector machines.

              Acquire the necessary knowledge of machine learning in robotics. Students will understand how to learn the motion of a robot in space from data and be able to use it for model learning and learning-based control. Students will learn linear regression and classification, polynomial regression, Gaussian kernel regression, and other kernel methods, as well as support vector machines and Gaussian process regression, and be able to use these methods in Python. Students will also acquire knowledge and skills for model learning and learning-based control.

advice:
This is a course of lab exercises in robotics. We will cover the following topics:

1.Measurement and Signal processing: Evaluation of sensor characteristics
This course deals with linearity, nonlinearity and hysteresis property in sensors, which can be evaluated with a potentiometer, a pressure conductive sensor and a phototransistor. Using the Arduino and the MATLAB & Simulink software, the data acquisition can be done interactively.
2.Experiment for mechanics of materials
Students will measure the load and deformation of a robot arm, summarize the results as a mechanical model and evaluate the model by experiments.

Students will construct a timer interrupt program, ADC/DAC program, PWM control and encoder reading program, and I2C program using Arduino, and run each program using an actual circuit, motor, and sensor.
4.Experiment for control engineering
Students will apply the classical control theory to DC servomotors using Arduino and a PC with MATLAB/Simulink software.

title: ロボティクス専門実験・演習Ｂ
subtitle: Robotics Major Lab/Exercises B
educationalGoal:
(1) Learn basic theory and method for robotics control.
(2) Deepen understanding and develop robotics application capabilities.
(3) Learn the skills needed to perform experiments and write reports.
(4) Learn how to arrange and present the content, results, and discussion in a report.
advice:
This is a course of lab exercises in robotics. We will cover the following topics:
1. Dynamic behavior
Students will deepen their understanding of the basis of vibration analysis of one- and two-degree-of-freedom vibration systems. In particular, students will measure the amplitude and phase of a vibration system affected by time-varying force to measure the vibration of the experimental apparatus. Students will learn the basic theory of a dynamic vibration absorber.
2. Robot control 1
Students will learn the operation of robot simulator and then program a robotic arm.
3. Robot control 2
Students will learn feedback control and programming. A driving circuit and a computer will be installed on the robot that was built in the previous course, Engineering Exercises for Robotics I.
4. Fundamentals and practice of reinforcement learning
Students will learn the fundamentals and implementation of reinforcement learning through both simulation experiments and real-world experiments using an inverted pendulum system.

4.Robot control

              (1) Learn basic theory and method for robotics control.
(2) Deepen understanding and develop robotics application capabilities.
(3) Learn the skills needed to perform experiments and write reports.
(4) Learn how to arrange and present the content, results, and discussion in a report.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is a course of lab exercises in robotics. We will cover the following topics:
1. Dynamic behavior
Students will deepen their understanding of the basis of vibration analysis of one- and two-degree-of-freedom vibration systems. In particular, students will measure the amplitude and phase of a vibration system affected by time-varying force to measure the vibration of the experimental apparatus. Students will learn the basic theory of a dynamic vibration absorber.
2. Robot control 1
Students will learn the operation of robot simulator and then program a robotic arm.
3. Robot control 2
Students will learn feedback control and programming. A driving circuit and a computer will be installed on the robot that was built in the previous course, Engineering Exercises for Robotics I.
4. Fundamentals and practice of reinforcement learning
Students will learn the fundamentals and implementation of reinforcement learning through both simulation experiments and real-world experiments using an inverted pendulum system.

title: イノベーション基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Innovations
educationalGoal: This course is designed to develop students' ability to discover and solve problems by consolidating the knowledge and skills they have acquired so far, with the creation of value in the real world in mind, leading to innovation. The basic process consists of organizing needs that exist in the real world, finding solutions, and comparing and evaluating cost-effectiveness and alternative solutions.
advice: In this course, students will work systematically in teams to solve real-world problems by integrating them individually or in teams from necessary knowledge, previous experience, and a lot of information. The flow of the process varies depending on the main theme, but basically, team activities proceed in the order of “issue discovery → understanding the current situation (proving the existence of the issue, proving the existence of the need to solve the issue (needs), and understanding existing measures) → determining the issue based on analysis of the cause and structure of the issue → setting preconditions and conditions for achievement toward solution → determining a solution plan”.
books: None.
requiredKnowledge: Content acquired through various courses taken by the time of the course. In particular, the concept of innovation with an awareness of quality, cost, delivery, and safety in the real world in the basic training course “Engineers and Sustainable Society.

Can gather information necessary to further discussions in team activities (work).
Able to aggregate individual knowledge and apply it to value-based problem solving.
Can recognize issues that exist in the real world with diverse solutions and creatively find solutions.
To be able to efficiently carry out effective team activities (work) in a team (organization).
Demonstrate a willingness to evaluate one's own abilities objectively.

title: 電気回路Ⅰ（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Electric Circuits I
educationalGoal: This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering curriculum. The objective is to acquire a basic knowledge of electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze and design electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will learn the fundamentals of electric circuits consisting of resistance (R), inductance (L), capacitance (C), and their combinations connected to an AC power source. In addition, students will learn about phasor representation of sinusoidal AC.
advice:
Below is an outline of the topics to be covered:

AC circuit basics: properties of sine wave AC, effects of resistance, inductance, and capacitance, average and RMS values, phasor indication of sinusoidal AC

This subject is not only important as preparation for subsequent courses (Electrical Circuit II, and Electrical Circuit III), but also each specialized topic should be studied keeping in mind that it is a basic course requirement.
Based on the level of student understanding as indicated by quiz results, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and course content.
books: Basic electric circuit (2nd edition) New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: It is important that you solve as many problems as possible in order to understand and practice the theory presented. In addition, continuous effort is required on a daily basis. We encourage you to 1) examine various reference books, 2) ask the lecturer questions, and 3) take advantage of the Mathematical and Science Education Research Center so that you can clarify what you don't understand.

activityGoals.body: Participants can draw and explain the waveform of a sine wave alternating current.
Participants can formulate the circuit equations for AC circuits consisting of R, L, and C.
Participants can calculate average and rms values of sine wave AC.
Participants can represent the phasor of sine wave AC.

They can represent correctly the phasor of a sine wave AC and sufficiently explain why complex numbers are introduced in the calculation of sine wave AC circuits.

In the calculation of an AC circuit, it is no exaggeration to say that it is common sense to use a so-called symbolic solution using phasors and complex numbers. In the subsequent course Electric Circuit IV, the circuit analysis techniques using symbolic solution becomes the base for learning more advanced and complex analysis methods.
advice:
1 Mutual induction
2 Useful theorems
3 Two-port circuit
4 Phasor trajectory

In addition, since the progress is adjusted while confirming the degree of understanding from the result of the quiz or the like, the schedule of the class and the learning content may be changed. Depending on the presence of Humanity and Nature Seminar, times and contents of review class may change (follow the instructions of the professor in charge)
books: Basic electric circuit(2nd edition)New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: In this course, it is important to solve more problems in order to understand the theory and put it into practice. Ask the professor in charge, 3. Use the Mathematics Education Center so that you can always clear things that you do not understand. In this classes, Mathematics such as simultaneous linear equations, determinants, matrices, differentiation / integration, basics of complex numbers, and trigonometric functions are utilized.

The electric circuits can be solved using useful theorems.
In a two-terminal pair circuit, calculations using at least Z, Y, and F matrix.

title: 高電圧パルスパワー工学（再履修クラス）
subtitle: High-Voltage Pulsed Power Engineering
educationalGoal:
Students will
(1) learn dielectric and electrical insulation phenomena in gas, liquid, and solid.
(2) learn how to generate AC, DC, and Impulse voltage.
(3) learn how to measure high voltage and high current.
(4) learn various high voltage testing.
advice:
Course description
1. Electrostatic fields and electrical field calculation
2. Elementary physics of electrical discharge
3. Electrical breakdown and conduction phenomena in gas
4. Electrical breakdown and conduction phenomena in liquid and solid dielectrics
5. Generation of various high voltages, measurement of high voltages and high currents,
high voltage insulation test techniques
6. Application of high-voltage and pulsed power engineering

Expectations
To understand the lecture well, knowledge about “electromagnetics (electrostatic fields)”, “electrical machinery (transformer)”, and “transient phenomena in liner circuits” are required.
books: Textbook: Fundamentals of high voltage engineering, ISBN: 9784817302380 (in Japanese)
requiredKnowledge: This course is strongly related to the following courses: “Electromagnetics (Electrostatics)”, “Transient Phenomena in Linear Circuits”, and “Electrical Machinery (Transformer)”. Therefore, reviewing the basic knowledge obtained from those related courses is necessary in advance.

activityGoals.body: Be able to calculate the electrical field strength by analytical formula derived from Gauss's law
Be able to understand the kinetics of charged particles and to explain elementary physics of electrical discharg
Be able to understand the Townsend breakdown theory, Paschen's law, and streamer theory in gas.
Be able to understand the electrical breakdown and conduction phenomena in liquid and solid dielectrics.
Be able to understand the AC, DC and impulse voltage generator, and insulation test techniques.
Be able to explain the application of high-voltage and pulsed power engineering.

title: 自動制御
subtitle: Automatic Control
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn framework of feedback control theory involving "Mathematical Expression","Laplace Conversions","Block Diagrams","Transfer Functions" and furthermore
(2) learn characteristics  "Transfer Functions","Stability","Transient & Frequency Responses","Steady States".
advice:
This is a basic course of Feedback Control. We will cover the following materials:

1. Basic concepts in feedback control: System elements and block diagram, representation with elementary blocks.
2. The various elements of a control process: Proportional, integrating, differentiating, 1st-order, 2nd-order,
   and delya-time lag blocks.
3. Transformation from time to frequency domains: The elementary blocks and the transfer functions. The Laplace
   transformation and the transfer functions. Examples of electric circuit systems.
4. Transfer characteristics of typical basic blocks: Specifications in the time domain (transient responses) and
   the frequency domain(frequency responses). The Lablace inversion and the time funcsions, Graphical resprese-
   ntation by the frequency functions.
5. Stability of linear control systems: The concept of stabiity, stability analysis using the Routh-Hurwitz
   crierion (matrices & determininants)
6. Desing of PI-control systems: Design method of the basic PI-control systems.
books:
Textbook: 実務者のためのPID制御設計[森北出版]
Reference books: やさしく学べる制御工学[森北出版]、わかる自動制御（増補改訂版）[日新出版]、システム設計のための基礎制御工学[コロナ社]
requiredKnowledge:
Acquisition of “Computer Engineering for Electrical Engineers” and “Electrical and Electronic Instrumentation”.
Enough skill of mathematics (especially matrix / inverse matrix and determinant calculations).
Basic knowledge of mathematics (the Laplace conversion & inversion and so on).
How to use a calculator.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the elementary blocks and their basic characteristics.
Be able to explain the Laplace conversion and inversion.
Be able to explain the transfer functions and represent control systems with the transfer functions & block diag
Be able to perform basic designs of the feedback control systems using the transfer functions.
Be able to explain analytical stability criteria on linear control systems.
Be able to designe the basic PI-control systems.

title: 電気回路Ⅳ（電子工学）
subtitle: Electric Circuits IV for Electronic Engineering
educationalGoal: In the previous study of electric circuits, the physical dimensions of a circuit has been assumed to be small enough. At the higher frequencies, however, the size of the circuit must be taken into account, and voltages and currents behave as waves. In this course, students will learn the theory of distributed-constant circuits, propagation of electric waves along transmission lines. They will also study about the tools and techniques for high-frequency circuit analysis and design.
advice:
1. Voltages and currents on distributed-constant circuits
2. Reflection Coefficient, standing waves, and input impedance looking into a transmission line.
3. Smith chart
4. Impedance matching for a distributed-constant circuit
5. Scattering matrix

Students are expected to understand the difference between lumped-constant circuits and distributed-constant circuits, relation between frequency and wavelength, and will learn about the equations for voltages and currents on distributed-constant circuits and their solutions.
Students are also expected to learn how to use Smith chart and scattering matrix.

title: 電子材料
subtitle: Electronic Materials
educationalGoal: In this lecture, we learn about the material properties of dielectrics and magnetic materials, which are the basic materials in the electronic field along with semiconductors. To understand the polarization phenomenon and dielectric loss of dielectrics and the physical meaning of the magnetism, and also about applications of ferroelectric and ferromagnetic materials to devices. Make it possible to recognize the importance of materials through lectures.
advice:
1. Basics of electronic materials : We learn the basic contents in learning electronic materials, especially the atomic orbital and electron configuration in solids, the bonding between atoms, band structures, and electrical conduction.
2. Dielectric materials and their properties : Learn about polarization, which is a general response phenomenon to the electric field of a solid. After learning the polarization under applying a DC electric field, the complex permittivity is derived under applying an AC electric field, and the dielectric loss. Furthermore, we learn about the properties of ferroelectrics that show strong polarization and their applications.
3. Magnetic materials and their properties : We understand from a microscopic point of view the magnetization phenomena that occur when a substance is placed in a magnetic field, and learn about the basic content of magnetism that determines the magnetic properties of the substance.               In this lecture, we learn about the material properties of dielectrics and magnetic materials, which are the basic materials in the electronic field along with semiconductors. To understand the polarization phenomenon and dielectric loss of dielectrics and the physical meaning of the magnetism, and also about applications of ferroelectric and ferromagnetic materials to devices. Make it possible to recognize the importance of materials through lectures.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              1. Basics of electronic materials : We learn the basic contents in learning electronic materials, especially the atomic orbital and electron configuration in solids, the bonding between atoms, band structures, and electrical conduction.
2. Dielectric materials and their properties : Learn about polarization, which is a general response phenomenon to the electric field of a solid. After learning the polarization under applying a DC electric field, the complex permittivity is derived under applying an AC electric field, and the dielectric loss. Furthermore, we learn about the properties of ferroelectrics that show strong polarization and their applications.
3. Magnetic materials and their properties : We understand from a microscopic point of view the magnetization phenomena that occur when a substance is placed in a magnetic field, and learn about the basic content of magnetism that determines the magnetic properties of the substance. Learn about the origin and classification of ferromagnetism, and their applications to the field of electrical and electronic engineering. In addition, we will learn about the basics and applications of spintronics that apply electron spin, which has attracted attention in recent years.

title: 音響工学
subtitle: Acoustical Engineering
educationalGoal: In our daily life, all kinds of sounds are surrounded. The sounds are essential to our lives. In this course, mathematically expression of the physical characteristics of sound waves and analysis of phenomena are learned. Also applied techniques of sound and audio, behavior of sounds related to room acoustics and hearing in daily life, and so on are learned.
advice:
1 Physical phenomenon of sound
   Characteristics of sound wave, vibration of string, vibration of air column
2 Physical quantity of sound
   Sound velocity, sound intensity, sound pressure level, noise level, distance attenuation,
absorption/reflection/refraction/transmission, diffraction
3 Audio application
   CD player, sound editing, sound processing
4 Room acoustics
   Basic concept, sound ray method, impulse response, reverberation time, room sound field, acoustic design
5 Hearing
  Hearing mechanism, sound perception, three elements of sound, pitch perception, direction perception

This course is more specialized in the field of acoustic in the "Introduction to Acoustics and Imaging", which has already been offered. It will also lead to the understanding of the "Acoustic and Imaging Systems" and "Optical Information Engineering" which will be offered in the next semester.

              授業科目の学習・教育目標

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Physical phenomenon of sound
2.Physical quantity of sound
3.Audio application
4.Room acoustics
5. Hearing

              In our daily life, all kinds of sounds are surrounded. The sounds are essential to our lives. In this course, mathematically expression of the physical characteristics of sound waves and analysis of phenomena are learned. Also applied techniques of sound and audio, behavior of sounds related to room acoustics and hearing in daily life, and so on are learned.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              1 Physical phenomenon of sound
   Characteristics of sound wave, vibration of string, vibration of air column
2 Physical quantity of sound
   Sound velocity, sound intensity, sound pressure level, noise level, distance attenuation,
absorption/reflection/refraction/transmission, diffraction
3 Audio application
   CD player, sound editing, sound processing
4 Room acoustics
   Basic concept, sound ray method, impulse response, reverberation time, room sound field, acoustic design
5 Hearing
  Hearing mechanism, sound perception, three elements of sound, pitch perception, direction perception
This course are conducted by following the syllabus, but since progress is adjusted while confirming the degree of understanding from the results of students' attitudes in the class, question situations, quizzes, etc., the course schedule and learning contents may be changed.
This course is more specialized in the field of acoustic in the "Introduction to Acoustics and Imaging", which has already been offered. It will also lead to the understanding of the "Acoustic and Imaging Systems" and "Optical Information Engineering" which will be offered in the next semester.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              No Required Materials.

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

title: エネルギーデバイス工学
subtitle: Energy Devices Engineering
educationalGoal: Harmonization with the environment is required to utilize modern electric energy. In this course, students learn the social background of environmental energy. Next, primary batteries, secondary batteries, fuel cells, solar cells, piezoelectric / thermoelectric conversion elements, etc. are taught as important energy conversion devices constituting an electric energy system. The development trend, the situation of practical use, the structure, the operation principle, and the characteristics are learned.
advice:
The following topics will be addressed in this lecture.

1. Environmental energy problems and energy conversion applied devices
 Current status of environmental energy problems / Overview of various energy conversion application devices
2. Fundamentals of electrochemical energy conversion
 Electrolysis and battery / principle of voltage generation / principle of current generation
3. Operation principle of electrochemical device
 Primary battery / Secondary battery / Fuel cell / Electric double layer capacitor
4. Fundamentals of photoelectric conversion, thermoelectric conversion, and piezoelectric conversion
 Principle of photovoltaic generation / Principle of thermoelectric generation / Principle of piezoelectric effect
5. Operating principle of photoelectric conversion, thermoelectric conversion, and piezoelectric conversion device
 Solar cell / Thermoelectric device / Piezoelectric device
6. Other power storage technologies
books: ELECTROCHEMISTRY [morikita] (in Japanese)
requiredKnowledge: This subject covers a wide range of energy conversion & storage technologies resulting from environmental energy problems. Therefore, in addition to knowledge in the fields of chemistry and physics, it is an integrated subject that requires a social perspective on the environment. Work to deepen understanding while referring to textbooks in each field as appropriate.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain global environmental energy issues and the role of various energy conversion devices.
Be able to explain an overview of electrochemical energy conversion, which is the basis of batteries
Be able to explain the characteristics of various devices to which electrochemical energy conversion is applied.
Be able to explain the principle of photoelectric, thermoelectric, and piezoelectric conversion and its applicat
Be able to explain the type, operation principle and development status about the power storage technologies.

title: 通信工学

educationalGoal: This course introduced the basic topology of communication systems, properties of basic information like voices and videos, imperfection of transmission systems that makes data errors, basis of digital modulation/demodulation and multiplexing scheme. advice:
This course is constructed following chapters:
i) Basic topology of telecommunication systems,
ii) Basic properties of information (voice, video, data) on telecommunication systems,
iii) Entropy of information,
iv) Communication disturbance due to imperfections of transmission (noise, linear/non-linear distortion),
v) Digital modulation/demodulation and its filtering techniques,
vi) Multiplexing techniques (Frequency division multiplex, Time division multiplex, Code division multiplex,)

title: 音響・映像システム
subtitle: Audio and Video Systems
keywords: AI, machine learning and pattern recognition
educationalGoal: Sound and image are indispensable as information communication media. In this course, especially participants study the information processing technology of audio and video systems which connect human and machine. They learn how to analyze audio and video in a computer and understand the data processing techniques required for machine recognition of audio and video. The goal is to use specific hardware and software to gain an experiential understanding of audio and visual technology.
advice:
1. Capturing and formatting audio and video signals
2. Digital transmission and recording of audio and video signals
3. Digital audio and video analysis
4. Digital audio and video processing
5. Digital audio and video reproduction

This course are conducted according to the syllabus. However, check the level of understanding based on the questions in the class and the results of the quizzes and exercises, then adjust the progress accordingly. Mathematical knowledge such as frequency conversion and matrix calculation is required to understand the technology in the lecture. If you have any questions about this type of knowledge, you should consult several reference books and ask to lecturer. In addition, several educational centers: Mathematical and Science Education Research Center and Center for Information Services and Processing can be used for the consultation.
Be sure to bring your laptop PC with headphones and network cable during the lecture to practice how to handle sound and video. In addition, prepare the internet connection for acquiring lecture materials and retrieving information.
books:
Textbooks: Multimedia System Technology (in Japanese) [Corona publishing]
Reference books: Introduction to Sound and Audio (in Japanese) [Corona publishing], Basic Studies of Video Systems -Fundamental Technologies for Digitization and their Applications- (in Japanese) [Corona publishing]
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: This course is based on the contents of "Introduction to Acoustics and Imaging" and "Acoustic Engineering", and requires knowledge of "Programming Practice for Electrical and Electronic Engineers". Since the computer becomes a basic learning tool, it is required to master the operation of the computer.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and explain the basics of capturing and formatting audio and video signals.
Be able to understand and explain the basics of digital transmission and recording of audio and video signals.
Be able to understand and explain the basics of digital audio and video analysis.
Be able to understand and explain the basics of digital audio and video processing.
Be able to understand and explain the basics of digital audio and video reproduction.

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Audio and video signals
2.Digital signal processing
3.AI, machine learning and pattern recognition
4.Virtual reality and augmented reality
5.System integration

              Sound and image are indispensable as information communication media. In this course, especially participants study the information processing technology of audio and video systems which connect human and machine. They learn how to analyze audio and video in a computer and understand the data processing techniques required for machine recognition of audio and video. The goal is to use specific hardware and software to gain an experiential understanding of audio and visual technology.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              1. Capturing and formatting audio and video signals
2. Digital transmission and recording of audio and video signals
3. Digital audio and video analysis
4. Digital audio and video processing
5. Digital audio and video reproduction

This course are conducted according to the syllabus. However, check the level of understanding based on the questions in the class and the results of the quizzes and exercises, then adjust the progress accordingly. Mathematical knowledge such as frequency conversion and matrix calculation is required to understand the technology in the lecture. If you have any questions about this type of knowledge, you should consult several reference books and ask to lecturer. In addition, several educational centers: Mathematical and Science Education Research Center and Center for Information Services and Processing can be used for the consultation.
Be sure to bring your laptop PC with headphones and network cable during the lecture to practice how to handle sound and video. In addition, prepare the internet connection for acquiring lecture materials and retrieving information.

              Textbooks: Multimedia System Technology (in Japanese) [Corona publishing]

title: 電気電子工学専門実験Ａ
subtitle: Major Laboratories for Electrical and Electronic Engineering A
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn basic knowledge regarding electrical and electronic measurement and experiments, developing the ability to actually perform measurement and analysis.
(2) learn to independently propose and find solutions for new challenges in the field of electric and electronic engineering.
(3) learn to create clear and meaningful lab reports
advice:
This course deals with the basic principles of fundamental laboratory techniques for electrical and electronic engineering. It also enhances the development of students’ skill in carrying out the experiment for electrical and electronic engineering. We will conduct the following six experimental subjects:

(1) Power device characteristics
(2) Amplifier
(3) Optical semiconductor device characteristics
(4) Transformer characteristics
(5) Power converter circuits
(6) Electronic circuit design

Students conduct experiments (1st week) and oral exam (2nd week) on an experimental subject.
books: Major Experiments for Electrical and Electronic Engineering A・B (Kanazawa Institute of Technology, 2022)
requiredKnowledge:
Knowledge of basic electrical and electronic engineering.
Basic laboratory skills (knowledge of “Introduction to Project Design” and “Project Design / Implementation and Operation”).

activityGoals.body: Be able to acquire basic knowledge about measurement, experiment, computer and automatic control
Be able to carry out the experiment for electrical and electronic engineering in safe and appropriate methods
Be able to theoretically calculate using the measured value and be able to create the clear and accurate tables
Be able to create the lab reports with theoretical discussions for experimental results

subtitle: Designing Skills in Electrical Engineering
educationalGoal: Many electrical equipment that support the functions of modern society are manufactured through electrical design. The definition of design is that producing the electrical equipment most economically and within the deadline, while determining the specifications to be realized and satisfying the given technical requirements, its size, shape. In this course, you will learn about both the concept of the design method and drawing by CAD through lectures and exercises.
advice:
In this course, you will learn the following items in order.

1. Fundamentals of design
2. Structure, principle and basic theory of synchronous machine
3. The nature and content of electrical equipment
4. Basic principles of electrical design
5. Design method of three-phase synchronous generator
6. Design exercise of three-phase synchronous generator
7. CAD drafting basics
8. CAD drafting exercises

(3) learn basis of the electrical machining, the lighting and the electrical heating.

5. Lighting
   5-1 Basis of lighting / 5-2 Lighting design / 5-3 Light sources
6. Air conditioning system and freezer machine
   6-1 Freezing cycle / 6-2 Freezer machine / 6-3 Air conditioning system / 6-4 Heat pump
7. Other electric power applications
   7-1 distributed power supply and smart grid / 7-2 Superconductor applications

subtitle: Telecommunications Law
keywords: National Exam for Chief Telecommunications Engineer
educationalGoal: This course introduces the laws and regulations required for obtaining qualifications to students taking this course.  Students acquire the knowledge of telecommunications law for the operation of the telecommunications business and for the national exam of the Chief Telecommunications Engineer.
advice:
The outline of this course is shown in below.

1. Introduction: Trends of telecommunication policy, Amendment of Telecommunications Business Act, Summary of telecommunications system etc.
2. Telecommunications business Act,Enforcement order and regulations: Purpose, Definition, Registration, Notifications, Facilities for telecommunications business, Terminal Facilities, Chief Telecommunications Engineer, Rules of Installation, Technician, Land-use.
3. Wire telecommunications Act, Enforcement order and regulations: Purpose, Definition, Technical Standards.
4. Radio Act and Enforcement regulations: Purpose, Definition, Radio Station license, Radio facilities, Radio operators, Operation, Supervision.
5. Treaty of International Telecommunications, the related law and regulations: The Treaty of International Telecommunication Union, Act on Prohibition of Unauthorized Computer Access, Summary of Electronic Signatures and Certification, Business and the related laws.
6. Telecommunications trends: Summary

To pass, students must earn at least 60 points out of 100.

subtitle: Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III
educationalGoal: To find some new challenges and these solutions in Design Project III (PD III) from a view point of electrical and/or electronic engineering, students acquire the basis of a comprehensive ability needed as engineer using their knowledge and skills through this seminar.
advice:
・	Through deeply understanding what kind of project in PD III, students clarify the necessary knowledge and skills.  To carry out the selected project and to confirm own ability regarding its project, students learn more knowledge and skills through taking other courses.
・To implement the project of PD III, students acquire the basic knowledge and skills needed in academic and major fields of the project.
・Students achieve some skills such as finding/solving of problems, personal development, self-management, and communication through the examination of the academic papers related in the project and project results up to the previous year.
・Students recognize the importance notices and safety instructions of equipment in the assigned laboratory, and cultivate the engineering ethics.
・Students deeply consider your major field and future career.
・Students understand the contents of your project which will be implemented in PD III, identify the problems and those improvements of your project, and acquire the ability of proposing solutions.
・Finally, students make a project proposal of PD III.
Through "Project Design Activity Support System" placed in the student portal, all students should submit the project proposal and also enter each activity regarding in PD III.
To pass, students must earn at least 60 points out of 100.

educationalGoal: This course is designed to develop students' ability to discover and solve problems by consolidating the knowledge and skills they have acquired so far, with the creation of value in the real world in mind, leading to innovation. subtitle: Design Project III(Hirama Junji)
educationalGoal:
Topic: Research based on the specialized knowledge and skills acquired during previous classes.  Project themes contribute topics in the following fields; electrical/electronic engineering, agriculture, biology. The results obtained in this research have the potential to greatly contribute to society.
Objective: To improve upon specialized technical knowledge and develop exceptional engineers.
advice:
This course summarizes the project design process while integrating and reviewing all of the subjects previously studied, from the basics to the specialized and advanced.Students enrolled in one of the subjects listed below will be divided into groups and conduct research activities throughout the school year. A research notebook will be submitted daily, and meetings once a week will be conducted.
(1)Development of equipment to physically control insect pests using light（This theme has been inactive since FY2024.）
(a)This topic focuses on developing a pesticide-free and environmentally friendly insect pest control
light source device by utilizing specially fluctuating ultra-bright light-emitting diodes (LED).
(b) Measure the light stimulus response (electrophysiology) from the retinal potential of insects (moths and stink bugs). Furthermore, verify the phototaxis of the insects by behavioral observation.
(2)Plant bioelectrophysiology
(a) Investigate the bioelectrophysiological phenomena of plants by measuring the bioelectric potential response to ambient environmental stimulation conditions.
(b) Optimized plant factory environmental control
(3) Biomagnetic field measurement application: Using a prototype MRI device, measure various biological information in a non-invasive and none-destructive manner.
(4) Development of ultra-low magnetic field measuring equipment: development of the Flux Gate Magnetometer

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（山口敦史研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Yamaguchi Atsushi)
educationalGoal: Training will be carried out to grow up engineers in the electrical & electronic fields with problem-finding ability, solution ability, and application ability through educational programs that emphasize basic knowledge and skills in the fields of electrical engineering and electronic engineering, which are highly important in modern society
advice:
This course is the final course of the project design course, including an introduction to project design, and is positioned as a course that integrates the items learned in all courses. Aim to review basic subjects and acquire advanced expertise through experiment and theoretical examination of project themes.
Divide into teams for each project theme and conduct research activities. Report research progress about once a week and discuss how to proceed.
books: N/A
requiredKnowledge:
Review what you have learned in mathematics, semiconductor engineering, and electronic properties.
English is also required to read academic papers.
Metal processing skills (Yumekobo license) and computer programming skills are also desired.

activityGoals.body: To clarify the purpose of the project theme and make a research plan.
To consider a problem-solving method of the project theme and execute it safely and continuously.
To analyze and evaluate the research results correctly based on the social needs.
To discuss actively in group and make a presentation on research results effectively
To summarize the research results as project reports..

achievementLevels.ideal: The significance and purpose of the project theme are fully understood and research activities are actively promoted. The research contents and results can be explained to others in an easy-to-understand manner. The Achievement can be summarized in papers and/or be presented at academic conferences.
achievementLevels.standard: The significance and purpose of the project theme are understood, and the contents can be explained. The problems in the research can be pointed out. Application of research results in related fields can be proposed. Design and fabrication of the equipment necessary to carry out research on the project theme, can be done. Research results can be presented at the Project Design III Presentation Review and related academic societies’ meeting, and good discussion can be made in Q&A sessions. Research activities can be continued based on the research plan until the end of the project.

subtitle: Design Project III(Aoki Shigeaki)
educationalGoal:
[Theme] Audio system, ultrasound, hearing, environmental noise
[Subject] Preliminary surveys will be conducted on each project theme, a research plan will be formulated, and research will be conducted according to the plan. In this project activity, students will learn research proposal methods, annual planning methods, research methods, presentation methods.
[Goal] Providing original results based on conventional research on the own project.
advice:
Project themes are conducted individually or in groups. Each progress is reported in a weekly meeting. The annual schedule is as follows.
7th term (previous semester): Determine the project theme. Review and submit the project proposal (research plan). At the end of the term, submit a project progress report summarizing the considerations and present it at the interim presentation.
8th term (second semester): Identify problems in the research subjects. Examine and verify solutions. At the end of the semester, submit a project report that summarizes the review process and its results, and presents it at the public presentation review meeting. Themes will be handed over to students in the next year.
The general theme includes the following project themes.
(1) Audio system
(2) Ultrasound
(3) Hearing
(4) Environmental noise
This course is the final course of the design project process, including an introduction to design project. This course integrates the items learned in all courses. The objectives are reviewing basic subjects and acquiring advanced expertise through the project themes and theoretical studies.
books: No Required Materials.
requiredKnowledge:
1. Design project III is characterized by creative activities that attempt a unique approach to the goal. Therefore, it is required to vigorously learn basic knowledge, identify problems and plan solutions to problems by themselves.
2. Abilities to review progress and find a better direction through discussions with the professor in charge, graduate students and classmates are required.
3. It is necessary to acquire the habit of keeping the activity contents.

Be able to embody the problem of project and its solution and execute it safely and continuously.

Be able to summarize the research results as a project report.

subtitle: Design Project III(Noguchi Keisuke)
educationalGoal:
Educational programs focusing on basic knowledge and skills in the fields of electrical engineering and electronics.
Students will:
(1) learn small antennas and wave propagation for mobile communication systems. (2) learn how to investigate each project theme. (3) learn objectives, research process, plan to annual schedule, research method and presentation of project. (4) achieve outcomes based on conventional research for project.
advice:
This course is the last subject in the design project, and it is positioned as a course which integrates the matters learned in all courses. Students will be encouraged to review basic courses and acquire advanced specialized knowledge through experiments and theoretical examinations through the project.

Each student has a project theme and works independently or as a group. Weekly meetings are held, and activities are reported in weekly reports. Annual schedule is as follows:

First semester :  Students will decide the project themes to be implemented and submit project proposals. Progress of activities is announced at an interim presentation held at the end of the semester.
Second semester : At the end of the semester, results of the activities are summarized to a project report. Based on the report, students will have a presentation at the final review in an open presentation meeting. After the open presentation meeting, students will have meetings with the next year's students to handover.

Project themes includes (1) small and planar antennas, (2) broadband and high efficient microstrip antennas, (3) antennas for sensor network systems, (4) wearable antennas, (5) automotive antennas and (6) wireless power transfer antennas.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（會澤康治研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Aizawa Koji)
educationalGoal: Educational programs focusing on basic knowledge and skills in the fields of electrical engineering and electronics, which are highly important, develop highly creative electrical and electronics engineers who have acquired problem-finding, solving, and applied skills. This is a culmination subject following the project design subjects and specialized seminars up to the third grade.
advice:
Each student has a project theme and works alone or in groups.  A seminar will be held weekly, and the progress will be reported in the weekly paper.   Students should acquire the licenses and qualifications for activities if necessary.  The annual schedule is as follows.
[Previous semester]  Students review the project themes and project proposals defined in the preparatory seminar, and carry out the project according to the action plan.  Students will also present the results of the project at an interim presentation after the end of the previous semester.
[Second semester]  Students carry out the project while reviewing the project proposal.  In addition, students will compile the results in a project report by the end of December and prepare a presentation at the design project III (PDIII) public presentation examination committee at the end of the semester.  The contents of the ongoing project will be handed over to students in the next fiscal year.
 The project theme is decided by consultation with professor.  This seminar is the final of the project design process. advice:

educationalGoal:
Students can discover new problems in the field of electricity and electronics and use their knowledge and skills to solve the problems.

advice:

Conduct research activities alone or in groups. Have a weekly meeting. Submit weekly reports based on
daily communication. If necessary, learning may take place using digital methods such as online (distance) or on-demand classes. AI will be used for research surveys and create reports.The annual schedule is as follows.
First semester: Create a research schedule for the first semester according to the project proposal.
Learn the basics of research and investigate related literature. Submit weekly reports and learn the process of accelerating and modifying your plan. The results of the semester will be presented in June and August.
Second semester: Create weekly reports and activate discussions. We hold briefings in October and December
to improve presentation skills. The results will be compiled into a dissertation and presented at the
public presentation judging committee. Summarize the handover materials for the next year's students.
[Learning advice]
Think and act on your own. Work on activities that give you a sense of achievement and solidarity when overcoming difficulties and questions.
[Example of project theme]
(1) Study on the effect of high voltage pulsed high electric field on batteries
(2) Study on the effects of the equalization circuit and method for assembled batteries
(3) Cell performance analysis and modeling of lead-acid batteries

              学習・教育目標

              1.Energy storage technology literacy
2.Energy storage device
3.Transient response and energy conversion
4.Reliability and safety evaluation
5.Utilizing online-class and AI

              　Students can discover new problems in the field of electricity and electronics and use their knowledge and skills to solve the problems.
　Set a theme for mastering batteries (power storage technology literacy), understand the social and technical background of electricity storage technology as an electrical expert, and learn how to solve problems and make presentations.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              [Outline of class]
Conduct research activities alone or in groups. Have a weekly meeting. Submit weekly reports based on
daily communication. If necessary, learning may take place using digital methods such as online (distance) or on-demand classes. AI will be used for research surveys and create reports.The annual schedule is as follows.
First semester: Create a research schedule for the first semester according to the project proposal.
Learn the basics of research and investigate related literature. Submit weekly reports and learn the process of accelerating and modifying your plan. The results of the semester will be presented in June and August.
Second semester: Create weekly reports and activate discussions. We hold briefings in October and December
to improve presentation skills. The results will be compiled into a dissertation and presented at the
public presentation judging committee. Summarize the handover materials for the next year's students.
[Learning advice]
Think and act on your own. Work on activities that give you a sense of achievement and solidarity when overcoming difficulties and questions.
[Example of project theme]
(1) Study on the effect of high voltage pulsed high electric field on batteries
(2) Study on the effects of the equalization circuit and method for assembled batteries
(3) Cell performance analysis and modeling of lead-acid batteries

educationalGoal: Cource objective is establishing the theme for supplying low-carbon safe and reliable power and energy in the local community（GX). advice:
[Aim and tasks of the projec] This course is the final course in the design project process, including the introduction to design project, and is regarded as a course that integrates the items learned in all design projects. Aim to review basic course and acquire advanecd expertise through experiments and theoretical studies. Project activities will be conducted alone or in groups. The results are put together in a paper and presented at the public presentation review board. In addtion, you will submit the hand-over materials for students of the next fisical year.
[Examples of project theme] (1) Collection and analysis of measurement data of Hakusan-roku campus energy management demonstration system, (2) Modeling and simulation of micro grid system, (3) V2X system for EV utilization, RES Hydrogen system utilizaition for energy management system.
books: No needed.
requiredKnowledge: The energy management system is an integareted field of study that deals with all of creation, transmission, storage use of electricity and energy, and from hardware devices such as power generatio, storage, demand, control and mobility.
