title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（池永訓昭研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Ikenaga Noriaki)
educationalGoal: Utilize knowledge and skills acquired so far to acquire vacuum technology and thin film fabrication technology. Find new themes such as new functional thin film materials with a view to application from from among actual issues in industry, and focus on developing the ability to plan and execute research to achieve the objectives. In particular, it deals with themes that make full use of plasma.  The goal is to acquire comprehensive skills as an engineer.
advice:
Students will persevere under the advice of their supervisors about the research themes they are working on, and obtain new knowledge while solving problems. Through research activities (project activities), acquire problem-finding / solving ability, self-development / self-management ability, communication ability, literature research ability, importance of safety inspection, and ethical judgment ability as an engineer. Aiming to actively present research results at academic societies, etc., so that questions and answers can be made accurately among experts.
Specific lessons are as follows:
1.Project activities: Divide into 1 or 2 people for each research theme. In the previous semester, we will mainly study basic knowledge and literature on plasma and functional thin films. In the second semester, students will learn basic research skills and communication skills by working on each research theme and at the same time summarizing the research results and reporting on the progress of each research theme.
2.Presentation of research results: In the second semester, oral presentations will be made at various academic societies for each research theme. In addition, regarding joint research themes based on actual issues with companies, other universities, and public institutions, we participate in regular meetings and actively participate in discussions to conduct specialized Q & A training. . Eventually, a project design III report will be created and presented at a public presentation.
books: Distribute each time
requiredKnowledge: In order to handle plasma, basic knowledge about the behavior of charged particles ("electromagnetism") must be understood. In addition, since improvements and repairs of the equipment are also required, prior knowledge of “electrical circuits”, “transient phenomena”, and “electrical materials” is also necessary, so it is important to review and deepen your understanding.

activityGoals.body: To be able to acquire basic vacuum technology and design more advanced vacuum equipment
To be able to explain scientific definition of plasma and basic calculations on behavior of charged particles
To be able to understand and apply various technologies using ions and plasma
To be able to acquire thin film fabrication technology using plasma and apply it to various fields
To be able to appropriately communicate your thoughts to third parties through discussions and presentations

In addition, regarding joint research themes based on actual issues with companies, other universities, and public institutions, we participate in regular meetings and actively participate in discussions to conduct specialized Q & A training. . educationalGoal:
Students will
(1) acquire basic knowledge of electromagnetism and thermodynamics.
(2) acquire engineering application skills and research promotion skills.
advice:
The target fields are as follows.

1. Methods and equipment design for efficiently heating materials that can be heated by microwaves
2. Development of cooling systems using thermoacoustic engines that use solar heat as input
3. Development of safe and easy-to-use far-infrared cooking appliances

We will develop microwave heating devices and plasma generators that contribute to industrial applications by improving heating efficiency. We will also develop thermoacoustic engine refrigeration devices that contribute to the development of local agriculture by cooling the surface of farmland and the water used in hydroponics in summer. Furthermore, we will present an engineering approach to making cooking more delicious in the process of developing a general-purpose far-infrared cooker.

               Each student has a project theme and works alone or in groups.  A seminar will be held weekly, and the progress will be reported in the weekly paper.   Students should acquire the licenses and qualifications for activities if necessary.  The annual schedule is as follows.
[Previous semester]  Students review the project themes and project proposals defined in the preparatory seminar, and carry out the project according to the action plan.  Students will also present the results of the project at an interim presentation after the end of the previous semester.
[Second semester]  Students carry out the project while reviewing the project proposal.  In addition, students will compile the results in a project report by the end of December and prepare a presentation at the design project III (PDIII) public presentation examination committee at the end of the semester.  The contents of the ongoing project will be handed over to students in the next fiscal year.
 The project theme is decided by consultation with professor.  This seminar is the final of the project design process. title: 形式言語とオートマトン
subtitle: Formal Languages and Automata
educationalGoal: Formal language is a mathematical description of a language and formal grammar is a set of rules that can be used to create sentences with a language. In this course, students learn regular language and context-free language. They also study several kinds of automata that can recognize those languages. The knowledge students learn in this course provide the foundations of the technology that processes natural languages and other languages.
advice:
In this course, students learn formal grammar and formal language, especially focusing on regular language and context-free language. They also study several kinds of automata that can recognize those languages. The topics are as follows:

1. Deterministic finite automaton
2. Nondeterministic finite automaton
3. Nondeterministic finite automaton with epsilon moves
4. Regular language
5. Regular grammar
6. Regular expression
7. Context-free grammar
8. Context-free language
9. Chomsky hierarchy
books: オートマトン・言語理論 第２版，冨田 悦次，横森 貴著，森北出版
requiredKnowledge: Review sets and their operations taken up in "Discrete mathematics", especially the notation of sets, subsets, power sets, and the direct product of sets.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain Chomsky hierarchy.
Be able to perform conversions between equivalent finite automata.
Be able to explain the definition of regular grammar and regular language.
Be able to perform conversions between regular grammar and finite automaton.
Be able to explain the definition of regular expression.
Be able to perform derivations in context-free grammar.

educationalGoal: In addition to IT knowledge, project management and business knowledge are required to build or use information systems. In information system construction, the user and the builder confirm the requirements for many items such as functions, reliability, shortening of disaster recovery time, and improvement of operability. In this course, students will learn basic knowledge about the construction and use of information systems.
advice: Information systems are created by integrating IT knowledge such as programs, databases, networks, and system configurations. In order to design a good information system, it is necessary to confirm the usage requirements for many items such as functions, reliability, operability, and operability. In design, it is necessary to consider important matters, costs and trade-offs. In information system construction, both the builder side and the user side are constructed by the project, so a project management method is required. title: デジタル通信と信号処理
subtitle: Digital Communications and Signal Processing
keywords: Discrete time signal and frequency characteristics
educationalGoal: Analog signals such as voice, music, images, and video are digitized and processed. Digital signal processing can be implemented as a computer program, which enables flexible and complex processing. In this course, students will learn the basics of digital signal processing by digitizing analog signals such as audio and video. They will also learn the basics of digital communications achieved by digital signal processing.
advice:
Students will systematically learn the following basic knowledge and theory about digital signal processing and digital communication:

1. Discrete time signals and systems.
2. Frequency characteristics of discrete-time systems.
3. z-transform and transfer function.
4. Sampling theorem.
5. Discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and fast Fourier transform (FFT).
6. Digital filter design method.
7. Baseband transmission, modulation/demodulation and multiple access.
books: Textbooks: Reference books: Reserved books:
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of the basics of mathematics such as exponential functions, trigonometric functions, complex numbers, and linear algebra is required. It is desirable that students have knowledge of probability statistics, Fourier transform, and Laplace transform. These are introduced in this course. Numerical calculation software such as Excel are used in the practices.

activityGoals.body: Understand and apply the convolution sum and frequency characteristics of discrete-time signals.
Understand and apply the relationship between z-transform, the transfer function and circuit.
Understand and apply the sampling theorem.
Understand and apply DFT and its fast calculation method.
Understand the basics of digital filter design.
Understand the basics of modulation/demodulation and multiple access.

title: コンピュータグラフィックス
subtitle: Computer Graphics
educationalGoal: Computer graphics (CG) is used in various fields such as numerical simulations, the visualization of engineering or scientific phenomena, and contents production for education or entertainment use (VR/AR). In addition, devices such as GPUs and 3D printers have been developed rapidly in recent years. In this course, students will systematically learn the technologies used in CG today. They will also acquire the skills needed to create CG content through programming using a CG library.
advice:
In this course, lectures on basic theories about 3D representation and modeling methods are provided, and programming exercises for implementing the theories learned are conducted. Specifically, students will learn and implement knowledge related to coordinate transformation, 3D modeling, hidden surface removal, shading, rendering, texture mapping, and animation in 3D space. Specific topics include the following:

1. Overview of 3D CG technology
2. 3D coordinate system
3. Coordinate and projective transformation in 3D space
4. 3D CG modeling
5. 3D CG animation
6. Overview of 3D CG rendering
7. Hidden surface removal and shading
8. Texture mapping
9. Radiosity and shadowing
10. Summary and reflection
books: Required Materials will be provided in the class.
requiredKnowledge:
1. Students must have basic mathematical skills such as trigonometric functions, matrices, and vector calculations.
2. Student must be able to program an application using C language.
3. Student should spend one hour preparing for the next class or exercise and spend more one hour for reflection.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain and use coordinate systems in 3D space.
Be able to explain coordinate and projection transformation of 3D CG and use them properly.
Be able to explain the basic methods of 3D modeling and implement them by programming.
Be able to explain hidden surface removal and shading techniques and select effective techniques.
Be able to explain 3D CG animation techniques and program basic animations.

              Computer graphics (CG) is used in various fields such as numerical simulations, the visualization of engineering or scientific phenomena, and contents production for education or entertainment use (VR/AR). In addition, devices such as GPUs and 3D printers have been developed rapidly in recent years. In this course, students will systematically learn the technologies used in CG today. They will also acquire the skills needed to create CG content through programming using a CG library.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, lectures on basic theories about 3D representation and modeling methods are provided, and programming exercises for implementing the theories learned are conducted. Specifically, students will learn and implement knowledge related to coordinate transformation, 3D modeling, hidden surface removal, shading, rendering, texture mapping, and animation in 3D space. Specific topics include the following:

1. Overview of 3D CG technology
2. 3D coordinate system
3. Coordinate and projective transformation in 3D space
4. 3D CG modeling
5. 3D CG animation
6. Overview of 3D CG rendering
7. Hidden surface removal and shading
8. Texture mapping
9. Radiosity and shadowing
10. Summary and reflection

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Required Materials will be provided in the class.

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              1. Students must have basic mathematical skills such as trigonometric functions, matrices, and vector calculations.
2. Student must be able to program an application using C language.
3. Student should spend one hour preparing for the next class or exercise and spend more one hour for reflection.

title: 知識情報処理
subtitle: Intelligent Information Processing
educationalGoal:
Intelligent information processing requires knowledge to be represented and stored systematically. Students will:
(1)	Learn how to represent and use knowledge for problem solving and transform knowledge into a data structure for knowledge representation in computers.
(2)	Touch briefly on AI programming and deepen their understanding of problem solving, machine learning, natural language processing, etc.
advice:
This course is a lecture/practice course that gives an overview of artificial intelligence, which has recently been in the spotlight again. First, students will learn an outline of intelligent information processing. Next, students learn about search algorithms used in computer shogi programs, localization techniques important for robot cars (automated driving vehicles), and machine learning for big data processing. Finally, students learn about natural language processing, image processing, etc. To deepen their understanding of each method, emphasis is placed on tackling the quizzes that are presented throughout the semester.

We will cover the following materials:

1. Basics of intelligent information processing.
2. Problem solving (state space model, various search algorithms, and dynamic programming).
3. Probabilistic methods (Bayesian theory, reinforcement learning, and localization).
4. Machine learning (clustering and pattern recognition).
5. Natural language processing.
books:
Textbooks：An Illusrated Guide to Artificial Intelligence
Reference books：None
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge: “Problem solving” requires basic algorithms, “inference” requires probability theory at a high school level, and “machine learning” requires understanding of linear algebra. Additionally, the quizzes include tasks that students are encouraged to solve in their favorite programming language because they take a considerable amount of time if done manually.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and explain the basic concepts of intelligent information processing.
Be able to understand and explain search algorithms and dynamic programming for problem solving.
Be able to understand and explain localization methods.
Be able to understand and explain how to apply machine learning to those problem and solve them.
Be able to understand and explain the basics of natural language processing and image processing.

(2) Acquire how to conduct scientific computing.

advice: This course provides instruction on utilizing a computer to handle data. This course covers various topics, including handling outliers, missing data values, representative parameters, and typical machine learning methods based on linear algebra and statistics. Students will learn about supervised and unsupervised learning, both part of machine learning, through practical analysis using Python libraries. Students will also learn how to visualize analysis results effectively. It is recommended that before taking this course, one should have a foundational understanding of Linear Algebra and Statistics. Depending on the progress of the lecture, other content may be added, and the timing of quizzes and achievement assessment tests may change. Please follow the specific instructions of the instructor.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course provides instruction on utilizing a computer to handle data. This course covers various topics, including handling outliers, missing data values, representative parameters, and typical machine learning methods based on linear algebra and statistics. Students will learn about supervised and unsupervised learning, both part of machine learning, through practical analysis using Python libraries. Students will also learn how to visualize analysis results effectively. It is recommended that before taking this course, one should have a foundational understanding of Linear Algebra and Statistics. Depending on the progress of the lecture, other content may be added, and the timing of quizzes and achievement assessment tests may change. Please follow the specific instructions of the instructor.

title: プログラミング言語とコンパイラ
subtitle: Programming Languages and Compiler
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn how a compiler works. This technology can also be used for analysis and processing of data formats distributed on the network. Students will also come to understand the control flow and data management methods of programming languages and gain a deeper understanding of programming languages by learning the compiler algorithms and their implementation technologies.
advice:
In this course, students learn practically how to develop compilers and interpreters through compact examples.

The following are the main items:
1) Programming language control structure and data management.
2) String search for text data, HTML, etc.
3) Compiler processing (lexical, syntax, expression, semantic analysis, code generation).
4) Memory management for program execution.
5) Execution environment (byte code, virtual machine, interpreter).
6) Compiler-related tools.

title: 情報工学専門実験・演習Ａ
subtitle: Information and Computer Science Major Lab/Exercises A
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will learn programming techniques, wireless network technologies, and data collection methods via evaluation of wireless sensor networks with a microcontroller.
They will also be given opportunities to master knowledge regarding the Internet and security using routers and switches, gain knowledge and skill via investigations and exercises related to IPv4/IPv6, and study how to control networks via packet capture.
advice:
This course covers the following topics:
1. Embedded programming with c and python language
2. Wireless network technologies for IoT systems
3. Communication protocols toward IoT systems
4. Information network construction method
5. Analysis of information transmission path by network capturing
6. Implementation of network capture program using C / C ++

NOTE:
A review of Programming I, Programming II, Fundamental Computer Architecture, and Information Networks is required.
books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Students of this course are expected to have the following:
1. C and Python programming skills.
2. Understanding of CPU, main memory, and register on an embedded processor.
3. Knowledge and skill related to the construction of information networks.
4. Knowledge related to information transmissions using packet capturing tools.
5. Understanding of packet capture implementation techniques.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain wireless technologies such as wireless LAN, ZigBee, and LoRaWAN.
Be able to explain a data collection method via MQTT.
Be able to design and evaluate a wireless sensor network.
Be able to explain network hierarchical structures.
Be able to understand Internet traffic using packet capture.
Be able to set a personal IP address on a personal computer.

              学習・教育目標

              1.Microcontroller

5.Programming

              In this course, students will learn programming techniques, wireless network technologies, and data collection methods via evaluation of wireless sensor networks with a microcontroller.
They will also be given opportunities to master knowledge regarding the Internet and security using routers and switches, gain knowledge and skill via investigations and exercises related to IPv4/IPv6, and study how to control networks via packet capture.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course covers the following topics:
1. Embedded programming with c and python language
2. Wireless network technologies for IoT systems
3. Communication protocols toward IoT systems
4. Information network construction method
5. Analysis of information transmission path by network capturing
6. Implementation of network capture program using C / C ++

NOTE:
A review of Programming I, Programming II, Fundamental Computer Architecture, and Information Networks is required.

1. C and Python programming skills.
2. Understanding of CPU, main memory, and register on an embedded processor.
3. Knowledge and skill related to the construction of information networks.
4. Knowledge related to information transmissions using packet capturing tools.

title: 情報セキュリティ
subtitle: Information Security
educationalGoal: In this course, you can learn cryptography and network security. The first half of the course deals with elliptic curve cryptography which is gradually spreading in practice. The second half of the course deal with adaptation of security technique such as encryption and authentication to the Internet.
advice:
In the first half of the course, the textbook "誤り訂正符号と暗号の基礎数理" is used and you can learn cryptography especially ellipctic curve cryptography.
In the second half of the course, the textbook "マスタリングTCP/IP　情報セキュリティ編" is used. The students learn adaptation of security technique such as encryption and authentication to the Internet environment. The students also learn general network security. Understanding TCP/IP is important.

Knowledge about TCP/IP is required.

title: 専門ゼミ
subtitle: Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III
keywords: Ethics and  crisis management for IT engineers
educationalGoal: Specialized seminars supplement the knowledge and skills that were not necessarily sufficient in past lectures, exercises, and experiments required for the PD3 project, and acquired new knowledge and skills in each activity area. The aim is to cultivate the basic academic and technical skills so that PD3 can be implemented voluntarily from the 7th term.
advice:
In order to carry out any research / work / assignment in PD3, the faculty presents the learning area program and clarifies the knowledge and skills required to carry out the project in this learning area program. The student confirms his / her ability, clarifies items to be supplemented and items to be newly acquired, and learns and acquires them.

In the course of the lesson, teachers clarify PD3 goals and action plans. Students conduct tests on these learning results to confirm their achievement, and prepare a project proposal for PD3.

Specifically, in performing PD3, learn the latest technology trends in specialized fields that are closely related to each project, and summarize the technology explanation and your opinion in the form of an essay.

After understanding such a common technical foundation, learn the outline of the technology related to PD3 and plan the project. In addition, each project of PD3
Since the use of equipment and applied software differ for each project, the students will actually experience the operation in the laboratory so that they can grasp the goals and action plan of the project as a real feeling. We will announce the project proposal as the final result of this course.
books: Materials will be provided at each laboratory.
requiredKnowledge:
If you do not earn credits for this course, you will not be allowed to take PD3. Two or more unauthorized absences will be rejected.
Be sure to read the booklet “Safety Guidelines for Experiments and Research” provided in the laboratory.

activityGoals.body: be able to have a clear image of PD3 goals and action plans.
be able to explain the theme of PD3
be able to acquire the knowledge and skills to perform PD3 autonomously
be able to give an overview of the latest technological trends in your area of study and your opinions.

educationalGoal: In this capstone project, students will conduct research activities related to IT systems based on the knowledge and skills related to computer science and technology that they have learned so far. Through these activities, students acquire the abilities needed for identifying a problem, designing the project, and implementing an IT system. Additionally, students will acquire generic abilities related to communicating with others, and evaluating results.
advice:
In accordance with the lab policy of "Research that affects society", you will study in implementation / development of "slightly intelligent agents" that respond to social needs using artificial intelligence or information technology in a broad sense.
On recommended steps, first identify your social needs, and then clarify existing technologies and new necessary functions to solve them. In doing so, make sure that the technology or function you handle belongs to the artificial intelligence and information technology fields in a broad sense. In the field of artificial intelligence, comprehensive materials will be provided, so be sure to acquire broad and well-balanced knowledge as well as technologies used to solve problems.
Your studies will be either system research that combines existing technologies and new functions, or elemental technology research that realizes new functions, or both. When you would like to tackle systems research, you will do collaborative works with other students.

Possible themes for 2026:
Natural language processing: Applied research into educational support technologies, applied research into collaborative filtering, and research into technologies that support group communication.
Computer vision: Research into applied technologies that combine image processing and information theory, and research into the fusion of images and 3D data.

advice:

3. Context-aware natural language processing
4. Web3 technologies (metaverse, NFTs)

title: 構造設計学
subtitle: Structual Design
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)	learn how to estimate deflection of beams and axial forces in trusses.
(2)	learn how to estimate axial force in short columns and buckling loads of long columns.
(3)	learn analysis of statically indeterminate structures.
(4)	learn the slope deflection method.
advice:
This course will cover the following topics:

1. Deflection of beams
2. Axial forces in truss structures
3. Stresses in short columns and the cross-sectional core
4. Buckling of long columns
5. Statically indeterminate structures
6. Rigid frames

In the study of deflection of beams, the second moment of area, bending moment and second-order differential equations are used. In the study of statically indeterminate structures, bending moment and shear force are used. Before taking this course, students are requested to understand Structural Mechanics I and II.

title: 空間情報工学
subtitle: Geoinformatics
educationalGoal: A variety of spatial information is necessary for environmental management of the earth and its regions. Students will acquire basic knowledge on geospatial information engineering, and technology for collecting, accumulating, and analyzing geospatial information.
advice:
This class focuses on remote sensing, geographic information systems, and 3D mapping in spatial information engineering. In recent years, environmental problems such as global environmental problems have attracted attention, and it is desirable to grasp changes in the environment. Remote sensing technology is a technology suitable for analyzing satellite data and monitoring the environment over a wide area. A geographic information system is a means of storing, searching, and analyzing geographic information. 3D mapping is used for advanced navigation systems and augmented reality technologies. The lectures match the basic materials that are distributed. We provide a wealth of examples such as remote sensing images and explain them using PowerPoint presentations. In addition, in order to deepen our knowledge, we conduct exercises using computers.
For exercises, students use software such as EISEI, Google Earth, Google Map, SKETCHUP, etc.
Special lectures will be held by invited representatives from companies that are making use of these technologies.
books: none
requiredKnowledge:
Students must be familiar with the concepts from Surveying 1 and Surveying 2. During the exercises, students need to bring a laptop computer that can connect to the Internet on campus. Materials and data used in the class will be distributed in the teaching material distribution system.
Use of private language in class is strictly prohibited.

keywords: history of city formation and transition
educationalGoal:
Students will:
1) acquire fundamental knowledge on city planning and local development (their concepts, important terms, and methods).
2) learn histories of city formations and transitions and their characteristics.
3) learn good examples of city planning & local development and their characteristics and significance.
advice:
this course provides basic knowledge and skills for city planning and local development in collaboration with local residents, local government, and other related entities. We will cover the following materials:

1. world histories of city formations and transitions from the ancient times to the present age, and their characteristics
2. urban problems in the modern era, theories and measures to deal with them, and present trends of urbanism
3. basic framework of city planning in Japan
4. details of local development activities
5. practical examples of local development and their methods

title: 構造設計演習
subtitle: Exercise of Structual Design
educationalGoal:
To understand the mechanism of seismic damage in infrastructures.
To understand basic theory of seismic design.
To understand dynamic analysis by solving the equation of motion.
To understand numerical programing of time history response analysis with finite difference method.
advice: In quake prone countries like Japan, specifications of substructures are decided from seismic design in most cases. Students will learn seismic damage and history of seismic design of reinforced concrete columns in this class. Static lateral force method was used in the past. On the other hand, dynamic analysis is now used for seismic design owing to the development of ICTs. Therefore, students will learn present style of seismic design through the programing of time history response analysis.

title: イノベーション基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Innovations
educationalGoal: This course is designed to develop students' ability to discover and solve problems by consolidating the knowledge and skills they have acquired so far, with the creation of value in the real world in mind, leading to innovation. The basic process consists of organizing needs that exist in the real world, finding solutions, and comparing and evaluating cost-effectiveness and alternative solutions.
advice: In this course, students will work systematically in teams to solve real-world problems by integrating them individually or in teams from necessary knowledge, previous experience, and a lot of information. The flow of the process varies depending on the main theme, but basically, team activities proceed in the order of “issue discovery → understanding the current situation (proving the existence of the issue, proving the existence of the need to solve the issue (needs), and understanding existing measures) → determining the issue based on analysis of the cause and structure of the issue → setting preconditions and conditions for achievement toward solution → determining a solution plan”.
books: [Reference book] Curtis R. Carlson and William W. Willmott, Five Principles of Innovation, Diamond (2012).
requiredKnowledge: Content acquired through various courses taken by the time of the course. In particular, the concept of innovation with an awareness of quality, cost, delivery, and safety in the real world in the basic training course “Engineers and Sustainable Society.

educationalGoal:
Achieving following abilities to be a civil engineer
(1)	Be able to conduct experiments, analyses or surveys.
(2)	Be able to design, construct, and maintain infrastructure.
(3)	Be able to explain the processes and effects involved in infrastructure.
(4)	Be able to analyze social changes taking the future into consideration.
(5)	Be able to develop sustainable society.
advice:
In the Tanaka laboratory, projects of structural mechanics, maintenance, or disaster prevention are carried out in Design Project III. A main theme will be proposed to each student by the instructor. Students will find problems related to the main theme as a first step. Second, they will conduct surveys. Then they will summarize their findings. Solutions will be conceived and implemented in accordance with plans formulated by the students themselves. In this course, each student proceeds with their project under the instruction of the supervisor.
The following details the activities for each semester.
First semester:Besides textbooks and lecture notes, students refer to specific papers and journals. By doing a literature survey, students review their basic knowledge of structural mechanics and reinforced concrete engineering. Then students make presentations outlining their theme, background on their project, and their project plan.
Second semester:Projects planned in the first semester are carried out by individuals or teams to their conclusion.
A minimum of 450 hours of learning time is required in this course. Preparation and review times shown in this syllabus are minimum values.

advice:

Students will find issues related to the main theme through documents study and literature review as a first step. In this course, each student proceeds with their project under the instruction of the supervisor.

First semester: Besides documents and lecture notes, students refer to specific papers and journals. By doing this literature survey, students obtain basic knowledge of pavement engineering. Then students make presentations outlining their theme, background on their project, and their project plan.
Second semester:Projects planned in the first semester are carried out by individuals or teams to their conclusion.
A minimum of 450 hours of learning time is required in this course. Preparation and review times shown in this syllabus are minimum values.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（中野一也研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Nakano Kazuya)
educationalGoal: Based on the KIT-IDEALS code of conduct, the learning objectives aim to cultivate engineers capable of achieving the educational goals of the Department of Environmental and Civil Engineering. Students will acquire the ability to plan, implement, and evaluate solutions to challenges through the utilization of spatial information, and learn to manage their own project processes. Through these activities, students will complete reports for Project Design III from an academic perspective, comparable to research papers or reports.
advice: At the Geoinformatics Laboratory(Nakano Lab.), projects center on surveying and geomatics. Students select topics from faculty proposals, spatial information projects, or self‑devised themes, with advanced tracks for those moving on to graduate study. Work is student‑led: think independently, act proactively, report to faculty, share with the lab, and refine with guidance. Students learn process and schedule management, practice self‑management, and execute planned research. Participation in the KIT Spatial Information Project and related events deepens understanding of advanced applications. In the first semester, students iterate literature summaries, presentations, and Q&A, while building spatial information literacy through hands‑on use of core tools (GIS, GNSS, remote sensing/photogrammetry, LiDAR). They deepen investigation of their themes and periodically consolidate findings, revising scope as needed. In the second semester, they conduct hypothesis testing, empirical experiments, analysis, and interpretation, individually or in teams, to raise project completeness. Weekly meetings provide progress reporting, with monthly reviews, plus active participation in KIT seminars. Total learning time is about 450 hours, including summer and winter activities; preparation and review time in the learning support plan is a minimum requirement.

              1.Geoinformatics
2.Photogrammetry and Laser Surveying
3.GNSS, Remote Sensing, and GIS
4.Spatial Information Processing
5.Spatial Information Literacy

              Based on the KIT-IDEALS code of conduct, the learning objectives aim to cultivate engineers capable of achieving the educational goals of the Department of Environmental and Civil Engineering. Students will acquire the ability to plan, implement, and evaluate solutions to challenges through the utilization of spatial information, and learn to manage their own project processes. Through these activities, students will complete reports for Project Design III from an academic perspective, comparable to research papers or reports.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              At the Geoinformatics Laboratory(Nakano Lab.), projects center on surveying and geomatics. Students select topics from faculty proposals, spatial information projects, or self‑devised themes, with advanced tracks for those moving on to graduate study. Work is student‑led: think independently, act proactively, report to faculty, share with the lab, and refine with guidance. Students learn process and schedule management, practice self‑management, and execute planned research. Participation in the KIT Spatial Information Project and related events deepens understanding of advanced applications. In the first semester, students iterate literature summaries, presentations, and Q&A, while building spatial information literacy through hands‑on use of core tools (GIS, GNSS, remote sensing/photogrammetry, LiDAR). They deepen investigation of their themes and periodically consolidate findings, revising scope as needed. In the second semester, they conduct hypothesis testing, empirical experiments, analysis, and interpretation, individually or in teams, to raise project completeness. Weekly meetings provide progress reporting, with monthly reviews, plus active participation in KIT seminars. Total learning time is about 450 hours, including summer and winter activities; preparation and review time in the learning support plan is a minimum requirement.

title: プログラミング基礎（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Fundamentals of Programming
educationalGoal:
Computer systems are constructions of hardware and software technology. This course focuses on the software side of the combination.
Programming is the skill used to create software, and knowledge regarding it also helps users employ software effectively.
Since the C language is widely used currently, this course teaches students about software design concepts through the practice of C programming.
advice:
In this course, students will learn the software design concepts by programming, debugging, compiling, and running sample programs.

The evaluation results of exams and reports will be reported to students, who will then be encouraged and required to use those results to improve their skills. Specifically, students in this course will learn about the following topics:

・Fundamental programming procedures
・Variable and type declarations
・Input, output, and calculation
・Branch and repetition
・Function
・File processing
・Pointer and structure
requiredKnowledge:
The installation of a development environment will be covered during the first class and each student must establish the environment before the second class.

Students will be expected to write source code during in the class, so advanced keyboard skills are expected.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the programming syntax of C.
Be able to program applications capable of handling numerous numbers, letters, and data.

educationalGoal:
In this course, students will:
(1) Learn human visual and auditory processing within the context of physiology and psychology.
(2) Learn cognitive, sensibility, and emotional information processing for media contents.
(3) Learn the method for creating affecting contents.
advice:
In this course.  based on the knowledge imparted during “Media Informatics I”, the cognitive, sensibility, and emotional information processing of media contents (pictures, movies, music, etc.) will be examined.
As a part of the course, students will learn and practice to simulate the human processing via computer programming.
Accordingly,  students should review the contents of “Color and Hearing Training” and “Media Informatics I”.

title: データベース
subtitle: Database System
educationalGoal:
A database is a system that shares, updates, and reuses data between multiple applications, thereby ensuring data consistency.
 In this course, students learn the fundamental theory of a relational database, database design, Structured Query Language (SQL), which is the language used for database management, and practical database operations using an actual database management system.
advice:
There are three essential abilities needed to manage a database:

(1)	The ability to handle SQL.
(2)	The ability to ensure data consistency based on the concept of normal form, primary key, and foreign key, etc.
(3)	The ability to design a database application system using transactions.

In this course we mainly focused on (1) and (2), but (3) will be also mentioned in the later classes.

Since SQL is used for comprehensive database operations such as design, handling, and/or maintenance, it will be necessary to polish student SQL management skills by providing them with significant amounts of experience.

With that point in mind, students will be required to connect with and use our database server and then use it to manipulate their own databases in order to foster skills and knowledge related to the operation and management of a relational database.

requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to have acquired fundamental knowledge related to computers via other courses such as “Information Technology Basic” or “Introduction to Server Management”

title: Ｗｅｂプログラミング
subtitle: Web Programming
educationalGoal: Websites not only show home pages, but also provide a more useful system by hosting applications on the internet that are associated with databases. In this course, students will master the scripting language that enables web programming to be executed on the server side. In addition, by acquiring technologies related to web production, students will develop an awareness of issues related to regional collaboration and future information dissemination to society.
advice:
In this course, students will learn programming for the processes executed on the server side for the purpose of mastering web applications using Apache for the web server and Hypertext Preprocesser 5 (PHP5) for the scripting language. Practice will take place on each student's laptop PC operating in a Windows environment.

Specific class topics include the installation and configuration of the PHP development environment, the basics of PHP grammar, PHP built-in functions, PHP programs on the web, and creating applications using classes and objects in PHP.

Before joining the class, students are requested to enter textbook program examples, practice using them, and understand the contents of the textbook.

Students should note that, because there is insufficient time to explain each legal item and each program in detail, they are expected to read the textbook thoroughly beforehand. In class, lectures will focus extensively on supplementary and advanced textbook explanations.

              Websites not only show home pages, but also provide a more useful system by hosting applications on the internet that are associated with databases. In this course, students will master the scripting language that enables web programming to be executed on the server side. In addition, by acquiring technologies related to web production, students will develop an awareness of issues related to regional collaboration and future information dissemination to society.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, students will learn programming for the processes executed on the server side for the purpose of mastering web applications using Apache for the web server and Hypertext Preprocesser 5 (PHP5) for the scripting language. Practice will take place on each student's laptop PC operating in a Windows environment.

Specific class topics include the installation and configuration of the PHP development environment, the basics of PHP grammar, PHP built-in functions, PHP programs on the web, and creating applications using classes and objects in PHP.

Before joining the class, students are requested to enter textbook program examples, practice using them, and understand the contents of the textbook.

Students should note that, because there is insufficient time to explain each legal item and each program in detail, they are expected to read the textbook thoroughly beforehand. In class, lectures will focus extensively on supplementary and advanced textbook explanations.

educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn the basics of game production using Unity. More specifically, they will build a development environment on their individual PCs and learn the game production process through 2D and 3D sample programs. By applying original ideas such as game design, images and animation expressions, and program functions, students will be able to acquire the application skills needed to expand into original game creation.

In this course, students will learn to understand the configuration and operation of the game sample program used by checking the game operations and rules described in each chapter in the textbook.
Based on this sample program, students will then try various ideas and work to create original games. In this class, the Unity game engine is used.

title: メディアデザイン
subtitle: Media Design
educationalGoal:
This course introduces excellent examples of design and art using media technology. Its purpose is to help students to understand how to use media technology in order to create design value. Content examples using XR technology such as VR, AR, and MR are also introduced.

In addition, students will acquire the basic methods of visual expression and interactive expression using graphic software and codes.
advice:
This course introduces excellent examples of design and art using media technology. Its purpose is to help students to understand how to use media technology in order to create design value. Content examples using XR (VR, AR, MR) technology  are also introduced.

Furthermore, students will:

3) Acquire mathematical concepts such as symmetry, the Fibonacci Sequence, and the Golden Ratio, which are the basics of visual expression, and then practice visual expression based on those concepts.

title: 情報セキュリティ
subtitle: Information Security
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will:
(1) Learn an overview of information security technology and its necessity.
(2) Learn basic knowledge of technologies such as cryptography and authentication.
(3) Learn application systems such as antivirus, digital watermarking, and biometric authentication.
advice:
This is a basic course on information security. The following materials will be covered:

1. Information security
 - overview of security technology
2. Cryptographic technology
 - common-key cryptosystem, and public-key cryptosystem
3. Authentication technology
 - hash function, digital signature
4. Security tools
 - client authentication, PKI, PGP, IPsec, TLS, and SSH
5. Application system
 - antivirus, countermeasures for unauthorized access, digital watermarking, and biometric authentication
6. Information ethics
 - ethical issues in information security

title: メディア情報専門実験・演習Ｂ
subtitle: Media Informatics Major Lab/Exercises B
educationalGoal:
This course is separated into following two parts.
The “PC Assembly and Network” part aims to foster the knowledge and skills needed to build a personal computer from parts and construct a simple network.
In the "Physical Computing" part, students are required to create an original system consisting of I/O devices connected to a microcomputer and learn about practical interaction designing.
advice:
"PC Assembly and Network"
 In this part of the course, the following experiments and exercises will be conducted: assembly of a standard desktop PC, configuration of the BIOS, installation of an operating system, assembly of the LAN cable, building and configuring Ethernet networks, connecting to local networks using a HUB, building servers, and troubleshooting.

“Physical Computing”
 The goal of this part of the course is to realize a human-oriented interaction through experiments designed to create many kinds of interactions using I/O devices connected to a microcomputer.
 Students are required to participate actively in the class and engage in teamwork. Safety must be observed at all times. Compliance with scheduled actions and careful treatment of the equipment and tools are also required. All items must be restored to their original conditions when the class is over. Copyright infringement related to class work is strictly prohibited.
 To pass this course, students grade points must exceed 60% for each part. If any point is less than 60%, the student will fail the entire course.
books:
Textbooks: None
Reference books: None
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Students are expected to have fundamental knowledge about PCs, networks, and programming.

Since safety is a top priority, students must follow instructions from supervisors and work carefully during the exercises.

activityGoals.body: Be able to assemble and configure a properly functioning PC based on correct knowledge and handling of the parts
Be able to construct a simple LAN using multiple PCs and hubs.
Be able to give a presentation about your work.
Be able to connect and control a microcomputer and input/output devices.
Be able to create and produce original interaction designs.

title: 画像情報処理
subtitle: Image Processing
educationalGoal:
The objective of this course is to ensure students understand the basic methods used to process digital image data using computers.
Learning Objectives:
1. Students will understand fundamental image processing techniques.
2. Students will be able to make programs that process real digital images and video image data using programming language.
advice:
In this course, students will learn the fundamental digital image processing methods that input, output, and transform digital images. In addition, students will learn to make programs that process real digital images using various fundamental techniques. Lectures and exercises regarding the following items will be given. The outline of the class content is as follows:
(1) Basics of image processing
    History of image processing, light and color, image digitization, image conversion
(2) Fundamental real image processing
　　Image data input/output, image data enhancement, geometric transformation, smoothing/sharpening, Binarization
(3) Programming method to realize various fundamental image processing methods
    Students will learn the skills necessary to make application programs through the creation of works aimed at contributing to the AI information society.
books: Textbooks：ディジタル画像処理 改訂第二版[ＣＧ－ＡＲＴＳ協会],reference books：none,reserved books：none
requiredKnowledge: It is important to use textbooks for preparation and review. The scope of the exam is based primarily on materials presented in the class, so it is necessary to understand the class contents well. If students study the class contents in advance and ask questions on matters than need clarification in the class, they can proceed more efficiently. In image processing programming exercises, it is important for students to review and acquire the presented lessons well.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and explain the basics of digital image processing.
Be able to make fundamental programs that process digital image data and video image data.
Be able to understand binary images, gray images, and color images and then display them.
Be able to understand and explain the manipulation of pixel values of image data, calculation between images.
Be able to understand and explain histograms, contour extraction, and edge extraction from image data.

title: Ｗｅｂアプリケーション

educationalGoal: The primary purpose of this course is to assist students in understanding the development concepts and environments of Web application, and to master the skills needed when administrating Web applications on three-tier system databases. In particular, students will learn database construction and how to make connections between Web applications and their newly constructed databases. Students will also be given the opportunity try to create a Web service that contributes to regional contents like “Cool Kanazawa”.
advice: In this course, students will learn about creating network access to a three-tier model database based on their acquired knowledge of networks, security, and Web programming. The first half of the course consists of lectures based on Chapters 1 to 8 of the assigned textbook and practice involving sample programs. In second half of the course, students will learn about model view controllers (MVCs) and develop Web applications through practice with the device. In the end of the course, students will submit their developed Web applications as reports.

              The primary purpose of this course is to assist students in understanding the development concepts and environments of Web application, and to master the skills needed when administrating Web applications on three-tier system databases. In particular, students will learn database construction and how to make connections between Web applications and their newly constructed databases. Students will also be given the opportunity try to create a Web service that contributes to regional contents like “Cool Kanazawa”.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, students will learn about creating network access to a three-tier model database based on their acquired knowledge of networks, security, and Web programming. The first half of the course consists of lectures based on Chapters 1 to 8 of the assigned textbook and practice involving sample programs. In second half of the course, students will learn about model view controllers (MVCs) and develop Web applications through practice with the device. In the end of the course, students will submit their developed Web applications as reports.

title: メディア情報学統合演習
subtitle: Media Informatics Integrated Exercises
educationalGoal: The goal of this course is to teach students the abilities needed to solve  problems in information society using Media Informatics knowledge and technology. Students are expected to develop the ability to create specialized and advanced systems or contents that consider environmental conservation based on human-centered designs.
advice: In this course, students are given opportunities to comprehensively use the basic knowledge of Media Informatics, including the programming and audiovisual design skills learned in specialized Department of Media Informatics courses, as a means of facilitating communication and knowledge. As part of efforts aimed at learning how to solve problems in the AI information society, students will study R&D methods at companies, after which they will be provided with opportunities to create systems or contents aimed at environmental conservation based on human-centered designs. It is thought that, by developing e-learning contents using Media Informatics, IT knowledge, instructional design theory, and Web programming skills, students will acquire practical skills that are useful in the AI information society.

title: イノベーション基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Innovations
educationalGoal: This course is designed to develop students' ability to discover and solve problems by consolidating the knowledge and skills they have acquired so far, with the creation of value in the real world in mind, leading to innovation. The basic process consists of organizing needs that exist in the real world, finding solutions, and comparing and evaluating cost-effectiveness and alternative solutions.
advice: In this course, students will work systematically in teams to solve real-world problems by integrating them individually or in teams from necessary knowledge, previous experience, and a lot of information. The flow of the process varies depending on the main theme, but basically, team activities proceed in the order of “issue discovery → understanding the current situation (proving the existence of the issue, proving the existence of the need to solve the issue (needs), and understanding existing measures) → determining the issue based on analysis of the cause and structure of the issue → setting preconditions and conditions for achievement toward solution → determining a solution plan”.
books: Textbook not used
requiredKnowledge: Contents acquired through various courses taken by the time of the course. The concept of innovation with an awareness of quality, cost, delivery, and safety in the real world in the basic training course “Engineers and Sustainable Society. In addition, a conscious attitude to awareness and the ability to think freely and creatively are required.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（松下裕研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Matsushita Yutaka)
educationalGoal: This course integrates what has been learned so far. The purpose of this course is to provide students with opportunities to discover problems (e.g., usability, response time) that are involved in the use of digital contents (videos and websites) and to propose solutions. In order to create digital contents useful for people and society, students will not only create digital contents based on the knowledge they have learned so far but will also assess the physiological properties and emotional states of people using the contents.
advice:
Our laboratory aims to teach mastery of the techniques used to effectively edit scenes of videos and to design attractive websites.

In order to create digital contents that people can easily use and enjoy, the assessment of their physiological properties and emotional states is just as important as the technique used to create the contents.

Therefore, aiming to develop a human sensory measurement technology based on data analysis methods and psychological knowledge, students will use their acquired knowledge to create novel digital contents.

Learning Tips:
Students of this course are expected to take a full year to solve the problems that they have raised. To ensure this work progresses smoothly, it is important that their research themes be set properly. Indeed, if students set a research theme to which they are strongly committed, they will be able to devote their energies to acquiring necessary knowledge and deriving new ideas, even when they experience difficulties.

Additionally, although some may feel that bibliographical search and information gathering process are redundant when determining themes, students should be aware that they are extremely helpful for solving related problems.
requiredKnowledge:
Students are required to have completed all the prerequisite subjects of the department.

Students must be able to generalize what they have learned from the first to third year.

Students are expected to have mastered some of the techniques used for creating digital contents or a technique of programming.

Be able to explain contents related to your specialized field.
Be able to deepen insights into "engineer ethics."
Be able apply specialized expertise to the project theme.
Be able to conduct CDIO-based research and development on the set project theme.

title: インダストリアルエンジニアリング
subtitle: Industrial Engineering
educationalGoal: Students understand the basic terms and methods for planning, management, and improvement in this course, and they also learn "Industrial Engineering" methods based on quantification and visualization, and improvements based on data acquisition and analysis. Industrial Engineering methods can be useful for not manufacturing industry but also many other industries.
advice:
This course deals with "Industrial Engineering (IE)" that is maximizing value while minimizing the input of resources such as people, materials, money, and information by clarifying value and waste.
Students learn the basic knowledge, principles, and methodologies of IE with a view to practical application as well as theoretical understanding through classroom lectures. The topics of this course covers so-called work studies such as time studies, motion studies, and process analysis in classical IE, improvement through standardization, statistical quality control methods, and design of experiments in modern IE. After understanding the basic knowledge and principles of these topics, students apply them to simple exercises to acquire practical skills in each classes.
books:
Textbooks: Sinjin IEer to mababu Jissen IE no Kyoukasho (ISBN:9784526081149, Nikkankougyoushinnbunsha)
Reference books: None
Reserved books: Seisan Kanri no Kiso (Rintarou Muramatsu, KunimotoShobo)
requiredKnowledge: Nothing special except logical thinking

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the basic terms of industrial engineering
Be able to apply the basic methods of industrial engineering to a given simple case
Be able to acquire and visualize data for a given simple case using statistical quality control methods
Be able to apply the concept of design of experiments to a given simple case
Be able to define the problem and make a plan to improve it (kaizen)

educationalGoal: This course is a cutting-edge (DX) marketing course that focuses on the concepts, theories, and methods of marketing activities necessary for corporate practitioners and managers learned through the lectures on "Marketing Basics" and "Marketing Strategy" in the Department of Management Systems / Marketing Course. The goal is to learn that you can be implemented and put into practice in society through case studies and field work.
advice:
[Outline of class (how to proceed)]
There are no written tests and quizzes. Case studies (discussion) and learning using cutting-edge (DX) marketing cases as teaching materials
As a corporate practitioner / manager (CMO) even after becoming a member of society through fieldwork (experiment) with a member of society invited from outside
You will learn as a practical practice.
【advice】
○ We ask you to have your own thoughts, not to memorize the whole knowledge.
○ Always pay attention to the latest market and give your own thoughts and interpretations to the movement. At that time, why did you think that way?
We ask you to present it logically.
○ We will place the utmost importance on actively participating in each lesson, expressing one's thoughts during the lesson, and exchanging opinions with other students. Absence / late
・ Poor attitude is strictly prohibited.

title: 先進プログラミング
subtitle: Advanced Programming
educationalGoal:
This course is a specialized core class to achieve the specialized core “Information design basic ability” goal of the Department of Management Information.
Students will learn Python, a general-purpose programming language so that they can create simple tools for data analysis.
advice:
This course deals with data representation and programming basics in AI applications basics.
Students will learn the basics and application of Python by completing several programming exercises.
By writing programs, students will produce a tool that will perform data analysis and then use the tool on open data.
Simply running the program in class is not sufficient; students will need to actually run the program on their own, especially as a means of review.
books: Specify in class.
requiredKnowledge:
Students should have a knowledge of general corporate management and information technology by taking other classes.
It is assumed that students will have an understanding of Web design, IT system basics, database management, programming basics, and applied programming; these topics should be reviewed as necessary.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the basic syntax of Python and do simple programming.
Be able to calculate sequences using Python.
Be able to create a simple graph using Python.
Be able to do simple data analysis using Python.
Be able to explain machine learning using Python.

title: アルゴリズムとデータ構造
subtitle: Algorithms and Data Structure
educationalGoal:
This course is for an educational goal to acquire Information design basic ability.
Students will:
(1)　acquire the basic algorithmic thinking ability to fuse and utilize　management and IT,
(2)　learn the fundamental algorithms which are useful to solve several problems,
(3)　acquire the ability to devise solutions for management organizations aim.
advice:
There is a need for managers and business promoters who understand IT in these days, so that various management functions and IT application systems should be vital for students who are willing to become modern business persons.
Up to now, students have learned web page creation method, IT system basics that enable IT passport acquisition, database construction techniques, hands-on efforts such as dynamic web page creation, and programming with Python. To understand the IT technology used in actual business from a bird's-eye view, it is necessary to solve problems rather than using individual applications. So students should understand algorithms that are methods and means to solve them.
The purpose of this class is to learn the outline of more than a dozen types of algorithms and to acquire the ability to solve problems using algorithms. Specifically, learning of the following ten algorithms that students normally use in an invisible form, they will deepen understanding through the proposal of practical solutions.
(1) Sort, (2) Recursion, (3) Quick sort, (4) Hash table, (5) Breadth-first search, (6) Dijkstra method, (7) Greedy algorithm, (8) Dynamic programming, (9) k-neighbors, (10) cryptography.
One of the purposes of this class is “deeply think about the answer by yourself”, so that students will have a simple assignment at each lecture. In addition, lectures will be held by using Python, students can learn by executing some actual programs.
books: Grokking Algorithms: An illustrated guide for programmers and other curious people, Manning Publications, Manning Publications; ISBN 978-1617292231
requiredKnowledge: It is necessary to have a certain level of knowledge about general corporate management and information technology by taking other subjects: Web design, IT system management, database management, programming basics, applied programming.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and explain information technology in general by learning basic knowledge of IT.
Be able to explain necessity and effectiveness of algorithms used in various information systems.
Be able to explain algorithms being important means and subject of corporate strategies.
Be able to devise and design algorithms to solve problems by yourselves.

educationalGoal:
This practicum in applied business management is a compulsory course for third-year students. In this course, students will: (1) Use the case method to develop the analytical and planning skills needed to formulate a business strategy. (2)
Exploring issues for regional revitalization based on open data analysis. (3) Implement their ideas and exercise their programming skills using Arduino.
advice:
This compulsory course uses the following:
1) Strategy planning in which students will review and analyze the strategies of ‘real’ companies and develop new strategies for these companies. (group activity)
Students will be required to create documents such as a strategic analysis report and devise a new strategic plan.
2Students will develop the ability to grasp problems faced in society structurally and propose logical solutions based on objective evidence by extracting and organizing social issues through basic analysis of social survey data, field surveys, literature research, etc., and repeatedly formulating and verifying hypotheses.
3) Programming for an original system using Arduino. (individual activity)
Students will be required to implement their ideas via Arduino and give a presentation describing the implementation.

title: アカデミックリーディング
subtitle: Academic Reading
educationalGoal:
This workshop-style course aims to foster practical skills for general management.
Students will apply much of what they have learned from their past three years of study, including analytical methods, marketing skills, and information technology, in simple exercises related to business cases.
advice:
This is a course for senior students, providing them an opportunity to brush up on learned skills and prior knowledge by working exercises in workshop style. subtitle: Data Analytics for Business
educationalGoal:
This course provides the principles and practices of basic methods of data science. Students learn data aggregation, regression analysis, cluster analysis, decision tree analysis, and artificial neural networks, which are the basis of recent deep learning.
Students also learn two types of data science tools: KNIME and Python with visual operations.
advice:
In recent years, mathematics, AI, and data science have attracted a great deal of attention of various fields. This course is especially designed for the students who have learned basic statistics. Students learn data aggregation, which is a first-step method of data science, and then learn typical data science techniques such as regression analysis, cluster analysis, decision tree analysis, artificial neural networks.
This course provides both classroom lectures and hands-on analysis exercises with KNIME and Python that are useful and use freeware tools for data analysis. Students learn theories, analytical skills, and some examples of business intelligence, which is considered to be the use of data in actual business.
The instructor expect students to acquire the ability of data analysis trough this class to develop business in the future.

title: システム思考
subtitle: Systems Thinking
educationalGoal: This course is for an educational goal of the Dept. of Management Systems to acquire "Information design basic ability". The environment surrounding us is composed of various things intricately intertwined. Even if systems are observed and analyzed from only one aspect and modeled or made into IT, not only the expected effect may not be obtained, but also new problems may be created. Students will learn not only static modeling, but also components behavior and feedback that change over time.
advice: The events occurring in the world are composed of various things and their relationships intricately intertwined. Students will learn methods to model and analyze dynamically changing structures and relationships, as well as changes and stability of the entire system. First, students will acquire the basic skills to read and understand the data accurately, and perform initial analysis based on practical tasks. Next, students will learn about the stock, flow, and feedback loop as the basic structure and behavior of the system. Then students will learn resilience, self-organization, hierarchy as a function of the system, and concrete the ability to search for intervention places as leverage points.
books:
Thinking in Systems: A Primer, Donella H. Meadows, Chelsea Green Pub Co; Illusrated version (2008/12/3), ISBN: 978-1603580557 (Kindle version is also available)
Factfulness Illustrated, Hans Rosling, et. al., Sceptre (2019/10/3) ISBN: 978-1473637467
requiredKnowledge: To take and earn credits for "System Modeling," which is a second-year class in the Department of Management Information is essential. It is not necessary to take other courses for basic information design skills up to the 1st semester of junior, but it is desirable that you have already taken them. It is also recommended that you will take "Advanced Programming Applications" at the same time.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and explain the basics of systems thinking.

3.Resilience, Hierarchy, Self organization
4.Levalage

              This course is for an educational goal of the Dept. of Management Systems to acquire "Information design basic ability". The environment surrounding us is composed of various things intricately intertwined. Even if systems are observed and analyzed from only one aspect and modeled or made into IT, not only the expected effect may not be obtained, but also new problems may be created. Students will learn not only static modeling, but also components behavior and feedback that change over time.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              The events occurring in the world are composed of various things and their relationships intricately intertwined. Students will learn methods to model and analyze dynamically changing structures and relationships, as well as changes and stability of the entire system. First, students will acquire the basic skills to read and understand the data accurately, and perform initial analysis based on practical tasks. Next, students will learn about the stock, flow, and feedback loop as the basic structure and behavior of the system. Then students will learn resilience, self-organization, hierarchy as a function of the system, and concrete the ability to search for intervention places as leverage points.

title: イノベーション基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Innovations
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn how to apply the concepts for innovation creation by SRI acquired in the Innovation Management course to various social situations. Specifically, the course will be incorporated into training for effective group discussions in job hunting activities.
advice:
In Japan, there is an urgent need to shift from rote learning to problem-finding and problem-solving education. In this context, there are increasing opportunities for elementary, junior high, and high school students to hone their ability to work in groups to find answers to unanswerable questions, including through exploratory activities. The number of students who enter universities through comprehensive selection and recommendations has been increasing in comparison to the number of students who enter through general examinations.
Under these circumstances, in order for students to make a good start in their desired careers, they must not only be able to do group work, but must also have the ability to produce higher results through group activities.
Based on this background, this course aims to help students learn how to apply the concepts for innovation creation by SRI, which they acquired in the Innovation Management course, in various social situations. Specifically, the course will be incorporated into training for effective group discussions in job hunting. In the class, students will actually conduct group discussions as exercises while receiving feedback from other groups and repeatedly making improvements, with the aim of acquiring advanced group discussion skills.
By utilizing videos and AI, students will also deepen their understanding of the evaluator's perspective , and based on this understanding, they will be able to envision their own ideal group discussion and deliverables.

              In this course, students will learn how to apply the concepts for innovation creation by SRI acquired in the Innovation Management course to various social situations. Specifically, the course will be incorporated into training for effective group discussions in job hunting activities.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In Japan, there is an urgent need to shift from rote learning to problem-finding and problem-solving education. In this context, there are increasing opportunities for elementary, junior high, and high school students to hone their ability to work in groups to find answers to unanswerable questions, including through exploratory activities. The number of students who enter universities through comprehensive selection and recommendations has been increasing in comparison to the number of students who enter through general examinations.
Under these circumstances, in order for students to make a good start in their desired careers, they must not only be able to do group work, but must also have the ability to produce higher results through group activities.
Based on this background, this course aims to help students learn how to apply the concepts for innovation creation by SRI, which they acquired in the Innovation Management course, in various social situations. Specifically, the course will be incorporated into training for effective group discussions in job hunting. In the class, students will actually conduct group discussions as exercises while receiving feedback from other groups and repeatedly making improvements, with the aim of acquiring advanced group discussion skills.
By utilizing videos and AI, students will also deepen their understanding of the evaluator's perspective , and based on this understanding, they will be able to envision their own ideal group discussion and deliverables.
