title: 学習・言語心理学
subtitle: Psychology of Learning and Language
educationalGoal: In this course, we will study high-level cognitive processes such as language and learning that support human intellectual activities. Beginning with behavioral learning theory, we will explain the model of knowledge acquisition in cognitive psychology. In addition, we will explain the characteristics and acquisition process of language as a tool for communication and thinking. Based on this knowledge, the goal is for students to be able to improve their own daily activities and apply them to the real world.
advice:
We use language, learn various things from past experiences, and change our behavior to live a smooth life. Language also distinguishes humans from other animals and plays a vital role in various cognitive activities. In this course, we aim to teach specialized knowledge on learning and language that supports our higher level cognitive activities, based on what was learned in previous courses.
Language and learning are associated with various interesting phenomena in our daily lives. I hope the lessons learned in this course will be used to understand the various phenomena experienced in daily life.
Classes will be centered on lectures, but exercises will be introduced as needed to aid understanding.
books: Reference books are indicated in each topic.
requiredKnowledge:
Fully understand basic information on learning, cognition and language learned from previous courses.
Be sure to fully understand the basic operations of a PC, as it may be necessary to perform exercises using a PC.

              学習・教育目標

              1.Respondent conditioning
2.Operant conditioning
3.Situated cognition
4.Language acquisition
5.Phonetics-syntactics-pragmatics

              In this course, we will study high-level cognitive processes such as language and learning that support human intellectual activities. Beginning with behavioral learning theory, we will explain the model of knowledge acquisition in cognitive psychology. In addition, we will explain the characteristics and acquisition process of language as a tool for communication and thinking. Based on this knowledge, the goal is for students to be able to improve their own daily activities and apply them to the real world.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              We use language, learn various things from past experiences, and change our behavior to live a smooth life. Language also distinguishes humans from other animals and plays a vital role in various cognitive activities. In this course, we aim to teach specialized knowledge on learning and language that supports our higher level cognitive activities, based on what was learned in previous courses.
Language and learning are associated with various interesting phenomena in our daily lives. I hope the lessons learned in this course will be used to understand the various phenomena experienced in daily life.
Classes will be centered on lectures, but exercises will be introduced as needed to aid understanding.

educationalGoal: Psychological information processing is grounded in the brain’s electrical activity. This course introduces EEG- and MEG-based brain-informatics approaches to examine the temporal dynamics of psychological processes, focusing on what these methods can and cannot measure. Through studies of neural oscillations and event-related potentials, students develop a foundational perspective on brain-informatics–based psychology.
advice:
This course introduces the basics of brain information science using EEG and MEG to study fundamental psychological processes such as perception, attention, and cognition. Students learn what EEG/MEG can measure and their limitations, the principles of signal generation and data acquisition, and gain perspectives for understanding research on neural rhythms, event-related potentials, and higher-order brain functions.

This course is subject to the course credit system.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students acquire a thorough understanding of psychological information-processing processes such as attention, memory, emotion, and cognitive control, based on brain-informatics approaches centered on electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG), including how these processes are generated and change over time. In addition, they can explain and critically evaluate the potential applications of these approaches to information and interface design that are adapted to human psychological information-processing characteristics, while taking into account the meanings and limitations of indices such as event-related potentials and neural oscillations.
achievementLevels.standard: Students understand the fundamental principles of measurement and analysis using electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) in relation to psychological information-processing processes such as attention, memory, emotion, and cognitive control, and can explain how these indices are associated with specific psychological processes. In addition, students can understand the principles of information design that take human psychological information-processing characteristics into account, based on findings from brain informatics.

title: 心理科学専門実験・演習Ａ
subtitle: Psychological Science Major Lab/Exercises A
educationalGoal:
In the “Questionnaire Method and Survey Practice” component, students will learn a series of processes from questionnaire preparation to surveys and analysis in psychological survey methods.
In the “Observation Method and Elderly Simulation” component, students will practice data collection and analysis in observation methods (including statistical analysis using nonparametric tests) through the experience of elderly simulation.
advice:
Of the major research methods in psychology, this course will focus on questionnaire methods and observation methods. As a comprehensive task of learning results so far, students will conduct complete a research study using these methods. Students form a team, determine the purpose of the survey and the behavior to be observed, set the survey items and performance tasks, collect and analyze the data, make a presentation for each team, and discuss the research results. In addition, each individual student will write a research paper summarizing the entire study.
In the “Questionnaire Method and Survey Practical Training” component, students will learn a series of processes from data collection to analysis, starting with selection of question items, with the aim of acquiring procedures and analysis methods for the questionnaire method.
The “Observation Method and Elderly Simulation” component aims to teach the procedure and analysis method of the observation method and to help students understand the method of hypothesis generation type research. The main objective of observation is human behavior in elderly simulation. Students also practice qualitative data analysis methods obtained by observation methods and statistical analysis using nonparametric methods.
This course requires students to bring a PC to every class. Strictly refrain from being late, taking unauthorized absences, and having an uncooperative attitude toward team activities.
books: none
requiredKnowledge:
Fully understand basic information on learning, cognition and language learned from previous courses.
Be sure to fully understand the basic operations of a PC, as it may be necessary to perform exercises using a PC.

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Questionnaire method
2.Factor analysis
3.Observation
4.Elderly simulation
5.Nonparametric test

              In the “Questionnaire Method and Survey Practice” component, students will learn a series of processes from questionnaire preparation to surveys and analysis in psychological survey methods.
In the “Observation Method and Elderly Simulation” component, students will practice data collection and analysis in observation methods (including statistical analysis using nonparametric tests) through the experience of elderly simulation.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Of the major research methods in psychology, this course will focus on questionnaire methods and observation methods. As a comprehensive task of learning results so far, students will conduct complete a research study using these methods. Students form a team, determine the purpose of the survey and the behavior to be observed, set the survey items and performance tasks, collect and analyze the data, make a presentation for each team, and discuss the research results. In addition, each individual student will write a research paper summarizing the entire study.
In the “Questionnaire Method and Survey Practical Training” component, students will learn a series of processes from data collection to analysis, starting with selection of question items, with the aim of acquiring procedures and analysis methods for the questionnaire method.
The “Observation Method and Elderly Simulation” component aims to teach the procedure and analysis method of the observation method and to help students understand the method of hypothesis generation type research. The main objective of observation is human behavior in elderly simulation. Students also practice qualitative data analysis methods obtained by observation methods and statistical analysis using nonparametric methods.
This course requires students to bring a PC to every class. Strictly refrain from being late, taking unauthorized absences, and having an uncooperative attitude toward team activities.

title: 心理実習
subtitle: Practical Training in Psychology
educationalGoal:
In this practical training, students will learn and understand the following issues through observation and other practical training.
(a) Team approach to those who need psychological support
(b) Multi-professional cooperation and community collaboration
(c) Understanding of professional ethics and legal obligations as a licensed psychologist
advice:
This class consists of off-campus practical training and pre- and post- instruction. Students will learn about the following three main topics through these activities.
(a) Team approach to those who need psychological support
(b) Multi-professional cooperation and community collaboration
(c) Understanding of professional ethics and legal obligations as a licensed psychologist
Practical training will be offered throughout the year. The classes are scheduled for various practical training at six facilities. First of all, in the preliminary study, the instructor will instruct the students on how to prepare for the practical training. Students are required to understand and comply with the code of ethics for licensed psychologists and the rules set for practical training at each facility. If students deviate from these rules, they may be suspended from practical training. In addition, students should research and understand the legal status and characteristics of each facility and its role in the community.
requiredKnowledge:
This course is required to obtain the national certification as a licensed psychologist.
Students must have completed all courses for licensed psychologists offered by the third year.

activityGoals.body: Ability to describe the roles of the staffs involved in providing support, based on their practical experience.
Ability to describe the significance of support through multi-professional and community collaboration.
Ability to be able to give examples of professional ethics and legal obligations as a licensed psychologist.

title: 精神疾患とその治療
subtitle: Psychiatric Disorders and Treatments
educationalGoal: Students will systematically understand the etiology, symptoms, diagnosis (DSM/ICD), course, and treatment methods (including the effects of pharmacotherapy and psychosocial support) of representative mental disorders. They will acquire knowledge of legal systems and social resources related to mental health and welfare, and understand multidisciplinary collaboration in medical settings as well as the role of certified psychologists within team-based care.
advice: This course aims to systematically learn the foundational knowledge regarding “mental disorders and their treatment” required of licensed psychologists. Based on the basic framework of psychiatry and mental health care, it provides an overview of representative mental disorders, covering conceptual understanding, clinical presentation (symptoms and course), approaches and procedures for diagnosis, and the objectives and methods of treatment. Treatment addresses both pharmacotherapy and psychosocial support, and students learn about the physical and psychological changes caused by psychotropic medications, as well as psychotherapy, rehabilitation, environmental adjustments, and the overall support systems that sustain community living. The course is conducted primarily through lectures, using textbooks, handouts, slides, and clinical case examples to deepen understanding (formats such as face-to-face or on-demand vary by university). Students are expected to read the assigned material in advance for each session, organize key points and questions, and attend class prepared. After class, it is important to review by organizing notes and materials and to relate terminology, concepts, and understanding of disorders (classification, diagnosis, treatment, and support). Since quizzes, reports, and worksheet submissions may be assigned, students are encouraged to articulate their understanding based on the lecture content and to actively ask questions both inside and outside of class. In particular, students aiming to become licensed psychologists should study with an awareness of collaboration with medical and related institutions, the role of psychologists in multidisciplinary teamwork, perspectives for supporting individuals and their families, and should also pay attention to systems, social resources, and ethical considerations (such as the protection of human rights).

title: 知覚・認知心理学Ｂ
subtitle: Psychology of Perception and Cognition B
educationalGoal:
Through reflecting the students' daily cognitive activities and connecting them with the theories covered in the class, students will:
- be able to understand the characteristics of human cognitive functions.
- be able to grasp the mechanism of human cognition and thought, as well as impediments to them.
advice:
This course will focus on the contents of cognitive psychology, which is a psychological area that captures human cognitive functions as information processing systems. Cognitive psychology has been developed by using a conceptual device called information processing (using a computer metaphor). Elucidation of human “intelligence” (cognitive characteristics of human information processing) is indispensable for the foundation of the realization of “intelligence” in machines such as artificial intelligence and robotics, which have attracted attention in recent years. Specifically, the following materials are covered.
 (1) Representation of knowledge and processing: (a) Declarative knowledge / Procedural knowledge, (2) Conscious processing and unconscious processing: (a) Attention, (b) Controlled processing and automatic processing, (3) Encoding processes and retrieval processes: (a) Memory, (b) Levels of processing, (c) False memory, (D) Defective memory,(4) Cognitive psychology in the real world.
 The above contents are learned through knowledge internalization (for example, lectures) and knowledge externalization (for example, report). We perform various cognitive activities in everyday life. It is desirable to understand the content of the course while being conscious of cognitive activities in daily life. Also, to deepen understanding of cognitive psychology, it is desirable to take Psychology of Perception and Cognition A that is offered separately.
 * Be sure to bring a computer each time as you will be using the e-syllabus.
This subject is subject to the course credit system.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（田中吉史研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Tanaka Yoshifumi)
educationalGoal: Students carry out psychological research activities, i.e., set their own research questions, collect data, carry out analysis, and prepare reports, while using the knowledge they have learned so far.　Examining phenomena and data from various perspectives, students are expected to be able to discover and organize problems by themselves, and to tackle their own research issues.
advice:
We conduct seminars regularly throughout the year, and students report and discuss their own activities and deepen their own research. When reporting in the seminar, please prepare a resume or slide presentation (submit the electronic file of the resume or slides later).
Spring semester: Reading prior research papers related to the research theme and discussing with class members, clarifying the overall picture of your research. Specifically, the research purpose, research positioning, and methods for empirical data collection are clarified and a research schedule is established. In addition, preliminary experiments/surveys will be conducted. The results will be reported at the interim presentation at the end of the semester.
Fall Semester: Based on the results of preliminary experiments/surveys, modify the plan for the experiments /surveys as necessary, conduct the main experiments/surveys, analyze the results, and deepen the discussion. Students will write a research paper, and give an oral presentation at the end of the year.
books: Reference books and research articles are presented during the course.
requiredKnowledge:
・Prepare a notebook and make a habit of taking notes on the documents. It is not only useful for writing papers later, but it is also very useful for expanding and organizing ideas.
・Review the data collection and statistical analysis methods learned in previous classes.
・To conduct research effectively, familiarize yourself with the specifications of the equipment and teachers in the laboratory.

activityGoals.body: Ability to discuss various problems around us from a psychological point of view.
Ability to choose a research method for the research theme, and conduct experimental design.
Ability to conduct the experiment, and obtain the data to fulfill the purpose.
Ability to interpret the obtained data objectively and write a thesis.
Ability to notice your role in seminar activities, and act in cooperation with other class members.
Ability to draft an action agenda for your future career.

subtitle: Design Project III(Tanaka Koji)
educationalGoal: The aim is to be able to design and propose things and Kotozukuri that are conscious of the cognitive functions by fusing psychology and engineering. The basic policy is to make use of the knowledge of the mind works learned so far and the skills of scientific measurement and evaluation to tackle each theme. Students should always be aware of how human cognitive functions are organically linked to knowledge and behavior related to social life, and tackle your own research agenda.
advice:
Seminars are held regularly throughout the year, and students will report on and discuss the status of each person's activities and research situation. At the end of the previous semester, a department presentation will be held to summarize the activities of the semester. At the end of the academic year, the results of the research will be compiled and presented.
In order to demonstrate superior capabilities in a knowledge-based society, setting appropriate goals for truly unanswered problems and taking action based on beliefs appropriate to those goals and using available evidence (rational thinking) and self-direction to practice them autonomously are important. For maturity of rational thinking skills, we must generalize and learn from experiences of independent activities that deal with problems that are not truly answered. Research activities seem like questions that have no answer. Seminars are conducted as follows: through various proactive, research and laboratory activities, students learn from experience and set the goal of nurturing their ability to continue to grow after graduation. Also, human research hits more walls than you can imagine. For this reason, research activities require resilience (a tough mind). With the goal of fostering resilience, seminars are conducted so that not only successful experiences but also failed experiences can be accumulated.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（川島朋也研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Kawashima Tomoya)
educationalGoal: The goal is to elucidate cognitive mechanisms related to attention and memory and provide basic data for developing practical systems. Students will engage in research projects involving psychological experiments and biological signal analysis to explore human mental processes. This includes deepening psychological knowledge and acquiring experimental planning, data analysis, and reproducibility skills. The research applies cognitive psychology to real-world issues, such as driving and polygraph testing.
advice:
Weekly seminars will be held to report and discuss research progress. Active participation in discussions of other lab members' presentations is also expected, fostering a collaborative approach to deepening insights.

Lab members will be required to thoroughly read papers related to their research topics, acquire specialized knowledge, and clarify the positioning of their own research. Understanding the methodologies of previous studies and developing the ability to apply them to one's own research is essential. In addition, detailed experimental and analytical plans should be formulated and accurately expressed in writing. Based on these plans, experiments should be designed and set up with preliminary reviews among lab members.

Data from key experiments will be subjected to hypothesis-driven and exploratory analyses. The results are discussed and, if necessary, new hypotheses are proposed, leading to further experiments. It is important to approach this whole process systematically and steadily.

              1.Cognitive Psychology

3.Psychophysiology
4.Attention
5.Memory

              The goal is to elucidate cognitive mechanisms related to attention and memory and provide basic data for developing practical systems. Students will engage in research projects involving psychological experiments and biological signal analysis to explore human mental processes. This includes deepening psychological knowledge and acquiring experimental planning, data analysis, and reproducibility skills. The research applies cognitive psychology to real-world issues, such as driving and polygraph testing.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Weekly seminars will be held to report and discuss research progress. Active participation in discussions of other lab members' presentations is also expected, fostering a collaborative approach to deepening insights.

Lab members will be required to thoroughly read papers related to their research topics, acquire specialized knowledge, and clarify the positioning of their own research. Understanding the methodologies of previous studies and developing the ability to apply them to one's own research is essential. In addition, detailed experimental and analytical plans should be formulated and accurately expressed in writing. Based on these plans, experiments should be designed and set up with preliminary reviews among lab members.

Data from key experiments will be subjected to hypothesis-driven and exploratory analyses. The results are discussed and, if necessary, new hypotheses are proposed, leading to further experiments. It is important to approach this whole process systematically and steadily.

              Not required

educationalGoal: In this Web design course, students will learn the concepts behind website construction, including information structure and effective navigation, as part of efforts to impart the knowledge necessary for designing easy-to-read and easy-to-use Web pages. In addition, the characteristics of multimedia material, the use of HTML and CSS, as well as techniques for making Web pages using a laptop computer, will be covered.
advice:
Students are expected to acquire the knowledge and skills of webpage production based on the basic concepts of information design, understand the outline of the World Wide Web (WWW), and master fundamental website creation procedures such as planning, design, production, operation and management through practical training.

title: 色覚・聴覚トレーニング

educationalGoal:
In this course, students will:
(1) Learn human visual and auditory processing within the context of physiology and psychology. (2) Train to be able to discriminate and identify the value, chroma, and hue of visual stimuli. (3) Train to be able to discriminate between slight differences in the frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli. Additionally, train to be able to identify the frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli quantitatively.
advice:
This is a basic skills course for “technical seeing and hearing”.
We will cover the following materials:

1. Human perception processing for visual and auditory stimuli.
2. Training for discrimination or identification of the value, chroma, and hue of visual stimuli.
3. Training for discriminating between slight difference in frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli.
4. Training for identifying the frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli.

The contents of this class are related to “Color Design Project” and “Audio Engineering Project”.

title: コミュニケーションドローイング
subtitle: Communication Drawing
educationalGoal:
Students learn sketch skills as communication tools and visualizing of ideas.
Creators think about products physical objects and dynamic phenomena. In this class, students learn logical freehand drawing skills to represent these objects freely.  In the second half, they will use their acquired skills to conduct emotional expression and communication training and acquire practical skills.
advice:
1. To understand drawing
    Creators think about physical objects and dynamic phenomena and reaction. Drawing methods of them are different. Therefore, students understand each of methods.

2. To acquire drawing skills
   Students learn the logical skills to draw physical objects and dynamic phenomena briefly.

3. Training of using drawing skills
   Students train drawing skills to express and communicate their own ideas each other.

4. Review of student's works
   All students present their own works and get reviews from teachers.

title: コンピュータシステムとＡＩ
subtitle: Computer Systems and AI
educationalGoal: Information technology (IT) and artificial intelligence (AI) are essential elements of modern society, and they are realized by computer systems. In this course, students will learn the structure and operating principles of a central processing unit (CPU), memory, and the input/output units that are the main components of a computer. In addition, students will learn the fundamentals of AI.
advice:
This course covers the following basics of computer systems:

1. Computer components
2. Principles of calculation, instruction execution control
3. Assembler language
4. Configuration of storage devices and memory
5. Calculation methods for performance evaluation
6. Fundamentals of AI
requiredKnowledge:
This is the first course covering the internal structure of computers.
Students should review numerical expressions such as binary.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the components of a computer
Be able to understand programs written in the assembler language.
Be able to explain calculation control.
Be able to understand the configuration of memory.
Be able to understand basic properties of an operating system.
Be able to understand the fundamentals of AI

title: コンピュータグラフィックス演習
subtitle: Computer Graphics Laboratory
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will:

(1) Learn the history of computer graphics (CG).
(2) Gain an understanding of geometric transformation.
(3) Acquire knowledge and basic theory related to modeling.
(4) Acquire knowledge and basic theory related to rendering.
(5) Create CG works about regions.
advice:
This course aims to teach students how to the master basic theory and expression techniques of CG, after acquiring basic knowledge of the field such as the history, systems, intellectual property (IP) rights issue, and so on.

Students will also experientially learn basic theory related to coordinate transformation, modeling and rendering through lectures and practices by using three-dimensional CG (3DCG) software.

A basic outline of the course subjects is provided below:

1. What is CG, History of CG, and Construction of CG System
2. 2D and 3D Coordinate Transformation
3. Modeling
4. Rendering
5. Copyright (IP)
books: none
requiredKnowledge:
Knowledge of geometry learned in junior and senior high school is required.
Knowledge related to physical optics is required.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand history and system of CG.
Be able to understand geometric transformation and create shapes by using it.
Be able to understand the basic knowledge and theory of modeling and express basic shapes.
Be able to understand the basic knowledge and theory of rendering and output realistic image.
Be able to create CG works about regions.

title: プログラミング総合
subtitle: Comprehensive Programing
educationalGoal: In this course, students aim to solidify their C language programming skills and improve their programming thinking skills through exercises that comprehensively utilize the C language programming skills they have learned.
advice:
This course aims to solidify the C language programming techniques learned so far. At the same time, students will also learn and deepen their understanding of applied grammar through lectures and exercises, such as structures, multi-dimensional arrays, and pointers.
Students will also learn about numerical calculation problems such as differentiation and integration.

The learning items are as follows.
- Review of control structures and functions
- Review of pointers and structures
- Applications of arrays (multi-dimensional arrays, etc.)
- Numerical calculations (differentiation, integration, etc.)

Students will practice using the C language development environment on their PC to deepen their understanding.

This class assumes that students have already taken "Introduction to Programming," "Programming I," and "Programming II."
Students will practice using their PC and C language development environment.
Students should thoroughly review the C language grammar and how to operate the development environment.

activityGoals.body: Be able to derive the optimal solution using C programming.
Be able to find and correct mistakes in the program.
Be able to create simple arithmetic programs.
Be able to create practical programs such as numerical calculations.

educationalGoal:
In this course, students will:
(1) Learn the mechanisms for synthesis of sound in a musical synthesizer and automatic performance methods through MATLAB programming.
(2) Learn the physical characteristics of sound and methods for the input or output of sound.
(3) Consider the impressions of sound created by programming.
(4) Discuss application of the contents for regional cooperation.
advice:
In this course, the mechanism for Fourier synthesis in a musical synthesizer and method for automatic performance will be examine based on the knowledge imparted in “Media Informatics I”.

In a part of the course, students will learn and practice how to create sound or music work via MATLAB programming.

Students are expected to review the contents of “Media Informatics I” and other courses related to computer programming.

title: 情報ネットワーク
subtitle: Information Networks
educationalGoal: This course introduces the basic knowledge of information network technology supporting the information society. Students will get an overview of the services provided on the Internet and learn various related communication and security technologies, focusing on the hierarchical protocols essential for realizing the services. Through these, students will  gain an understanding of what the Internet is like and acquire basic network operation techniques.
advice:
Students will learn the basic knowledge related to computer networks as shown below.

1. Basic mechanisms of computer networks
2. TCP/IP hierarchy model and OSI reference model
3. Network service and application layer
4. Transport layer
5. Internet layer and routing
6. Network interface layer and hardware
7. Security
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to have credits of “Information Technology Basic” and “Introduction to Server Management”.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the basic mechanisms of computer networks.
Be able to explain the functions of each layer in the TCP/IP hierarchy model.
Be able to explain the protocol of the application layer that provides services such as Web and email.
Be able to explain the mechanism of data transfer at the transport, internet and network interface layer.
Be able to explain the security technology used on the Internet.
Be able to examine the network configuration using basic network commands and tools.

title: 多変量データの統計科学の基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Statistical Science for Multivariate Data
educationalGoal: In evaluation problems related to humanities and social sciences, many properties must be often handled simultaneously and comprehensively, and multivariate analysis methods can often provide effective solutions. In this course, students will learn the concepts of and ways of using multivariate analysis via Excel functions. The primary goal is to give them the opportunity to master the method of prediction analysis and learn how to summarize multivariate data. Another goal is to ensure they are capable of using these methods in future learning activities.
advice:
The course focuses on the following items:

1. Features and summary of multivariate analysis (prediction and data summarization)
2. The concept and use method of multiple regression analysis
3. The concept and use method of principal component analysis
4. How to use Excel functions

Students are expected to review the basic knowledge of linear algebra. In addition, they should learn the contents of descriptive statistics in “Statistics for Information”. It is also desirable to understand the contents of hypothesis testing.
requiredKnowledge:
Review linear algebra (i.e., matrices and vectors).
Students must be sure to master the lecture contents by reviewing because each item is closely related to previous lessons.

Bring a laptop PC (unless otherwise noted) because the lessons will always include practice sessions using Excel.

activityGoals.body: Be able to use multivariate analysis in future learning activities such as Project Design III.
Be able to distinguish the prediction model concept from the data summarization concept.
Be able to understand the basic concepts and application methods of multiple regression analysis.
Be able to understand the basic concepts and application methods of principal component analysis.

              In evaluation problems related to humanities and social sciences, many properties must be often handled simultaneously and comprehensively, and multivariate analysis methods can often provide effective solutions. In this course, students will learn the concepts of and ways of using multivariate analysis via Excel functions. The primary goal is to give them the opportunity to master the method of prediction analysis and learn how to summarize multivariate data.               The course focuses on the following items:

1. Features and summary of multivariate analysis (prediction and data summarization)
2. The concept and use method of multiple regression analysis
3. The concept and use method of principal component analysis
4. How to use Excel functions

title: 心理学研究法
subtitle: Psychological Research Methods
educationalGoal: This course is designed to help students obtain fundamental knowledge on how to conduct psychological research. In this course we learn about the characteristics and background philosophy of four basic methods (experiments, observation, survey research, interviews) and the ethics of scientific research.
advice:
This course is an introduction to methods of scientific psychological research. Students learn research
methods (experiments, observation, survey research, and interviews) in psychology, and will gain information
on not only technical aspects of each method, but also the philosophical background of each method and the
ethics of psychological research. Classes consist of lectures and exercises on research methods. Students are
required to actively participate in the exercises, understand the characteristics, and be able to apply the
knowledge acquired to their own psychological research.

              This course is an introduction to methods of scientific psychological research. Students learn research
methods (experiments, observation, survey research, and interviews) in psychology, and will gain information

title: 知覚・認知心理学Ａ
subtitle: Psychology of Perception and Cognition A
educationalGoal: The basis of human behavior is information processing. This course focuses on sense perception (the mental process of sensory input) and cognition (the mental process of information processing). The neural basis and neural disorder of sense perception and cognition will also be introduced. In addition, the opportunity to think about how to apply sensory and perceptual knowledge to information design will be provided.
advice:
Lectures will primarily be delivered using slides.
Textbooks of Introduction to Psychology A and B will be used as reference books. Supplementary materials will be distributed for units and charts not included in the reference books.
In addition to lectures, demonstrations and exercises designed to aid understanding of the course content will be incorporated into the lessons.
Please note that the weekly learning content and schedule may be adjusted depending on the progress of the course.
This subject is eligible for the course credit system.

requiredKnowledge: It is advisable to review what you have learned in Chapter 5 of Introduction to Psychology A. If you find anything in the class content difficult, please refer to reference books or books in the Library Center collection, or ask questions directly to the faculty member. Students are expected to approach class with a positive attitude, deepening their understanding of the knowledge they have learned in class by experiencing it through their own senses and perceptions.

title: 心理学基礎実験実習Ⅰ
subtitle: Practice of Elementary Psychological Experiments I
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to understand the concept of experimental psychology and to acquire deeper knowledge of experimental methods to obtain accurate results through exercises of elementary psychological experiments. Students will also learn statistical analysis and evaluation of experimental data and basic skill of writing psychological reports.
advice:
The class will be roughly divided into three terms with a total of five experiments (the themes of experiments are subject to change).
In this class, students participate in the entire process of psychological research using experimental methods, namely conducting experiments (especially experiments on sensation and perception, memory, cognition and social behavior), analyzing the experimental data, and writing paper on the results of experiments. Throughout the semester students will participate in several cycles of research (conducting experiments, analysis, writing reports).
It is very important to have practical experience in conducting experiments, to understand psychological phenomena and to analyze the data, and to acquire skill of writing report. Therefore, marks will be deducted for absence and tardiness.
Students must bring their own PC to every class.
This course is also linked to "Psychological Statistical Methods" and "Psychological Experiments," which are offered at the same semester, so students are expected to gain a deeper understanding of how to conduct experimental research in psychology considering the relationship with the contents of these courses.
books:
Writing Manual of the Japanse Psychological Association.
Other materials will be indicatd in each topic.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of psychology and experimental methods studied in the “Introduction to Psychology” and “Method of Psychological Research”courses in the previous semesters is required.

              The aim of this course is to understand the concept of experimental psychology and to acquire deeper knowledge of experimental methods to obtain accurate results through exercises of elementary psychological experiments. Students will also learn statistical analysis and evaluation of experimental data and basic skill of writing psychological reports.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              The class will be roughly divided into three terms with a total of five experiments (the themes of experiments are subject to change).
In this class, students participate in the entire process of psychological research using experimental methods, namely conducting experiments (especially experiments on sensation and perception, memory, cognition and social behavior), analyzing the experimental data, and writing paper on the results of experiments. Throughout the semester students will participate in several cycles of research (conducting experiments, analysis, writing reports).
It is very important to have practical experience in conducting experiments, to understand psychological phenomena and to analyze the data, and to acquire skill of writing report. Therefore, marks will be deducted for absence and tardiness.
Students must bring their own PC to every class.
This course is also linked to "Psychological Statistical Methods" and "Psychological Experiments," which are offered at the same semester, so students are expected to gain a deeper understanding of how to conduct experimental research in psychology considering the relationship with the contents of these courses.

educationalGoal: Recent research in psychology tends to yield increasingly large datasets obtained through experiments and surveys. Through reflection on previous learning and connecting students with the theories covered in the course, students will:

advice:
This course will focus on two areas of educational psychology and school psychology. Learning educational psychology will help to refine the way of learning and learning school psychology will help improve the quality of learning in school education where students are currently located. title: 認知情報データ解析応用
subtitle: Applied Data Analysis in Psychology and Information Design
educationalGoal: The goals of this course are: 1) to provide students with the basic knowledge to use data analysis software in psychological research, and 2) to apply this knowledge to actual data analysis. In addition, we aim to statistically analyze data from previous psychological research and make socially and scientifically meaningful claims and suggestions. Acquire essential research skills in Project Design III.
advice:
Current psychological research requires researchers to use R software, which allows for a variety of statistical analyses, from basic to multivariate (e.g., regression, factorial).
Students also deepen their understanding of sample size design and power analysis, as well as indicators such as effect sizes and confidence intervals in addition to p-values, and gain the ability to calculate them.
R is so useful that students use it in their Project Design III, but it is difficult to learn how to use. Students should take advantage of office hours and peer instruction.

This course is subject to the course credit system.
books: None

title: 観察法
subtitle: Observational Method
educationalGoal: The observational method is the most basic scientific research method, which involves looking closely at phenomena, especially human behavior in the case of psychology. The observational method is also used in hypothesis-testing research as well as in exploratory hypothesis-generating research. In this course, students will learn the basic concepts of the observation method, how to plan and conduct observations, and how to analyze the data, with practical exercises.
advice:
In this class, the following topics will be studied with practical exercises.
1. Basic characteristics of observation methods
2. Types of observation methods
3. How to perform observation methods
4. Basic analysis methods in observation methods
5. Appropriate interpretation of observation data

In the practical training, teams of several students will be formed to experience the flow of each type of observation method, from setting the research objectives, planning and conducting observations (data collection), to analysis and interpretation.

Since research using observation methods often focuses on the casual behaviors that people take in their daily lives, we recommend that participants in this class pay attention to people's daily behaviors and their characteristics.

The lecture content and schedule are subject to change slightly.
This course is subject to the course credit system.
books: Reference books are introduced in the class.
requiredKnowledge:
Review the basics of observation methods learned in "Research Methods in Psychology".
In addition, it will be helpful to review the knowledge of other research methods learned in previous classes and the methods used to obtain various findings in psychology, in order to understand the characteristics and implementation of the observation method.

activityGoals.body: Ability to understand and to explain the basic features of the observation method.
Ability to understand and to perform the characteristics and implementation of natural observation.
Ability to understand and to perform the characteristics and implementation of experimental observation.
Ability to understand and to perform analysis of observation data based on the time-sampling method.
Ability to understand and to perform analysis of observation data based on the event-sampling method.
Ability to interpret the results of obsabational data analysis appropriately, and to create new hypothesis.

title: 建築情報デザイン
subtitle: Architectural Information Design
educationalGoal:
This course is a higher class of "Architectural CAD" and learns more advanced techniques of creating and managing building 3D model.
Specifically, through learning basic visual programming on CAD, students understand rational, precise, and flexible method of defining and editing the shape of a building (or a part of it) based on rules.
Students should also consider the application and significance of various 3D model creation techniques in a series of processes from design to construction.
advice:
In this course, the lesson will be conducted as the following process.

1st week; Orientation
2nd-4th week; Creation and editing of architectural 3D form using CAD + Visual Programming
5th-7th week; Creating and arranging members using CAD + Visual Programming
8th week; Submission of Assignment 1
9th-12th week; Various techniques of CAD + Visual Programming
13th week; Submission of Assignment 2
14th week; further developing examples of CAD + Visual Programming
15th week; self-check
books: Tutorial movies will be prepared during a course period.
requiredKnowledge: Classes will be conducted assuming that students had some experience using 3D CAD software in fields of architecture.

activityGoals.body: Students can understand the significance and accuracy of 3D data at each stage of building construction process.
Students can understand structural features and ideas from the related documents about buildings.
Students can consider visual programming specifications based on the constitution of the building shape.
Students can efficiently create and edit 3D models using visual programming.
Students can think about the role and potential of visual programming in CAD software.

title: 建築環境設計Ⅰ
subtitle: Environmental Design for Architecture I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn about current conditions and methods for realizing zero-energy buildings.
(2) learn about current conditions and methods for realizing green buildings.
(3) learn about calculation of heat load and cooling coil capability.
advice: As an advanced stage of learning about architectural thermal environment and air conditioning, students will learn about actual examples of human body temperature cold sensation evaluation, methods for calculating residential heat loss coefficients, and on-site condensation checks. Furthermore, in order to realize energy-saving buildings, students will acquire the latest knowledge about national energy-saving standards, the concept of primary energy consumption, and ZEB. In order to learn about regional collaboration, students will investigate energy-saving buildings located in each region. In addition, students will learn the basics of air-conditioning equipment design by calculating the indoor load of a building and the capacity of the required cooling coil through exercises.
requiredKnowledge: Students need credits from Introduction of Building Equipment, Architectural Environment I and II, and Building Equipment.

Building heat load calculations can be done manually.

              Students will:

(3) learn about calculation of heat load and cooling coil capability.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              As an advanced stage of learning about architectural thermal environment and air conditioning, students will learn about actual examples of human body temperature cold sensation evaluation, methods for calculating residential heat loss coefficients, and on-site condensation checks. Furthermore, in order to realize energy-saving buildings, students will acquire the latest knowledge about national energy-saving standards, the concept of primary energy consumption, and ZEB. In order to learn about regional collaboration, students will investigate energy-saving buildings located in each region. In addition, students will learn the basics of air-conditioning equipment design by calculating the indoor load of a building and the capacity of the required cooling coil through exercises.

title: 現代建築論
subtitle: Contemporary Architectural Theory
educationalGoal: Starting with modernism that began in the 20th century, modern architecture has continued to change in various regions and countries. Behind this change are changes in global society and economy, people's lifestyles, values, and philosophies, as well as technological innovations in various fields. Learn how modern architecture has changed and evolved under these influences. In addition, through such learning, students will develop the ability to understand, design, and create architecture from a historical perspective and critical thinking.
advice:

1. What is modernism?
2. Modernist architects and architecture
3. Modernism and Regionalism 1
4. Modernism and regionalism 2
5. Postmodernism 1
6. Postmodernism 2
7. high tech
8. Bubble economy and the end of the 20th century
9. Program and architecture1
10. Program and architecture 2
11. Contemporary Japanese Architecture 1
12. Contemporary Japanese Architecture 2
13. Exam
14. Architect Toyo Ito

title: サステイナブル建築
subtitle: Sustainable Architecture
keywords: Long life and reuse of building
educationalGoal: Learn what sustainable building is based on basic knowledge of architectural planning, structural planning, environment, planning, materials and construction planning. Learn the requirements of sustainable architecture and the means to achieve them. The goal is to be able to set planning, design, construction and maintenance standards for sustainable buildings. Students will also learn about sustainable architecture in cooperation with the local community.
advice:
1. Learn what is sustainable. (Terms, historical background, construction market trends)
2. Learn what building evaluation is. (Overview of building evaluation, evaluation items of various buildings, green buildings in each country)
3. Learn about the elements of sustainable architecture. (Long life, coexistence with nature, energy saving, resource saving / circulation saving, inheritance, etc.)
4. Learn what life cycle management is. (Life cycle cost, facility management, building diagnosis / long-term maintenance plan)

Lectures and case studies based on handouts will be provided. Preparing and reviewing the contents of lectures using handouts to deepen understanding.

title: 建築法規
subtitle: Laws and Regulations of Architecture
keywords: The role of the Building Standards Law and the composition
The harmony with the area (restrictions for grouping)
educationalGoal:
When a building is made in our country, Building Standards Law is set as the standard of the floor to plan for securement of public welfare while respecting the fundamental human rights set as the Constitution of Japan.
The standard which should be considered is set as the environment of the city and the area about an achieved thing, location of the building and the scale, etc. while securing the sanitary society and structure safety about beauty and the function asked from architectural space.
advice:
It's explained about a building code decree and it's made only a point about architects law and a builder law and so on related decree mainly.
Tuition uses a chart and an illustration much and makes an effort toward simple explanation while advancing it by a text "teaching materials for building law" and referring to statute at large.
Further, the knowledge is trained by trying the exercise by which it's for an architect examination question.
The item of the syllabus planning is as follows.
1.The role of the building law, 2. The construction of the construction decree and definition of terminology,
3. Calculation method of the area and the height,4. The general structure and lighting
5. Ventilation and sound insulation, 6. Wooden pillar and wall framing,7. The structural strength and structure calculation, 8.Fire resistive building and quasi-fire-proof building, 9.Restriction on interior finish, 10. Refuge facilities and smoke eliminating equipment, 11. Land use regulation of a building by use zones, 12. Relation between a road and a site building, 13. The building coverage and rate of building volume, 14. Restriction of the height, 15. Sun shadow regulation, 16. Fire-proof district and quasi-fire-preventive district, 17. District plans, 18. Procedure about construction, 19. Registered Architect Law, 20. The city planning law
requiredKnowledge:
Registered Architect Law was revised in March, 2020. Without also passing through business experience about registered architect of the first class as well as the second-class architect test for which you could take an examination immediately after graduation, this change could take an examination now.
A pass trains a possible force with a basic target in a building law test of second class registered architect at this session. A pass also tries a first class registered architect examination question simultaneously with that, and aims at the possible ability in a registered architect of the first class legal test.

title: 建築デザイン総合演習Ｂ
subtitle: Architectural Integrated Exercises for Design B
educationalGoal: This class is the final stage of the architectural design exercise. Understand the function and composition of large public buildings or complex urban spaces, and plan and design them. In particular, at the stage just before Project Design Ⅲ, the goal is to develop a variety of conditions and functions, and to develop creative abilities that can be integrated as plans and design proposals.
advice:
Assignment is design and planning of buildings and cities with special surrounding environment and complicated required functions. The design issues are roughly divided into three issues (see below).
However, in addition to general design drawings, students propose appropriate and attractive expressions using drawings and sentences showing concepts, model photographs, CG, etc.
1) A large-scale building that satisfies the various functions of facilities, such as elementary school buildings and multicultural buildings in central Kanazawa, and that requires attractive architectural spaces. (two assignments).
2) Planning issues for integrated urban design of buildings and external spaces by decoding and re-editing the contexts of cities and towns (two assignments).
3) Renovation of buildings with changing the use of existing public buildings (one asignment).
４）The task of designing the roof of the plaza while learning techniques such as optimization using visual programming (one asignment).

For the first task, you can freely choose one of the four tasks (1), (2), and (3), and for the second task, you can freely choose one from the four options (1), (2), and (4), and create your work.
books: None
requiredKnowledge:
This course is based on basic knowledge of architecture in general and the design ability of architectural design I and II, Architectural Integrated Exercises for Design A.
Students try to apply the knowledge related to the planning and design of architecture and exterior space learned in various classes to the design work.
If you choose Course D in ④ above and have not completed the credits for "Architectural Information Design" in the previous semester, you will need to study visual programming (Rhino+Grasshopper) in advance.

activityGoals.body: Students can analyze the characteristics of the urban area, traditional space, natural environment of location.
Students can develop their ability to organize and design various spaces as architecture and urban space.
Students can analyze the characteristics of the local culture and community and reflect them in urban design.
Students can understand and propose about conversion of existing architecture by renovation project.
Students can work on three-dimensional shape optimization of architectural forms using visual programming.
Students can create and express drawings, models, photographs, and texts as works, and presentate beautifully.

educationalGoal: Students will conduct comprehensive exercises in the structural and environmental fields of architecture. They will learn the technology and design skills to realize living spaces that are environmentally friendly and comfortable, as well as safe and secure.
advice:
Course work for experiments and exercises by learning area:

[Structural experiments]
・Concrete production and compressive strength testing
・Reinforcing bar tensile tests

title: イノベーション基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Innovations
educationalGoal: This course is designed to develop students' ability to discover and solve problems by consolidating the knowledge and skills they have acquired so far, with the creation of value in the real world in mind, leading to innovation. The basic process consists of organizing needs that exist in the real world, finding solutions, and comparing and evaluating cost-effectiveness and alternative solutions.
advice: In this course, students will work systematically in teams to solve real-world problems by integrating them individually or in teams from necessary knowledge, previous experience, and a lot of information. The flow of the process varies depending on the main theme, but basically, team activities proceed in the order of “issue discovery → understanding the current situation (proving the existence of the issue, proving the existence of the need to solve the issue (needs), and understanding existing measures) → determining the issue based on analysis of the cause and structure of the issue → setting preconditions and conditions for achievement toward solution → determining a solution plan”.
books: [Reference book] Curtis R. Carlson and William W. Willmott, Five Principles of Innovation, Diamond (2012).
requiredKnowledge: Content acquired through various courses taken by the time of the course. In particular, the concept of innovation with an awareness of quality, cost, delivery, and safety in the real world in the basic training course “Engineers and Sustainable Society.

              This course is designed to develop students' ability to discover and solve problems by consolidating the knowledge and skills they have acquired so far, with the creation of value in the real world in mind, leading to innovation. The basic process consists of organizing needs that exist in the real world, finding solutions, and comparing and evaluating cost-effectiveness and alternative solutions.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, students will work systematically in teams to solve real-world problems by integrating them individually or in teams from necessary knowledge, previous experience, and a lot of information. title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（川﨑寧史研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Kawasaki Yasushi)
educationalGoal: Students will properly understand the building facility plans and acquire the ability to propose projects by themselves. In addition, students will design a project’s architecture, interior space, and open space, and develop the skills and ability to express these attractively. To that end, students will fully understand proper architectural plans, as well as the design of architecture and space, through their own research and exercises.
advice:
1. 1st semester: Production and expression of architectural planning and space design
Students produce suitable and attractive architectural and spatial design works through participation in architectural planning/design issues and open design competitions.

2. 1st and 2nd semesters: Participation in extracurricular projects
Students will participate in regional collaboration activities such as "Tsukimi Kouro" in the center of Kanazawa City, create space objects and interior designs, and place them in the center of the city to design urban spaces. Through this project, students will gain a sense of scale in urban space and understand the effects of spatial design.

3. 2nd semester: Creating composite architectural works
Based on their project proposals, students plan and design building facilities including open spaces and produce final works. Each work is a culmination of four years of study, and the goal is to satisfy the basic architectural requirements such as for design, planning, structures, the environment, and the city, and to propose attractive spaces and unique designs everywhere.
books:

requiredKnowledge:
Students should review architectural plans and be familiar with the basics of facility planning. They should also always be reading architectural journals and acquire the habit of understanding the latest architectural designs and trends.
Students must actively participate in design activities in extracurricular classes and daily life, and develop design skills by themselves.

Students can design architectures and open space designs that fully consider urban spaces and the environment.

educationalGoal:
Students choose either "work" or "thesis" as the framework for their activities, with the following goals:
(1)In case of "work": Students should propose architectural design with high originality and reasonable logic as "works" based on architectural programming.
(2)In the case of "thesis": Students propose and verify new application methods of technologies such as BIM and xR for architectural design and production, and present them as "thesis".
advice:
1) Students should execute project activities as follows;

In case of "works"; studying theme, investigating architectural works, books, sites, etc., making concepts, planning and schematic design
In case of "thesis"; studying theme, survey of relevant published paper, making concepts, practice & application and analysis of results

2) Students must have a interim presentation and receive evaluation.

3) Students must create of a final report as follows;

In case of "work": organizing the final design proposal and creating drawings and models
In case of "thesis": organizing the process of research and writing the thesis

4) Students must give a presentation at the public presentation review of Design Project III, where they must be evaluated and passed.

educationalGoal: Architecture and cities are required to have various functions for human life. There, environmental comfort is important. The fundamental goal of the lab is to know the psychological response to the physical environment. In this subject, we study the psychological system of human environmental recognition and evaluation. The laboratory aims to contribute to the construction of architectural and urban spaces.
advice:
* Project flow
[1] Rewrite the proposal created during the third grade. Make an oral presentation in the seminar and submit the revised proposal.
[2] To obtain the necessary knowledge for the project, abstract related documents.
[3] Conduct surveys and experiments based on proposals. Use the method appropriate for the purpose of the project.
[4] Hold an interim report meeting twice a year. Create a summary paper in the prescribed format. And give an oral presentation.
[5] Submit a project report and an outline on a fixed date, and give a presentation outside the university at a public review board.

* Unlike general lectures and experiments, there is no fixed methodology. It is necessary to devise original ideas after carefully conducting past case studies. I want you to always have a spirit of challenge.

* Some activities are required during the spring break. If the direction is not fixed by that time, the activities will be delayed later and it will be difficult to reach the ideal level.

educationalGoal: The mission is to increase added value (building added value) in each aspect of building planning, design, construction, and operation, taking into account economic efficiency, productivity, regionality, functionality, and applicability. Under this mission, the project theme can be searched and selected based on the knowledge of the building structure, then the implementation plan, survey, analysis, development, etc. can be implemented based on the theme, and the obtained results are considered.
advice:
◆ Primary semester Acquisition of basic knowledge and setting of project (1) Learn basic knowledge about each activity area. (2) Receive guidance through seminars on whether the theme selected by each person is appropriate for Project Design (1) and complete the project proposal. (3) Investigate, analyze, develop, etc., according to each project proposal.発 表 Announce the results of the previous semester at an interim presentation in the seminar (at the seminar camp).

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（河原大研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Kawahara Hiro)
educationalGoal: The objective of the project is to discover issues related to wood-based materials and timber structures in light of the social background, and to gain new knowledge by collecting, evaluating, and analyzing information. The learning outcomes will be confirmed by compiling the obtained findings into a report and making a presentation.
advice:
[Previous term]
Acquisition of basic knowledge / Project setting / Project execution
1) Learn the basic knowledge of each participant's area of activity.
2) Receive guidance on the appropriateness of their chosen theme for Project Design III through reports in the Plenary Seminar and complete their project proposals.
3) Conduct field surveys, structural experiments, structural analysis, and structural design according to each own project proposal.
4) Present and report the results of the first semester
[Latter term]
Project Implementation / Summary of Project Outcomes
1) Based on the feedback from the presentation of the results of the first semester, continue to conduct field surveys, structural experiments, structural analysis, and structural design.
2) Present the progress results at the interim presentation in the field of building structure.
3) Summarize the results of the entire project and submit a project report.
4) The contents of the project report will be presented at the public presentation review meeting of Project Design III.
books: None
requiredKnowledge: It is necessary to acquire content related to structural mechanics for architecture, building materials, and structural experiments. On the premise of contributing to society, you should be aware of the SDGs and try to gather information for community cooperation on a daily basis.

activityGoals.body: You are able to identify social conditions, discover problems, and imagine ideal conditions.
You are able to conduct the necessary research, experiments, and analyses on a topic of your own choosing.
You are able to summarize the results from your investigations, experiments, and analyses in a project report.
You are able to present the contents of the project report in a logical manner.
You are able to identify and develop your own career path and move forward without regrets as a career path.

[Case studies and analysis / Visualization and structuring of analytical results, proposal development and production of works / Presentation of outcomes (Midterm review in December, Public final review)]

title: 進路セミナーⅠ
subtitle: Career Planning Seminar I
educationalGoal: In addition to measuring the future career and forming a professional view as an engineer, students will set goals and envision advancement/employment plans suitable for themselves, and recognize the voluntary and ambitious actions needed to prepare to achieve those goals.
advice:
The course addresses the following two main issues:
1.	Investigating occupational awareness through lectures by career teachers and senior students, and through internships, open desks, etc., in students' search for the ideal career path.
2.	Planning and beginning to address issues that require a relatively long period of preparation and proactive behavior, such as acquiring qualifications, developing general common sense, and successfully completing the comprehensive aptitude test (SPI).

* Some lectures may be delivered via on-demand video.

title: 情報工学入門とキャリアデザイン
subtitle: Introduction to Information Engineering and Career Design
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)	learn about the connection between engineering and society, as well as the connection between engineering and the local community.
(2)	learn about the history of those technologies and the technologies of the present and future, and clarify their consciousness in relation to becoming an “engineer who thinks and acts independently”.
advice:
This is an introductory course to engineering (Information and Computer Science). We will cover the following materials:
1.	Understanding of the College of Engineering: Students are expected to learn and understand the history of the related fields of the College of Engineering, the role and importance of the current and future fields, and the importance of standardization through lectures by teachers and engineers working in society.
2.	Understanding of the Department of Information and Computer Science: Students are expected to understand the curriculum in the Department of Information and Computer Science (ICS), the expansion of "areas of study", and their relationship with society.
3.	Exercises that foster the ability to think logically about the essence of phenomena and things (scientific skills): Students are expected to understand the role that information engineering has played in society, culture, and history through concrete examples. In order for them to take on such roles, the knowledge and basic skills acquired in the department are important.
4.	Introduction of research fields: Students are expected to understand the contents of the "areas of study" in the department of ICS and research efforts in that area.
5.	Comprehensive exercises: Students engage in exercises and group activities based on their portfolios and the tasks given in classes to date, and then submit the result as reports to confirm them.
books:
Textbooks：Introduction to Computers: Introduction to Information Systems, 8th Edition
Reference books：None
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge: It is important for students to pay close attention to the technologies they are interested in, and then to tackle those subjects proactively and voluntarily so that they can understand the “areas of study” of the department including the past, present, and future prospects of their research fields. They must also formulate learning objectives and learning plans for future specialized subjects, and determine the direction of their success in their future of society.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the role of the College of Engineering in society and make individualized study plans.
Be able to understand research fields of the department, and consider future study methods and course plans.
Be able to explain the mechanism of a computer and the role of programming.
Be able to explain the role of solutions using information technology.
Be able to explain how services provided by information technology work.
Be able to describe their career development process in their own words and communicate it to third parties.

In Programming I (this course) and the subsequent course, Programming II, students will learn how to write programs in Python to accomplish certain tasks. This introductory course covers the following topics.

For (3), students will have a lot of opportunities to engage in hands-on exercises where they can acquire working knowledge of computer programming.

educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn how to store information as “binary data” on computer systems.
(2) Learn logic circuits to understand the behavior of computer systems.
(3) Learn the basic mechanism of processing “machine code” inside computer systems.
advice:
Learn the fundamentals of the configuration and behavior of program-stored computers for base systems of AI and IoT. Understand the function of instructions and concrete operation of computers through circuit design exercises.

title: 論理回路
subtitle: Logic Circuits
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn basic logic circuits consisting of commonly used circuit components.
(2) learn the actions of logical gates and flip-flop.
(3) learn the basic design approach of logic circuits.
advice:
This is the basic course of computer architecture. We will cover the following materials:
1. Characteristics of logical gates.
2. Truth table for given a logic circuit.
3. Simplification of a logic circuit using a Karnaugh map.
4. Circuit architecture and design methodology of encoders, decoders, data selectors, multiplexers, coincidence circuits, binary adders, flip-flops, shift registers, and counters.

Students are required to calculate binary numbers.
Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and characteristics.
Students are expected to understand actions of logical circuits using a logic circuit simulator.
Students are expected to review each course content.
books: Japanese textbook
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of binary arithmetic is required.

activityGoals.body: Be able to calculate positive and negative binary numbers.
Be able to explain the actions of logic circuits consisting of logic gates such as AND, OR, and NOT.
Be able to explain the actions of cascaded decoders.
Be able to explain a data latch mechanism using various flip-flops.
Be able to design an accumulator circuit with adders and general-purpose registers.
Be able to design a shift register and counter circuits with a combination of flip-flops.

              学習・教育目標

              1.Boolean Algebra

              Students will:
(1) learn basic logic circuits consisting of commonly used circuit components.
(2) learn the actions of logical gates and flip-flop.
(3) learn the basic design approach of logic circuits.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is the basic course of computer architecture. We will cover the following materials:
1. Characteristics of logical gates.
2. Truth table for given a logic circuit.
3. Simplification of a logic circuit using a Karnaugh map.
4. Circuit architecture and design methodology of encoders, decoders, data selectors, multiplexers, coincidence circuits, binary adders, flip-flops, shift registers, and counters.

Students are required to calculate binary numbers.
Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and characteristics.
Students are expected to understand actions of logical circuits using a logic circuit simulator.
Students are expected to review each course content.

title: 情報ネットワーク
subtitle: Information Networks
educationalGoal: This course introduces the knowledge and theory of TCP/IP protocols supporting the current Internet, and imparts various related communication technologies to students taking this course. Through this, students will gain an understanding of computer networks such as LAN and WAN to acquire basic skills related to network operations.
advice:
Students will systematically learn the basic knowledge and theories related to computer networks as shown below.

1. Basic mechanisms of computer networks
2. OSI reference model and TCP/IP
3. Physical layer and datalink layer
4. Network layer and transport layer
5. Routing protocol and application layer
books: textbooks, reference books, reserved books
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge and skills (binary number calculation, programming, etc.) related to first-year computer learning are required.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the basic mechanisms of computer networks.
Be able to explain the functions of each layer in the OSI reference model and TCP/IP protocols.
Be able to explain the basic mechanisms of the Internet.
Be able to perform network diagnostics using basic network commands and tools.

achievementLevels.ideal:
By the end of the course, students should be able to explain the following items systematically related to computer networks:

1. Basic information and communication systems
2. OSI reference model and TCP/IP models
3. Physical layer and datalink layer
4. Network layer and transport layer
5. Routing protocol and application layer

Additionally, students should be able to use appropriate network commands and tools for network maintenance and management.
achievementLevels.standard:
By the end of the course, students should be able to explain the basic contents of the following items related to computer networks:

1. Basic information and communication systems
2. OSI reference model and TCP/IP model
3. Physical layer and datalink layer
4. Network layer and transport layer
5. Routing protocol and application layer

Additionally, students should be able to use appropriate network commands and tools for basic network diagnostics.
