title: 知能情報入門とキャリアデザイン
subtitle: Introduction to Intelligent Information and Career Design
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)	learn about the connection between engineering and society, as well as the connection between engineering and the local community.
(2)	learn about the history of those technologies and the technologies of the present and future, and clarify their consciousness in relation to becoming an “engineer who thinks and acts independently”.
advice:
This is an introductory course to engineering (artificial intelligence). We will cover the following materials:
1.	Understanding of the College of Engineering: Students are expected to learn and understand the history of the related fields of the College of Engineering, the role and importance of the current and future fields, and the importance of standardization through lectures by teachers and engineers working in society.
2.	Understanding of the Department of artificial intelligence: Students are expected to understand the curriculum in the Department of Information and Computer Science (ICS), the expansion of "areas of study", and their relationship with society.
3.	Exercises that foster the ability to think logically about the essence of phenomena and things (scientific skills): Students are expected to understand the role that information engineering has played in society, culture, and history through concrete examples. In order for them to take on such roles, the knowledge and basic skills acquired in the department are important.
4.	Introduction of research fields: Students are expected to understand the contents of the "areas of study" in the department of artificial intelligence and research efforts in that area.
5.	Comprehensive exercises: Students engage in exercises and group activities based on their portfolios and the tasks given in classes to date, and then submit the result as reports to confirm them.
books:
Textbooks：Introduction to Computers: Introduction to Information Systems, 9th Edition
Reference books：None
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge: It is important for students to pay close attention to the technologies they are interested in, and then to tackle those subjects proactively and voluntarily so that they can understand the “areas of study” of the department including the past, present, and future prospects of their research fields. They must also formulate learning objectives and learning plans for future specialized subjects, and determine the direction of their success in their future of society.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the role of the College of Engineering in society and make individualized study plans.
Be able to understand research fields of the department, and consider future study methods and course plans.
Be able to explain the mechanism of a computer and the role of programming.
Be able to explain the role of solutions using information technology.
Be able to explain how services provided by information technology work.
Be able to describe their career development process in their own words and communicate it to third parties.

title: 知能情報プログラミングⅠ
subtitle: Intelligent Information Programming I
educationalGoal: The goal of this course is to be able to write and execute basic computer programs in Python which is often used in data science and AI. By completing this course, students are expected to obtain skills to setup an appropriate development environment on their PC, to write basic Python programs, and to execute them.
advice:
In Intelligent Information Programming I (this course) and the subsequent course, Intelligent Information Programming II, students will learn how to write programs in Python to accomplish certain tasks. This introductory course covers the following topics.

  (1) How to install software necessary for developing programs in Python and running them.
  (2) How to edit and save programs written in Python and execute them.
  (3) How to combine basic building blocks of Python to accomplish certain tasks.

For (3), students will have a lot of opportunities to engage in hands-on exercises where they can acquire working knowledge of computer programming.
books: (See Japanese syllabus)
requiredKnowledge:
There is no prerequisite course for Intelligent Information Programming I.

Students have to bring a PC, an AC adapter, and a network cable to the class due to exercises where students are asked to write programs and upload them during class hours for later grading.  It is required to be able to turn on PC, to shutdown PC, and to type on the keyboard.  The network connection permmission is also required until the 3rd week.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain what operations it takes to run a program.
Be able to assign various values to variables, and to use the print function to display their contents.
Be able to write expressions combining properly named variables and operators, and to evaluate them.
Be able to define lists and tuples, and to write programs that use them.
Be able to use control flow structures such as conditional statements and loops in writing programs.
Be able to define functions for relatively simple tasks.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In Intelligent Information Programming I (this course) and the subsequent course, Intelligent Information Programming II, students will learn how to write programs in Python to accomplish certain tasks. This introductory course covers the following topics.

  (1) How to install software necessary for developing programs in Python and running them.
  (2) How to edit and save programs written in Python and execute them.
  (3) How to combine basic building blocks of Python to accomplish certain tasks.

For (3), students will have a lot of opportunities to engage in hands-on exercises where they can acquire working knowledge of computer programming.

title: 論理回路
subtitle: Logic Circuits
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn basic logic circuits consisting of commonly used circuit components.
(2) learn the actions of logical gates and flip-flop.
(3) learn the basic design approach of logic circuits.
advice:
This is the basic course of computer architecture for AI and DS. We will cover the following materials:
1. Characteristics of logical gates.
2. Truth table for given a logic circuit.
3. Simplification of a logic circuit using a Karnaugh map.
4. Circuit architecture and design methodology of encoders, decoders, data selectors, multiplexers, coincidence circuits, binary adders, flip-flops, shift registers, and counters.

Students are required to calculate binary numbers.
Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and characteristics.
Students are expected to understand actions of logical circuits using a logic circuit simulator.
Students are expected to review each course content.

activityGoals.body: Be able to calculate positive and negative binary numbers.
Be able to explain the actions of logic circuits consisting of logic gates such as AND, OR, and NOT.
Be able to explain the actions of cascaded decoders.
Be able to explain a data latch mechanism using various flip-flops.
Be able to design an accumulator circuit with adders and general-purpose registers.
Be able to design a shift register and counter circuits with a combination of flip-flops.

title: 情報ネットワーク
subtitle: Information Networks
educationalGoal: This course introduces the knowledge and theory of TCP/IP protocols supporting the current Internet, and imparts various related communication technologies to students taking this course. Through this, students will gain an understanding of computer networks such as LAN and WAN to acquire basic skills related to network operations.
advice:
Students will systematically learn the basic knowledge and theories related to computer networks as shown below.

1. Basic mechanisms of computer networks
2. OSI reference model and TCP/IP
3. Physical layer and datalink layer
4. Network layer and transport layer
5. Routing protocol and application layer
books: textbooks, reference books, reserved books
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge and skills (binary number calculation, programming, etc.) related to first-year computer learning are required.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the basic mechanisms of computer networks.
Be able to explain the functions of each layer in the OSI reference model and TCP/IP protocols.
Be able to explain the basic mechanisms of the Internet.
Be able to perform network diagnostics using basic network commands and tools.

achievementLevels.ideal:
By the end of the course, students should be able to explain the following items systematically related to computer networks:

1. Basic information and communication systems
2. OSI reference model and TCP/IP models
3. Physical layer and datalink layer
4. Network layer and transport layer
5. Routing protocol and application layer

Additionally, students should be able to use appropriate network commands and tools for network maintenance and management.
achievementLevels.standard:
By the end of the course, students should be able to explain the basic contents of the following items related to computer networks:

1. Basic information and communication systems
2. OSI reference model and TCP/IP model
3. Physical layer and datalink layer
4. Network layer and transport layer
5. Routing protocol and application layer

Additionally, students should be able to use appropriate network commands and tools for basic network diagnostics.

lessons.content:
Overview for information & communication
network (Part 1):
Learn the history of various communication
technologies and protocol standardization.

Review of lecture content
(history of information
network, etc.) and
preparation for Chapter 1
(basic network knowledge)
of the textbook.

lessons.content:
Overview for information & communication
network (Part 2):
Outline network technologies and usage
patterns in recent years and learn about their
relationship with this course.
lessons.assignments:
Review of lecture contents
(current network usage) and
preparation for Chapter 2
(basic knowledge of TCP/IP)
of the textbook.

lessons.content:
Fundamentals of TCP/IP:
Learn the basic principles of TCP/IP networks,
the mechanisms and roles of layering and
encapsulation using the OSI reference model,
coexistence of different models within a
network, and multiprotocol networks.
lessons.assignments:
Review of lecture contents
(OSI reference model and TCP/
IP), and preparation for
Chapter 3 (Datalink) of the
textbook.

Learn about datalink systems, MAC address,
Ethernet, etc.

Review and preparation of
lecture contents
(various datalink systems).

lessons.content:
Datalink (Part 2):
Learn about wireless communication, PPP,
public access network, etc.
lessons.assignments:
Review of lecture contents
(various datalink systems),
and preparation for Chapter 4
(IP protocol) of the
textbook.

lessons.content:
IP protocol:
Learn about IP, IP address (IPv4/IPv6),
routing, IP segmentation and reconstruction.
lessons.assignments:
Review not only the basic
contents of IP and IP address
calculation.

lessons.content:
IP related technologies:
Learn about DNS, ARP, ICMP, DHCP, NAT, etc.
lessons.assignments:
Review of lecture contents
(IP-related technologies)
and preparation for Chapter 5
(Technologies related to IP)
of the textbook.

lessons.content:

Exam or exercises will be conducted to deepen
understanding of the content and exercises
relating to the lectures that have been given
thus far.

Review of the contents of
the lectures learned in the
first half.
Preparation for Chapter 6 (TCP
 and UDP) of the
textbook.

lessons.content:
TCP and UDP (Part 1):
Learn about TCP, UDP, port number, window
control, retransmission control, flow control,
and congestion control.
lessons.assignments:
Review and preparation for
Chapter 6 (TCP and UDP) of
the textbook.

lessons.content:
TCP and UDP (Part 2):
Learn about TCP, UDP, port number, window
control, retransmission control, flow control,
and congestion control. Additionally,
exercises using these protocols will be
conducted.
lessons.assignments:
Review of Chapter 6
(TCP and UDP) and preparation
for Chapter 7
(Routing Protocol) of the
textbook.

lessons.content:
Routing Protocol:
Learn about static routing, dynamic routing,
and routing algorithms such as RIP and OSPF.
lessons.assignments:
Review of lecture contents
(Routing Protocol) and
preparation for Chapter 8
(Application Protocol) of the
textbook.

lessons.content:
Application Protocol:
Learn about the server-client communication
mechanism using the TCP/IP protocol and
actually use various protocols.

Review of lecture contents
(various protocols in
Application layer) and
preparation for Chapter 9
(security) and appendix
(Physical layer) of the
textbook.

in the Internet, its realization technologies
and physical layer.

title: 情報工学特別講義Ⅱ
subtitle: Special Lecture for Information and Computer Science 2
educationalGoal:
“Fundamental Information Technology Engineer Examination (FE)” is known as the gateway to success for new ICT engineers. The FE is divided into the first half and the second half on the test day, and it is necessary to pass both of the examinations at the same day.
Students will learn the basic ICT skills to pass the first half of the FE exam.
advice:
This is a basic countermeasure course to pass the first half of the FE exam. We will cover the following materials:
1. Computer basics
2. Radix conversion and complement
3. Computer components
4. Basic theory of computers
5. OS and middleware
6. System components
7. Multimedia technologies
8. Information Networks
9. Database systems
Students are expected to bring their textbook and other necessary materials to every class.
Students are expected to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class and on a regular basis.
books:

title: 機械系製図Ⅰ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the principles of orthographic projection, which is the basis of mechanical drawing.
(2) learn the ability to accurately create 2D&3D drawings according to the third angle projection method.
(3) practice 2D-CAD&3D-CAD and handwritten drafting to create and edit drawings efficiently.
advice:
Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas.
Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions.
This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings.
We will cover the following topics:
1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons
2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings
3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises
4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures
5. Size tolerance and fit
6. The role of CAE in manufacturing
books:
Textbooks: Mechanical Drawing , Morikita Publishing (in Japanese)
Reference books: None   Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Lectures are “stacked” learning (work on new subjects is based on the knowledge and abilities acquired in the previous week's class). Therefore, students should review the material in the weekly lectures thoroughly and fully understand it by the next lecture. Reference materials and assignment diagrams used in the class will be distributed using the electronic syllabus of this course. A network printer can be used.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the principles of orthographic projection and express the shape of machine parts.
Be able to understand the basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings and draw drawings.
Be able to draw front, top, and side views of machine parts.
Be able to sketch mechanical parts accurately and create hand-drawn mechanical drawings based on these sketches.
Be able to create machine drawings using 2D-CAD & 3D-CAD figure creation and figure editing functions.
Be able to summarize of the role of CAE in manufacturing by obtaining information related to design and CAD.

              授業科目の学習・教育目標

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Orthographic projection method and drafting
2.Handwritten drafting and CAD
3.Sketch drawing of parts
4.Basics of design and drafting
5.Regional cooperation

              Students will:
(1) learn the principles of orthographic projection, which is the basis of mechanical drawing.
(2) learn the ability to accurately create 2D&3D drawings according to the third angle projection method.
(3) practice 2D-CAD&3D-CAD and handwritten drafting to create and edit drawings efficiently.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas.
Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions.
This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings.
We will cover the following topics:
1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons
2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings
3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises
4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures
5. Size tolerance and fit
6. The role of CAE in manufacturing

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Textbooks: Mechanical Drawing , Morikita Publishing (in Japanese)
Reference books: None   Reserved books: None

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              Lectures are “stacked” learning (work on new subjects is based on the knowledge and abilities acquired in the previous week's class). Therefore, students should review the material in the weekly lectures thoroughly and fully understand it by the next lecture. Reference materials and assignment diagrams used in the class will be distributed using the electronic syllabus of this course. A network printer can be used.

title: ロボット基礎力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Engineering Mechanics I
educationalGoal: In this course, students will understand the basic concepts of dynamics (force, moment of force, center of gravity, inertia force, etc.) and acquire basic analytical methods for elementary problems in statics such as the balance of force and moment of force acting on a rigid body, and in dynamics such as parabolic motion of a mass under gravity.
advice:
Mechanics is the basis of mechanical subjects, and the basis of mechanical design and dynamic motion analysis of robots. Dynamics includes analytical mechanics, vibration, material dynamics, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, and quantum mechanics. This is an introductory course for specialized robotics subjects, and it provides a foundation in mechanics and dynamics. This course covers the following basic topics:
1. Power
2. Synthesis and decomposition of force
3. Moment of force
4. Equilibrium of force
5. Center of gravity
6. Movement and force
books:
Textbook: Engineering Mechanics [Corona Publishing]
Reference book: Thinking mechanics [Academic book publisher]
requiredKnowledge:
Many exercise problems require familiarity with the mathematics and physics used in basic engineering.
Acquire the content of this class, which is essential for understanding specialized subjects in the following year.

Understand the concept of force and combined multiple forces, and find any directional component of a force.
Understand the concept of force moments and calculate force moments.
Derive the equilibrium equation of forces and calculate them.
Understand the concept of the center of gravity (or centroid) and find the center of gravity.
Understand the relationship between motion and force and calculate inertial force.

title: 機械系製図Ⅱ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing II
educationalGoal: Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.
advice:
In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises.
In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I".
It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture.
The contents handled in this lecture are as follows.
・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing
・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance
・ Surface roughness   ・ Dimension filling method  ・ Bolts and nuts  ・ Keys and keyways
・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings
・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints
books:
Textbooks: Mechanical Drawing , Morikita Publishing (in Japanese)
Reference books: None   Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
(1) You can draw on the CAD software drawing creation screen. Your ability should be at a level where it is easy to create a model of the text. Basically, items that should have been learned in Mechanical Drawing I (functions written in the text, drawing methods) are not taught in this course.
(2) 3D (3D objects) can be modeled using 3D drafting, the 3rd angle method (2D drafting) and using two-dimensional drafting (plan view, front view, side view). (3) You have mastered the method of downloading materials and uploading reports using the student portal.

activityGoals.body: Be able to transmit a design using mechanical drawing.
Be able to draw a two-dimensional mechanical drawing from a bird's-eye view or a photograph of the machine parts
Be able to imagine the shape of a part drawn from a two-dimensional mechanical drawing created by a third party.
Be able to indicate the machine design, tolerance, and accuracy for the manufacturing method of machine parts.

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.JIS standards and mechanical drawings
2.Mechanical design
3.Manufacturing methods and accuracy/tolerance
4.CAD

              Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises.
In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I".
It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture.
The contents handled in this lecture are as follows.
・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing
・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance
・ Surface roughness   ・ Dimension filling method  ・ Bolts and nuts  ・ Keys and keyways
・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings
・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Textbooks: Mechanical Drawing , Morikita Publishing (in Japanese)
Reference books: None   Reserved books: None

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              (1) You can draw on the CAD software drawing creation screen. Your ability should be at a level where it is easy to create a model of the text. Basically, items that should have been learned in Mechanical Drawing I (functions written in the text, drawing methods) are not taught in this course.
(2) 3D (3D objects) can be modeled using 3D drafting, the 3rd angle method (2D drafting) and using two-dimensional drafting (plan view, front view, side view). (3) You have mastered the method of downloading materials and uploading reports using the student portal.

title: 電気回路Ⅰ
subtitle: Electric Circuit I
educationalGoal:
(1) Learn the foundations of electronics.
(2) Understand the basic concepts of electric circuits.
(3) Acquire the capability to formulate and analyze various phenomena in electric circuits mathematically.
advice:
This is a basic course on electric circuits. We will mainly cover the following topics:
1. Basic concepts of electric circuits
2. Expressing relationships between voltages and currents in DC circuits in mathematical formulas and calculating voltage, current, and electric power in such circuits
3. Expressing transient phenomena in electric circuits consisting of DC power supplies, resistors, capacitors, and inductors in differential equations

Students are expected to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to complete exercises independently.
Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.

title: アルゴリズムとデータ構造
subtitle: Algorithms and Data Structure
educationalGoal:
In order to develop good programs, knowledge about data structures and algorithms is necessary. The objectives of this course are the following:
1. Learning fundamental knowledge about data structures and algorithms.
2. Developing data structure and algorithm selection skills suitable for the problems.
advice:
A data structure is a form in which data is stored in a computer, and an algorithm is a "procedure used to solve a problem" that abstracts a program. In order to write a good program, a good data structure and a good algorithm are necessary. Since multiple data structures and algorithms can be used to solve a problem, students of this course will learn about time complexity, which is a typical index for comparing them. They will also compare multiple algorithms with varying time complexities in these lessons.

The order of the learning contents shown in the lesson schedule is a guideline. Students should follow the instructions of the teacher in charge for additional details. At a minimum, the following contents will be addressed: sort algorithms (basic and advanced techniques, including merge sort and quick sort), basic data structures (array, list, stack, queue, tree, and graph), and search algorithms on graph. Other contents may be added.
books: 「アルゴリズムとデータ構造」（第2版）森北出版株式会社
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge about inequality, polynomial functions, exponential functions, logarithm functions, numerical sequences, and recurrence relation.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand several data structures.
Be able to understand several algorithms.
Be able to judge algorithms from the viewpoint of computational complexity.
Be able to select the best algorithm and best data structure for a given problem.

subtitle: Fundamentals of Computer Architecture
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn data processing using a computer.
(2) Learn computer architecture that define assignments between hardware and software for data processing.
(3) Learn the basic structure and operating principles of a computer.
advice:
This is the basic course on computer architecture. We will cover the following materials:

1.	Data flow and control flow
2.	Instruction set architecture
3.	Pipeline processing
4.	Cache and virtual memory
5.	Embedded processor

Students are required to calculate binary numbers.
Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and characteristics.
Students are expected to understand the actions of logical circuits using a logic circuit simulator.
Students are expected to review the contents of each course.

Be able to show the internal structure of a CPU and explain the calculation process.
Be able to explain the structure of an instruction word in a computer system and addressing mode.
Be able to explain memory hierarchy with some examples.
Be able to explain the characteristic of embedded processor with some examples.

title: ソフトウェアデザイン
subtitle: Software Design
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will achieve the following three objectives:
1) Learn the basic concepts of software design, especially the concept of object-oriented development.
2) Acquire knowledge on a typical software design description language (UML).
3) Learn software design technology through experience from the design to implementation process.
advice:
To develop the software required for an information processing system, it is necessary to analyze the requirements for the system, analyze the system, design the system, conduct system building, software design, software implementation, and system verification, and then perform operational testing.

To understand the importance of software design, it is important to experience it during the system development process.

In this course, students will experience object-oriented development using UML and the Java language. The following main topics will be covered:

1) Object-oriented overview
2) Object-oriented development procedure
3) Analysis, design, and modeling using ULM
4) Program creation using Java

Note: Bring your own laptop computer.
books:

Reference books: None
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Check the following three points learned in 'Programming II' (Java basics) and 'Programming III' (Object-oriented programming). Areas not understood sufficiently must be reviewed.
1) Be able to explain basic object-oriented concepts such as class, method, objects, inheritance, etc.
2) Be able to read and explain the Java source code in the examples.
3) Be able to create and run a simple object-oriented Java program.
4) Be able to program in the Python language and operate SQL databases.

Be able to explain the systems development procedure using UML.

Be able to define classes in the Java programming language.
Be able to explain the terms of a given software testing technique.
Be able to draw the design in UML diagram from program implementation.

title: 確率と統計
subtitle: Probability and Statistics
educationalGoal: Probability and statistics are two of the basic knowledge of science and technology. Machine learning has been attracting attention in recent years, and probability and statistics are the basis of machine learning. In this course, students will acquire basic knowledge of probability and statistics, which are essential in science and technology, through classroom lectures and practical training.
advice:
In this course, you will learn the basic contents of probability and statistics in classroom lectures, and deepen your understanding through computer exercises.
You will use Python for most computer exercises.
The order of the learning contents shown in the course schedule is a guide, and the details will be provided by the instructor. At least the following contents will be included:
1. Probability (dependent and independent, conditional probability, random variable, normal distribution)
2. Statistics (representative values, scatter, correlation, statistical hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, Bayesian inference)
Other contents may be added at the discretion of the instructor.

If necessary, study by yourself during the course period to supplement the programming abilities required to acquire this course.

              Probability and statistics are two of the basic knowledge of science and technology. Machine learning has been attracting attention in recent years, and probability and statistics are the basis of machine learning. In this course, students will acquire basic knowledge of probability and statistics, which are essential in science and technology, through classroom lectures and practical training.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, you will learn the basic contents of probability and statistics in classroom lectures, and deepen your understanding through computer exercises.
You will use Python for most computer exercises.
The order of the learning contents shown in the course schedule is a guide, and the details will be provided by the instructor. At least the following contents will be included:
1. Probability (dependent and independent, conditional probability, random variable, normal distribution)
2. Statistics (representative values, scatter, correlation, statistical hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, Bayesian inference)
Other contents may be added at the discretion of the instructor.

If necessary, study by yourself during the course period to supplement the programming abilities required to acquire this course.

educationalGoal:
In this class, students learn various algorithm design techniques to design efficient algorithms for many complex problems.
Furthermore, students also learn knowledge on hard problems, and algorithmic approaches to such hard problems.
advice:
In this class, students learn various algorithm design techniques, such as, greedy method, divide-and-conquer, and dynamic programming.
Students also learn base of undecidability, i.e., there exists problems that can not be solved by computers. On the other hand, student learn base of intractability, i.e., it is believed that many problems can not be solved in polynomial time.
In spite of such negative facts, students learn some tractable approaches for such hard problems.

title: アルゴリズムとデータ構造
subtitle: Algorithms and Data Structure
educationalGoal:
In order to develop good programs, knowledge about data structures and algorithms is necessary. The objectives of this course are the following:
1. Learning fundamental knowledge about data structures and algorithms.
2. Developing data structure and algorithm selection skills suitable for the problems.
advice:
A data structure is a form in which data is stored in a computer, and an algorithm is a "procedure used to solve a problem" that abstracts a program. In order to write a good program, a good data structure and a good algorithm are necessary. Since multiple data structures and algorithms can be used to solve a problem, students of this course will learn about time complexity, which is a typical index for comparing them. They will also compare multiple algorithms with varying time complexities in these lessons.

The order of the learning contents shown in the lesson schedule is a guideline. Students should follow the instructions of the teacher in charge for additional details. At a minimum, the following contents will be addressed: sort algorithms (basic and advanced techniques, including merge sort and quick sort), basic data structures (array, list, stack, queue, tree, and graph), and search algorithms on graph. Other contents may be added.
books: 「アルゴリズムとデータ構造」（第2版）森北出版株式会社
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge about inequality, polynomial functions, exponential functions, logarithm functions, numerical sequences, and recurrence relation.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand several data structures.
Be able to understand several algorithms.
Be able to judge algorithms from the viewpoint of computational complexity.
Be able to select the best algorithm and best data structure for a given problem.

title: コンピュータアーキテクチャ基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Computer Architecture
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn data processing using a computer.
(2) Learn computer architecture that define assignments between hardware and software for data processing.
(3) Learn the basic structure and operating principles of a computer.
advice:
This is the basic course on computer architecture. We will cover the following materials:

1.	Data flow and control flow
2.	Instruction set architecture
3.	Pipeline processing
4.	Cache and virtual memory
5.	Embedded processor

Students are required to calculate binary numbers.
Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and characteristics.
Students are expected to understand the actions of logical circuits using a logic circuit simulator.
Students are expected to review the contents of each course.
books:

Reference books: Introduction to Logic Circuits (in Japanese)
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of binary arithmetic and basic logic gates is required.

activityGoals.body: Be able to add and subtract values in a computer system using column addition.
Be able to show the internal structure of a CPU and explain the calculation process.
Be able to explain the structure of an instruction word in a computer system and addressing mode.
Be able to explain memory hierarchy with some examples.
Be able to explain the characteristic of embedded processor with some examples.

title: ソフトウェアモデリング
subtitle: Software Modeling
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will achieve the following learning objectives:
  1. Understand the basic concepts of software design, with a focus on object-oriented development.
  2. Gain fundamental knowledge of UML as a software design description language.
  3. Develop practical software design skills through the design and implementation process.
advice:
To develop software for information processing systems, it is necessary to follow a series of processes, including system requirements analysis, system analysis, system design, system construction, software design and implementation, system verification, and operational testing.

In order to understand the importance of software design, students need to gain hands-on experience with design activities as part of the system development process.

In this course, students will learn object-oriented development through practical exercises using UML and the Java programming language. The main topics covered in this course are as follows:
  1. Overview of object-oriented concepts
  2. Object-oriented development process
  3. Analysis, design, and modeling using UML
  4. Program development using Java

Note: Students are required to bring their own laptop computer and the designated textbook to each class.
books:
Textbooks: 実践UMLによるシステム開発ー事例で学ぶ「オブジェクト指向」のシステム設計[工学社]
Reference books: None
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Students are expected to have reviewed and understood the following topics covered in Programming II (Java Basics) and Programming III (Object-Oriented Programming).
  1. Ability to explain basic object-oriented concepts, such as classes, methods, objects, and inheritance.
  2. Ability to read and explain example source code.
  3. Ability to create, compile, and execute a simple object-oriented Java program.
  4. Basic ability to program in Python and to use SQL databases.

activityGoals.body: Explain key terms and concepts related to object-oriented programming.
Describe the system development process using UML.
Understand the meanings of graphical symbols in UML diagrams, and create and use UML diagrams appropriately.
Define and implement classes using the Java programming language.
Explain the terminology associated with representative software testing techniques.
Create UML design diagrams based on program implementations.

  6. Understand representative software testing techniques and

achievementLevels.standard:
By completing this course, students will be able to:
  1. Explain key terms related to object-oriented software
    development and Java programming.
  2. Understand the overall system development process and

  3. Explain the relationship between system development
    components and Java class definitions.

title: 確率と統計
subtitle: Probability and Statistics
educationalGoal: Probability and statistics are two of the basic knowledge of science and technology. Machine learning has been attracting attention in recent years, and probability and statistics are the basis of machine learning. In this course, students will acquire basic knowledge of probability and statistics, which are essential in science and technology, through classroom lectures and practical training.
advice:
In this course, you will learn the basic contents of probability and statistics in classroom lectures, and deepen your understanding through computer exercises.
You will use Python for most computer exercises.
The order of the learning contents shown in the course schedule is a guide, and the details will be provided by the instructor. At least the following contents will be included:
1. Probability (dependent and independent, conditional probability, random variable, normal distribution)
2. Statistics (representative values, scatter, correlation, statistical hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, Bayesian inference)
Other contents may be added at the discretion of the instructor.

If necessary, study by yourself during the course period to supplement the programming abilities required to acquire this course.
books:
「ゼロからはじめるデータサイエンス第２版」，[株式会社オライリー・ジャパン],(2020).
「新版　確率統計」　実教出版
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of mathematics is required. Specifically, you should have a general understanding of the basics of inequalities, equations, elementary functions such as polynomial functions and exponential functions, and calculus.

activityGoals.body: Be able to express your thoughts on statistical information on various events.
Acquire basic probability and statistical knowledge and experience with a view to developing into data science.
Learn the basics of how to handle data and understand the possibility of creating new value from data.
Learn the application examples of probability and statistics, and understand the significance of returning what

              Probability and statistics are two of the basic knowledge of science and technology. Machine learning has been attracting attention in recent years, and probability and statistics are the basis of machine learning. In this course, students will acquire basic knowledge of probability and statistics, which are essential in science and technology, through classroom lectures and practical training.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, you will learn the basic contents of probability and statistics in classroom lectures, and deepen your understanding through computer exercises.
You will use Python for most computer exercises.
The order of the learning contents shown in the course schedule is a guide, and the details will be provided by the instructor. At least the following contents will be included:
1. Probability (dependent and independent, conditional probability, random variable, normal distribution)
2. Statistics (representative values, scatter, correlation, statistical hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, Bayesian inference)
Other contents may be added at the discretion of the instructor.

If necessary, study by yourself during the course period to supplement the programming abilities required to acquire this course.

title: ロボット材料力学
subtitle: Mechanics of Materials
educationalGoal:
Understand how force application to and deformation of a material is important as a basis of the structural design of machines and robots.
Learn step-by-step stress and strain and the deformation of stressed objects, truss structures, and beams by lecture and exercises.
Represent the inner stress caused by external forces as a mathematical model useful for design.
advice:
1. Students will use mathematical tools (matrix, vector, and differential equations) and physical tools (units, force, and moment). In this course, these tools are reviewed and supplemented. Students are expected to review mathematics and physics.
2. Students are expected to work hard on exercises during the class and review them afterward. Students are expected to complete all exercises.
3. Questions should not be left unsolved. Review of basic mathematics and physics is recommended.
books: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials Second edition, Kyoritsu Syuppan (in Japanese)
requiredKnowledge:
Scientific calculator
Linear algebra (vector, matrix, and differential equations)

Draw a stress-strain graph and explain its characteristics and how it reflects deformation
Draw a shear force diagram (SFD) and bending moment diagram (BMD) to improve your understanding
Use load parameters to derive a differential equation of beam deflection
Solve a differential equation for beam deflection

title: ロボット設計演習Ⅰ
subtitle: Engineering Exercise for Robotics I
educationalGoal:
(1) Learn mechanical design skills by designing a microcomputer car in a team environment.
(2) Practice mechanical drawing skills while designing the microcomputer car.
(3) Apply knowledge of mechanical design and machining to an actual robotic system.
advice:
This is a practical course in designing a robotic microcomputer car. We will cover the following topics:

1. Design of a steerage mechanism
2. Design of the structural frame
3. Machining and assembly of parts

Students are required to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to work together on a team to complete tasks in class.
Students are expected to machine some car parts after school hours.
books:
Textbooks:New JIS mechanical drawing(5th edition),Moritika Publishing(in Japanese)
Reference books:None
Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge:
Completion of Engineering Mechanics I and II, Mechanics of Materials, and Mechanical Drawing I and II.
Sufficient skill in plate machining, drill press machining, milling machining, and (lathe) turning.
Students are required to not only have enough skills but also acquire a YUMEKOBO license (Sheet metal working, Drilling Machine, Lathes, and Milling Machine).

activityGoals.body: Understand and explain the major points of the design.
Understand the design process and how to design a microcomputer car.
Make detailed technical drawings compliant with JIS requirements with a computer-aided design system.
Create an assembly drawing and part drawings based on the machining that will be used for manufacturing.

title: 電気回路Ⅱ
subtitle: Electric Circuit II
educationalGoal:
(1) Acquire the ability to mathematically formulate various phenomena in electric circuits.
(2) Solve first-order differential equations to perform DC transient analysis.
(3) Use complex numbers to analyze AC circuits.
advice:
This is a fundamental course in electric circuits. We will mainly cover the following topics:
1. Expressing transient phenomena in electric circuits consisting of DC power supplies, resistors, capacitors, and inductors in differential equations
2. Solving first-order differential equations in electric circuits consisting of DC power supplies, resistors, capacitors, and inductors
3. Using complex numbers to analyze electric circuits consisting of AC power supplies, resistors, capacitors, and inductors

Students are expected to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to complete exercises independently.
Students are required to be aware of the instructor's messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.
books: Introduction to Electric Circuits and Systems (in Japanese)
requiredKnowledge:
Completion of ``Electric Circuit I.''
Sufficient mathematical calculation skills (especially polynomial and fractional expressions).
Basic knowledge of differential calculus.

activityGoals.body: Express transient phenomena with differential equations.
Express relationships among voltage, current, and electric power in DC circuits.
Express relationships among voltage, current, and electric power in AC circuits.
Calculate voltage, current, and electric power in AC circuits using complex numbers.

title: 制御工学入門
subtitle: Introduction to Control Engineering
educationalGoal:
(1) Review complex numbers for frequency response.
(2) Learn Laplace transforms for solving linear differential equations.
(3) Acquire the capability to formulate transfer functions and block diagrams.
advice:
This is a basic course in control engineering. We will mainly cover the following topics:
1. Calculation using complex numbers and Laplace transforms.
2. Solving linear differential equations using inverse Laplace transforms.
3. Obtaining transfer functions from differential equations and block diagrams.
4. Transient response analysis using Laplace transforms.

Students are expected to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to complete exercises independently.
Students are required to be aware of the instructor's messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.

Completion of Engineering Mechanics I/II and Electric Circuit I/II.
Basic knowledge of differential calculus.

Obtain transfer functions from differential equations.

(2) Learn frequency response analysis by using vector locus and Bode plots.

Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.

              This is a basic course in control engineering. We will mainly cover the following topics:

3. Determining stability of a system by Hurwitz stability criterion.

advice:
In “Mathematical Fundamentals of Robotics”, two subjects are designated from the required subjects offered in the same semester as active learning consisting of comprehensive exercises. This course, which can be taken as an elective, is intended to promote your learning skills and to deepen your understanding of the required courses.

              学習・教育目標

              1.Mathematical basics

              Acquire the mathematical knowledge necessary to learn robotics.
Further improve your basic academic ability by participating in lectures and exercises related to the content of other classes offered during the same semester.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In “Mathematical Fundamentals of Robotics”, two subjects are designated from the required subjects offered in the same semester as active learning consisting of comprehensive exercises. This course, which can be taken as an elective, is intended to promote your learning skills and to deepen your understanding of the required courses.

In Mathematical Fundamentals of Robotics II, the exercises for Electronic Circuit and Introduction to Control Engineering/Control Engineering I are carried out every other week. Depending on the level of understanding of students in the course, the content of the lecture and the learning objectives are reviewed, together with the taking of quizzes and completion of exercises.

Summarizing and reviewing the lessons learned in the latter two courses is a preparation and review task for this course.

title: 信号処理
subtitle: Signal Processing
educationalGoal:
(1) Learn the foundations of signal processing, including analog-to-digital conversion.
(2) Understand the basic concepts for digital signals processing, including convolution, Z-transform, sampling theorem, and Fourier analysis.
(3) Acquire the ability to evaluate signals transmitted between linear time-invariant (LTI) systems and to extract the features underlying signals.
advice:
This is a basic course in signal processing for discrete time signals. We will mainly cover the following topics:
1.	Basic concepts of digital signal processing.
2.	Expressing LTI systems with linear convolution.
3.	Expressing discrete time transfer functions using Z-transform and its frequency domain property.
4.	Expressing Fourier series and Fourier transform for continuous and discrete time signals in relation to the sampling theorem.

Students are expected to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to complete exercises independently.
Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.
books: Hitoshi Kiya, Digital Signal Processing (in Japanese), Ohmsha
requiredKnowledge:
Sufficient mathematical calculation skills (especially those covered in Control Engineering I).
Basic knowledge of differential and integral calculus.

activityGoals.body: Explain expressions of discrete time signals obtained by sampling various continuous time signals
Explain the characteristics of transient responses and frequency responses of discrete LTI systems
Explain the Fourier analysis

Students are expected to check for various messages and materials in class.

3. Atomic absorption spectrometry (AAS)
4. Optical emission spectrometry (OES)
5. X-ray analysis
6. Thermal analysis

title: エネルギー固体化学
subtitle: Solid State Chemistry for Energy Conversion and Storage
educationalGoal:
Three general objectives will be addressed in this course:
-Learn about methods to form and analyze solids for energy conversion and storage.
-Acquire the ability to solve problems using the appropriate analysis method.
-Acquire the ability to synthesize and analyze inorganic compounds to fabricate optical, electrical, and magnetic devices.
advice: There will be two quizzes and a final examination during the course. The exercise sheets will be also distributed in the class. All of the exams will be closed-notes and closed-book, although the key equations will be provided on the exam sheets.
books:
Anthony R. West, Solid State Chemistry and Its Applications, Wiley
Peter Atkins, Elements of Physical Chemistry 7th Edition, Oxford University Press
requiredKnowledge:
Student should be familiar with:
1.	Fundamentals of physics and mathematics.
2.	Fundamentals of 1st and 2nd year university chemistry.

activityGoals.body: Understanding inorganic crystal structures.
Understand diffraction methods to determine crystal structures and analytical methods to determine the elements.
Understand the optical, electrical, and magnetic properties of solids.
Understanding the band structure of solids.
Understanding the principles and function of typical optical, electrical, and magnetic devices.
Understanding the role of inorganic solids in energy conversion and storage.

subtitle: Environmental Analysis
educationalGoal: To fully understand environmental issues, such as pollution, that have multiple effects on the global environment, you will learn about the natural environment (air, water, soil) and the circulation of matter in the environment. In addition, you will be able to explain the role of environmental analysis in environmental issues and understand the principles of environmental measurement technology.
advice: To understand environmental issues, such as pollution, that significantly affect the global environment, an understanding of the natural environment (air, water, soil) and the circulation of substances through it are necessary. In this course, you will learn about the natural environment, material circulation, and environmental issues. You will also learn the principles and application of measurement methods used for environmental analyses, especially water quality measurements.

educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) the classification of inorganic materials (ceramics, glasses, and metals).

advice:

educationalGoal: This class provides knowledge about the design of new materials for a sustainable society. After the class, you will understand the properties and functions of bio-productive materials, such as pigments, oils, enzymes, and polymers. In addition, you will also learn about organic polymers that mimic biological functions. In the second half of the class, several life phenomena (protein biosynthesis, cellular stress response, apoptosis, aging, regenerative medicine, and stem cells) are discussed with the function of the related biomolecules.

title: 応用有機化学
subtitle: Advanced Organic Chemistry
educationalGoal: Electronic theories in organic chemistry can help you understand the reactivity of organic compounds in terms of the electron density distribution of atoms and molecules that occur during reactions using in organic synthesis. The courses introduce you to the foundations of the Electronic theory of organic chemistry.
advice:
Course Description and Expectations for Students
The course introduces the Electronic theory of organic chemistry with the following topics:

- Understanding covalent bond from the viewpoint of electronic theory of organic chemistry
- Polarization of organic compounds
- Inductive effect, electrometric effect, resonance effects, and hyperconjugation
- Substitution reaction of hydrocarbons
- Electrophilic and nucleophilic reactions
- Addition to carbon-carbon double bonds
- Elimination reaction
- Rearrangement reaction
- Fundamentals of Molecular Orbital theory
- Radical reactions
books:
教科書および参考書
Required Materials(textbooks, reference books).
Fundamental of Electronic theory of organic chemistry 4th Ed., Minoru Imoto, Tokyo Kagaku Dohjin , in Japanese will be used as a textbook.
requiredKnowledge: All participants should have completed all undergraduate courses of organic chemistry, physical chemistry, and chemical reaction theory with a grade A or better.

activityGoals.body: You should be able to explain the electronic factors that influence organic reactions.
You should be able to design a synthetic scheme for an organic compound using the Electronic theory.
You should be able to explain elimination and addition reaction in terms of the Electronic theory.
You should be able to describe polarization in organic molecules.

              1.Electronic theory of organic chemistry

4.Frontier orbital theory

              Electronic theories in organic chemistry can help you understand the reactivity of organic compounds in terms of the electron density distribution of atoms and molecules that occur during reactions using in organic synthesis. The courses introduce you to the foundations of the Electronic theory of organic chemistry.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Course Description and Expectations for Students
The course introduces the Electronic theory of organic chemistry with the following topics:

- Understanding covalent bond from the viewpoint of electronic theory of organic chemistry
- Polarization of organic compounds
- Inductive effect, electrometric effect, resonance effects, and hyperconjugation
- Substitution reaction of hydrocarbons
- Electrophilic and nucleophilic reactions
- Addition to carbon-carbon double bonds
- Elimination reaction
- Rearrangement reaction
- Fundamentals of Molecular Orbital theory
- Radical reactions

educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) structures, classifications, and properties of biomaterials, such as glycans, lipids, and amino acids.

advice:
Biochemistry of glycans, lipids, and amino acids is very important to the pharmaceutial, food, and chemical industries. In this course, reactions and the mechanisms of enzymes and coenzymes will be presented first. Then, structures, classifications, properties, metabolism, and biosyntheses of glycans, lipids, amino acids and proteins, and nucleotides will be studied.

title: 運動機能論
subtitle: Motor Function
educationalGoal:
This course provides an overview of the neuroscience of:
(1) motor control
(2) learning through motor control of the peripheral and central nervous systems
(3) mind, brain, and health, and the intersection of psychology and cognitive neuroscience.
advice: This course provides an overview of the neuroscience of motor control and learning through motor control of the peripheral and central nervous systems, mind, brain, and health, and the intersection of psychology and cognitive neuroscience. Fundamental biological, psychological, social, and environmental factors are introduced with an emphasis on critical functions related to motor control and animal neuroscience of learning, such as sensitive periods, and neuroplasticity. In addition, factors that facilitate and roadblocks that inhibit optimization of learning are explored as we discuss key cognitive constructs (language, attention, memory, executive functions, brain disorders), with special attention on neurocognitive processes and motor control. These studies will be directly applied by each student in future Project Design III activities conducted in an area of each student’s personal interest.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry is required. High school-level knowledge of biology, and students should have knowledge of basic cell biology, anatomy of human body, and sensory physiology.

activityGoals.body: Describe the basic cellular structures and functions of neurons
Describe the basic signaling process in the brain
Describe the pharmacological approach to brain disorders
Describe the plasticity of brain circuits
Describe motor control in humans
Describe the role of the hippocampus in the short-term memory formation

However, biological technologies are still developing, and often encounter unexpected difficulties in their development. This course will review a range of topics in life sciences, introduce the cutting edge of biological engineering and technologies, and cultivate understanding of the interrelationship between life sciences and human societies.
advice: The lectures in this course are designed for students having knowledge learned in the first and second grade courses including “Basic Biology”, “Structure and Function in Physiology”, “Structure and Function of the Cell”, “Molecular Biology”, “Neuroscience” and “Sensory Information”.

title: 脳科学
subtitle: Brain Science
educationalGoal: Brain science is an integrated study of biology and other scientific disciplines. Therefore, the objective of this lecture is to apply the various knowledge we have learned to the brain. Specifically, based on the premise that the brain is composed of DNA, RNA, proteins, cells, etc., we will continue to study the mechanisms in the brain  that are fundamental for the brain to function. And we want to emphasize that the brain is the only organ that processes information. We are also considering lectures and exam questions and quizzes from this perspective.
advice:
1: What are the shapes and characteristics of the cells that make up the brain? Start by drawing a neuron
2: Understand that there is a molecular basis (i.e., DNA, proteins, their structure and function) that supports brain function
3: There are cells (neurons, glia, and blood vessels) that make up the brain. Understand the role of these cells.　
4: How memory works: how neurons generate electricity.
5: Diseases of the brain: What happens to neurons, will be the final summary of the lecture.
Brain science is built on a foundation of biology.
In other words, it is important for students to have studied the basics of biology in order to understand this class.
In particular, the class will proceed by reviewing the knowledge of "Neuroscience" in the second year and the knowledge of neurons learned in the second year. In addition, students are required to take the first-year course "Structure and Function of Cells" and the second-year course. In addition, the required first-year course "Structure and Function of Cells" and the second-year elective courses "Molecular Biology" and "Cell Biology" will help you understand this course.
books:
Textbooks：Unspecified
Reference HP: https://bsd.neuroinf.jp/wiki/脳科学辞典:索引
requiredKnowledge:
"Brain Science" is an advanced version of "Neuroscience" in the second year. Students are required to review the knowledge of neurons they have learned there, as well as the content they have learned in "Basic Biology," "Cell Structure and Function," "Biochemistry," "Molecular Biology," and "Cell Biology" from the first year.
Review and retrospect the contents learned in "Basic Biology," "Structure and Function of Cells," "Biochemistry," "Molecular Biology," and "Cell Biology" in the second year from the first year.

Explain the basic structure and role of the synapse in the brain function
Explain brain disease
Explain the interaction of neuron and glia

title: 細胞工学
subtitle: Cell Engineering
educationalGoal:
Biology and technology are harnessed to serve many purposes including:
(1)	gene therapies,
(2)	drug therapies, biologics,
(3)	food production and biofuel development,
(4)	understanding the breadth of biotechnology and how it can serve as a research tool.
advice:
This course is designed to acquaint a non-scientist professional with aspects of science as they apply to the biotechnology industry. Biology and technology are harnessed to serve many purposes including gene therapies, drug therapies, biologics, food production and biofuel development.
 Grasping the breadth of biotechnology can be confusing to a student. This is because modern-day research not only studies biological problems in a classical sense, but also puts biological principles to work as research tools.
 Antibodies are an example of a fundamental component of the immune system, yet antibodies are also used as tools by researchers to detect other proteins and are being developed in ways to work like drugs to treat diseases such as cancer. In a wider sense, the inner workings of cells are examined to identify defects in diseases, yet cells are also used to make products like biofuels.
 This course is specifically designed to give an overview of the biotech industry and to teach the scientific principles that apply to numerous biotechnology sectors.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology. Students should have learned basic cell biology.

              Students will:
(1) acquire knowledge of bioinformation and brain science.
(2) learn about life science and evolution
(3) learn about analysis of biological sequences (RNA)
(4) learn basic statistical mechanics for protein structure

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is an advanced course on bioinformatics. We will cover the following materials:

1. Evolutionary significance of biological sequences.
2. Methods of analysis of biological sequences.
3. Methods of analysis of protein structure.

Students will also learn advanced issues, such as stochastic context free-grammars.
Students are expected to understand the basics of bioinformation and brain science.
Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms used in basic bioinformatics and brain science.
Students are expected to solve the exercises independently.
Students should pay attention to the teacher’s instructions in the class since the schedules for quizzes, tests and reports may change as the class progresses.
Students should attend all classes, as the handouts may not be received.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（辰巳仁史研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Tatsumi Hitoshi)
educationalGoal: Dynamic reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton is crucial for a number of cellular processes including cytokinesis, cell motility, and morphogenesis.
advice: Students will attend lectures introducing several research concepts. Dynamic reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton is crucial for a number of cellular processes including cytokinesis, cell motility, and morphogenesis. However, filamentous actin alone is relatively stable, and acceleration of filament disassembly is often required to promote actin cytoskeletal dynamics. ADF/cofilin is one of the major factors to accelerate disassembly of actin filaments by enhancing filament fragmentation and monomer dissociation from the pointed end. However, in vitro studies indicate that ADF/cofilin alone severs actin filaments only weakly and optimally when a cluster of ADF/cofilin molecules bind to an actin filament at low densities. When ADF/cofilin binds to the side of actin filaments at high densities, fragmentation of the filaments is rather infrequent. These biochemical properties suggest that ADF/cofilin alone may not be sufficient to account for rapid turnover of actin filaments observed in live cells. ADF/cofilin is one of the major factors to accelerate disassembly of actin filaments by enhancing filament fragmentation. Tension dependent changes in actin filament fluctuations, and ADF/cofilin molecules bind to an actin filament. It is possible that a mechano-dependent process is involvement in cell re-organization.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology. Students should have learned basic cell biology.

Describe the basic cellular signaling process
Describe basic cellular metabolism
Describe basic cell biology
Describe single molecular imaging
Describe live cell imaging

title: 有機化学
subtitle: Organic Chemistry
educationalGoal: Organic compounds outnumber inorganic compounds in the world around us. However, elements that compose organic compounds are relatively few and the bonding types are simple. The purpose of this course is to learn the fundamentals of organic chemistry, including the classification, naming, characteristics, and reactions of organic compounds. You will be able to predict the properties of an organic compound from its chemical structure.
advice:
This course will cover:
1. Atomic structure
2. Properties of chemical bonds
3. Acids and bases
4. Functional groups
5. Alkanes and alkyl groups
6. Configuration of ethane
7. Cycloalkanes
8. Naming of alkenes and electronic structures
9. Reactions of organic compounds
10. Polar covalent bonds
11. Additions of HX to alkenes
12. Reactions of alkenes
13. Methods for producing alkenes
14. Conjugated dienes and alkynes
15. Electrophilic aromatic substitutions
16. Consideration of regional issues from the view of organic chemistry.
books:
Textbooks: Fundamentals of Organic Chemistry, Japanese 7th edition [Tokyo kagaku dojin]
Reference books: Unspecified
Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Organic chemistry is the basis of biotechnology and applied chemistry. You will need the textbook for this course. Chapters 1 to 6 of the textbook are about organic chemistry, chapters 7 to 12 are about organic synthesis, and the subsequent chapters present concepts of analytical chemistry and biochemistry.

title: 化学と安全
subtitle: Fundamentals of Laboratory Safety
educationalGoal: Experiments play a major role in chemistry education and research. The curriculum for this course places great importance on experimentation and laboratory work. Because chemical experiments often involve handling dangerous substances and equipment, serious injury can result from mistakes in handling, often caused by a lack of knowledge. This course will provide the knowledge needed to perform chemical experiments safely.
advice:
1. Introduction (fundamentals of safety, safety first, Heinrich's law)

title: 化学熱力学
subtitle: Chemical Thermodynamics
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn the physical states of substances and their roles in energy supply.
(2) Learn the relationship between thermodynamics and the information in order-disorder states, the statistics.
Thermodynamics is basic to science and engineering. This course is designed to solve practical problems in chemistry using thermodynamics.
advice:
This is an introductory course for materials science. We will cover the following material:
1. Basic concepts about the phases of substances
2. The behavior of atoms or molecules in gas
3. The first law of thermodynamics (including enthalpy, thermo chemistry, Hess’s law)
4. Second law of thermodynamics (including entropy and Gibbs energy, chemical changes and equilibria)
5. Introduction to statistical mechanics (concepts behind entropy)
6. Units and dimensions in science and engineering (SI system)
Students are expected to bring their textbook and a scientific calculator or personal computer to every class.
Students are expected to check regularly for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website, especially before every class.
books: Elements of Physical Chemistry, 7th Edition, P. Atkins, J. de Paula, and D. Smith, Oxford Universty Press (2020).
requiredKnowledge: Basic calculation skills and a knowledge of SI units.

title: 無機化学
subtitle: Inorganic Chemistry
educationalGoal: Students will learn the basics of inorganic chemistry, such as atomic structure (electron configuration, atomic orbitals), chemical bonding, and crystal structures, and the technical terms used in inorganic chemistry. In addition, students will learn about chemical properties that can be explained theoretically by examining the electronic structure. Concepts and theories acquired in this course are the minimum necessary for understanding the properties and reactivity of inorganic compounds.
advice:
Students will learn essential concepts in modern inorganic chemistry, with the goal of gaining an understanding of the structure and properties of a variety of inorganic compounds without the need for a teacher.

1. Structure of atoms: electron configuration and atomic orbitals, the periodic table and element blocks
2. Chemical bonding and structures: covalent bonding and Lewis structures, ionic bonds, metal bonds, van der Waals bonds, hydrogen bonds; atomic radius and ion radius, lanthanide contraction, Born-Harber cycle, Mardelung constant, metal crystals; ionic crystals (rock salts, cesium chloride types, zinc blende type); ionization energy, electron affinity, electronegativity
3. Reactions: definitions of acid and base (Arrhenius, Brsted-Lowry, Lewis), HSAB
requiredKnowledge: Pay attention to units as you solve calculation problems. Bring a scientific calculator.

activityGoals.body: Describe electron configurations and atomic orbitals for each element on the periodic table.
Explain trends in ionic radius and electronegativity from the periodic table.
Calculate lattice energy using the Born-Harber cycle.
Describe representative crystal structures and their relation to the ionic radius ratio.
Explain the principles of X-ray diffraction and calculate d from θ and reflection index.
Define the different types of acids and bases, including Arrhenius, Bronsted, and Lewis types.

title: 化学反応論
subtitle: Chemistry of Phase and Reaction
educationalGoal:
After completing this course, you will be able to:
1. Explain the foundations of phase diagrams.
2. Explain the theories of chemical kinetics.
3. Perform calculations using chemical kinetics with the thermodynamic concepts.
4. Recognize the value of chemical kinetics in our local and global situation.
advice: Chemistry of Phase and Reactions is a foundation course for School of Applied Chemistry, also highly related to Laboratory course on sophomore and junior. The course is designed to help build a foundation of Chemical Kinetics, Chemical equilibrium, and Phase diagram. Through the course, these foundations will be described from the view of thermodynamics (e.g. the concept of enthalpy, entropy, and Gibb's free energy). At the end of the course, you can solve single answer problems using these foundations.
books:
Textbooks: Peter Atkins and Julio de Paula (2020), Elements of Physical Chemistry Seventh Edition 7th Ed. (In Japanese)
Reference Books: Haruaki Tazaki (2000), Thermodynamics (In Japanese)
Reserved Books in the Library: not applicable
requiredKnowledge: General knowledge of inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, physics, and math are required. B008-01 "Chemical Thermodynamics" with a grade of B or better.

activityGoals.body: You will be able to describe three states of matter and phase shift.
You will be able to explain the foundations of phase diagrams.
You will be able to describe the reaction rate in terms of the Arrhenius equation.
You will be able to determine the effect of temperature on rates using the collision model.
You will be able to Perform calculations using chemical kinetics with the thermodynamic concepts.

title: 環境化学
subtitle: Environmental Chemistry
educationalGoal:
Environmental chemistry deals with chemical reactions on the cyclical changes
and behavior of matter in the environment. You will learn the chemical reactions
related to the behavior of matter and energy in the atmosphere, lithosphere,
and hydrosphere to understand the ecosystem of the hydrosphere. The goal is
to gain an understanding of the limnological environment from published data
and to contribute to the conservation of the aquatic environment.
advice:
1.	Structure of the earth, global energy balance, and greenhouse effect.
2.	Cycles of matter, such as the carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorous cycle in the environment.
3.	Introduction to the aquatic environment and water cycle.
4.	Chemistry of water.
5.	Acidity of environmental water and acid rain issues.
6.	Oxidation and reduction in limnological environments.
7.	Effect of dissolution of substances on water quality.
books: Textbook: Limnological Chemistry, Kaoru Fujinaga (Ed.), Kyoritsu Shuppan
requiredKnowledge: A knowledge of high school level chemistry and biology is required to understand the lectures.

Explain the carbon and nitrogen cycles.
