title: 電気化学
subtitle: Electrochemistry
educationalGoal: Electrochemistry deals with chemical phenomena involving electron exchange. Applications are numerous and include batteries, chemical synthesis by electrolysis, chemical sensors, surface treatment, and metal plating. An understanding of the field requires knowledge of standard electrode potential, the Nernst equation, and other information. Students will learn basic concepts, formulas, and applications such as batteries, chemical synthesis by electrolysis, and metal plating.
advice:
1. Basic concept of electrochemical systems (such as how electrolysis proceeds and electrode interface description)
2. Energy and equilibrium (such as standard Gibbs free energy of formation and chemical potential)
3. Standard electrode potential and the Nernst equation
4. Electrolysis current (relation between potential and current and the dynamics of electrode interface)
5. State-of-the-art electrochemistry (electrochemical STM, solid electrolytes, secondary batteries, fuel cells, solar cells)
requiredKnowledge: A knowledge of units is required to solve calculation problems. Bring a scientific calculator.

activityGoals.body: Explain electrolysis in a simple electrochemical system, such as a water and electrolyte solution.
Determine correctly whether a reaction proceeds spontaneously from the changes in Gibbs free energy.
Calculate standard electrode potential and electromotive force using thermodynamic data and the Nernst equation.
Explain energy conversion between chemical energy and electrical energy.

educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) roles of various substances common to all organisms,
(2) the mechanism of metabolism,
(3) the mechanism of gene expression and cell division,
(4) types of immunity, and
(5) biodiversity and environmental degradation in ecosystems.
advice:
Together with Basic Biology 2, this course provides basic knowledge of biology.

We will cover the following materials:
1. Biomolecules and the chemistry of life,
2. Energy, enzymes, and metabolism,
3. Control of gene expression,
4. The process of cell division,
5. Types and mechanism of immunity, and
6. Biodiversity and the interconnectedness of life.

Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms.
Students are expected to complete exercises independently.

educationalGoal: Human Structure and Function majors can explain how the human body works, based on a deep understanding of the relationship between physiology and anatomy. This is the first course designed to provide foundational knowledge of the human body deemed necessary for discipline-specific courses in neuroscience and brain science. This course introduces not only the proximal factors, but also the ultimate factors of the mechanisms of the human body.

The structure of the organs and tissues that form the body of an animal when observed with an optical microscope is shown, and the organs are composed of various cells using the brain as a subject.
Explain the relationship between how it is built and its functions. If your brain health subsequently fails, for example, take dementia or Alzheimer's disease.
Raise and think about human life.
We will accept questions from students at any time and proceed in an interactive lecture format.

title: 細胞の構造と機能
subtitle: Structure and Function of the Cell
educationalGoal: Cells are important elements of all living things on Earth. Humans, plants and animals, every living organism, is composed of cells. Naturally, if cells are the structural and functional units of living things, there must be something peculiar about them. What is it about cell structure and function that make them so important?
advice:
This course will cultivate understanding of the molecular mechanisms that govern cells, the structural and functional units of living things. The basic cellular processes of organelles and localization, movement, proliferation and signal transduction in cells will be introduced. To cultivate your familiarity of the science behind what we know from modern biology, we will discuss the experimental techniques utilized to study cell structure and function.

The lectures are designed to be interactive. In addition to instructor presentations, we will often break into short discussions about current issues and analyze data. Additionally, students will give feedback in questionnaires given in the classroom on the successes and failures of each lecture in order to continually improve the course.

This course will work on your skills in scientific writing. We will discuss how to read and interpret primary contents of the textbook, and how to construct precise and concise scientific writing.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology.

activityGoals.body: Describe the basic cellular structures
Describe the basic cellular signaling process
Describe basic cellular metabolism
Describe basic cell division
Describe basic cell migration
Describe the application of cell biology in industry

title: 神経科学
subtitle: Neuroscience
educationalGoal: This course is intended for Brain Science majors. The goal of this course is to introduce students to the study of neuroscience. Students will learn fundamental information about cellular biology and the electrophysiological properties of neurons, neuroanatomy, psychopharmacology, and how the activity of neurons can yield sensory perception, motor control, and complex behavioral functions such as learning and motivation.
advice: We will explain the structure and function of neurons (nerve cells), which are the basic units of the brain and nervous system that produce our behavior, and the brain, which is an aggregate of them. We will explain the mechanism of the neural circuit that supports each process from the acceptance of various senses to the integrated processing in the brain and the production of behavior as motor output, including talks at the molecular level. In addition, we will explain the formation and plasticity of the nervous system involved in higher-order functions of the brain such as the development of the nervous system and learning and memory. Rather than simply setting the viewpoint to human behavior, we will learn concretely about their neural basis through neuroethology and comparative physiology, while contrasting with the behavior of other animals. We will accept questions from students at any time and proceed in an interactive lecture format.

title: 微生物学
subtitle: Microbiology
educationalGoal: Humans have been producing various fermented foods, such as bread, liquor, cheese, yogurt, and miso, using microorganisms since ancient times. In recent years, microorganisms have become widely used in the fields of pharmaceuticals, environmental protection, waste recycling, material production, and energy in addition to food. Students will learn about the microorganisms and their various applications.
advice:
It is important to have basic knowledge of microbiology, biochemistry, organic chemistry, molecular biology, gene engineering and protein engineering.

1. Microorganisms: culture and observation
2. Types and cell structure: composition of a typical prokaryotic cell
3. Growth and metabolism: ATP production, nutrition and metabolism
4. Genetic engineering: heredity, repair, mutation, and recombinant microorganisms in biotechnology
5. Function of microorganisms: fermentation, medicine, production of useful substances
6. Environmental protection: current environmental protection and initiatives
books: Microbiology ISBN978-4-7598-1104-9 KAGAKUDOUJIN
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of microbiology, biochemistry, organic chemistry, molecular biology, gene engineering and protein engineering.

activityGoals.body: Ability to explain how to operate laboratory equipment and instruments used to culture microorganisms.
Ability to explain the cell structure, classification, metabolism of a microorganism.
Ability to explain the mutation and transformation of microorganisms.
Ability to explain the effective use of microorganisms, such as environmental protection and energy production.
Ability to explain the relationship between the use of microorganisms and local industries.

              Humans have been producing various fermented foods, such as bread, liquor, cheese, yogurt, and miso, using microorganisms since ancient times. In recent years, microorganisms have become widely used in the fields of pharmaceuticals, environmental protection, waste recycling, material production, and energy in addition to food. Students will learn about the microorganisms and their various applications.

              It is important to have basic knowledge of microbiology, biochemistry, organic chemistry, molecular biology, gene engineering and protein engineering.

2. Types and cell structure: composition of a typical prokaryotic cell
3. Growth and metabolism: ATP production, nutrition and metabolism
4. Genetic engineering: heredity, repair, mutation, and recombinant microorganisms in biotechnology
5. Function of microorganisms: fermentation, medicine, production of useful substances
6. Environmental protection: current environmental protection and initiatives

title: 機械系製図Ⅰ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the principles of orthographic projection, which is the basis of mechanical drawing.
(2) learn the ability to accurately create 2D&3D drawings according to the third angle projection method.
(3) practice 2D-CAD&3D-CAD and handwritten drafting to create and edit drawings efficiently.
advice:
Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas.
Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions.
This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings.
We will cover the following topics:
1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons
2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings
3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises
4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures
5. Size tolerance and fit
6. The role of CAE in manufacturing
books:
Textbooks: New JIS mechanical drawing (6th edition) , Morita Kita Publishing (in Japanese)
 JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Siemens NX ,Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese)
Reference books: None   Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Lectures are “stacked” learning (work on new subjects is based on the knowledge and abilities acquired in the previous week's class). Therefore, students should review the material in the weekly lectures thoroughly and fully understand it by the next lecture. Reference materials and assignment diagrams used in the class will be distributed using the electronic syllabus of this course. A network printer can be used.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the principles of orthographic projection and express the shape of machine parts.
Be able to understand the basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings and draw drawings.
Be able to draw front, top, and side views of machine parts.
Be able to sketch mechanical parts accurately and create hand-drawn mechanical drawings based on these sketches.
Be able to create machine drawings using 2D-CAD & 3D-CAD figure creation and figure editing functions.
Be able to summarize of the role of CAE in manufacturing by obtaining information related to design and CAD.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Accurately understand the third trigonometric method and basic drafting rules used for machine drafting.(2) Accurately understand the basic line types used in machine drawings and their roles.(3) Select the necessary projections by analyzing the geometric features of parts and determine the main projections appropriately.(4) Sketch machine parts accurately, and create hand-drawings based on the sketches.
(5) Understand the size tolerances and surface roughness of machine parts and accurately indicate them in drawings.(6) Gain an understanding of the relationship between design and CAD/CAE, and explain this to a third party by giving a specific example.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Understand the trigonometry and basic drawing rules used to create mechanical drawings. (2) Understand the basic line types used in machine drawings and their roles. (3) Select a necessary projection by analyzing the shape characteristics of a part and determine a main projection.(4) Sketch mechanical parts and make hand-drawn 2D mechanical drawings based on these sketches. (5) Understand the size tolerances of machine parts, the size tolerances of surface roughness products, and the surface roughness, and indicate them in drawings.
(6) Gain an understanding of the relationship between design and CAD/CAE, and explain this to a third party in an easy-to-understand manner.

title: 工業力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Engineering Mechanics I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the basic concepts of the static mechanics.
(2) learn what kind of forces act on the rigid bodies.
(3) learn how to calculate the balance condition of forces.
(4) learn how to calculate the center of gravity.
advice:
This is a basic engineering mechanics course.
We will cover the following materials:
1. Force
2. Synthesis and decomposition of forces
3. Moments of forces
4. Balance of forces
5. Center of gravity of rigid bodies
Students will also learn about advanced issues not included in the textbooks.
Students will be expected to understand the meanings of the terms and formulas.
Students will be expected to solve the exercises on their own.
Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of lectures, quizzes, tests and reports may change as the class progresses.
Students should not be absent from the class, as the handouts may be not received.
books: Textbooks: Kougyou Rikigaku (4th edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.)
requiredKnowledge:
Sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential/integral and vector inner/outcome calculations)
Basic knowledge of mechanics
How to use scientific calculator

activityGoals.body: Be able to indicate the forces on the rigid bodies and to describe their magnitude using SI unit correctly
Be able to synthesize and decompose the forces
Be able to calculate the moments of forces
Be able to formulate the balance of forces and moments of forces and calculate the reaction forces
Be able to calculate the center of gravity for the rigid bodies
Be able to explain the stability of the rigid bodies

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Synthesize the forces acting at the same points and in the different directions.
(2) Decompose the forces in any directions and synthesize the forces acting at the different points and in the different directions.
(3) Calculate the moments of force on the actual rigid bodies.
(4) Calculate local loads on the actual rigid bodies from the balance of forces.
(5) Calculate the center of gravity of the actual rigid bodies.
(6) Evaluate the stability of the actual rigid bodies.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Explain the three elements to indicate the force vectors, and describe the forces using SI unit.
(2) Decompose the forces into the x and y axis and synthesize three forces acting at the different points.
(3) Calculate the moments of force acting on the rigid bodies, and indicate them in suitable SI units.
(4) Calculate the reaction forces at the rotational support points.
(5) Calculate the center of gravity of objects composed of the simple rigid bodies.
(6) Evaluate the stability of the simple rigid bodies.

title: 電気基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn the basic of electronics for a machine engineer
(2) Learn the basic concepts such as electric current and voltage
(3) Learn the principles and the functions such as resistor, condenser and coil
(4) Learn the principle of motor
advice:
This is a basic course in electric engineering.

Step 1: students will understand the concepts as follows,
 electric current, voltage, resistance, electric power, magnetic field, magnetic force, alternating current, electric field
Step 2: students will understand the laws and use them as follows,
 Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's current law, Joule's law, Coulomb's law, Ampere's law, Biot-Savart law, Fleming's law, Faraday's law
Step 3: students will apply them to electric circuits and equipments as follows,
 voltage and current measurement, Wheatstone bridge, heater, temperature measurement, electromagnetic induction, motor, electric transformer, electric storage

Lecture and exercise explanations will be provided on demand as needed.
books: Text book: Introduction to Electrical Engineering, Morikita Publishing (in Japanese)
requiredKnowledge:
Students are required basic mathematical skills.
It is desirable to understand differentiation and integration.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the difference between direct current and alternating current.
Be able to explain the relationship between current, voltage, and power throuhg a resistor.
Be able to explain the functions of a condenser and  a coil.
Be able to explain the principle of a motor.

title: 機械系製図Ⅱ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing II
educationalGoal: Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.
advice:
In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises.
In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I".
It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of computer aided design (CAD) from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture.
The contents handled in this lecture are as follows.
・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing
・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance
・ Surface roughness   ・ Dimension filling method  ・ Bolts and nuts  ・ Keys and keyways
・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings
・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints
In addition, it is necessary to be able to fully understand the design at the actual manufacturing site.
 Copying in drafting drawings is against the ethics of engineers, and credits for this subject are revoked when it is found.

requiredKnowledge:
(1) You can draw on the CAD software drawing creation screen. Your ability should be at a level where it is easy to create a model of the text “Mechanical Drawing”. title: 工業力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Engineering Mechanics II
educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1)Newton's laws of motion.
(2)Motion of mass or rigid body subjected force or torque.
(3)Basics of dynamics.
(4)Inertial forces and other factors necessary for designing high-speed machines.
advice:
Students will learn methods for analyzing the motion of mass points and rigid bodies by solving equations of motion through exercises based on the items. We will cover the following topics:
1. Motion of mass
2. Laws of motion
3. Inertia, centripetal and centrifugal forces
4. Moment of inertia
5. Planar motion of rigid bodies

Students are required to understand these concepts, tackle practice problems, and then cultivate the ability to apply their knowledge to practical problems.
Students are also required to tackle exercises using schematic drawings, and then imagine the application of forces and moments and the subsequent motion of mass points and rigid bodies.
Students are expected to pay attention to significant figures and units.
books: Textbooks: Kougyou Rikigaku (4th edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.)
requiredKnowledge: It is important to try a lot of exercises. A good understanding of high school math and physics is needed. Always use a scientific calculator in class. Students with poor attitudes may be asked to leave and may not be allowed to attend. Recommend using office hours. In addition, the content of this class is indispensable for understanding of specialized subjects in the next year.

activityGoals.body: Be able to build an equation of motion for a mass and calculate its velocity and location.
Be able to explain the laws of motion and calculate inertial, centripetal and centrifugal forces.
Be able to calculate the moment of inertia.
Be able to build equations of motion or machine models.
Be able to solve equations of motion by applying mathematics

              学習・教育目標

              1.Motion of mass

              Students will learn:
(1)Newton's laws of motion.
(2)Motion of mass or rigid body subjected force or torque.
(3)Basics of dynamics.
(4)Inertial forces and other factors necessary for designing high-speed machines.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Students will learn methods for analyzing the motion of mass points and rigid bodies by solving equations of motion through exercises based on the items. We will cover the following topics:
1. Motion of mass
2. Laws of motion
3. Inertia, centripetal and centrifugal forces
4. Moment of inertia
5. Planar motion of rigid bodies

Students are required to understand these concepts, tackle practice problems, and then cultivate the ability to apply their knowledge to practical problems.
Students are also required to tackle exercises using schematic drawings, and then imagine the application of forces and moments and the subsequent motion of mass points and rigid bodies.
Students are expected to pay attention to significant figures and units.

              Textbooks: Kougyou Rikigaku (4th edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.)

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              It is important to try a lot of exercises. A good understanding of high school math and physics is needed. Always use a scientific calculator in class. Students with poor attitudes may be asked to leave and may not be allowed to attend. Recommend using office hours. title: 材料力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Strength of Materials I
educationalGoal: Investigating the strength of materials can clarify the forces that act on various parts of bridges, steel towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, living tissues and cells, etc., and the deformations they cause. The results can be used for safety design. It is therefore a foundational subject in mechanical engineering. In this course, students will gain a thorough understanding of the investigation of the strength of materials through lectures and practice.
advice:
This is a basic strength of materials course. We will cover the following topics:

1. Stress and strain                                     6. Statically indeterminate problems
2. Hooke’s law                                           7. Thermal stress and stress concentration
3. Mechanical properties of materials        8. Thin-walled cylinders subjected to internal pressure
4. Allowable stress and safety factors        9. Beams and their support conditions
5. Frame structure                                   10. Shearing forces and bending moments of beams

In this course, it is important to do many practice exercises, but the study of the strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand just by memorizing formulas and patterns. To solve a problem, one should start with an understanding of the basic formulas needed, and then set the appropriate boundary conditions for the problem. In addition, it is necessary to be able to concretely imagine the actual forces, moments, and deformations using schematic diagrams.
Furthermore, students should work on issues related to local companies, and deepen their understanding of the relationship between the strength of materials and society/technology. Lecture and exercise explanations will be provided on demand as needed.
books:
Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: Basic Strength of Materials, Morikita Publishing Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Gaining understanding by working through many different problems is the best way to learn strength of materials. As a prerequisite, it is necessary to fully understand "Industrial Mechanics I". In addition, students will be expected to move on to "Strength of Materials II" and "Strength of Materials III", which will be offered subsequently, as they are applications of this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the concept of normal stress, shear stress, normal strain, shear strain, and Hooke's law.
Be able to explain the deformation and fracture behavior of materials by drawing stress-strain characteristics.
Be able to explain the relationship between material properties, reference strength, and the allowable stress.
Be able to explain the frame structure, thermal stress, thin-walled cylinders and stress concentration.
Be able to explain the shearing force and bending moment generated in a beam by drawing SFDs and BMDs.
Be able to explain the relationship between strength of materials and society/technology.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1. Understand the concept of stress and strain.
2. Distinguish the nominal stress and true stress, nominal strain and true strain.
3. Design safe structures using standard strength and allowable stress.
4. Design safe structures in frame structures, thermal stress problems, a thin-walled cylinder subject to internal pressure.
5 Draw SFDs and BMDs for various beams loaded with a concentrated load and an equally distributed load.
6. Understand in depth the relationship between the strength of materials and society/technology.
achievementLevels.standard:
1. Calculate stresses and strains.
2. Perform calculations on the basis of safety factors.
3. Calculate stresses in a frame structure and a thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure, and in a thermal stress problem.
4. Draw SFDs and BMDs of a cantilever beam and a simple support beam loaded with a concentrated load and an equally distributed load.
5. Understand the relationship between strength of materials and society/technology.

title: 材料科学Ⅰ
subtitle: Materials Science I
educationalGoal: In this course, we will give an overview of the industrial materials and learn the basics of the relationship between structure and physical and chemical properties, as well as methods for evaluating the characteristics of materials.
advice:
The outline of the class is as follows:

Classification of machine materials and characteristics of metals, plastics, and ceramics
Structure of materials
Basics of crystallography
Theoretical strength and crystallographic dislocations in materials, resolved shear stress, and dislocation and deformation of a single crystal
Plastic deformation of materials
Materials evaluation, tensile test, stress versus strain curves, and hardness test
Phase transition of metals
books:
Textbooks:
Reference books:
Reserved books:
requiredKnowledge:
Understand the basics of trigonometric functions, exponential functions, logarithmic functions, and vectors.
Memorize the elemental symbols, such as those for carbon, magnesium, aluminum, titanium, iron, and copper, related to materials science.
Regarding material structure, it is desirable to have knowledge of high school chemistry.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain basic characteristics of metals, plastics, and ceramics.
Be able to explain types, features, and examples of atomic bonds.
Be able to explain the basics of crystallography (especially Bravais lattice and Miller index).
Be able to explain the difference between elastic and plastic deformation based on materials science.
Be able to explain basics of materials evaluation.
Be able to explain the relationship between equilibrium phase diagram and phase formation.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1: Explain the relationship between typical practical materials and specific applications.
2 & 3: Explain the crystal structure and physical and chemical characteristics of typical pure materials.
4: Explain the phenomena caused by elastic or plastic deformation (for example, slip and twinning deformation) using a crystallographic viewpoint.
5: Propose an appropriate material evaluation test method.
6: Explain phase rate and microstructure at a particular point.
achievementLevels.standard:
1: Explain the characteristics used to measure practical materials and their physical properties (such as Young’s modulus and melting point).
2: Explain the bond types in pure substances and their characteristics.
3: Illustrate crystal planes and directions.
4: Explain the deformation process of mild steel using the stress versus strain curve.
5: Explain material evaluation test methods (for example, tensile test and hardness test) and data processing.

title: 機械力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Dynamics of Machines I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)	learn the kinematics of rigid bodies when forces and moments of force act on them.
(2)	learn the concepts of momentum, work, and energy.
(3)	learn about machines in which friction is utilized.
advice:
This is a basic course on the dynamics of machines. We will cover the following topics:

1. Kinematics of rigid bodies
2. Dynamics of impact
3. Work and energy
4. Dynamics of friction
5. SImple machines

If time permits, students will also learn about advanced issues not covered in the textbooks, such as three-dimensional motion.
Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and formulas.
Each student is expected to solve the exercises by himself or herself.
Students should pay attention to the teacher's instructions in class. The schedule of quizzes, tests, and reports may change as the class progresses.
Students should not be absent from class, as they may miss handouts.
Where understanding is insufficient, utilise AI to deepen comprehension. However, if AI is employed in the report, clearly state how it was utilised.
books:
Textbooks: (in Japanese)
Reference books: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics [Wiley]
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Acquisition of Industrial Mechanics I and II.
Enough skill in mathematics (especially differential/integral and vector inner/outcome calculations).
Basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and moment of force).
How to use a calculator.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the meaning of terms and to use SI units correctly.
Be able to explain the kinetics of rigid bodies.
Be able to explain changes in the motion of rigid bodies when they impact each other.
Be able to describe the energy of rigid bodies in motion.
Be able to analyze the motion of a machine using friction.

(2) Express the three-dimensional motion of rigid bodies by equations and explain their behavior.
(3) Analyze oblique impact and non-central impact.
(4) Calculate the energy of rigid bodies in three-dimensional motion.
(5) Formulate equations of motion for machines using frictional forces and explain their motions.

(1) Explain the meaning of terms such as momentum, linear impulse, energy, conserved force, and coefficient of restitution, and correctly use SI units for velocity, acceleration, angular velocity, momentum, angular momentum, work, energy, and power.
(2) Express the planar motion of rigid bodies with equations.
(3) Analyze the direct central impact of rigid bodies.
(4) Calculate the energy of rigid bodies in planar motion.
(5) Describe the frictional force in mathematical terms.

educationalGoal:
Knowledge of the basic properties of materials, design techniques, and processing techniques is indispensable to manufacturing machine parts.

(1) learn the functions and structures of various machine tools
(2) learn how to select an advantageous machining method for the requirements under the basic production manufacturing technology
(3) learn how to measure cutting force and cutting edge temperature

title: 材料力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Strength of Materials II
educationalGoal: The strength of materials can clarify the forces and deformations on various parts of bridges, steel towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, and living tissues and cells. Those results can be used to improve designs for safety. Therefore, it is an important subject that forms the basis of mechanical engineering. In this course, students will learn about bending stress in a beam, deflection of a beam, torsion, and combined stress based on the content learned in "Strength of Materials I".
advice:
This is a basic course on the strength of materials. We will cover the following topics:
 1. Bending stress in a beam                                 5. Stress on oblique section in the rod subjected to uniaxial tension
 2. Deflection of a beam                                       6. Principal stress and principal shearing stress
 3. Torsion of shaft with circular cross section     7.  Mohr's stress circle
 4. Power transmission shaft                	            8.Combined stress problem
All of these topics are based on stress, strain, Hook's law, a beam and its supporting condition, and shearing force and bending moment of a beam, which were learned in "Strength of Materials I". Therefore, while reviewing the content of "Strength of Materials I" topic by topic, it is essential to make an effort to develop a bottom-up understanding by carefully considering the topics' relationship with the content of "Strength of Materials II".
It is important to do many exercises and review the answers, but the study of strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand by just remembering formulas and patterns. For all problems, start by understanding the basic formula and continue the attitude of answering the problem by setting appropriate boundary conditions for it. Furthermore, students should work on issues related to local companies, and deepen their understanding of the relationship between the strength of materials, society, and technology. Lecture and exercise explanations will be provided on demand as needed.
books:
Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: Strength of Materials, Basic, Morikita Publishing Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reserved books: None specified
requiredKnowledge: Students should have a good understanding of balance of force, stress, and strain, Hook's law, support condition of a beam, and shearing force and bending moment of a beam learned in "Strength of Materials I". In addition, it is necessary to fully understand differential and integral calculation methods.

Be able to determine torsional stress.

Be able to explain the principal stress and principal shearing stress, and to draw a Mohr's stress circle.
Be able to explain the relationship between strength of materials, society, and technology.

title: 熱力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Thermodynamics I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn basic knowledge of the irreversibility in the nature world
(2) Learn how to convert energy and obtain work from heat
(3) Acquire design skills for energy conversion in mechanical engineering
advice:
Mechanical systems convert energy and perform useful work. Effective energy management is essential for operating such systems and for conserving energy in support of a sustainable society, and thermodynamics is the academic discipline that underpins green technologies. Accordingly, this introductory course focuses on the fundamentals of energy conservation and energy conversion.

1. Definitions of heat, temperature, and systems
2. Thermal equilibrium and the zeroth law of thermodynamics
3. The first law of thermodynamics
4. Equation of state of ideal gases and thermodynamic process of ideal gas
5. Gas cycle

Students are advised not merely to memorize formulas, but to envision the physical phenomena that the equations represent
constantly.
Note: This course plan is subject to change. Details will be provided in the first week of class.

Be able to explain gas cycles and apply the knowledge to probrems about design of thermal equipment

title: 機械力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Dynamics of Machines II
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn the basics of vibration problems that occur in machines.
(2) Learn how to apply vibration analysis to mechanical designs.
(3) Learn how to make a dynamic model of vibration phenomena consisting of multi-freedom vibration, and use it for analysis.
advice:
This is a basic and applied course in mechanical dynamics. We will cover the following topics:

1. Non-damping vibration (keywords: linear vibration, torsional vibration, pendulum vibration)
2. Viscous damping phenomenon (keywords: damping ratio, viscous damping coefficient)
3. Forced vibration (keywords: forced vibration by external force, forced vibration by displacement)
4. Application to various vibration problems (keywords: critical speed, vibration measurement)
5. Application to multi-freedom vibration (keyword: dynamic absorber)

Students are required to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to check for various messages and materials in class.
Students should not be absent from class, as they may not receive the handouts.
books:
Textbooks: Introduction to Vibration Engineering, Tokyo Denki University (in Japanese)
Reference books: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Complete Industrial Mechanics I and II, and Dynamics of Mechanics I.
Have sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential/integral and vector inner/outcome calculations)
Have basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and moment of force).
Know how to use a calculator.

activityGoals.body: Be able to express an appropriate model for mechanical vibration.
Be able to formulate a motion equation based on the expressed vibration model.
Be able to analyze a vibration motion equation.
Be able to apply to various vibration problems consisting of multi-freedom vibration.

(1) Express mechanical vibration with the appropriate vibration model.
(2) Create a formula of motion based on the expressed vibration model.

(4) Apply the formula to various vibration problems within the multi-freedom vibration model, and design a fundamental dynamic absorber.
(5) Explain the regional vibration problem.

(1) Express mechanical vibration with a simplified vibration model.
(2) Create a formula of motion based on the expressed vibration model.
(3) Calculate the solution for the formula of motion.
(4) Apply the formula to various vibration problems within the multi-freedom vibration model, and explain a fundamental dynamic absorber.
(5) Explain the regional vibration problem.

title: 材料科学Ⅱ
subtitle: Materials Science II
educationalGoal: To design and manufacture machines and structures that exhibit superior performance, it is necessary to select materials based on an understanding of the characteristics of the elements of which they are composed. In addition, the microstructures and properties of materials change after heat treatment and processing. In this course, students learn how to modify materials by heat treatment and processing.
advice:
The outline of the class is as follows:
Fe-C phase diagram and normal microstructures
Heat treatment and microstructure of steel
Work hardening, recovery, and re-crystallization
Solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening, and crystal grain refinement strengthening
books:

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the relationship between an Fe-C phase diagram and normal microstructures.
Be able to explain basic heat-treatment methods for steel.
Be able to explain basic heat-treatment methods for aluminum alloys.
Be able to explain microstructures obtained by plastic deformation, and recovery and re-crystallization

2: Propose heat-treatment conditions of steels using the Fe-C phase diagram, continuous cooling transformation (CCT) curve, and time-temperature transformation (TTT) curve.
2 and 3: Explain the relationship between mechanical properties and phase transformation and/or precipitation caused by heat treatment.
4: Explain the recovery and re-crystallization process for work-hardened materials.

1: Explain the relation between carbon content in carbon steels and normal microstructures.
2 and 3: Explain basic technical terms of heat treatment, for example, quenching, tempering, annealing, normalizing, solid-solution treatment, and aging.
4: Explain the relationship between work-hardening and lattice defects.

title: 数値計算プログラミング
subtitle: Numerical analysis and programming
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Acquire numerical computation skills.
(2) Develop the ability to perform numerical analysis.
(3) Learn algorithms for high-accuracy computation.
advice:
This course teaches numerical computation methods using Python programming. Numerical computation requires an understanding of numerical algorithms as well as the ability to create and execute programs. Students will develop numerous programs through exercises and reports. Through this process, students will acquire the skills to implement and solve various engineering problems as computer programs.

[Learning Topics]
1. Basic linear calculus
2. Numerical solving of simultaneous linear equations
3. Numerical calculation of eigenvalues and eigenvectors
4. Numerical solving of nonlinear equations
5. Interpolation and least squares methods
6. Numerical differentiation and integration
7. Numerical solving of ordinary differential equations

This course emphasizes programming exercises, so students should prepare thoroughly before each class. After class, students are expected to refine the coding programs and apply them to various engineering problems.

title: 制御工学
subtitle: Control Engineering
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)	Learn the basics of developing control system
(2)	Learn Laplace transformation and the transfer functions of control systems
(3)	Learn the simulation method of control system by MATLAB/Simulink
(4)	Learn the basics of control system analysis based on the transient and frequency response.
advice:
This is a basic course in control engineering. We will cover the following topics:

1. Laplace transform
2. Transfer function
3. Block diagram
4. Board diagram
5. Stability of control system
6. Design of control system

Students are expected to understand the meaning of the analysis method for control systems.
Students are expected to determine the stability of a control system.

Text:
https://www.morikita.co.jp/books/mid/091842
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable that you fully understand and master the contents of the mechanics and mathematics courses.

activityGoals.body: Be able to Laplace transform a simple mathematical model of a system and express it using a transfer function.
Be able to use MATLAB/Simulink to create a block diagram of a system.
Be able to express the dynamic characteristics of a system as transient and frequency response characteristics.
Be able to can use MATLAB/Simulink to simulate the responsiveness of control systems.
Be able to learn the latest technology from local technicians and explore a given task.

title: 機械系製図Ⅰ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the principles of orthographic projection, which is the basis of mechanical drawing.
(2) learn the ability to accurately create 2D&3D drawings according to the third angle projection method.
(3) practice 2D-CAD&3D-CAD and handwritten drafting to create and edit drawings efficiently.
advice:
Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas.
Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions.
This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings.
We will cover the following topics:
1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons
2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings
3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises
4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures
5. Size tolerance and fit
6. The role of CAE in manufacturing
books:
Textbooks: New JIS Mechanical Drawing (6th edition), Morikita Publishing (in Japanese),
Mechanical Drawing Operation Method using Siemens NX, Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese)
Reference books: None   Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Lectures are “stacked” learning (work on new subjects is based on the knowledge and abilities acquired in the previous week's class). Therefore, students should review the material in the weekly lectures thoroughly and fully understand it by the next lecture. Reference materials and assignment diagrams used in the class will be distributed using the electronic syllabus of this course. A network printer can be used.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the principles of orthographic projection and express the shape of machine parts.
Be able to understand the basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings and draw drawings.
Be able to draw front, top, and side views of machine parts.
Be able to sketch mechanical parts accurately and create hand-drawn mechanical drawings based on these sketches.
Be able to create machine drawings using 2D-CAD & 3D-CAD figure creation and figure editing functions.
Be able to summarize of the role of CAE in manufacturing by obtaining information related to design and CAD.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Accurately understand the third trigonometric method and basic drafting rules used for machine drafting.(2) Accurately understand the basic line types used in machine drawings and their roles.(3) Select the necessary projections by analyzing the geometric features of parts and determine the main projections appropriately.(4) Sketch machine parts accurately, and create hand-drawings based on the sketches.
(5) Understand the size tolerances and surface roughness of machine parts and accurately indicate them in drawings.(6) Gain an understanding of the relationship between design and CAD/CAE, and explain this to a third party by giving a specific example.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Understand the trigonometry and basic drawing rules used to create mechanical drawings. (2) Understand the basic line types used in machine drawings and their roles. (3) Select a necessary projection by analyzing the shape characteristics of a part and determine a main projection.(4) Sketch mechanical parts and make hand-drawn 2D mechanical drawings based on these sketches. (5) Understand the size tolerances of machine parts, the size tolerances of surface roughness products, and the surface roughness, and indicate them in drawings.
(6) Gain an understanding of the relationship between design and CAD/CAE, and explain this to a third party in an easy-to-understand manner.

educationalGoal:
Students will:

(1)understand the definition of machine.
(2)learn the basics of mechanical engineering.
(3)disassemble and assemble an actual machine.
(4)learn the structure, mechanism, and principles of the machine.
(5)learn the mathematics for mechanical engineering.
advice:
This is an introductory subject of mechanical engineering. We will cover the following:

1. Lectures and actual works
2. Basics of mechanical engineering
3. Basics of mechanical elements
4. How to use tools and measuring instruments
5. How to disassemble/assemble
6. Mathematics for mechanical engineering

Students are required to actively participate in class.
Students are required to understand the names of the mechanical elements.
Students are required to understand the major field of mechanical engineering.
Students are required to understand how to use tools.
Students are required to understand mathematics for mechanical engineering.

title: 工業力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Engineering Mechanics I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the basic concepts of the static mechanics.
(2) learn what kind of forces act on the rigid bodies.
(3) learn how to calculate the balance condition of forces.
(4) learn how to calculate the center of gravity.
advice:
This is a basic engineering mechanics course.
We will cover the following materials:
1. Force
2. Synthesis and decomposition of forces
3. Moments of forces
4. Balance of forces
5. Center of gravity of rigid bodies
Students will also learn about advanced issues not included in the textbooks.
Students will be expected to understand the meanings of the terms and formulas.
Students will be expected to solve the exercises on their own.
Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of lectures, quizzes, tests and reports may change as the class progresses.
Students should not be absent from the class, as the handouts may be not received.
books:
Textbooks: Kougyou Rikigaku(4th edition), Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: None   Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:

Basic knowledge of mechanics
How to use scientific calculator

activityGoals.body: Be able to indicate the forces on the rigid bodies and to describe their magnitude using SI unit correctly
Be able to synthesize and decompose the forces
Be able to calculate the moments of forces
Be able to formulate the balance of forces and moments of forces and calculate the reaction forces
Be able to calculate the center of gravity for the rigid bodies
Be able to explain the stability of the rigid bodies

(1) Synthesize the forces acting at the same points and in the different directions.
(2) Decompose the forces in any directions and synthesize the forces acting at the different points and in the different directions.
(3) Calculate the moments of force on the actual rigid bodies.
(4) Calculate local loads on the actual rigid bodies from the balance of forces.
(5) Calculate the center of gravity of the actual rigid bodies.

achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Explain the three elements to indicate the force vectors, and describe the forces using SI unit.
(2) Decompose the forces into the x and y axis and synthesize three forces acting at the different points.
(3) Calculate the moments of force acting on the rigid bodies, and indicate them in suitable SI units.
(4) Calculate the reaction forces at the rotational support points.
(5) Calculate the center of gravity of objects composed of the simple rigid bodies.
(6) Evaluate the stability of the simple rigid bodies.

title: 電気基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn the basic of electronics for a machine engineer
(2) Learn the basic concepts such as electric current and voltage
(3) Learn the principles and the functions such as resistor, condenser and coil
(4) Learn the principle of motor
advice:
This is a basic course in electric engineering.

Step 1: students will understand the concepts as follows,
electric current, voltage, resistance, electric power, magnetic field, magnetic force, alternating current, electric field
Step 2: students will understand the laws and use them as follows,
Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's current law, Joule's law, Coulomb's law, Ampere's law, Biobersal's law, Fleming's law, Faraday's law
Step 3: students will apply them to electric circuits and equipments as follows,
voltage and current measuremnt, whetastone brigde, heater, temperature measuremnt, electromagnetic induction, motor, electric transformer, electric storage

title: 機械系製図Ⅱ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing II
educationalGoal: Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.
advice:
In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises.
In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I".
It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture.
The contents handled in this lecture are as follows.
・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing
・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance
・ Surface roughness   ・ Dimension filling method  ・ Bolts and nuts  ・ Keys and keyways
・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings
・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints
In addition, it is necessary to be able to fully understand the design at the actual manufacturing site.
 Copying in drafting drawings is against the ethics of engineers, and credits for this subject are revoked when it is found.
books:
Textbooks:New JIS mechanical drawing(6th edition),Moritika Publishing(in Japanese)
JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Siemens NX,Kanazawa Institute of Technology(in Japanese)
Reference books:None Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge:
(1) You can draw on the CAD software drawing creation screen. Your ability should be at a level where it is easy to create a model of the text “Mechanical Drawing”. Basically, items that should have been learned in Mechanical Drawing I (functions written in the text, drawing methods) are not taught in this course.
(2) 3D (3D objects) can be modeled using 3D drafting, the 3rd angle method (2D drafting) and using two-dimensional drafting (plan view, front view, side view). (3) You have mastered the method of downloading materials and uploading reports using the student portal.

activityGoals.body: Be able to transmit a design using mechanical drawing.
Be able to draw a two-dimensional mechanical drawing from a bird's-eye view or a photograph of the machine parts
Be able to imagine the shape of a part drawn from a two-dimensional mechanical drawing created by a third party.
Be able to indicate the machine design, tolerance, and accuracy for the manufacturing method of machine parts.
Be able to prepare and explain the results of preparation and review as works at the specified time.
Be able to explain the design process and role at the manufacturing site.

        ＊印は、実務経験のある教員を示しています。

              授業科目の学習・教育目標

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.JIS standards and mechanical drawings
2.Mechanical design
3.Manufacturing methods and accuracy/tolerance
4.CAD
5.Regional cooperation

              Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises.
In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I".
It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture.
The contents handled in this lecture are as follows.
・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing
・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance
・ Surface roughness   ・ Dimension filling method  ・ Bolts and nuts  ・ Keys and keyways
・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings
・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints
In addition, it is necessary to be able to fully understand the design at the actual manufacturing site.
 Copying in drafting drawings is against the ethics of engineers, and credits for this subject are revoked when it is found.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Textbooks:New JIS mechanical drawing(6th edition),Moritika Publishing(in Japanese)
JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Siemens NX,Kanazawa Institute of Technology(in Japanese)
Reference books:None Reserved books:None

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              (1) You can draw on the CAD software drawing creation screen. Your ability should be at a level where it is easy to create a model of the text “Mechanical Drawing”. Basically, items that should have been learned in Mechanical Drawing I (functions written in the text, drawing methods) are not taught in this course.
(2) 3D (3D objects) can be modeled using 3D drafting, the 3rd angle method (2D drafting) and using two-dimensional drafting (plan view, front view, side view). (3) You have mastered the method of downloading materials and uploading reports using the student portal.

              No.

                E,H,J,K,L,O
                Be able to transmit a design using mechanical drawing.

                ②
                E,H,J,K,L,O
                Be able to draw a two-dimensional mechanical drawing from a bird's-eye view or a ph

title: 工業力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Engineering Mechanics II
educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1)Newton's laws of motion.
(2)Motion of mass or rigid body subjected force or torque.
(3)Basics of dynamics.
(4)Inertial forces and other factors necessary for designing high-speed machines.
advice:
Students will learn methods for analyzing the motion of mass points and rigid bodies by solving equations of motion through exercises based on the items. We will cover the following topics:
1. Motion of mass
2. Laws of motion
3. Inertia, centripetal and centrifugal forces
4. Moment of inertia
5. Planar motion of rigid bodies

Students are required to understand these concepts, tackle practice problems, and then cultivate the ability to apply their knowledge to practical problems.
Students are also required to tackle exercises using schematic drawings, and then imagine the application of forces and moments and the subsequent motion of mass points and rigid bodies.
Students are expected to pay attention to significant figures and units.
books: 工業力学　森北出版
requiredKnowledge: It is important to try a lot of exercises. A good understanding of high school math and physics is needed. Always use a scientific calculator in class. Students with poor attitudes may be asked to leave and may not be allowed to attend. Recommend using office hours. In addition, the content of this class is indispensable for understanding of specialized subjects in the next year.

activityGoals.body: Be able to build an equation of motion for a mass and calculate its velocity and location.
Be able to explain the laws of motion and calculate inertial, centripetal and centrifugal forces.
Be able to calculate the moment of inertia.
Be able to build equations of motion or machine models.
Be able to solve equations of motion by applying mathematics

title: 材料力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Strength of Materials I
educationalGoal: Investigating the strength of materials can clarify the forces that act on various parts of bridges, steel towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, living tissues and cells, etc., and the deformations they cause. The results can be used for safety design. It is therefore a foundational subject in mechanical engineering. In this course, students will gain a thorough understanding of the investigation of the strength of materials through lectures and practice.
advice:
This is a basic strength of materials course. We will cover the following topics:

1. Stress and strain                                     5. Beams and their support conditions
2. Hooke’s law                                           6. Shearing forces and bending moments of beams
3. Mechanical properties of materials        7. Bending stress in a beam
4. Allowable stress and safety factors        8. Deflection of a beam

In this course, it is important to do many practice exercises, but the study of the strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand just by memorizing formulas and patterns. To solve a problem, one should start with an understanding of the basic formulas needed, and then set the appropriate boundary conditions for the problem. In addition, it is necessary to be able to concretely imagine the actual forces, moments, and deformations using schematic diagrams.
Furthermore, students should work on issues related to local companies, and deepen their understanding of the relationship between the strength of materials and society/technology.

requiredKnowledge: Gaining understanding by working through many different problems is the best way to learn strength of materials. title: 機械材料Ⅰ
subtitle: Engineering materials I
educationalGoal: In this course, we will give an overview of the industrial materials and learn the basics of the relationship between structure and physical and chemical properties, as well as methods for evaluating the characteristics of materials.
advice:
The outline of the class is as follows:

Classification of machine materials and characteristics of metals, plastics, and ceramics
Structure of materials
Basics of crystallography
Theoretical strength and crystallographic dislocations in materials, resolved shear stress, and dislocation and deformation of a single crystal
Plastic deformation of materials
Materials evaluation, tensile test, stress versus strain curves, and hardness test
Phase transition of metals
books:
Textbooks: Mechanical Materials(3rd edition), Tokyo Denki University Press (in Japanese)
Reference books: None
Reserved books: Introduction Structure and Properties of Metallic Materials, Taiga Publishing Co., Ltd. (in Japanese)
requiredKnowledge:
Understand the basics of trigonometric functions, exponential functions, logarithmic functions, and vectors.
Memorize the elemental symbols, such as those for carbon, magnesium, aluminum, titanium, iron, and copper, related to materials science.
Regarding material structure, it is desirable to have knowledge of high school chemistry.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain basic characteristics of metals, plastics, and ceramics.
Be able to explain types, features, and examples of atomic bonds.
Be able to explain the basics of crystallography (especially Bravais lattice and Miller index).
Be able to explain the difference between elastic and plastic deformation based on materials science.
Be able to explain basics of materials evaluation.
Be able to explain the relationship between equilibrium phase diagram and phase formation.

title: 基礎流体力学
subtitle: Basic Fluid Mechanics
educationalGoal: Fluid mechanics plays a significant role in advanced mechanical systems and manufacturing. This course introduces the fundamental principles of fluid mechanics. Students learn the basic properties of fluids, Bernoulli's theorem, the equation of continuity, and the momentum equation. Students gain foundational skills in applying fluid mechanics knowledge to effectively use AI, machine learning, and advanced CAE through practical exercises.
advice:
This course primarily introduces fluid mechanics. In particular, the flow of an ideal fluid, which is inviscid and incompressible, is discussed. Furthermore, the flow mechanisms of a real fluid are also explained. The contents and keywords of this course are as follows:

1. Characteristics of fluid and flow phenomena: Difference of solid, liquid, and gas, Dimension and Unit, Density, Viscosity, Compressibility and sound velocity, Steam pressure, Surface tension
2. Hydrostatics: Definition of pressure, Hydrostatic pressure, Manometer, Total hydrostatic force, Buoyancy force, Hydraulic pressure drive system
3. Basic equations of flow: Condition of flow, Representation method of fluid flow, Flow velocity, Flow rate and acceleration, Derivation of basic equations of flow
4. Bernoulli's theorem and equation of continuity: Derivation of equation of continuity, Application of equation of continuity, Derivation of Bernoulli's equation, Application of Bernoulli's equation
5. Momentum theorem: Momentum theorem, Application, Equation of angular momentum

Detailed schedules and plans will be explained during the first week of classes. Additionally, some sessions will incorporate flipped classroom sessions utilizing pre-study materials via on-demand resources.
books: 流れ学[朝倉書店]（in Japanese）
requiredKnowledge: The students must take a note in the class. The preparation and the review of the contents of the class must be done. Every class includes exercises and mini-examinations (quizzes). An attitude of willing action and learning is strongly required to the students.

activityGoals.body: Fluid characteristics such as compressibility and viscosity can be explained.
Relationship between fluid depth and pressure can be expressed and total hydrostatic force can be calculated.
Basic equations of fluid flow can be derived for easy examples.
Basic fluid flow can be calculated using the equation of continuity and Bernoulli's equation.
Momentum theorem can be applied to calculation of an actual fluid force.
Relationship between the course content and the local communities can be understood and discussed together.

(5) Momentum theorem and its use for basic design problems in machinery that uses fluids.               キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Characteristics of fluid
2.Pressure
3.Equations of fluid flow
4.Momentum theorem
5.Contribution to local community, IoT

              Fluid mechanics plays a significant role in advanced mechanical systems and manufacturing. This course introduces the fundamental principles of fluid mechanics. Students learn the basic properties of fluids, Bernoulli's theorem, the equation of continuity, and the momentum equation. Students gain foundational skills in applying fluid mechanics knowledge to effectively use AI, machine learning, and advanced CAE through practical exercises.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course primarily introduces fluid mechanics. In particular, the flow of an ideal fluid, which is inviscid and incompressible, is discussed. Furthermore, the flow mechanisms of a real fluid are also explained. The contents and keywords of this course are as follows:

1. Characteristics of fluid and flow phenomena: Difference of solid, liquid, and gas, Dimension and Unit, Density, Viscosity, Compressibility and sound velocity, Steam pressure, Surface tension
2. Hydrostatics: Definition of pressure, Hydrostatic pressure, Manometer, Total hydrostatic force, Buoyancy force, Hydraulic pressure drive system
3. Basic equations of flow: Condition of flow, Representation method of fluid flow, Flow velocity, Flow rate and acceleration, Derivation of basic equations of flow
4. Bernoulli's theorem and equation of continuity: Derivation of equation of continuity, Application of equation of continuity, Derivation of Bernoulli's equation, Application of Bernoulli's equation
5. Momentum theorem: Momentum theorem, Application, Equation of angular momentum

Detailed schedules and plans will be explained during the first week of classes. Additionally, some sessions will incorporate flipped classroom sessions utilizing pre-study materials via on-demand resources.

title: 機械力学
subtitle: Dynamics of  Machines
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)	learn the kinematics of rigid bodies when forces and moments of force act on them.
(2)	learn the concepts of momentum, work, and energy.
(3)	learn about machines in which friction is utilized.
advice:
This is a basic course on the dynamics of machines. We will cover the following topics:

1. Kinematics of rigid bodies
2. Dynamics of impact
3. Work and energy
4. Dynamics of friction
5. SImple machines

If time permits, students will also learn about advanced issues not covered in the textbooks, such as three-dimensional motion.
Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and formulas.
Each student is expected to solve the exercises by himself or herself.
Students should pay attention to the teacher's instructions in class. The schedule of quizzes, tests, and reports may change as the class progresses.
Students should not be absent from class, as they may miss handouts.

Reference books: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics [Wiley]
Reserved books: None

Acquisition of Industrial Mechanics I and II.
Enough skill in mathematics (especially differential/integral and vector inner/outcome calculations).
Basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and moment of force).
How to use a calculator.

Be able to explain the kinetics of rigid bodies.
Be able to explain changes in the motion of rigid bodies when they impact each other.
Be able to describe the energy of rigid bodies in motion.
Be able to analyze the motion of a machine using friction.

(5) Formulate equations of motion for machines using frictional forces and explain their motions.

(1) Explain the meaning of terms such as momentum, linear impulse, energy, conserved force, and coefficient of restitution, and correctly use SI units for velocity, acceleration, angular velocity, momentum, angular momentum, work, energy, and power.
(2) Express the planar motion of rigid bodies with equations.
(3) Analyze the direct central impact of rigid bodies.
(4) Calculate the energy of rigid bodies in planar motion.
(5) Describe the frictional force in mathematical terms.

title: アドバンスドマニュファクチャリングⅠ
subtitle: Advanced Manufacturing I
educationalGoal:
(1) learn the functions and structures of various machine tools
(2) learn how to select an advantageous machining method for the requirements under the basic production manufacturing technology
(3) Learn the basic theory of removal machining
(4) Learn how to select cutting tool materials and cutting conditions
(5) Learn measurement methods to evaluate the required precision
advice:
This class will cover the following topics:
1. Outline of manufacturing technology(Trends in machining Technology, Classification of fundamental machining methods
2. Fundamentals of cutting theory (Chip Formation and shear mechanism, Cutting force and cutting temperature)
3. Fundamental machining methods (Function and structure of milling machines, Lathes, Drilling machines, etc., Selection of cutting conditions)
4. NC machine tools (Functions and structure of CNC Lathes, Machining Centers, Multi-tasking machine tool, etc.)
5. Cutting tools and tool damage (Various tool materials, Understanding tool damage and Product accuracy, etc.)
6. Workpiece evaluation methods (Dimensional accuracy, Geometric accuracy, Surface roughness)
books:
Textbooks:
Reference books: None
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to watch videos on machining methods and the functions of machine tools. This will help you understand actual machine motion and machining systems. It is also important to experience the actual machining process by visiting processing plants and industrial fairs. Obtaining a license for Yumekobo machine tools and actually operating them is useful for deepening your understanding.

title: 機械要素設計
subtitle: Mechanical Elements Design
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)	Understand the mechanical elements.
(2)	Learn the method of machine design.
(3)	Practice the design of a screw, shaft, and gear.
advice:
This is a course on the basics of machine design. We will cover the following topics:

1. Basics of design:
  (1) procedure of the design, (2) design and processing, and (3) reliability design
2. Strength and stiffness of materials:
  (1) load and material properties, (2) fatigue strength and deformation stress, and (3) detailed design and safety factor
3. Mechanical elements:
  (1) screws, (2) shafts and bearings, and (3) gears

Students should strive to improve their design ability.

title: アドバンスドマニュファクチャリングⅡ
subtitle: Advanced Manufacturing II
educationalGoal: Many of production machining technologies have names that indicate their purpose and characteristics. This lecture is positioned as an extension of "Manufacturing process and systems" and "Machining Engineering" to broaden the view of production machining technology and to understand its methods. In addition, students will learn about the production process to realize the manufacturing of products and parts. They will also learn about shape creation in various manufacturing processes.
advice:
In this class, students will study the following topics.
1. Production Manufacturing, Process and Machine tools
2. Machine materials, Surface finishing and Coating
3. Deformation processing (Casting, Plastic molding)
4. Additive processing (Welding, Joining), Plasticity processing
5. Removal processing (Cutting, Grinding, Polishing)
6. Special machining (Electrical machining, Laser machining, Micro machining)
7. Additive manufacturing (Additive production)
8. Form Shaping Theory
9. Production System

The class schedule may be changed to reflect on the above content with quizzes and exercises as appropriate.
books: Textbook:(1)はじめての生産加工学1 基本加工技術編[講談社]、(2)はじめての生産加工学2 応用加工技術編[講談社]
requiredKnowledge: As this is a practical study, it is recommended that students make use of videos on machining, machine tools, and production systems. In addition to the related videos that will be shown in class, they will also be useful in deepening the understanding of this lecture. It is also important to take advantage of opportunities such as visits to machining facilities and industrial exhibitions to observe and experience the actual machining process.

              　Many of production machining technologies have names that indicate their purpose and characteristics. This lecture is positioned as an extension of "Manufacturing process and systems" and "Machining Engineering" to broaden the view of production machining technology and to understand its methods. In addition, students will learn about the production process to realize the manufacturing of products and parts. They will also learn about shape creation in various manufacturing processes.

              　In this class, students will study the following topics.
1. Production Manufacturing, Process and Machine tools
2. Machine materials, Surface finishing and Coating
3. Deformation processing (Casting, Plastic molding)
4. Additive processing (Welding, Joining), Plasticity processing
5. Removal processing (Cutting, Grinding, Polishing)
6. Special machining (Electrical machining, Laser machining, Micro machining)
7. Additive manufacturing (Additive production)
8. Form Shaping Theory
9. Production System

The class schedule may be changed to reflect on the above content with quizzes and exercises as appropriate.

subtitle: Control Engineering
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)	Learn the basics of developing control system
(2)	Learn Laplace transformation and the transfer functions of control systems
(3)	Learn the simulation method of control system by MATLAB/Simulink
(4)	Learn the basics of control system analysis based on the transient and frequency response.
advice:
This is a basic course in control engineering. We will cover the following topics:

1. Laplace transform
2. Transfer function
3. Block diagram
4. Board diagram
5. Stability of control system
6. Design of control system

Students are expected to understand the meaning of the analysis method for control systems.
Students are expected to determine the stability of a control system.

Be able to use MATLAB/Simulink to create a block diagram of a system.

title: 振動工学
subtitle: Vibration Engineering
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn the basics of vibration problems that occur in machines.
(2) Learn how to apply vibration analysis to mechanical designs.
(3) Learn how to make a dynamic model of vibration phenomena consisting of multi-freedom vibration, and use it for analysis.
advice:
This is a basic and applied course in mechanical dynamics. We will cover the following topics:

1. Non-damping vibration (keywords: linear vibration, torsional vibration, pendulum vibration)
2. Viscous damping phenomenon (keywords: damping ratio, viscous damping coefficient)
3. Forced vibration (keywords: forced vibration by external force, forced vibration by displacement)
4. Application to various vibration problems (keywords: critical speed, vibration measurement)
5. Application to multi-freedom vibration (keyword: dynamic absorber)

Students are required to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to check for various messages and materials in class.
Students should not be absent from class, as they may not receive the handouts.
books:
Textbooks: Introduction to Vibration Engineering, Tokyo Denki University (in Japanese)
Reference books: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Complete Industrial Mechanics I and II, and Dynamics of Mechanics I.
Have sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential/integral and vector inner/outcome calculations)
Have basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and moment of force).
Know how to use a calculator.

activityGoals.body: Be able to express an appropriate model for mechanical vibration.
Be able to formulate a motion equation based on the expressed vibration model.
Be able to analyze a vibration motion equation.
Be able to apply to various vibration problems consisting of multi-freedom vibration.
