achievementLevels.ideal:
Be able to do the following things based on an understanding of various vibration phenomena in industrial machines:
(1) Express mechanical vibration with the appropriate vibration model.
(2) Create a formula of motion based on the expressed vibration model.
(3) Calculate the solution for the formula of motion.
(4) Apply the formula to various vibration problems within the multi-freedom vibration model, and design a fundamental dynamic absorber.
(5) Explain the regional vibration problem.
achievementLevels.standard:
Be able to do the following things based on an understanding of various vibration phenomena:
(1) Express mechanical vibration with a simplified vibration model.
(2) Create a formula of motion based on the expressed vibration model.
(3) Calculate the solution for the formula of motion.
(4) Apply the formula to various vibration problems within the multi-freedom vibration model, and explain a fundamental dynamic absorber.
(5) Explain the regional vibration problem.

title: 機械材料Ⅱ
subtitle: Engineering materials II
educationalGoal: To design and manufacture machines and structures that exhibit superior performance, it is necessary to select materials based on an understanding of the characteristics of the elements of which they are composed. In addition, the microstructures and properties of materials change after heat treatment and processing. In this course, students learn how to modify materials by heat treatment and processing.
advice:
The outline of the class is as follows:
Fe-C phase diagram and normal microstructures
Heat treatment and microstructure of steel
Work hardening, recovery, and re-crystallization
Solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening, and crystal grain refinement strengthening
books:
Textbooks: Mechanical Materials(3rd edition), Tokyo Denki University Press (in Japanese)
Reference books: None

requiredKnowledge: It is strongly recommended that students take this course after reviewing and fully understanding the contents of Engineering Materials I.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the relationship between an Fe-C phase diagram and normal microstructures.
Be able to explain basic heat-treatment methods for steel.
Be able to explain basic heat-treatment methods for aluminum alloys.
Be able to explain microstructures obtained by plastic deformation, and recovery and re-crystallization

2 and 3: Explain the relationship between mechanical properties and phase transformation and/or precipitation caused by heat treatment.
4: Explain the recovery and re-crystallization process for work-hardened materials.

title: 材料力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Strength of Materials II
educationalGoal: The strength of materials can clarify the forces and deformations on various parts of bridges, steel towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, and living tissues and cells. Those results can be used to improve designs for safety. Therefore, it is an important subject that forms the basis of mechanical engineering. In this course, students will learn about tension & compression, torsion, and combined stress based on the content learned in “Strength of Materials I.”
advice:
This is a basic course on the strength of materials. We will cover the following topics:
1. Frame structure   2. Thermal stress and stress concentration
3. Thin-walled cylinders subjected to internal pressure
4. Torsion of shaft with circular cross section   5. Power transmission shaft
6. Stress on oblique section in the rod subjected to uniaxial tension
7. Principal stress and principal shearing stress   8. Mohr’s stress circle   9. Combined stress problem
All of these topics are based on stress, strain, Hook’s law, a beam and its supporting condition, shearing force and bending moment of a beam, and bending stress and deflection of a beam, which were learned in “Strength of Materials I.” Therefore, while reviewing the content of “Strength of Materials I” topic by topic, it is essential to make an effort to develop a bottom-up understanding by carefully considering the topics’ relationship with the content of “Strength of Materials II.”
It is important to do many exercises and review the answers, but the study of strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand by just remembering formulas and patterns. For all problems, start by understanding the basic formula and continue the attitude of answering the problem by setting appropriate boundary conditions for it. Furthermore, students should work on issues related to local companies, and deepen their understanding of the relationship between the strength of materials, society, and technology.
books:
Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: Strength of Materials, Basic, Morikita Publishing Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reserved books: None specified
requiredKnowledge: Students should have a good understanding of balance of force, stress, and strain, Hook’s law, support condition of a beam, and shearing force and bending moment of a beam, and bending stress and deflection of a beam learned in “Strength of Materials I.” In addition, it is necessary to fully understand differential and integral calculation methods.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the frame structure, thermal stress, thin-walled cylinders and stress concentration.
Be able to determine torsional stress.
Be able to determine the diameter of a transmission shaft.
Be able to determine the stress in the oblique cross section of a bar subjected to uniaxial tension.
Be able to explain the principal stress and principal shearing stress, and to draw a Mohr's stress circle.
Be able to explain the relationship between strength of materials, society, and technology.

title: 制御系プログラミング
subtitle: Programming for control systems
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Understand how physical phenomena can be modeled using differential equations and analyzed with computers.
(2) Acquire the ability to implement numerical computation algorithms and perform analyses through programming.
(3) Develop the ability to interpret analytical results and improve programs for higher accuracy.
advice:
This course introduces mathematical models used to represent physical phenomena and provides training in numerical computation methods using MATLAB/Simulink. Students will learn how to construct models (block diagrams) and perform control system simulations.

Topics include:
Programming using MATLAB
1. Numerical computation with MATLAB (basic operations and matrix calculations)
2. Vibration analysis using MATLAB (differential equations; spring–mass–damper models)
3. Signal processing using MATLAB (FFT: Fast Fourier Transform)
4. Control system analysis using MATLAB (transfer functions, Bode plots, transient response)
5. Control system design using Simulink (transient response, PID control)

Classes will be conducted primarily through exercises. Students are expected to prepare adequately before each class.
books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Students are expected to have a basic understanding of MATLAB usage as learned in the introductory AI course. Knowledge of programming languages such as C or Python is desirable.

Concurrent enrollment in Control Engineering (required) and Mechanical Dynamics II (elective), which supports understanding of vibration models, is recommended.

activityGoals.body: Be able to develop programs for input/output operations and numerical calculations.
Be able to solve differential equations using numerical methods.
Be able to perform frequency analysis using numerical computation.
Be able to plot transient responses and Bode diagrams for mechanical models.
Be able to simulate and evaluate system responses from control block diagrams.
Be able to develop and apply programs to solve problems in mechanical engineering.

title: 航空宇宙工学入門とキャリアデザイン
subtitle: Introduction to Aerospace Engineering and Career Design
keywords: Technologies Related to Aircraft and Spacecraft
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn about current and future technologies supporting the modern world.
(2) learn to think for oneself.
(3) establish a learning posture conducive to developing their future career.
(4) learn to think about the essence of phenomena and objects and to think about things logically.
(5) learn the ability to design in their major engineering field.
advice:
This is an introduction to engineering as it relates to aeronautics and astronautics. The objectives of this subject are shown below.

1. Understanding of the system of the Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics
2. Understanding the Role of Aircraft and Spacecraft-Related Technologies in Society
3. Obtaining the ability to investigate the essence of phenomena and objects through suitable exercises
4. Introduction to the research field
5. General exercises

Students should learn the relationship between engineering and society and the role of engineers.
Student should understand the importance of basic knowledge and attain a self-driven attitude toward learning in the department of aeronautics and astronautics.
The level of students’ achievement will be evaluated through reports and presentations with a view of their ability to convert their knowledge into practice.

title: 機械系製図Ⅰ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the principles of orthographic projection, which is the basis of mechanical drawing.
(2) learn the ability to accurately create 2D&3D drawings according to the third angle projection method.
(3) practice 2D-CAD&3D-CAD and handwritten drafting to create and edit drawings efficiently.
advice:
Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas.
Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions.
This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings.
We will cover the following topics:
1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons
2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings
3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises
4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures
5. Size tolerance and fit
6. The role of CAE in manufacturing
books: Textbooks: New JIS mechanical drawing (6th edition) , Morita Kita Publishing (in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Siemens NX ,Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese) Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Lectures are “stacked” learning (work on new subjects is based on the knowledge and abilities acquired in the previous week's class). Therefore, students should review the material in the weekly lectures thoroughly and fully understand it by the next lecture. Reference materials and assignment diagrams used in the class will be distributed using the electronic syllabus of this course. A network printer can be used.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the principles of orthographic projection and express the shape of machine parts.
Be able to understand the basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings and draw drawings.
Be able to draw front, top, and side views of machine parts.
Be able to sketch mechanical parts accurately and create hand-drawn mechanical drawings based on these sketches.
Be able to create machine drawings using 2D-CAD & 3D-CAD figure creation and figure editing functions.

title: 航空機の原理
subtitle: Principle of Aircraft
educationalGoal: An aircraft and its components are designed by combining knowledge of engineering fields such as aerodynamics, structure, engine and control. In order to begin studying in specialized fields, it is important to know the relationship between what is learned in each field and the aircraft. In this course, students will learn how the mechanical elements of aircraft relate to mechanisms and principles through lectures and practical training.
advice:
This course includes lectures and practical training.
In lectures, students will learn aerodynamic forces acting on aircraft, aircraft flight stability, aircraft structural configurations and materials, and aircraft engines without using mathematical formulas nor technical drawings. Moreover, students will also learn the names and outlines of the major subjects in the department of aeronautics which deal with each engineering field.
In practical training, students will learn the basic mechanisms and operating principles of airspeed gauges of aircraft through disassembling and assembling them.
requiredKnowledge: Since this subject is an introductory subject in the curriculum of the department of aeronautics, this subject requires no prior knowledge nor skills.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain how the aircraft wing generates the lift.
Be able to explain aircraft static flight stability, especially pitch static stability.
Be able to explain the types of aircraft materials and their mechanical properties.
Be able to explain the types of aircraft engines and their major components.
Be able explain the relationships between the major subjects of department of aeronautics.
Be able to understand how the aircraft airspeed gauge operates while disassembling and assembling it.

5.Introduction to major subjects

              An aircraft and its components are designed by combining knowledge of engineering fields such as aerodynamics, structure, engine and control. In order to begin studying in specialized fields, it is important to know the relationship between what is learned in each field and the aircraft. In this course, students will learn how the mechanical elements of aircraft relate to mechanisms and principles through lectures and practical training.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course includes lectures and practical training.
In lectures, students will learn aerodynamic forces acting on aircraft, aircraft flight stability, aircraft structural configurations and materials, and aircraft engines without using mathematical formulas nor technical drawings. Moreover, students will also learn the names and outlines of the major subjects in the department of aeronautics which deal with each engineering field.
In practical training, students will learn the basic mechanisms and operating principles of airspeed gauges of aircraft through disassembling and assembling them.

title: 機械系製図Ⅱ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing II
educationalGoal: Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.
advice:
In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises.
In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I".
It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture.
The contents handled in this lecture are as follows.
・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing
・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance
・ Surface roughness   ・ Dimension filling method  ・ Bolts and nuts  ・ Keys and keyways
・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings
・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints
In addition, it is necessary to be able to fully understand the design at the actual manufacturing site.
 Copying in drafting drawings is against the ethics of engineers, and credits for this subject are revoked when it is found.
books: Textbooks:New JIS mechanical drawing(5th edition),Moritika Publishing(in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Solid Edge,Kanazawa Institute of Technology(in Japanese) Reference books:None Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge:
(1) You can draw on the CAD software drawing creation screen. Your ability should be at a level where it is easy to create a model of the text “Mechanical Drawing”. Basically, items that should have been learned in Mechanical Drawing I (functions written in the text, drawing methods) are not taught in this course.
(2) 3D (3D objects) can be modeled using 3D drafting, the 3rd angle method (2D drafting) and using two-dimensional drafting (plan view, front view, side view). (3) You have mastered the method of downloading materials and uploading reports using the student portal.

Be able to draw a two-dimensional mechanical drawing from a bird's-eye view or a photograph of the machine parts
Be able to imagine the shape of a part drawn from a two-dimensional mechanical drawing created by a third party.
Be able to indicate the machine design, tolerance, and accuracy for the manufacturing method of machine parts.
Be able to prepare and explain the results of preparation and review as works at the specified time.
Be able to explain the design process and role at the manufacturing site.

              学習・教育目標

              1.JIS standards and mechanical drawings
2.Mechanical design
3.Manufacturing methods and accuracy/tolerance
4.CAD
5.Three-dimensional data

              Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises.
In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I".
It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture.
The contents handled in this lecture are as follows.
・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing
・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance
・ Surface roughness   ・ Dimension filling method  ・ Bolts and nuts  ・ Keys and keyways
・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings
・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints
In addition, it is necessary to be able to fully understand the design at the actual manufacturing site.
 Copying in drafting drawings is against the ethics of engineers, and credits for this subject are revoked when it is found.

              Textbooks:New JIS mechanical drawing(5th edition),Moritika Publishing(in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Solid Edge,Kanazawa Institute of Technology(in Japanese) Reference books:None Reserved books:None

Basically, items that should have been learned in Mechanical Drawing I (functions written in the text, drawing methods) are not taught in this course.
(2) 3D (3D objects) can be modeled using 3D drafting, the 3rd angle method (2D drafting) and using two-dimensional drafting (plan view, front view, side view). (3) You have mastered the method of downloading materials and uploading reports using the student portal.

title: 工業力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Engineering Mechanics II
keywords: Rectilinear and Angular Motions of Rigid Bodies
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the kinematics of particles and rigid bodies under forces and moments
(2) learn the basic concepts of Newton's laws of motion
(3) learn the basic concepts of inertial forces and moments of inertia
(4) learn the plane motion of rigid bodies
(5) learn the basis of angular motion of rigid bodies and torques
(6) research the application to real structures in their localities
advice:
This is a basic course of dynamics of machines. The following subjects will be covered:
1. Rectilinear motion of a particle (horizontal motion) and the concepts of position, velocity and acceleration
2. Motion of a freely falling body (vertical motion),curvilinear motion of a particle,and motion of projectile
3. Rotational motion of a particle, tangential and normal components of acceleration, and relative motion of
   two particles
4. The basis of Newtonian Mechanics, Newton's Laws of Motion, and Equation of Motion
5. Inertia force, D’Alembert's Principle, rotational motion of a particle, and centrifugal force
6. Rotational motion of a rigid body and the moments of inertia of masses
7. Theorems of the moment of inertia; Parallel-axis Theorem, and Vertical-axis Theorem of the moment of inertia
8. Moments of inertia of common geometric shapes such as slender rod, thin rectangular plate, rectangular
   prism, thin disk, circular cylinder, and sphere
9. Rolling motion of a rigid body, combination of momentum and angular momentum, Equation of angular motion
Students will be expected to understand the meaning of technical terms and formulas.
Students will be expected to solve the exercises by themselves.
Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class because the schedules of quizzes, tests
   and reports may be changed as the class progresses.
Students should not be absent from the class as the handouts may not be received.

title: 材料力学
subtitle: Strength of  Materials
educationalGoal: Strength of Materials clarify the forces and deformations of various parts of bridges, towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, etc. These results can be used for design safety. It is an important subject that forms the basis of mechanical engineering. In this course, students should gain a thorough understanding of the basics of the strength of materials through lectures and practice. Students will explore examples of structures in the community where material mechanics is utilized, and will also make effective use of generative AI.
advice:
Students must thoroughly learn the following as the necessary basic knowledge for engineers at any stage of their career.
It is important to work through many exercise answers, but the study of strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand by just memorizing formulas and patterns. For all problems, students will start from an understanding of the basic formula and solve the problem by setting appropriate boundary conditions for the problem.

1. Stress and strain, 2. Hooke’s law, 3. Mechanical properties of materials, 4. Allowable stress and safety factors,
5. Frame structure, 6. Thermal stress, 7. Stress concentration,
8. Thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure,
9. Beams and their supporting conditions, 10. Shearing force and bending moment of a beam,
11. Stress on beams, 12. Deflection of beams

Furthermore, students should understand the real applications of structure by applying strength of materials in their locality.
books:
Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: Unspecified
Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: As a prerequisite, it is necessary to fully understand the course Industrial Mechanics I. Students need to fully understand the content of this course as the basis of the courses Mechanics of Aircraft Structure and Design of Aircraft Structure in later semesters.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain concept of normal stress, shear stress, normal strain, shear strain and Hooke's law.
Be able to explain deformation and fracturing behavior of materials by drawing stress-strain characteristics.
Be able to explain relationship between material properties, reference strength and the allowable stress.
Be able to explain stress in frame structure and thermal stress, and also explain stress concentration.
Be able to explain the shearing force and bending moment occurring in a beam by drawing SFDs and BMDs.
Be able to determine the stress and deflection occurring in a beam and to design safe structures.

              授業科目の学習・教育目標

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Stress, Strain
2.Tension, Compression
3.Beams
4.Regional collaboration

              Strength of Materials clarify the forces and deformations of various parts of bridges, towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, etc. These results can be used for design safety. It is an important subject that forms the basis of mechanical engineering. In this course, students should gain a thorough understanding of the basics of the strength of materials through lectures and practice. Students will explore examples of structures in the community where material mechanics is utilized, and will also make effective use of generative AI.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Students must thoroughly learn the following as the necessary basic knowledge for engineers at any stage of their career.
It is important to work through many exercise answers, but the study of strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand by just memorizing formulas and patterns. For all problems, students will start from an understanding of the basic formula and solve the problem by setting appropriate boundary conditions for the problem.

1. Stress and strain, 2. Hooke’s law, 3. Mechanical properties of materials, 4. Allowable stress and safety factors,
5. Frame structure, 6. Thermal stress, 7. Stress concentration,
8. Thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure,
9. Beams and their supporting conditions, 10. Shearing force and bending moment of a beam,
11. Stress on beams, 12. Deflection of beams

Furthermore, students should understand the real applications of structure by applying strength of materials in their locality.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: Unspecified
Reserved books: Unspecified

              As a prerequisite, it is necessary to fully understand the course Industrial Mechanics I. Students need to fully understand the content of this course as the basis of the courses Mechanics of Aircraft Structure and Design of Aircraft Structure in later semesters.

title: 流れ学Ⅰ
subtitle: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the fundamentals of fluid dynamics and aerodynamics
(2) learn the fluid properties of air because aircraft fly in the air
(3) learn the measurement principles of fluid devices
(4) learn fundamental equations and their application
advice:
This is a fundamental fluid dynamics and aerodynamics course. Students will learn fluid properties, fluid statics, inviscid flow, and incompressible flow. We will cover the following materials:

1. Fluid properties and flow phenomena: units and dimensions, fluid properties, fluid statics
2. Forces and moments on a body: pressure, hydrostatic pressure, manometer, buoyancy
3. Fluid and body dynamics: fundamentals of fluids, continuity equation, Bernoulli equation
4. Laws of similarity: flow similarity, dimensionless numbers (Reynolds, Mach numbers)

Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests and reports may change as the class progresses.
Students are expected to solve the exercises by themselves to understand the course.
Students are also expected to review their notebooks for better understanding.
Students are expected to actively participate in the presentation and discussion.

title: 航空材料力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Mechanics of Materials for Aeronautics I
educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) Bars with circular cross section under torsional moment
(2) Stress-strain relationship for 3D elastic body and elastic
    bodies under plane-stress or plane-strain conditions
(3) Normal and shear stresses on an arbitrary cross section of
    slender bar under uniaxial tensile load
(4) Combined stress problem
advice:
On the basis of 'Industrial Mechanics' and 'Strength of Materials', students will study advanced topics
in Strength of Materials.
We will cover the following materials:

(1) Torsion of bars with circular cross section
(2) Relationship between stress and strain (for 3D elastic body or 2D elastic body under plane-stress
    or plane-strain)
(3) Normal and shear stresses on an arbitrary cross section of slender bar under uniaxial tensile load
(4) Combined stress problem (principal stresses and principal shear stress, Mohr's stress circle)

Students should thoroughly review what they have learned in  'Industrial Mechanics' and
'Strength of Materials' before taking this course.
books: Required materials will be specified in the first lesson.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of industrial mechanics and mechanics of materials.

activityGoals.body: Be able to calculate torsional stiffness and shear stress of bars with circular cross sections
Be able to express the relationship between stresses and strains for plane-stress and plane-strain
Be able to calculate normal and shear stresses on an arbitrary cross section of slender bar under tension
Be able to calculate principal stresses and principal shear stress of thin flat plate under in-plane load
Be able to draw the Mohr's stress circle and obtain principal stress and principal shear stress from it

title: 飛行力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Dynamics of Flight I
educationalGoal: The “dynamics of flight” is the foundation of aeronautical engineering. In this course, students will learn what kind of forces act on an aircraft in flight and learn about the balance and dynamics characteristics for stable flight.
advice:

Next, students will learn to analyze qualities of flight after learning linearization of the equation of motion.
In addition to learning design standards, students will deepen their understanding of qualities of flight by learning the basics of flight control.

title: 振動工学
subtitle: Vibration Engineering
educationalGoal: Structural vibration behavior should be well investigated in the process of aircraft structural design. For example, to design a wing structure, it is necessary to clarify its vibration behaviors such as its response to a gust load and its bending-torsional flutter property. In this course, students will learn the basics of vibration engineering necessary to treat practical problems on structural vibration in aircrafts.
advice:
In order to understand the nature of structural vibration, students will learn how to express the motions of various vibration systems in mathematical equations, how to solve the equations, and how to examine the meanings of the obtained solutions. Students are required not only to study actively during the class but also to work hard on exams and assignments.

In this course, we will cover the following materials:
1. Basic knowledge of vibration in mechanical systems
     Types of vibration, Harmonic vibration, Synthesis of vibration
2. Response of single degree of freedom systems to initial excitation
     Undamped or damped systems, viscous damping, coulomb damping
3. Response of single degree of freedom systems to harmonic excitation
     Response to harmonic force or harmonic displacement excitation, Vibration isolation
4. Response of single degree of freedom systems to nonperiodic excitation
     Impulse response, Inditial response
5. Vibration measurement and control
     Vibration measurement, seismic system
books: Vibration Engineering, Third edition (in Japanese), Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge:
Knowledge of Industrial Mechanics and Mechanical Mechanics.
Basic knowledge of industrial mechanics, including equilibrium (balance) of forces and the equation of motion for an accelerated object.

activityGoals.body: Be able to create an analysis model for the structural vibration
Be able to derive equations of motion based on the analysis model and solve them
Be able to explain the resonance phenomenon
Be able to explain the effect of the damping on responses to both initial excitation and harmonic excitation
Be able to analyze the simple vibration problems and capture the nature of the phenomenon

title: 電気数学Ⅰ
subtitle: Mathematics for Electrical and Electronic Engineering I
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to learn the basic mathematics related to electrical and electronic engineering, and to acquire basic knowledge of electricity, such as electrical circuits, electromagnetism, and electronic circuits. The aim is also to cultivate the ability to apply this knowledge to specific problems through physical and mathematical considerations. This course is the basis for the subsequent “Mathematics for Electrical and Electronic Engineering Ⅱ” and “Electric Circuits I” courses.
advice:
Development of basic mathematical skills:
Students will learn about methods of solving linear simultaneous equations using substitution, addition and subtraction, and determinants, as well as basic functions (trigonometric ratios, trigonometric functions, exponential functions, logarithmic functions), complex numbers, and other topics that will be widely required in the future in the basic mathematics for  electrical and electronic Engineering.
books: A textbook written in Japanese will be used.
requiredKnowledge: This course is an introduction to the field of electrical and electronic engineering. It is important to review mathematics (simultaneous equations, trigonometric functions, exponential functions, etc.) learned in high school for future learning. It is desirable to study areas that were not taken in high school using self-study and learning support systems in our university.

To understand how to calculate basic functions

title: 電気回路基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits
educationalGoal: This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering curriculum. The objective is to acquire a basic knowledge of electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze and design electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will learn about electric circuits having resistance (R) that are connected to DC power sources. Particular emphasis will be placed on how to formulate and solve the network equations based on Ohm’s law and Kirchhoff’s law.
advice:
Below is an outline of the topics to be covered:

DC circuits: electric circuits and Ohm’s law, Kirchhoff’s law, superposition principle, Thevenin’s Theorem, Δ-Y conversion, electric power, electric power quantity Calculation

This subject is not only important as preparation for subsequent courses (Electrical Circuit I, Electrical Circuit II, and Electrical Circuit III), but also each specialized topic should be studied keeping in mind that it is a special basic course requirement.
Since the progress is adjusted while checking the level of student understanding indicated by quiz results, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and the course content.
books: Basic electric circuit (2nd edition) New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: It is important that you solve as many problems as possible in order to understand and practice the theory presented. In addition, continuous effort is required on a daily basis. Therefore, we encourage you to 1) examine various reference books, 2) ask the lecturer questions, and 3) take advantage of the Mathematical and Science Education Research Center so that you can clarify what you don’t understand.

activityGoals.body: Participants can explain Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s law in DC circuits.
Participants can formulate and solve equations for DC networks.
Participants can calculate the maximum power condition in DC circuits.
Participants can calculate DC circuits using the superposition principle and Thevenin's theorem.

Using their knowledge, they can correctly calculate voltages, currents, and energy in DC circuits. They can also fully explain the equilibrium conditions of a bridge circuit. They can sufficiently explain the superposition principle and Thevenin’s theorem and correctly apply them to DC circuits.
achievementLevels.standard: Participants can explain the basic physical and mathematical implications of Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s laws. Using their knowledge, they can calculate voltages, currents and energy in the DC circuits. They can also explain the equilibrium conditions of a bridge circuit. They can explain the superposition principle and Thevenin’s theorem and apply them to DC circuits.

title: 電気回路Ⅱ（先取り履修・オンデマンド授業）
subtitle: Electric Circuit II
keywords: Electric power, Maximum electric power problem
educationalGoal: In this course, students will acquire basic knowledge of AC in electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze AC circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. It deals with basic circuits of resistance (R), inductance (L) or capacitance (C), which are a review of "Electrical Circuit I", to slightly complicated application circuits that combine them. Here, students will learn the circuit analysis method by the symbolic method and acquire the basics of the advanced analysis method required in the subsequent "Electrical Circuit III".
advice:
1.	Phasor of a complex number and symbolic method of AC circuit
2.	Series and parallel connection of complex impedance and complex admittance
3.	Phase condition problem in series-parallel circuit
4.	Series resonant circuit and parallel resonant circuit
5.	Calculation of the electric power, complex electric power and maximum electric power problem by symbolic method
books: Basic electric circuit(2nd edition)New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: In this course, it is important to solve more problems in order to understand the theory and put it into practice. Moreover, since they are one by one, continuous efforts are required. Therefore, do not leave what you do not understand, so be sure to clear 1) check various reference books, 2) ask the teachers, 3) use the Mathematics Education Center. In this course, students use mathematical equations such as simultaneous linear equations, determinants, matrices, differentiation / integration, basics of complex numbers, and trigonometric functions.

To be able to calculate the phase condition problems of series and parallel circuits and basic problems of AC
To be able to calculate the problems of series and parallel resonant circuits using symbolic method
To be able to calculate the power problems using symbolic method

title: 電気磁気学Ⅰ
subtitle: Electromagnetics I
educationalGoal: The learning and educational goal is to acquire basic knowledge of electricity and to acquire basic electrical and electronic abilities that can be applied to specific problems through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will acquire the basic mathematics necessary for analyzing various physical phenomena in "electromagnetism", the basic rules regarding electric charges, electric fields, potentials, and capacitances in electrostatic fields, and the ability to solve problems of electrostatic fields.
advice:
The class covers the following items.
Chapter 1 : Charge and Coulomb force (Phenomenon to charge, charge and properties, conductor and nonconductor, electrostatic induction, Coulomb's law, Coulomb force, Coulomb force and plane coordinates, composition of multiple Coulomb forces in plane coordinates, Coulomb force and space coordinates)
Chapter 2 : Electric field and electric potential (electric field, synthetic electric field by multiple electric charges, synthetic electric field by electric charge distributed continuously, electric field lines, small area passing, lines of electric force, potential, potential due to multiple charges, equipotential surface, spatial representation of potential, Gauss's law and its application)
Chapter 3 : Capacitance of conductor system (the nature of charged conductor, capacitance, capacitance of various conductor systems, electric imaging method, contact of capacitor, Energy of the capacitor)
Chapter 4 : Dielectrics (Dielectric properties, polarization, electric field and electric flux density in dielectric, electric field and electric flux density in two dielectrics, conduction with dielectric energy stored between bodies, force between conductors filled with dielectrics)
Chapter 5 : Current (Transfer of charge, ohm's law, resistance and resistor, conductance and conductivity, Joule heat and power, electric field in conductor, current density)
If necessary, learning may take place using digital methods such as online (distance) or on-demand classes.
books:
Textbook，A.Mikami, M.Masahiko, S.Makino, Y.Fujita, H.Yanagibashi,"Basic electromgnetics Ⅰ",
Kanazawa Institute of Technology,(2026)
requiredKnowledge:
This class is an introductory subject of "electromagnetics", and it is planned to take "electromagnetics II" and "electromagnetics III". So, the following background knowledge and skills are required.
1. Review the basic mathematics such as functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, vector analysis.
2. In electromagnetics, many new "units" are used. Understand the main units of physical quantities and the configuration of unit systems.
3. Be aware of the definitions and key formulas of technical terms.

activityGoals.body: The nature of charge, the Coulomb law acting between charges can be understood.
Understanding the relationship between electric field and potential formed by charge, and using Gauss's law.
The basic problem of the capacitance of a conductor system, electrostatic energy can be solved.
Understanding the electrical polarization of dielectrics.

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Charge and coulomb force
2.Electric field and electric potential
3.Capacitance of conductor system
4.Dielectric material
5.Online/ On-demand class

              The learning and educational goal is to acquire basic knowledge of electricity and to acquire basic electrical and electronic abilities that can be applied to specific problems through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will acquire the basic mathematics necessary for analyzing various physical phenomena in "electromagnetism", the basic rules regarding electric charges, electric fields, potentials, and capacitances in electrostatic fields, and the ability to solve problems of electrostatic fields.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              The class covers the following items.
Chapter 1 : Charge and Coulomb force (Phenomenon to charge, charge and properties, conductor and nonconductor, electrostatic induction, Coulomb's law, Coulomb force, Coulomb force and plane coordinates, composition of multiple Coulomb forces in plane coordinates, Coulomb force and space coordinates)
Chapter 2 : Electric field and electric potential (electric field, synthetic electric field by multiple electric charges, synthetic electric field by electric charge distributed continuously, electric field lines, small area passing, lines of electric force, potential, potential due to multiple charges, equipotential surface, spatial representation of potential, Gauss's law and its application)
Chapter 3 : Capacitance of conductor system (the nature of charged conductor, capacitance, capacitance of various conductor systems, electric imaging method, contact of capacitor, Energy of the capacitor)
Chapter 4 : Dielectrics (Dielectric properties, polarization, electric field and electric flux density in dielectric, electric field and electric flux density in two dielectrics, conduction with dielectric energy stored between bodies, force between conductors filled with dielectrics)
Chapter 5 : Current (Transfer of charge, ohm's law, resistance and resistor, conductance and conductivity, Joule heat and power, electric field in conductor, current density)
If necessary, learning may take place using digital methods such as online (distance) or on-demand classes.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Textbook，A.Mikami, M.Masahiko, S.Makino, Y.Fujita, H.Yanagibashi,"Basic electromgnetics Ⅰ",
Kanazawa Institute of Technology,(2026)

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              This class is an introductory subject of "electromagnetics", and it is planned to take "electromagnetics II" and "electromagnetics III". So, the following background knowledge and skills are required.
1. Review the basic mathematics such as functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, vector analysis.
2. In electromagnetics, many new "units" are used. Understand the main units of physical quantities and the configuration of unit systems.
3. Be aware of the definitions and key formulas of technical terms.

title: 電気数学Ⅱ（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Mathematics for Electrical and Electronic Engineering II
educationalGoal: This subject continues from "Mathematical Basics for Engineering I" in the first semester of the first year and is the base of "Basic for of Engineers" in the second year. While learning the fundamentals of mathematics, students will establish the foundation of their thinking and learning attitude as an engineer.
advice:
1.Introduction of research fields
Students will learn about the research area in the field of electrical and electronic engineering, and will learn about the research efforts in that area through some specific examples.

2. Development of mathematical skills
Students will review and have trainings on differentiation (differentiation method, derivatives of commonly used functions, and application of differentiation), integration (indefinite integration, definite integration, and application of integration), and vector (vector basics, vector and plane coordinates, vector and space coordinates, scalar product, and vector product), which will be widely needed in their future.
books: A textbook written in Japanese will be used.
requiredKnowledge: This course is an introduction to the field of electrical and electronic engineering. It is important to pay close attention to the technology in which each student is interested. It is also important to review mathematics (functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, exponential functions, vectors, differential methods, integration methods, and etc.) learned in high school for future learning. It is desirable to study areas that were not taken in high school using self-study and learning support systems in our university.

activityGoals.body: To Understand the role of the Faculty of Engineering in modern society and to make your own study plan.
To understand the basics of thinking as an engineer and the attitude of learning.

              This subject continues from "Mathematical Basics for Engineering I" in the first semester of the first year and is the base of "Basic for of Engineers" in the second year. While learning the fundamentals of mathematics, students will establish the foundation of their thinking and learning attitude as an engineer.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              1.Introduction of research fields
Students will learn about the research area in the field of electrical and electronic engineering, and will learn about the research efforts in that area through some specific examples.

2. Development of mathematical skills
Students will review and have trainings on differentiation (differentiation method, derivatives of commonly used functions, and application of differentiation), integration (indefinite integration, definite integration, and application of integration), and vector (vector basics, vector and plane coordinates, vector and space coordinates, scalar product, and vector product), which will be widely needed in their future.

              A textbook written in Japanese will be used.

It is also important to review mathematics (functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, exponential functions, vectors, differential methods, integration methods, and etc.) learned in high school for future learning. educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) understand "Academic Field" of the two courses in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering.
(2) understand the specialized subject groups in each field, which start from 3rd term.
(3) understand outlines of the subject group to determine the specialized field.
(4) summarize study and registration plans using logical sentences.
advice:
This is a career design course to clarify future field of student and the image of electrical / electronic engineers and researchers. Students will understand what to learn from now on, and make study and registration plans using logical sentences.
1. Self-analysis and career design
Students will investigate technical trends and industry/corporate with relation to electric and electronic engineering, and set goals for higher education/employment.
2. Understanding specialized fields and required subjects in the course (compulsory subject)
Through classes and surveys, students will understand outlines of specialized fields and required subjects (compulsory subjects) for electrical engineering course and electronic engineering course. In addition, students will understand the relationship between laboratories in Design project III and the required subjects of each course.
3. Determination of course and making study/registration plans
Students will determine their course and clarify their learning objectives. After that, students will summarize their study/registration plans from 4th term.
books: No textbooks will be used.
requiredKnowledge:
(1) Students should actively ask questions and deepen their understanding.
(2) Students are encouraged to take specialized subjects so as to take into account their future design.
(3) It is important to read the textbooks used for each subject on a daily basis and to try to understand the context by remembering the meaning of the technical terms in the subject.

title: 電気回路Ⅲ
subtitle: Electric Circuits III
educationalGoal: In this class, including a review of Electric Circuit I and II, contents from the basic circuit combining resistance (R), inductance (L) or capacitance (C) and their combination to a slightly more complex AC circuit are learned. In the calculation of an AC circuit, it is no exaggeration to say that it is common sense to use a so-called symbolic solution using phasors and complex numbers. In the subsequent course Electric Circuit IV, the circuit analysis techniques using symbolic solution becomes the base for learning more advanced and complex analysis methods.
advice:
1 Mutual induction
2 Useful theorems
3 Two-port circuit
4 Phasor trajectory

In addition, since the progress is adjusted while confirming the degree of understanding from the result of the quiz or the like, the schedule of the class and the learning content may be changed. Active learnings, that is, exercises, quizzes, presentation discussions, questions and answers, short breaks, etc. are conducted so that students concentrate on classes. Depending on the presence of Humanity and Nature Seminar, times and contents of review class may change (follow the instructions of the professor in charge)
books: Basic electric circuit(2nd edition)New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: In this course, it is important to solve more problems in order to understand the theory and put it into practice. Moreover, since it is the accumulation of learning one by one, daily continuous efforts are required. Therefore, you are required to do things like 1. Check various reference books, 2. Ask the professor in charge, 3. Use the Mathematics Education Center so that you can always clear things that you do not understand. In this classes, Mathematics such as simultaneous linear equations, determinants, matrices, differentiation / integration, basics of complex numbers, and trigonometric functions are utilized.

activityGoals.body: The mutual induction phenomenon can be explained. The basic mutual induction can be analyzed.
The electric circuits can be solved using useful theorems.
In a two-terminal pair circuit, calculations using at least Z, Y, and F matrix.
The problem of phasor trajectory can be solved using symbolic solutions.

              In this class, including a review of Electric Circuit I and II, contents from the basic circuit combining resistance (R), inductance (L) or capacitance (C) and their combination to a slightly more complex AC circuit are learned. In the calculation of an AC circuit, it is no exaggeration to say that it is common sense to use a so-called symbolic solution using phasors and complex numbers. educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn basic analog electronic circuits consisting of diode or transistor.
(2) understand basic amplifiers with bipolar transistor.
(3) understand design methods of analog electronic circuits.
(4) learn circuits and mechanisms of FET or operational amplifier.
(5) learn pulse circuits such as multi-vibrator.

title: 電気電子プログラミング
subtitle: Programming for Electrical and Electronic Engineering
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the fundamental concepts and methods of programming using C language. (2) learn how to solve problems and transform the solutions into computer programs written in C language. The goal of this course is to provide an introduction not just to C but also to logical thinking. (3) learn some applications of C programming in electrical and electronic engineering.
advice:
This course is designed to familiarize students with computer programming, with an emphasis on a widely used language, C.
The classes incorporate lecture with hands-on programming exercises.
We will cover the following materials:
1. Elementary programming in C
2. Selection statements
3. Repetition statements
4. Modular programming with functions
a. Integrated learning  - For applied problems related to the field of electrical and electronic engineering -
b. Overview of advanced C language syntax

Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the detailed course schedules may change depending on the students' progress in understanding.
books:
Textbooks: None
Reference books: None
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
You are expected to bring your Windows laptop to class with you to work on programming exercises.
No prior programming knowledge is required.
This course and “Computer Engineering for Electrical and Electronic Engineers” are complementary. “Feedback Control” is related to this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to demonstrate problem-solving skills by developing algorithms to solve problems.
Be able to write C programs that perform sequential operations.
Be able to incorporate the selection control structure into C programs.
Be able to incorporate the repetition control structure into C programs.
Be able to decompose the solution into modules at the function level.

title: 過渡現象論
subtitle: Transient Phenomena in Linear Circuits
educationalGoal:
The aim of this course is to help students acquire the necessary knowledge needed to understand the theory to learn in “Feedback Control” course in the 5th term.
Students will:
(1) solve transient electrical circuits using circuit equations and initial conditions.
(2) analyze transient phenomena of more complex circuits by Laplace transform.
(3) understand the various transient phenomena that occur in electrical circuits.
advice:
1. Transient phenomena and differential equation (circuit equations)
     Learn the basics needed to analyze transient phenomena.
     //Transient phenomena and steady phenomena, differential equations of electrical circuits and its solutions

2. Transient phenomena of electrical circuits
     Solve the transient phenomena of various circuits according to the solution of differential equation.
     //AC and DC circuit of RC, RL, LC, and LCR

3. Analysis by Laplace transform
     Learn how to analyze transient phenomena in electrical circuits using Laplace transform.
     //Laplace transform and inverse transform, Laplace transform for functions and its application to circuits.

There is possibility to change the learning contents (progress) of the course schedule depending on the situation.
Exercises, quizzes, discussions and questions, etc. are included to help students concentrate on this class.
The order of learning may be changed as needed, and digital technology may be used for learning such as online (remote) or on-demand classes.
books: Some materials will be shown in lecture.
requiredKnowledge:
1. Fundamentals of electrical circuits.
2. Fundamentals of mathematics such as exponential, trigonometric function, differential and integral, etc.
3. Attitude to take each class seriously and review and deepen understanding.
4. Attitude to learn theoretical thinking and applied methods through exercises without relying on memorization.

title: 電気計測
subtitle: Electrical Measurement
educationalGoal: Electrical and electronic measurements are a way of measuring various electrical quantities. In some cases, it is possible to step out of the world of electronics and measure physical quantities such as length, weight, and speed. In this lecture, the students will learn what the units and measurement terms are and how to apply them. Additionally, they will learn the construction and measurement principles behind major electrical and electronic equipment so that they can understand the fundamentals of electric and electronic measurements.
advice:
We will cover the following materials
(1) Fundamental Instrumentation
  SI unit, Standard apparatus, measurement terminology
(2) Pointer type meter
  moving coil type, moving iron type, rectifier type, etc.
(3) Electrical instrumentation apparatus
    Electronic galvanometer, Electronic power meter
(4) Digital Instrumentation apparatus
  digital voltmeter
(5) Recording Instrument and waveform measurement
 Pen recorder, oscilloscope
(6) Various electrical quantities instrument
      Voltage, current, resistor, power, frequency, magnetic field, etc.
requiredKnowledge: All you need to study this subject is to understand the basic electric circuits and basic electromagnetics you have already learned.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the measurement terminology and to used SI unit.
Be able to explain the basic block diagram of electrical instrumentation apparatus(mainly analog type)
Be able to explain the basic block diagram of electrical instrumentation apparatus(mainly digital type)
Be able to explain the various measuring apparatus, oscilloscope, impedance bridge, frequency counter.
Be able to choose the variable measuring apparatus in the intended purpose.

title: 電気エネルギー発生工学
subtitle: Electric Power Generation
educationalGoal:
Students will
(1) learn the working principles and systems of thermal power plants
(2) learn the working principles and systems of nuclear power plants
(3) learn the various renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, geothermal and fuel cell.
(3) learn the working principle and systems of a hydro power plant
advice:
Course Description
1. Outline (the demand for electrical energy)
2. Thermal power plant

3. Nuclear power plant
3.1 Principle, basic fundamentals of nuclear fission  3.2 Facilities and reactor types  3.3 Basics safety principles   3.4 Plutonium use in a thermal reactor, nuclear fuel cycle, and nuclear waste treatment
4. Renewable energy
4.1 Solar power   4.2 Wind power   4.3 Geothermal power plant   4.4 Fuel cell
5. Hydro power plant
5.1 Principle, basic fundamentals for hydraulics   5.2 Facilities  5.3 Output and efficiency calculation
Expectations for Students
To understand the lecture well, basic knowledge about physics such as thermodynamics, hydraulics etc. is required.

To be able to calculate energy efficiency for various hydro power plants and to explain various devices

(2)Students will learn Fourier series of periodic wave.

title: 電子回路Ⅱ
subtitle: Electronic Circuits II
educationalGoal: Electronic circuits is a very important topic. In this subject, Digital Circuits, the objective is to learn the fndamentals of Boolean equations (logic algebra) and logic circuits, and to understand the principles behind how various logic circuits operate.In addition to combined logic circuits such as AND, OR, and NOT gates, the students will learn to understand and explain the operating principles of sequential circuits such as flip-flops and counters as well as more functional circuits such as analog to digital(A/D) and digital to analog (D/A) converters.
advice:
We will cover the following materials.
1. Fundamental logic circuits and boolean function
   AND, OR, NOT, EX-OR
2. Design for combination logical circuit
   Conversion circuit (NAND, NOR)
   Simplification using the karnaugh map
   Logical circuit design
   Adder Circuit
3. Flip Flop(FF) Circuit
    Synchronous / asynchronous 4 types of FF
    RS-FF, JK-FF, T-FF, D-FF
4. Counter Circuit
   Synchronous/asynchronous type UP/DOWN counter
   Ripple counter
   Shift resister
5. A/D and D/A converter circuit
   Principle and design
books: wakaru dejitaru densikairo   nishin syuppan
requiredKnowledge: All you need to study this subject is to understand the physical electronics and basic electric circuit.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the digital electronics and fundamental logicl circuits.
Be able to design the basic combination logical circuit.
Be able to explain the 4 types for Flip Flop.
Be able to design the synchro and asynchro type digital counter circuit.
Be able to explain the principle opreration for A/D and D/A converter.

achievementLevels.ideal:
●To sufficiently explain the design of combined logic circuits (NAND, mutual conversion to NOR circuits, simplification using Karnaugh maps, Adder circuits, etc.).
● To sufficiently explain asynchronous/synchronous flip-flop circuits (Triggering FF circuits, RS-FF, JK-FF, T-FF, D-FF). In addition, the ability to apply multiple FF components to design digital circuits.
● The ability to explain synchronous counters, asynchronous counters, shift registers, and to design complex counter circuits.
● To sufficiently explain A/D and D/A converter basic construction and operation principles.
achievementLevels.standard:
● Have the ability to design basic combination logic circuits, and particularly be able to explain the simplification process using Karnaugh map.
● Be able to explain specifications for the 4 types of FFs.
● Be able to explain synchronous/asynchronous digital counters.
● Be able to explain the principle of A/D and D/A converter circuits.

title: 半導体工学基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Semiconductor Physics
educationalGoal: This course provides the foundational knowledge of semiconductors, which underpin all modern technological domains. Specifically, students gain an understanding of crystal structures, classical electron conduction models, the fundamentals of quantum mechanics, energy band theory, and semiconductor material properties from a microscopic perspective at the atomic and molecular level. Additionally, students learn the fundamentals of semiconductor manufacturing processes, such as high-purity crystal growth and photolithography.
advice:
In this course, you will learn the following topics:
(1) History and social context of semiconductor devices (Introduction)
(2) High-purity crystal growth and semiconductor device fabrication processes
(3) Crystal structure
(4) Classical electronic conduction models
(5) Fundamentals of quantum mechanics
(6) Energy band theory in solids
(7) Semiconductor properties and fundamentals of semiconductor devices
Regarding (1) and (2), we may utilize generative AI to investigate the latest information.
books: Denshi Buttusei [Morikita]
requiredKnowledge: Many students may find this subject somewhat more challenging compared to others. This is likely because you will be studying an entirely new branch of physics (quantum mechanics) that you have not encountered before. However, as you progress in understanding the “Fundamentals of Quantum Phenomena”;which reveal the essence of things;you will likely find it a truly fascinating subject. The key to studying this subject is to have a solid grasp of the physics (classical physics) and mathematics you have learned so far.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the role, physical properties, and fundamentals of semiconductor devices.
Be able to explain bonding forces and representative crystal structures.
The motion of electrons can be explained using the Drude theory, mobility, relaxation time, effective mass.
Understand the fundamentals of quantum mechanics and be able to apply the Schrodinger wave equation in practice.
Changes in energy levels of atoms, molecules, and crystalline states, and the formation of energy bands.
Using energy band theory, one can explain the differences between conductors, semiconductors, and insulators.

title: 電気電子キャリアデザイン
subtitle: Career Design for Electrical and Electronic Engineers
keywords: Recommended Subjects in the Specialized Field
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) understand "Academic Field" of the two courses in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering.
(2) understand the specialized subject groups in each field, which start from 3rd term.
(3) understand outlines of the subject group to determine the specialized field.
(4) summarize study and registration plans using logical sentences.
advice:
This is a career design course to clarify future field of student and the image of electrical / electronic engineers and researchers. Students will understand what to learn from now on, and make study and registration plans using logical sentences.
1. Self-analysis and career design
Students will investigate technical trends and industry/corporate with relation to electric and electronic engineering, and set goals for higher education/employment.
2. Understanding specialized fields and required subjects in the course (compulsory subject)
Through classes and surveys, students will understand outlines of specialized fields and required subjects (compulsory subjects) for electrical engineering course and electronic engineering course. In addition, students will understand the relationship between laboratories in Design project III and the required subjects of each course.
3. Determination of course and making study/registration plans
Students will determine their course and clarify their learning objectives. After that, students will summarize their study/registration plans from 4th term.
books: No textbooks will be used.
requiredKnowledge:
(1) Students should actively ask questions and deepen their understanding.
(2) Students are encouraged to take specialized subjects so as to take into account their future design.
(3) It is important to read the textbooks used for each subject on a daily basis and to try to understand the context by remembering the meaning of the technical terms in the subject.

(1) understand "Academic Field" of the two courses in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering.
(2) understand the specialized subject groups in each field, which start from 3rd term.
(3) understand outlines of the subject group to determine the specialized field.
(4) summarize study and registration plans using logical sentences.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is a career design course to clarify future field of student and the image of electrical / electronic engineers and researchers. Students will understand what to learn from now on, and make study and registration plans using logical sentences.
1. Self-analysis and career design
Students will investigate technical trends and industry/corporate with relation to electric and electronic engineering, and set goals for higher education/employment.
2. Understanding specialized fields and required subjects in the course (compulsory subject)
Through classes and surveys, students will understand outlines of specialized fields and required subjects (compulsory subjects) for electrical engineering course and electronic engineering course. In addition, students will understand the relationship between laboratories in Design project III and the required subjects of each course.
3. Determination of course and making study/registration plans
Students will determine their course and clarify their learning objectives. After that, students will summarize their study/registration plans from 4th term.

              No textbooks will be used.

              (1) Students should actively ask questions and deepen their understanding.
(2) Students are encouraged to take specialized subjects so as to take into account their future design.
(3) It is important to read the textbooks used for each subject on a daily basis and to try to understand the context by remembering the meaning of the technical terms in the subject.

educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn basic analog electronic circuits consisting of diode or transistor.
(2) understand basic amplifiers with bipolar transistor.
(3) understand design methods of analog electronic circuits.
(4) learn circuits and mechanisms of FET or operational amplifier.
(5) learn pulse circuits such as multi-vibrator.
advice:
Course outline is shown as follows:

1. Fundamental electric circuit
2. Circuit consisting of diode
3. Mechanism of transistor
4. Amplifier using bipolar transistor
5. Grounding methods, equivalent circuit for signal

title: 電気電子プログラミング
subtitle: Programming for Electrical and Electronic Engineering
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the fundamental concepts and methods of programming using C language. (2) learn how to solve problems and transform the solutions into computer programs written in C language. The goal of this course is to provide an introduction not just to C but also to logical thinking. (3) learn some applications of C programming in electrical and electronic engineering.
advice:
This course is designed to familiarize students with computer programming, with an emphasis on a widely used language, C.
The classes incorporate lecture with hands-on programming exercises.
We will cover the following materials:
1. Elementary programming in C
2. Selection statements
3. Repetition statements
4. Modular programming with functions
a. Integrated learning  - For applied problems related to the field of electrical and electronic engineering -
b. Overview of advanced C language syntax

Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the detailed course schedules may change depending on the students' progress in understanding.
books:
Textbooks: None
Reference books: やさしく学べるC言語 ANSI規格準拠[森北出版]、新・明解C言語 入門編（第2版）[SBクリエイティブ]、猫でもわかるC言語プログラミング（第3版）[SBクリエイティブ]
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
You are expected to bring your Windows laptop to class with you to work on programming exercises.
No prior programming knowledge is required.
This course and “Computer Engineering for Electrical and Electronic Engineers” are complementary. “Feedback Control” is related to this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to demonstrate problem-solving skills by developing algorithms to solve problems.
Be able to write C programs that perform sequential operations.
Be able to incorporate the selection control structure into C programs.
Be able to incorporate the repetition control structure into C programs.
Be able to decompose the solution into modules at the function level.
Be able to make a computer execute a program you have written in C language.

title: 過渡現象論
subtitle: Transient Phenomena in Linear Circuits
educationalGoal:
The aim of this course is to help students acquire the necessary knowledge needed to understand the theory to learn in “Feedback Control” course in the 5th term.
Students will:
(1) solve transient electrical circuits using circuit equations and initial conditions.
(2) analyze transient phenomena of more complex circuits by Laplace transform.
(3) understand the various transient phenomena that occur in electrical circuits.
advice:
1. Transient phenomena and differential equation (circuit equations)
     Learn the basics needed to analyze transient phenomena.
     //Transient phenomena and steady phenomena, differential equations of electrical circuits and its solutions

2. Transient phenomena of electrical circuits
     Solve the transient phenomena of various circuits according to the solution of differential equation.
     //AC and DC circuit of RC, RL, LC, and LCR

3. Analysis by Laplace transform
     Learn how to analyze transient phenomena in electrical circuits using Laplace transform.
     //Laplace transform and inverse transform, Laplace transform for functions and its application to circuits.

There is possibility to change the learning contents (progress) of the course schedule depending on the situation.
Exercises, quizzes, discussions and questions, etc. are included to help students concentrate on this class.
The order of learning may be changed as needed, and digital technology may be used for learning such as online (remote) or on-demand classes.
books: Some materials will be shown in lecture.
requiredKnowledge:
1. Fundamentals of electrical circuits.
2. Fundamentals of mathematics such as exponential, trigonometric function, differential and integral, etc.
3. Attitude to take each class seriously and review and deepen understanding.
4. Attitude to learn theoretical thinking and applied methods through exercises without relying on memorization.

activityGoals.body: Be able to show circuit equations (differential equation) from electric circuits.
Be able to show initial conditions from electric circuits and apply to circuit equations.
Be able to solve differential equations and express the transient phenomenon with equations.
Be able to graph transient phenomena based on the equations.
Be able to understand Laplace transform.
Be able to solve transient phenomena of electrical circuits by Laplace transform.

              1.Transient Analysis

5.Online/on-demand classes

              The aim of this course is to help students acquire the necessary knowledge needed to understand the theory to learn in “Feedback Control” course in the 5th term.
Students will:
(1) solve transient electrical circuits using circuit equations and initial conditions.
(2) analyze transient phenomena of more complex circuits by Laplace transform.
(3) understand the various transient phenomena that occur in electrical circuits.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              1. Transient phenomena and differential equation (circuit equations)
     Learn the basics needed to analyze transient phenomena.
     //Transient phenomena and steady phenomena, differential equations of electrical circuits and its solutions

2. Transient phenomena of electrical circuits
     Solve the transient phenomena of various circuits according to the solution of differential equation.
     //AC and DC circuit of RC, RL, LC, and LCR

3. Analysis by Laplace transform
     Learn how to analyze transient phenomena in electrical circuits using Laplace transform.
     //Laplace transform and inverse transform, Laplace transform for functions and its application to circuits.

There is possibility to change the learning contents (progress) of the course schedule depending on the situation.
Exercises, quizzes, discussions and questions, etc. are included to help students concentrate on this class.
The order of learning may be changed as needed, and digital technology may be used for learning such as online (remote) or on-demand classes.

title: 半導体工学基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Semiconductor Physics
educationalGoal: This course provides the foundational knowledge of semiconductors, which underpin all modern technological domains. Specifically, students gain an understanding of crystal structures, classical electron conduction models, the fundamentals of quantum mechanics, energy band theory, and semiconductor material properties from a microscopic perspective at the atomic and molecular level. Additionally, students learn the fundamentals of semiconductor manufacturing processes, such as high-purity crystal growth and photolithography.
advice:
In this course, you will learn the following topics:
(1) History and social context of semiconductor devices (Introduction)
(2) High-purity crystal growth and semiconductor device fabrication processes
(3) Crystal structure
(4) Classical electronic conduction models
(5) Fundamentals of quantum mechanics
(6) Energy band theory in solids
(7) Semiconductor properties and fundamentals of semiconductor devices
Regarding (1) and (2), we may utilize generative AI to investigate the latest information.
books: Denshi Buttusei [Morikita]
requiredKnowledge: Many students may find this subject somewhat more challenging compared to others. This is likely because you will be studying an entirely new branch of physics (quantum mechanics) that you have not encountered before. However, as you progress in understanding the “Fundamentals of Quantum Phenomena”;which reveal the essence of things;you will likely find it a truly fascinating subject. The key to studying this subject is to have a solid grasp of the physics (classical physics) and mathematics you have learned so far.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the role, physical properties, and fundamentals of semiconductor devices.
Be able to explain bonding forces and representative crystal structures.
The motion of electrons can be explained using the Drude theory, mobility, relaxation time, effective mass.
Understand the fundamentals of quantum mechanics and be able to apply the Schrodinger wave equation in practice.
Changes in energy levels of atoms, molecules, and crystalline states, and the formation of energy bands.
Using energy band theory, one can explain the differences between conductors, semiconductors, and insulators.
