title: 電子回路Ⅱ
subtitle: Electronic Circuits II
educationalGoal: Electronic circuits is a very important topic. In this subject, Digital Circuits, the objective is to learn the fndamentals of Boolean equations (logic algebra) and logic circuits, and to understand the principles behind how various logic circuits operate.In addition to combined logic circuits such as AND, OR, and NOT gates, the students will learn to understand and explain the operating principles of sequential circuits such as flip-flops and counters as well as more functional circuits such as analog to digital(A/D) and digital to analog (D/A) converters.
advice:
We will cover the following materials.
1. Fundamental logic circuits and boolean function
   AND, OR, NOT, EX-OR
2. Design for combination logical circuit
   Conversion circuit (NAND, NOR)
   Simplification using the karnaugh map
   Logical circuit design
   Adder Circuit
3. Flip Flop(FF) Circuit
    Synchronous / asynchronous 4 types of FF
    RS-FF, JK-FF, T-FF, D-FF
4. Counter Circuit
   Synchronous/asynchronous type UP/DOWN counter
   Ripple counter
   Shift resister
5. A/D and D/A converter circuit
   Principle and design
books: wakaru dejitaru densikairo   nishin syuppan
requiredKnowledge: All you need to study this subject is to understand the physical electronics and basic electric circuit.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the digital electronics and fundamental logicl circuits.
Be able to design the basic combination logical circuit.
Be able to explain the 4 types for Flip Flop.
Be able to design the synchro and asynchro type digital counter circuit.
Be able to explain the principle opreration for A/D and D/A converter.

title: 分布定数回路
subtitle: Distributed Constant Circuits
educationalGoal: In the previous study of electric circuits, the physical dimensions of a circuit has been assumed to be small enough. At the higher frequencies, however, the size of the circuit must be taken into account, and voltages and currents behave as waves. In this course, students will learn the theory of distributed-constant circuits, propagation of electric waves along transmission lines. They will also study about the tools and techniques for high-frequency circuit analysis and design.
advice:
1. Voltages and currents on distributed-constant circuits
2. Reflection Coefficient, standing waves, and input impedance looking into a transmission line.
3. Smith chart
4. Impedance matching for a distributed-constant circuit
5. Scattering matrix

Students are expected to understand the difference between lumped-constant circuits and distributed-constant circuits, relation between frequency and wavelength, and will learn about the equations for voltages and currents on distributed-constant circuits and their solutions.
Students are also expected to learn how to use Smith chart and scattering matrix.
books:
Textbooks: Fundamentals of Transmission Lines (in Japanese) [Corona publishing]
Reference books: None
Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge:
Understanding of Electric Circuits I, II and III, especially theory of alternating voltage and current.
Enough skills of circuit analysis using complex numbers.

Be able to analyze basic lumped-constant circuits.
Be able to use Smith chart.
Be able to design matching circuit.

title: 電気数学Ⅰ
subtitle: Mathematics for Electrical and Electronic Engineering I
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to learn the basic mathematics related to electrical and electronic engineering, and to acquire basic knowledge of electricity, such as electrical circuits, electromagnetism, and electronic circuits. The aim is also to cultivate the ability to apply this knowledge to specific problems through physical and mathematical considerations. This course is the basis for the subsequent “Mathematics for Electrical and Electronic Engineering Ⅱ” and “Electric Circuits I” courses.
advice:
Development of basic mathematical skills:
Students will learn about methods of solving linear simultaneous equations using substitution, addition and subtraction, and determinants, as well as basic functions (trigonometric ratios, trigonometric functions, exponential functions, logarithmic functions), complex numbers, and other topics that will be widely required in the future in the basic mathematics for  electrical and electronic Engineering.
books: A textbook written in Japanese will be used.
requiredKnowledge: This course is an introduction to the field of electrical and electronic engineering. It is important to review mathematics (simultaneous equations, trigonometric functions, exponential functions, etc.) learned in high school for future learning. It is desirable to study areas that were not taken in high school using self-study and learning support systems in our university.

title: 電気回路基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits
educationalGoal: This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering curriculum. The objective is to acquire a basic knowledge of electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze and design electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will learn about electric circuits having resistance (R) that are connected to DC power sources. Particular emphasis will be placed on how to formulate and solve the network equations based on Ohm’s law and Kirchhoff’s law.
advice:
Below is an outline of the topics to be covered:

DC circuits: electric circuits and Ohm’s law, Kirchhoff’s law, superposition principle, Thevenin’s Theorem, Δ-Y conversion, electric power, electric power quantity Calculation

This subject is not only important as preparation for subsequent courses (Electrical Circuit I, Electrical Circuit II, and Electrical Circuit III), but also each specialized topic should be studied keeping in mind that it is a special basic course requirement.
Since the progress is adjusted while checking the level of student understanding indicated by quiz results, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and the course content.
books: Basic electric circuit (2nd edition) New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: It is important that you solve as many problems as possible in order to understand and practice the theory presented. In addition, continuous effort is required on a daily basis. Therefore, we encourage you to 1) examine various reference books, 2) ask the lecturer questions, and 3) take advantage of the Mathematical and Science Education Research Center so that you can clarify what you don’t understand.

activityGoals.body: Participants can explain Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s law in DC circuits.
Participants can formulate and solve equations for DC networks.
Participants can calculate the maximum power condition in DC circuits.
Participants can calculate DC circuits using the superposition principle and Thevenin's theorem.

              This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering curriculum. The objective is to acquire a basic knowledge of electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze and design electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will learn the fundamentals of electric circuits consisting of resistance (R), inductance (L), capacitance (C), and their combinations connected to an AC power source. In addition, students will learn about phasor representation of sinusoidal AC.

              Below is an outline of the topics to be covered:

AC circuit basics: properties of sine wave AC, effects of resistance, inductance, and capacitance, average and RMS values, phasor indication of sinusoidal AC

This subject is not only important as preparation for subsequent courses (Electrical Circuit II, Electrical Circuit III, and Electrical Circuit IV), but also each specialized topic should be studied keeping in mind that it is a basic course requirement.
Based on the level of student understanding as indicated by quiz results, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and course content.

title: 電気回路Ⅱ（先取り履修・オンデマンド授業）
subtitle: Electric Circuit II
keywords: Electric power, Maximum electric power problem
educationalGoal: In this course, students will acquire basic knowledge of AC in electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze AC circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. It deals with basic circuits of resistance (R), inductance (L) or capacitance (C), which are a review of "Electrical Circuit I", to slightly complicated application circuits that combine them. Here, students will learn the circuit analysis method by the symbolic method and acquire the basics of the advanced analysis method required in the subsequent "Electrical Circuit III".
advice:
1.	Phasor of a complex number and symbolic method of AC circuit
2.	Series and parallel connection of complex impedance and complex admittance
3.	Phase condition problem in series-parallel circuit
4.	Series resonant circuit and parallel resonant circuit
5.	Calculation of the electric power, complex electric power and maximum electric power problem by symbolic method
books: Basic electric circuit(2nd edition)New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: In this course, it is important to solve more problems in order to understand the theory and put it into practice. Moreover, since they are one by one, continuous efforts are required. Therefore, do not leave what you do not understand, so be sure to clear 1) check various reference books, 2) ask the teachers, 3) use the Mathematics Education Center. In this course, students use mathematical equations such as simultaneous linear equations, determinants, matrices, differentiation / integration, basics of complex numbers, and trigonometric functions.

activityGoals.body: To be able to analyze and establish circuit equations of R, L, C series and parallel circuits by symbolic method
To be able to calculate the phase condition problems of series and parallel circuits and basic problems of AC
To be able to calculate the problems of series and parallel resonant circuits using symbolic method
To be able to calculate the power problems using symbolic method

title: 電気磁気学Ⅰ
subtitle: Electromagnetics I
educationalGoal: The learning and educational goal is to acquire basic knowledge of electricity and to acquire basic electrical and electronic abilities that can be applied to specific problems through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will acquire the basic mathematics necessary for analyzing various physical phenomena in "electromagnetism", the basic rules regarding electric charges, electric fields, potentials, and capacitances in electrostatic fields, and the ability to solve problems of electrostatic fields.
advice:
The class covers the following items.
Chapter 1 : Charge and Coulomb force (Phenomenon to charge, charge and properties, conductor and nonconductor, electrostatic induction, Coulomb's law, Coulomb force, Coulomb force and plane coordinates, composition of multiple Coulomb forces in plane coordinates, Coulomb force and space coordinates)
Chapter 2 : Electric field and electric potential (electric field, synthetic electric field by multiple electric charges, synthetic electric field by electric charge distributed continuously, electric field lines, small area passing, lines of electric force, potential, potential due to multiple charges, equipotential surface, spatial representation of potential, Gauss's law and its application)
Chapter 3 : Capacitance of conductor system (the nature of charged conductor, capacitance, capacitance of various conductor systems, electric imaging method, contact of capacitor, Energy of the capacitor)
Chapter 4 : Dielectrics (Dielectric properties, polarization, electric field and electric flux density in dielectric, electric field and electric flux density in two dielectrics, conduction with dielectric energy stored between bodies, force between conductors filled with dielectrics)
Chapter 5 : Current (Transfer of charge, ohm's law, resistance and resistor, conductance and conductivity, Joule heat and power, electric field in conductor, current density)
If necessary, learning may take place using digital methods such as online (distance) or on-demand classes.
books:
Textbook，A.Mikami, M.Masahiko, S.Makino, Y.Fujita, H.Yanagibashi,"Basic electromgnetics Ⅰ",
Kanazawa Institute of Technology,(2025)
requiredKnowledge:
This class is an introductory subject of "electromagnetics", and it is planned to take "electromagnetics II" and "electromagnetics III". So, the following background knowledge and skills are required.
1. Review the basic mathematics such as functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, vector analysis.
2. In electromagnetics, many new "units" are used. Understand the main units of physical quantities and the configuration of unit systems.
3. Be aware of the definitions and key formulas of technical terms.

activityGoals.body: The nature of charge, the Coulomb law acting between charges can be understood.
Understanding the relationship between electric field and potential formed by charge, and using Gauss's law.
The basic problem of the capacitance of a conductor system, electrostatic energy can be solved.
Understanding the electrical polarization of dielectrics.

              キーワード
              学習・教育目標

              1.Charge and coulomb force
2.Electric field and electric potential
3.Capacitance of conductor system
4.Dielectric material
5.Online/ On-demand class

              The learning and educational goal is to acquire basic knowledge of electricity and to acquire basic electrical and electronic abilities that can be applied to specific problems through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will acquire the basic mathematics necessary for analyzing various physical phenomena in "electromagnetism", the basic rules regarding electric charges, electric fields, potentials, and capacitances in electrostatic fields, and the ability to solve problems of electrostatic fields.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              The class covers the following items.
Chapter 1 : Charge and Coulomb force (Phenomenon to charge, charge and properties, conductor and nonconductor, electrostatic induction, Coulomb's law, Coulomb force, Coulomb force and plane coordinates, composition of multiple Coulomb forces in plane coordinates, Coulomb force and space coordinates)
Chapter 2 : Electric field and electric potential (electric field, synthetic electric field by multiple electric charges, synthetic electric field by electric charge distributed continuously, electric field lines, small area passing, lines of electric force, potential, potential due to multiple charges, equipotential surface, spatial representation of potential, Gauss's law and its application)
Chapter 3 : Capacitance of conductor system (the nature of charged conductor, capacitance, capacitance of various conductor systems, electric imaging method, contact of capacitor, Energy of the capacitor)
Chapter 4 : Dielectrics (Dielectric properties, polarization, electric field and electric flux density in dielectric, electric field and electric flux density in two dielectrics, conduction with dielectric energy stored between bodies, force between conductors filled with dielectrics)
Chapter 5 : Current (Transfer of charge, ohm's law, resistance and resistor, conductance and conductivity, Joule heat and power, electric field in conductor, current density)
If necessary, learning may take place using digital methods such as online (distance) or on-demand classes.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Textbook，A.Mikami, M.Masahiko, S.Makino, Y.Fujita, H.Yanagibashi,"Basic electromgnetics Ⅰ",
Kanazawa Institute of Technology,(2025)

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              This class is an introductory subject of "electromagnetics", and it is planned to take "electromagnetics II" and "electromagnetics III". So, the following background knowledge and skills are required.
1. Review the basic mathematics such as functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, vector analysis.
2. In electromagnetics, many new "units" are used. Understand the main units of physical quantities and the configuration of unit systems.
3. Be aware of the definitions and key formulas of technical terms.

title: 測量学Ⅰ
subtitle: Surveying I
educationalGoal: This course covers the fundamental knowledge of surveying, including Surveying Act, public surveying work regulations, and basic surveying principles. Students will learn the principles, equipment, and characteristics of various surveying methods such as observation data processing, distance surveying, and leveling. Spatial information technologies such as GNSS and GIS are introduced here, with detailed study reserved for Surveying II.
advice:
Exercises for each class, solutions to surveyor and assistant surveyor examination questions, and appreciation of "THURUGIDAKE TEN NO KI" correspond to the "Comprehensive Skills" learning component of the CLIP learning process. While surveying methods are diverse, the course progresses by incorporating exercises across a broad spectrum from basic to applied surveying. Furthermore, advanced surveying techniques will be introduced initially, but detailed content will be covered in Surveying II.
1."Overview": History of Surveying Development, Spatial Information Engineering.2."Surveying Act": Surveying-Related Laws, Surveying Act, Standards for Public Surveying Work Regulations, Coordinate Reference Systems. 3."Processing Observed Values": Observed Value Errors, Error Propagation Calculation Methods, Least Squares Method, Processing Observed Values, Calculation Methods for Processing Observed Values, Conversion Between Radians and Degrees. 4."Distance Surveying": Concepts of distance surveying, direct distance measurement, errors in distance surveying. 5."Leveling Surveying": Classification of leveling surveying, definitions of leveling surveying terminology, direct leveling, indirect leveling, types of levels and instruments. 6. Conduct practice exercises for the Assistant Surveyor Examination covering items 1 through 5 above (Relevance to Qualification Certification) , but the schedule may change due to viewing historical documentary films related to surveying. Additionally, a mid-term review test will be administered around the middle of the course. Students who register descriptions related to class management in [Self-Check] may receive extra credit under "Other".)
books: Reference the Japanese syllabus.
requiredKnowledge: This course is indispensable for taking Surveying Practice/Seminar I and II and is useful preparation for Spatial Information Engineering. Surveying Practicum/Exercise I and II present the lecture contents as a specific application. Spreadsheet software(Excel) can be applied to many survey calculations. Students need to be able to submit reports made using spreadsheets.Additionally, it requires the ability to create Word files for report preparation and a basic level of IT literacy related to this task.

Students can solve basic and applied question from national registered surveyors.(0.1H, 0.1M)
Students can explain the importance of surveying and spatial information technology.(0.1H, 0.1M)

achievementLevels.ideal: Students can explain the Surveying Act and operation specifications for public surveys. They can explain the coordinate reference system accurately, particularly the difference between the world geodetic system and the Japanese geodetic system. Students can handle surveying errors by applying basic mathematical knowledge. They can use the least squares method and process observed values. They can explain the relationship between radians and degrees, and can use Excel to create worksheets. They can also explain the concepts of distance measurement and error, can handle errors, understand and explain the leveling method.
achievementLevels.standard: Students know about the Surveying Act and specifications for public surveys. They can explain the basics of coordinate reference systems. They can also use basic mathematical knowledge and can handle survey errors. Students can  explain the relationship between radians and degrees, the concepts of and errors in distance surveys, leveling, and can outline GNSS, GIS, Remote sensing technology.

title: 構造力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Structural Mechanics I
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)	learn the basic theory of structural mechanics which is essential in infrastructure design.
(2)	learn the static mechanics of rigid bodies.
(3)	learn about the equilibrium of forces acting on static structures.
(4)	learn about cross-sectional forces in beam members.
advice:
This is a structural mechanics course. We will cover the following topics:

1. Infrastructure design
2. Mechanics of rigid bodies
3. Moment
4. Equilibrium of forces
5. Reaction forces
6. Boundary conditions
7. Cross-sectional forces

Students will also learn about Q-diagrams and M-diagrams for cross sectional forces. Structural mechanics II and Structural design follow, and are based on this course. Therefore, students should come to understand the topics listed above in this course.
books: 基礎から学ぶ構造力学，藤本一男・西田進・中村一平・本田秀行・木村定雄，森北出版，2005
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of mathematical derivation and integration.

activityGoals.body: Students can compose or decompose forces.
Students can estimate moment.
Students can describe the equilibrium of forces on a free body.
Students can analyze the reaction forces on static structures using the equilibrium of external forces.
Students can analyze the cross sectional forces on static beams.

title: 測量学Ⅱ
subtitle: Surveying II
educationalGoal: In Surveying II, students learn about spatial information technologies such as GIS, GNSS, and RS, which are new surveying fields. Specifically, the course covers traverse surveying, GNSS surveying, and geographic information systems. Some subjects will be instructed using flipped teaching.
advice:
(1) Students will learn traverse surveying; calculation of azimuths, bearings, latitudes and departures, adjustments to latitudes and departures, total latitude and total departure, and area. These are taught using flipped teaching (active learning) e-learning.
(2) Students will do traverse survey exercises using a 3D simulator (active learning)
(3) Students will do GIS (geographic information system) exercises using QGIS (active learning)
(4) Students will become acquainted with other spatial information technologies (GNSS (GPS), laser surveying, etc.)
(5) Students will do national examination exercises on topics 1 to 4 listed above (related to national qualifications)
(6) Students will create exam question candidates in cooperation with senior SA (active learning).
books: Same the Japanese syllabus.
requiredKnowledge: This subject is indispensable preparation for Surveying Practicum/Exercise I and II and Spatial Information Technology. Students can acquire practical skills by taking Surveying Practicum/Exercise I and II. Students can create Excel calculation sheets that they can apply it to many survey calculations. The Power Point slides used in the lecture will be posted on the e-syllabus. This course is closely related to the Registered Surveyor examination.

activityGoals.body: Students can explain the principles of, equipment used, and characteristics of various surveying methods (0.1L)
Students can select survey methods correctly depending on the terrain and purpose of the survey. (0.1L)
Students can deepen their knowledge of spatial information technology and design/planning. (0.1M, 0.1H)
Students can solve basic and applied problems that appear on national exams for registered surveyors (0.1L, 0.1)
Students can explain the importance of surveying and spatial information engineering(0.1L, 0.1M)
Students can actively involved in flipped learning, including questions in collaboration with SA. (0.1L, 0.1M)

achievementLevels.ideal: In traverse surveying, students understand azimuth, bearing, latitude and distance, and accurately calculate error and area. They can create a data calculation sheet with Excel. They can explain raster data and vector data in GIS and positioning methods in GNSS in detail. Students understand the details of the coordinate reference system, spatial data collection and measurement methods, and can explaine mesh code of map management. They can solve advanced application problems from registered and assistant surveyors’ national tests. They can also create exam and practice question candidates in cooperation with senior SA.
achievementLevels.standard: In traverse surveying, students understand azimuth, bearing, latitude and distance. They understand the concepts of spatial information technology and understand the three fields (GIS, GNSS, remote sensing) that make up spatial information engineering. They understand the Japanese coordinate reference system, spatial data collection and measurement methods and mesh coding. They can solve basic problems from registered and assistant surveyors’ national tests. Students can do temporary tutoring.

title: 構造力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Structural Mechanics II
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1)　learn the strength and stress-strain relationship of materials.
(2)　learn about the sectional moment of inertia and moment of inertia area.
(3)　learn how to estimate flexural and shear stresses in beams.
(4)　learn how to estimate axial forces in trusses.
(5)　learn how to estimate axial force in short columns and buckling loads of long columns.
advice:
This is the second basic structural mechanics course. We will cover the following topics:

1. Stress and strain
2. Sectional moment of inertia and moment of inertia area
3. Stress in structural members
4. Estimating shear stress and flexural stress in beam members
5. Axial forces in truss structures
6. Stresses in short columns and the cross-sectional core
7. Buckling of long columns

These concepts are often used in structural design. Students should gain a deep understanding of this material. The concepts are also useful in studying Structural Design, Project Design, Reinforced Concrete and Structural Design Practice.

title: 測量実習・演習Ⅰ
subtitle: Surveying Practicum / Exercises I
educationalGoal:
(1) Practice the surveying methods learned in Surveying I and Surveying II
(2) Practice distance, control point, leveling and declination surveys and reports.
(3) Reports are equivalent to company reports. Students will learn how to create data in required formats.
(4) Students who master the topics in Surveying I/II and Surveying Practicum I/II will have the skills necessary for an Assistant Surveyor national license.
advice: Field training is implemented as a practice of active learning and [self-inspection], which is "comprehensive ability" learning. 1. Distance surveying: "Learn the basics of distance measurement." pacing, cloth tape measure, steel tape measure and distance measurement by total station. 2. Leveling: Learn how to handle automatic levels and electronic levels. Conduct small-scale direct leveling to understand the person. Understand survey error adjustments. 3. Handling the total station: Learn how to use the total station (TS) and how to handle equipment using the built-in programs. 4. Angular survey: Learn the basics of horizontal angle observation (double observation) by the single measurement method using a total station. With the measurement of eccentric elements as the subject. Then conduct angle observations around Building 2 and 3, and practice repeatedly so that observations can be made accurately. 5. (Advice): Moodle teaching materials (Surveying I, II) are useful for practical training and writing reports, so please refer to them. Please note that the schedule may change due to the weather, as the training will be held outdoors.
books: Reference the Japanese syllabus.

Therefore, the contents of the classroom lectures (especially It is necessary to fully understand the advanced courses such as "Surveying II", "Surveying Practice/Exercise II", "Spatial Information Technology", etc. There is in addition, there are related subjects such as "Environmental Civil Engineering Experiments and Exercises B" and "Exercises in Geoinformatics".

Leveling: Learn how to handle automatic levels and electronic levels. Conduct small-scale direct leveling to understand the person. Understand survey error adjustments. 3. Handling the total station: Learn how to use the total station (TS) and how to handle equipment using the built-in programs. 4. Angular survey: Learn the basics of horizontal angle observation (double observation) by the single measurement method using a total station. With the measurement of eccentric elements as the subject. Then conduct angle observations around Building 2 and 3, and practice repeatedly so that observations can be made accurately. 5. title: 土質力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Soil Mechanics II
educationalGoal:
This course aims to provide a basic knowledge of percolation of soil and concept of effective stress. As appicable examples fo soil water drainage, stability of dam or sheet pile coffer dam by using flow net will be learned.
Secondary, the differences between total and effective stress in Mohr's circle should be understand and be able to choose proper parameters of strength, internal friction and adhesive stress.
advice:
This course will impart a solid grounding in Soil Mechanics. The contents are shown as followings.
1. Soil compaction
Compacting factor test, characteristics of compacted soil.

2.Percolation of soil
Darcy's law, permeability, flownet, boiling and piping, drainage

3.Shear strength of soil
Shear strength, Mohr's circle, testing method of shear stregth, shear properties of sand and clay, increasing strength by consolidation
books: Soil Mechanics, Yasufuku et.al., Riko-tosho

be able to understand the differences between total and efferctive stress. [0.2K]
be able to understand characteristics of soil compaction. [0.2K]

title: 建築の計画とデザイン
subtitle: Architectural Planning and Design
educationalGoal: Students gain not only an overview of the architectural field but also the expanse of the construction industry. Then they come to understand the importance of planning various elements of architecture that influence the consciousness and actions of people. Furthermore, throughout discussion with construction professionals, students develop their interest in architecture, cultivate a questioning attitude to problems, and acquire an ability to plan for the future.
advice:
This course explains not only the relationship between architectural planning and society but also the influence of architectural planning on town development and the landscape. Concretely, we presents students the goals of studying architecture by showing the superior instances of architecture and exterior spaces. Next, we expand the viewpoint of architectural planning to the fields of town development and landscapes. Furthermore, we show students various jobs related to architectural planning, and their awareness of architectural jobs and their morals grow.
The subjects of this course are as follows:
　1. Fields of architecture: first and eleventh lectures
　2. Design and history of architecture and exterior space: second to fifth lectures
　3. Areas covered by architectural planning: sixth to tenth lectures
　4. Jobs related to architectural planning: twelfth to fifteenth lectures
requiredKnowledge: It is important that students not only learn from the textbook of this course but also read as many books and magazines on architecture as possible. Furthermore, it is more important that students observe architecture and urban space in their daily lives. This attitude is needed for the four years of learning in this college as well as in this course.

activityGoals.body: Students acquire knowledge about attractive architecture and urban space, and develop their interest and motivat
Students understand the basics of architectural planning related to buildings and landscapes.
Students become familiar with jobs related to architectural planning and their mutual relationships.
Students understand the fields of architecture (architectural planning, structural engineering, and environmenta

title: 日本建築史
subtitle: History of Japanese Architecture
educationalGoal: Students learn the history of Japanese architecture from ancient to modern times and understand its architectural design and technical features, space composition, social background, and regionality. They learn about the role and characteristics of architecture and streets.
advice:
Students learn about temple architecture, shrine architecture, and residential architecture from ancient to modern Japan.

1. History of residential buildings and cities, townscapes.

2. Ancient temples and shrines.

3. Medieval temples and shrines.

4. Early modern temples and shrines.

5. Modern temples and shrines.
books: none
requiredKnowledge: Students must have an interest in Japanese history, art history, archeology, folklore, etc., and try to understand Japanese architecture and architectural culture from a broad perspective.

activityGoals.body: Students understand the history of Japanese architecture and summarize key points.
Students can learn by themselves and write their own considerations.
Students can research historical Japanese architecture and explain its characteristics.

title: 建築構造力学Ⅰ（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Structural Mechanics for Architecture I
educationalGoal: Students learn the mechanical characteristics of statically determinate beams, trusses, and frames, which are basic models of building structures. They understand the balance of forces that work on buildings and learn how to find reaction forces. Students understand the concept of resultant stress and the balance of free bodies, and learn how to determine the distribution of resultant stress in beams and frames. They learn how to find the axial forces in trusses by solving the nodal balance.
advice:
1. Building structures and structural mechanics
2. Equilibrium of force
3. Structure modeling and reaction forces
4. Loads and external forces
5. Mechanical classification of structures
6. Stress and resultant stress
7. Reaction forces and resultant stresses in statically determinate structures
8. Sectional properties
9. Material properties
10. Stress and member design
books:
Textbooks： Step up structural mechanics wrighten by Ota Kazuhiko
Reference books：None
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge:
Students must understand trigonometric functions and elementary mechanics.
A scientific calculator is required for testing.
Students should review the application of vector operations in Linear Algebra.

activityGoals.body: Building structure and loads/external forces can correspond to the dynamic model.
Students can determine the reaction forces of static structures.
Students can draw diagrams of axial force, shear force, and bending moment of a statically determinate structure
Students can explain the basic cross-sectional and mechanical properties of materials.
Students can determine the stress in a beam.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1)	Students have acquired a basic knowledge of structural mechanics.
(2)	Students can describe the underlying formulas and find the exact solutions to those formulas.
(3)	Students can represent the resulting solutions graphically.
(4)	Students can show a simple structural model and can calculate stress.
(5)	Students can present a proposal to plan a rational building from a mechanical point of view for a simple building.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1)	Students have acquired a basic knowledge of structural mechanics.
(2)	Students can write the underlying formulas and understands the procedure for finding the solution.
(3)	Students can represent the resulting solution graphically.

title: 建築設計基礎
subtitle: Basic Representation of Architectural Design
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will learn the basic ideas and framework of activities for proposing architectural designs. To be specific, the purpose is to be able to consider about how to proceed architectural design work including structures and design elements by conceptualizing the 3-d composition of architectural design and expressing it with sketches, models, and CAD models.
In addition, it will be basic literacy for "Architectural Design Studio I/II" in the second year.
advice:
This lesson is composed of following contents.

# 1st week; Orientation: Class outline explanation, assignment explanation

# 2-6th week; theme 1 "Small space design inspired by basic solids"
Students have to propose a new small space by edit a given basic solid by creating a model and a presentation board.

# 7-9th week; theme 2 "Reading and communicating spatial design"
Students have to create a presentation board that can convey the essence of a real architectural work to others.

# 10-14th week; theme 3: "Spatial design inspired by site and context"
Students have to propose a new small space based on observation and analysis of the site by creating a model and a presentation board.

# 15th week; Review of outcomes and the entire class
books: none
requiredKnowledge:
Architectural design consists of absorbent of various knowledge and experience, and integration of them into proposals of architecture and cityscapes.
Students should actively collect information of the characteristic architecture, its background, the relationship between the space and people, and try to acquire the habit of connecting them to your own ideas.
In addition, always check out expression samples such as sketches, models and words in architectural books and magazines and learn to use them yourself.

activityGoals.body: Students can gather information on characteristic architecture and understand their characteristics.
Students can organize their own thoughts and idea, and summarize them in sketches and words.
Students can create a model expressing their own idea and explain it easily to others.
Students can study their own design idea three-dimensionally using 3D CAD.
Students can create presentation board that can convey design concept and composition to others.

              You will be able to learn the design method and drafting for small-scale buildings, and also develop the ability to summarize and present your ideas. First, you need to understand the surrounding environment of the target site set in cooperation with the area. Next, you design your intended architectural space based on the conditions such as the architectural use, function, composition, beauty, and measurable shape of the subject. The basic contents of the design must be represented in draftings and the like.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This learning is the first step in architectural design. The first project is the design of a "cafe" with a single function. The second project is the design of the "house", the most well-known architecture.

title: 西洋建築史
subtitle: History of Occidental Architecture
educationalGoal: This course aims to provide students with a historical understanding of several style characteristics and aesthetic compositions of the architecture that form the cities and regions of the West, originating from ancient Oriental architecture to modern periods. This course also aims at understanding of spatial characteristics of each architectural style, technical features of each historical period that fulfilled the requirements of use, function and structure, as well as the philosophy and social background underpinning them.
advice:
1. Ancient Oriental architecture, Ancient Greek architecture, Hellenistic architecture
2. Ancient Roman architecture
3. Early Christian Architecture and Byzantine Art and Architecture
4. Romanesque architecture
5. Gothic architecture
6. Medieval city
7. Renaissance architecture and architects (15th century)
8. Mannerist Architecture (16th Century)
9. Baroque architecture, Rococo architecture
10. Neoclassicism and 19th century architecture
11. The origin of modern design
12. Development of modern and contemporary architecture
books: 有名建築事典：イラスト＆解説500[学芸出版社]
requiredKnowledge: Use Google Earth etc. to understand the geographical relationship of the architecture mentioned in the lecture, and read books and architectural magazines to get in touch with the latest trends.

activityGoals.body: To obtain an overview of the historical development of Western architectural design.
To perceive morphological characteristics of styles in each period and to identify them.
To understand the relationship between architectural uses, function and structure as well as its expression.
To think critically about things from a variety of perspectives, including historical approaches.

To acquire a basic knowledge of the history of Western architecture necessary for taking the Ikkyu-kenchikushi examination, with exploring major trends in Western architecture, names for elements in ancient to late architecture, and names of architects.
To understand architectural characteristics in each period (style, construction method, material, decoration, idea of architects, social background, etc.) and to acquire the ability to analytically understand and appreciate architecture according to its basic design and external feature.

title: 建築構法計画
subtitle: Building System Design
educationalGoal: In this course, students develop the knowledge required for planning, constructing, and maintaining buildings while comprehensively considering building materials, structural systems, and equipment. Specifically, they acquire the basic knowledge of building systems to standardize or componentize buildings, and learn new about designs in the environmental age.
advice:
This course explains the typical of structural systems and building elements from the viewpoints of required performance and construction work, and shows examples of superior building element design. In the first half of this course, structural systems are explained, outlining all the materials used and the points that need supervision in each type of construction work. In the latter half, finishing layers and substrates are explained with respect to each building element.
The contents of this course are as follows.
　1. Structural systems: steel construction, reinforced concrete construction, and wooden construction.
　2. Building elements: roofs, walls, openings, floors, stairs, and ceilings.
　3. Building system design methods: prefabrication, modular coordination, and componentization.
requiredKnowledge: Students don't need any special background, because this course is a first step in learning building production. Students are urged to deepen their understanding of structural systems and building elements by observing many buildings in their daily lives.

activityGoals.body: Students can explain the basics of building materials and building systems.
Students can explain the constituent elements and required performance of basic structural systems that support.
Students can explain the constituent elements and required performance of basic building elements that partition
Students can explain the merits of prefabrication, componentization, and industrialization of buildings.

title: 建築構造力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Structural Mechanics for Architecture II
educationalGoal: First, they must understand how to decide whether a structure is statically determinate or indeterminate. In addition, students learn to estimate structural deformation using the principle of virtual work and simple solutions for statically indeterminate structures. We give a lecture on the slope-deflection method and finding solutions using the linear moment distribution method of modeling statically indeterminate structures. Students will be able to solve for design stresses at the end of this class.
advice:
1. Outline and review
2. Deformation of members (elastic curves, Mall's theorem)
3. Deformation of statically determinate structures using the principle of virtual work
4. Solution of primary statically indeterminate structures using the stress method
5. Buckling of compression members
6. Solution of statically indeterminate frames using the deflection angle method
7. Solution of statically indeterminate frames using the fixed moment method
8. Solution of statically indeterminate frames using the slope-deflection method

title: 建築環境学Ⅱ
subtitle: Architectural Environment II
educationalGoal: "Basic ability to plan, design, build and operate safe, beautiful and comfortable architecture and urban space" is the educational goal of the department. In this lecture, you will learn the basics from the physical, physiological and psychological aspects, especially regarding sound and visual environment.
advice:
1. Acoustic environment
1.1 Basics of sound environment planning --- objective and concept of sound environment control, physical quantity of sound, perception of sound
1.2 Sound propagation --- Sound field, sound absorption and sound insulation, air sound control method, noise evaluation
1.3 Sound plan-room acoustics, optimal reverberation time, acoustic disturbance
2. Visual environment
2.1 Basics of Lighting Environment Plan --- Lighting Purpose and Concept, Light Perception, Light Physical Quantity, Comfort, Light Source Characteristics
2.2 Lighting plan --- Lighting equipment and lighting system, artificial lighting and daylighting
2.3 Lighting calculation --- Estimation and design of illuminance by point-by-point method and luminous flux method

● Self-confirmation sheet: Submit a summary of the lesson content from notes and textbooks (review). The status of submission is included in the evaluation as self-study status. You will need to make a copy if necessary.
● Scientific calculator: A calculator is required for various exercises and quizzes.
books: Illustrated Text Building Environmental Engineering 2nd Edition (SHOKOKUSYA)
requiredKnowledge: It is a continuous and evolving content of "Architectural environment I". Review of the previous knowledge.

title: 建築エンジニアリング情報演習Ⅰ
subtitle: Architectural Engineering Information Practice I
educationalGoal: In architectural design, it is important to visualize ideas with 3D models and drawings using digital media and to communicate smoothly with others using the data.  In this course, students will learn about architectural expression with BIM software, which has been spreading in recent years as the basis of digital architectural representation.  Specifically, students will learn about creating 3D models and drawing of the building designed by themselves, lighting simulation, utilizing attribute information, and making presentations.
advice:
In this course, exercise lessons will be conducted using BIM software in the CAD room as follows.

#1st week; Explanation of the purpose and outline of the course, introduction of BIM software

#2-6th week; How to make 3D model of residential building using BIM software

#7-9th week; How to make drawings of residential building using BIM software

#10-13th week; How to make presentation board of residential building using BIM software

#14th week; Application of BIM software with smart device

#15th week; Lesson for looking back and self-check
books: Archicad Magic(PDF reference book downloadable from manufacturer's website)
requiredKnowledge:
# Students must tackle assignments with residential building designed by themselves in "Architectural Design Studio I" in the last semester.
# Students shouldn't be absent because the exercises will be carried out in a stackable manner.
# Students should have awareness to enhance computer utilization skills such as software installation, data management, and printer settings.

activityGoals.body: Students can create 3D model of a design proposal appropriately using BIM software.

educationalGoal: Learn basic knowledge about building structures and materials, and develop the ability to show structural plans to plan and design mechanically rational building spaces.

8. Earthquake mechanisms and calculation of seismic forces
9. Structural planning for vertical and horizontal forces

title: 建築設備学
subtitle: Building Equipment
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn about human thermal sensation and comfortable ranges of temperature and humidity.
(2) learn how to calculate the heating and cooling loads of buildings.
(3) learn about various kind of air conditioning systems.
(4) learn about heat source equipment such as boilers, refrigerators, and heat pumps.
advice:
In this course, after recognizing the quantitative size of the transmission heat loads of buildings through exercises, students learn about the calculation methods for various heat loads, such as direct gains from solar radiation, ventilation, lighting, human bodies, and indoor heat generated by machine and instruments.
Next, students learn about air conditioning equipment and the kinds of systems that correspond to different heating and cooling loads.
Students will also come to understand the features of the various compositions of heat source equipment used to control energy consumption and carbon dioxide emissions.
1. Passive design of architecture
2. Ａir conditioning design /heat load calculation
3. Using of moist air diagram
4. Air conditioning system
5. Air conditioning equipment
6. Heat source system
7.Environmental facility planning from the viewpoint of regional.
8. Green architecture in harmony with the environment
9. Water supply, drainage and sanitation facilities
books:
Environmental Design and Systems for Architecture
ICHIGAYA Publishing Co.,Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: Students should have taken Introduction to Building Equipment, Architectural Environment I.

activityGoals.body: Students can calculate the heating and cooling loads of buildings.
Students can explain the meaning of terms related to air conditioning equipment, etc.
Students can explain the differences in the kinds of air conditioning and heat source systems.
Students can solve the problems that appear on the Japanese registered architect examination.
Students can give an overview of the Building Energy Efficiency Act.
Students can explain the feature of eco-buildings.

advice:

1.	Investigating occupational awareness through lectures by career teachers and senior students, and through internships, open desks, etc., in students' search for the ideal career path.
2.	Planning and beginning to address issues that require a relatively long period of preparation and proactive behavior, such as acquiring qualifications, developing general common sense, and successfully completing the comprehensive aptitude test (SPI).

* Some lectures may be delivered via on-demand video.
* The contents and methods presented here are subject to change depending on the infectious disease and the availability of the speaker.
books: Textbooks are not used.
requiredKnowledge: Career seminars are lectures mainly for job hunting, and are held to prepare students for the employment front. In addition, this learning will be reference material for employment placement in the following year.

title: 建築の計画とデザイン
subtitle: Planning and Design of Architecture
educationalGoal: Students gain not only an overview of the architectural field but also the expanse of the construction industry. Then they come to understand the importance of planning various elements of architecture that influence the consciousness and actions of people. Furthermore, throughout discussion with construction professionals, students develop their interest in architecture, cultivate a questioning attitude to problems, and acquire an ability to plan for the future.
advice:
This course explains not only the relationship between architectural planning and society but also the influence of architectural planning on town development and the landscape. Concretely, we presents students the goals of studying architecture by showing the superior instances of architecture and exterior spaces. Next, we expand the viewpoint of architectural planning to the fields of town development and landscapes. Furthermore, we show students various jobs related to architectural planning, and their awareness of architectural jobs and their morals grow.
The subjects of this course are as follows:
　1. Fields of architecture: first and eleventh lectures
　2. Design and history of architecture and exterior space: second to fifth lectures
　3. Areas covered by architectural planning: sixth to tenth lectures
　4. Jobs related to architectural planning: twelfth to fifteenth lectures
requiredKnowledge: It is important that students not only learn from the textbook of this course but also read as many books and magazines on architecture as possible. Furthermore, it is more important that students observe architecture and urban space in their daily lives. This attitude is needed for the four years of learning in this college as well as in this course.

title: 建築構造力学Ⅰ（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Structural Mechanics for Architecture I
educationalGoal: Students learn the mechanical characteristics of statically determinate beams, trusses, and frames, which are basic models of building structures. They understand the balance of forces that work on buildings and learn how to find reaction forces. Students understand the concept of resultant stress and the balance of free bodies, and learn how to determine the distribution of resultant stress in beams and frames. They learn how to find the axial forces in trusses by solving the nodal balance.
advice:
1. Building structures and structural mechanics
2. Equilibrium of force
3. Structure modeling and reaction forces
4. Loads and external forces
5. Mechanical classification of structures
6. Stress and resultant stress
7. Reaction forces and resultant stresses in statically determinate structures
8. Sectional properties
9. Material properties
10. Stress and member design
books:
Textbooks： Step up structural mechanics wrighten by Ota Kazuhiko
Reference books：None
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge:
Students must understand trigonometric functions and elementary mechanics.
A scientific calculator is required for testing.
Students should review the application of vector operations in Linear Algebra.

activityGoals.body: Building structure and loads/external forces can correspond to the dynamic model.
Students can determine the reaction forces of static structures.
Students can draw diagrams of axial force, shear force, and bending moment of a statically determinate structure
Students can explain the basic cross-sectional and mechanical properties of materials.
Students can determine the stress in a beam.

title: 建築デザイン基礎
subtitle: Basic Representation of Architectural Design
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will learn the basic ideas and framework of activities for proposing architectural designs. To be specific, the purpose is to be able to consider about how to proceed architectural design work including structures and design elements by conceptualizing the 3-d composition of architectural design and expressing it with sketches, models, and CAD models.
In addition, it will be basic literacy for "Architectural Design Studio I/II" in the second year.
advice:
This lesson is composed of following contents.

# 1st week; Orientation: Class outline explanation, assignment explanation

# 2-6th week; theme 1 "Small space design inspired by basic solids"
Students have to propose a new small space by edit a given basic solid by creating a model and a presentation board.

# 7-9th week; theme 2 "Reading and communicating spatial design"
Students have to create a presentation board that can convey the essence of a real architectural work to others.

# 10-14th week; theme 3: "Spatial design inspired by site and context"
Students have to propose a new small space based on observation and analysis of the site by creating a model and a presentation board.

# 15th week; Review of outcomes and the entire class
books: none
requiredKnowledge:
Architectural design consists of absorbent of various knowledge and experience, and integration of them into proposals of architecture and cityscapes.
Students should actively collect information of the characteristic architecture, its background, the relationship between the space and people, and try to acquire the habit of connecting them to your own ideas.
In addition, always check out expression samples such as sketches, models and words in architectural books and magazines and learn to use them yourself.

activityGoals.body: Students can gather information on characteristic architecture and understand their characteristics.
Students can organize their own thoughts and idea, and summarize them in sketches and words.
Students can create a model expressing their own idea and explain it easily to others.
Students can study their own design idea three-dimensionally using 3D CAD.
Students can create presentation board that can convey design concept and composition to others.

educationalGoal: You will be able to learn the design method and drafting for small-scale buildings, and also develop the ability to summarize and present your ideas. First, you need to understand the surrounding environment of the target site set in cooperation with the area. Next, you design your intended architectural space based on the conditions such as the architectural use, function, composition, beauty, and measurable shape of the subject. The basic contents of the design must be represented in draftings and the like.
advice:
This learning is the first step in architectural design. The first project is the design of a "cafe" with a single function. The second project is the design of the "house", the most well-known architecture.

○projectＩ　"Cafe"：　　　　　　　○projectⅡ　“House”： 　　　
Explanation of project 　             　　　Explanation of project
Lecture on related contents　　　　　  Lecture on related contents
Esquisse　　　　　　　　　　           Esquisse

Teaching materials: Distribute prints for each project and add explanations.
books:
Texts: “Architectural Works 2025” Kanazawa Institute of Technology, “3rd Collection of Compact Architectural Design Documents” Maruzen-pub.co.
Reference Books:“Revised Edition Architectural Drawing for Masterpiece Houses”Gakugei-pub.co., “Architectural Drafting for Beginning Students, 3rd ed.”ichigaya-pub.co.,
Reserved Books: Not specified
requiredKnowledge: It is important familiar accustomed to architecture. It is important to get the pleasure of creating your own work. Let's go to actually see the new architecture that has been talked about. Habit of reading architecture magazines is important. It is important to always think about architecture. Sketch when you come up with something on a daily basis. It is important to increase opportunities to move your hands. It is important to discuss with fellow each other. It is also important to help senior class architectural drafting.

activityGoals.body: Understand the conditions of use, function, configuration, beauty, etc. required for architectural design.
The design image and concept can be clearly shown. You can design as an integrated architecture.
The basic contents that the architecture and the district should have can be expressed by draftings.
Esquisse steps and assignment submissions can proceed according to the schedule.
As a basis for future architectural design 2, etc., basic design techniques can be acquired.

title: 西洋建築史
subtitle: History of Occidental Architecture
educationalGoal: This course aims to provide students with a historical understanding of several style characteristics and aesthetic compositions of the architecture that form the cities and regions of the West, originating from ancient Oriental architecture to modern periods. This course also aims at understanding of spatial characteristics of each architectural style, technical features of each historical period that fulfilled the requirements of use, function and structure, as well as the philosophy and social background underpinning them.
advice:
1. Ancient Oriental architecture, Ancient Greek architecture, Hellenistic architecture
2. Ancient Roman architecture
3. Early Christian Architecture and Byzantine Art and Architecture
4. Romanesque architecture
5. Gothic architecture
6. Medieval city
7. Renaissance architecture and architects (15th century)
8. Mannerist Architecture (16th Century)
9. Baroque architecture, Rococo architecture
10. Neoclassicism and 19th century architecture
11. The origin of modern design
12. Development of modern and contemporary architecture
books: 有名建築事典：イラスト＆解説500[学芸出版社]
requiredKnowledge: Use Google Earth etc. to understand the geographical relationship of the architecture mentioned in the lecture, and read books and architectural magazines to get in touch with the latest trends.

activityGoals.body: To obtain an overview of the historical development of Western architectural design.
To perceive morphological characteristics of styles in each period and to identify them.
To understand the relationship between architectural uses, function and structure as well as its expression.
To think critically about things from a variety of perspectives, including historical approaches.

思考・推論・創造する力
コラボレーションとリーダーシップ
発表・表現・伝達する力

achievementLevels.ideal: To understand the purpose and meaning of studying the history of architecture, and to develop the ability to understand and briefly explain the developmental process of architectures and cities in each region and period, relevant qualitative changes in space and the ideals and social background underpinning them, and to think about the subject matter, meaning in “Architecture”, while maintaining a basic knowledge of the history of Western architecture.
achievementLevels.standard:
To acquire a basic knowledge of the history of Western architecture necessary for taking the Ikkyu-kenchikushi examination, with exploring major trends in Western architecture, names for elements in ancient to late architecture, and names of architects.
To understand architectural characteristics in each period (style, construction method, material, decoration, idea of architects, social background, etc.) and to acquire the ability to analytically understand and appreciate architecture according to its basic design and external feature.

title: 建築構法計画
subtitle: Building System Design
educationalGoal: In this course, students develop the knowledge required for planning, constructing, and maintaining buildings while comprehensively considering building materials, structural systems, and equipment. Specifically, they acquire the basic knowledge of building systems to standardize or componentize buildings, and learn new about designs in the environmental age.
advice:
This course explains the typical of structural systems and building elements from the viewpoints of required performance and construction work, and shows examples of superior building element design. In the first half of this course, structural systems are explained, outlining all the materials used and the points that need supervision in each type of construction work. In the latter half, finishing layers and substrates are explained with respect to each building element.
The contents of this course are as follows.
　1. Structural systems: steel construction, reinforced concrete construction, and wooden construction.
　2. Building elements: roofs, walls, openings, floors, stairs, and ceilings.
　3. Building system design methods: prefabrication, modular coordination, and componentization.
requiredKnowledge: Students don't need any special background, because this course is a first step in learning building production. Students are urged to deepen their understanding of structural systems and building elements by observing many buildings in their daily lives.

activityGoals.body: Students can explain the basics of building materials and building systems.
Students can explain the constituent elements and required performance of basic structural systems that support.
Students can explain the constituent elements and required performance of basic building elements that partition
Students can explain the merits of prefabrication, componentization, and industrialization of buildings.

title: 建築構造力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Structural Mechanics for Architecture II
educationalGoal: First, they must understand how to decide whether a structure is statically determinate or indeterminate. In addition, students learn to estimate structural deformation using the principle of virtual work and simple solutions for statically indeterminate structures. We give a lecture on the slope-deflection method and finding solutions using the linear moment distribution method of modeling statically indeterminate structures. Students will be able to solve for design stresses at the end of this class.
advice:
1. Outline and review
2. Deformation of members (elastic curves, Mall's theorem)
3. Deformation of statically determinate structures using the principle of virtual work
4. Solution of primary statically indeterminate structures using the stress method
5. Buckling of compression members
6. Solution of statically indeterminate frames using the deflection angle method
7. Solution of statically indeterminate frames using the fixed moment method
8. Solution of statically indeterminate frames using the slope-deflection method

title: 建築環境学Ⅱ
subtitle: Architectural Environment II
educationalGoal: "Basic ability to plan, design, build and operate safe, beautiful and comfortable architecture and urban space" is the educational goal of the department. advice:

2. Visual environment
2.1 Basics of Lighting Environment Plan --- Lighting Purpose and Concept, Light Perception, Light Physical Quantity, Comfort, Light Source Characteristics
2.2 Lighting plan --- Lighting equipment and lighting system, artificial lighting and daylighting
2.3 Lighting calculation --- Estimation and design of illuminance by point-by-point method and luminous flux method

title: 建築構造計画
subtitle: Structural Planning for Architecture
educationalGoal: Learn basic knowledge about building structures and materials, and develop the ability to show structural plans to plan and design mechanically rational building spaces.
advice:
■Learn the basics of structural planning to be safe from loads and external forces, and to select structural types, shapes, materials, and member arrangements from the mechanical standpoint that are suitable for the intended use of the building. A basic knowledge of materials and structural mechanics is required.

1. Materials, structural types, loads
2. External forces, structural systems
3. Beam and column planning
4. Foundation structure planning
5. Collapse load
6. Structural designers' ideas and examples of structural planning
7. Review of external forces, introduction of structural analysis tools
8. Earthquake mechanisms and calculation of seismic forces
9. Structural planning for vertical and horizontal forces
10. Deformation and torsional behavior of structures

title: 建築設備学
subtitle: Building Equipment
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn about human thermal sensation and comfortable ranges of temperature and humidity.
(2) learn how to calculate the heating and cooling loads of buildings.
(3) learn about various kind of air conditioning systems.
(4) learn about heat source equipment such as boilers, refrigerators, and heat pumps.
advice:
In this course, after recognizing the quantitative size of the transmission heat loads of buildings through exercises, students learn about the calculation methods for various heat loads, such as direct gains from solar radiation, ventilation, lighting, human bodies, and indoor heat generated by machine and instruments.
Next, students learn about air conditioning equipment and the kinds of systems that correspond to different heating and cooling loads.
Students will also come to understand the features of the various compositions of heat source equipment used to control energy consumption and carbon dioxide emissions.
1. Passive design of architecture
2. Ａir conditioning design /heat load calculation
3. Using of moist air diagram
4. Air conditioning system
5. Air conditioning equipment
6. Heat source system
7.Environmental facility planning from the viewpoint of regional.
8. Green architecture in harmony with the environment
9. Water supply, drainage and sanitation facilities
books:
Environmental Design and Systems for Architecture
ICHIGAYA Publishing Co.,Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: Students should have taken Introduction to Building Equipment, Architectural Environment I.

activityGoals.body: Students can calculate the heating and cooling loads of buildings.
Students can explain the meaning of terms related to air conditioning equipment, etc.
Students can explain the differences in the kinds of air conditioning and heat source systems.
Students can solve the problems that appear on the Japanese registered architect examination.
Students can give an overview of the Building Energy Efficiency Act.
Students can explain the feature of eco-buildings.

educationalGoal: In addition to measuring the future career and forming a professional view as an engineer, students will set goals and envision advancement/employment plans suitable for themselves, and recognize the voluntary and ambitious actions needed to prepare to achieve those goals.
advice:
The course addresses the following two main issues:
1.	Investigating occupational awareness through lectures by career teachers and senior students, and through internships, open desks, etc., in students' search for the ideal career path.
2.	Planning and beginning to address issues that require a relatively long period of preparation and proactive behavior, such as acquiring qualifications, developing general common sense, and successfully completing the comprehensive aptitude test (SPI).

* Some lectures may be delivered via on-demand video.
* The contents and methods presented here are subject to change depending on the infectious disease and the availability of the speaker.
books: Textbooks are not used.
requiredKnowledge: Career seminars are lectures mainly for job hunting, and are held to prepare students for the employment front. In order to prepare for job hunting and job examinations, all students need to take this course regardless of their advancement or employment. In addition, this learning will be reference material for employment placement in the following year.

title: 物理学基礎実験
subtitle: Basic Experiments in Physics
educationalGoal:
●To understand basic knowledge and skills for physics experiments, which include the basic operation of laboratory equipment and safety precautions.
●To understand the methods of data processing using computer.
●To design and conduct physics experiments, and to analyze and report the results
 of them.
●To plan, conduct, and teach physics experiments in the subject "Science" in secondary school.
advice: This course mainly aims at students who wish to be science teachers at secondary school.  Through learning basic physics experiments, students will acquire knowledge on how to operate laboratory equipment and safety necessary for conducting experiments in the subject "Science" of secondary school.  Students will experience how to conduct experimental lessons in the subject "Science".
requiredKnowledge: In order to teach Science at secondary school, it is necessary to understand knowledge of physics in senior high school.  Therefore, students should review high school physics thoroughly before this course.  This course does not only cover the contents specified in the Course of Study of Science, but also the laws of conservation of angular momentum in mechanics and Maxwell's equations in electromagnetism, which are useful for the subject "Science".

activityGoals.body: Be able to conduct experiments using instruments and devices appropriately in reference to an experiment guide.
Be able to process the data of the experimental results using a computer.
Be able to consider experimental results and explain formula and rules.
Be able to design experiment plans and conduct them.

Learn data analysis of the experimental results using a computer. Plan and conduct geological experiments, and Prepare a report describing the experimental method and results. Learn how to achieve high educational effects in geological experiments when geological experiments conduct.

Learn the safety training, the use of experimental tools and instruments correctly, and the knowledge of data analysis using a computer throughout basic experiments in geoscience for junior high school and high school. Conduct field works such as minerals sampling and stratum observation in addition to indoor experiments. Fieldwork will be conduct on Saturday in April. requiredKnowledge: It is necessary to a deeper understanding than what you teach in order to teach geological experiments in Junior high school and High school. title: 地球環境学
subtitle: Environmental Science of Earth
keywords: Chemical composiiton of the earth's crust
educationalGoal: The earth can be divided into the atmosphere, the lithosphere, and the hydrosphere, but elements such as carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus circulate among all of these spheres. This course will cover the behavior of substances in the global environment and the chemical reactions related to the behavior of the substances. The goal of this course is to raise awareness of the factors affecting the global environment.
advice:
1. Chemical composition of the earth's crust.
2. The evolution of the earth and changes in the atmosphere.
3. Basics of analytical chemistry.
4. Basics of aquatic environment.
5. Chemical equilibria in environmental water.
6. Environmental problems.
books:
(Textbook) An Introduction to Environmental Chemistry, Julian E. Andrews, et al., Wiley-Blackwell,
ISBN: 9780632059058
requiredKnowledge: A knowledge of high school level chemistry and biology is required to understand the lectures.

activityGoals.body: Understand the origins of the earth and changes in the global environment.
Understand atmospheric changes of the earth from the beginning to the present.
Describe the greenhouse effect caused by carbon dioxide..
Understand major chemical equilibria in environmental water.
Understand the mecanisms of seasonal variations in the water quality of lakes.
Understand global environmental problems.

Can describe the following:
- Atmospheric changes of the earth over time
- Mechanism of the variation of water quality in lake water
- Environmental problems with a concrete example.

Students also must be able to give a presentation on a global environmental problem based on journal articles.
achievementLevels.standard:

- Atmospheric changes of the earth over time
- Chemical composition of earth's crust
- Biogeochemical cycle of substances
- Mechanism of variation of water quality in lake water
- Environmental problems

Can also understand an article on a global environmental problem.

title: 人間と哲学
subtitle: Humanity and Philosophy
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal: To cultivate intelligence and originality, this course focuses on a philosophical text from another era and aims to improve reading comprehension and ability to think independently. Specifically, students learn to follow the structure of a text and identify the connection between claims and reasons. By discussing philosophical ideas with others, students learn to understand others’ ideas, think together, and develop critical thinking skills. Through these practices, students cultivate the thinking skills necessary for engineers who can think and act independently.
advice:
Course Description:
・In each class, students read a philosophical text and discuss a task assigned to their group. During the discussion, the instructor gives a short lecture and students take a short quiz based on the lecture. Students also formulate questions about the text. In the following week, after receiving the instructor’s answers to and explanations of those questions, each group prepares and submits a written response to the assigned task.
・A philosophical essay should be submitted at Class #10. Students choose one of the provided essay questions.
・A final report should be submitted after Class #14.

Expectations for Students:
・This course emphasizes accurate reading of texts (including reconstructing arguments), developing original thinking on that basis (including constructing your own arguments), and considering how philosophical methods can be applied to your own scientific or engineering research. Keep these aims in mind in group discussions, quizzes, and the philosophical essay.
・Look up unfamiliar terms on your own using an encyclopedia or a reference book.
books:
Discourse on the Method (Rene Descartes) (『方法序説』,デカルト,岩波書店,1997)
『デカルト「方法序説」を読む』,谷川多佳子,岩波書店,2014
requiredKnowledge:
・To have made a habit of reading and acquire reading comprehension.
・To have cultivated writing skills through "Basic Style for Study A and B".

activityGoals.body: To be able to understand philosophical ways of thinking and explain them concretely.
To be able to identify claims and reasons in texts written in different eras and with different assumptions.
To be able to analyze abstract questions, make them concrete, and develop your own answers.
To be able to express the process and results of thinking about the relation between technology and philosophy.
To be able to think critically about technology and philosophy and explain their relationship in clear writing.
To be able to self-evaluate the target abilities for students in this course.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1. Understanding philosophical ways of thinking and explaining them concretely in your own words.
2. Identifying claims and reasons in texts written by others from different eras and assumptions.
3. Making abstract questions concrete through analysis and answering them with appropriate reasons.
4. Expressing, in logical writing, the process and results of thinking with others about technology and philosophy.
5. Thinking critically about technology and philosophy and explaining it persuasively in clear writing.
6. Constantly evaluating your understanding of the course with the Target Abilities in mind.
achievementLevels.standard:
1. Understanding philosophical ways of thinking and explaining them concretely.
2. Identifying some claims and reasons in texts written by others from different eras and assumptions.
3. Analyzing abstract questions and answering them with reasons.
4. Expressing, in writing, the process and results of thinking with others about technology and philosophy.
5. Thinking critically about technology and philosophy and explaining it in clear writing.
6. Evaluating your understanding of the course to some extent with the Target Abilities in mind.
