title: グローバルＰＤ
subtitle: Global PD
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal: Global PD is a service-learning design course in which teams of students from across the world work together on 2 weeks projects that benefit the community. Students use the Design Thinking methodology to co-create innovative solutions to real-life issues. Through this project, students should be able to apply their teamwork and communication skills, develop a better understanding of themselves, fostering empathy for the community, and realize the positive impact for the community in need.
advice:
In Global PD, students will learn and experience:

[Multidisciplinary Design]
- Learn how to be better designers, gain design knowledge and skills.
- Learn how to identify and acquire new knowledge
- Learn to collaborate with people from other disciplines and develop an appreciation for cross-disciplinary contributions in design.

[Professional Preparation]
- Develop a broad set of skills needed to be successful in the changing global societies

[Service-Learning]
- Provide significant service to the community while learning
- Gain an understanding of the role that engineering and their discipline can play in society
books:
Reference Books:
1) Change by Design, Revised and Updated: How Design Thinking Transforms Organizations and Inspires Innovation, Tim Brown, Harper Business(2019)
2) Tsutawaru design no Kihon / Basics and Rules for Commnunication materials, Yuma Takahashi, Natsu Katayama, Gijutsuhyouronsya(1996) , in Japanese
requiredKnowledge: In Global PD, students are encouraged to work together and share information under multi-disciplinary, cross-cultural settings. Since, we expect every student to practice honorable, ethical, and professional behavior both inside and outside the classroom.

activityGoals.body: Student should be able to collaborate with  persons who have a multi-disciplinary and cross-cultural backgrounds
Student should be able to use the design thinking methodology to co-create innovative solutions to real issues
Students should be able to express their ideas and concepts using prototypes
Students should be able to work on a global team
Students should be able to manage their health, safety, and security overseas
Students should be able to share their outcomes with stakeholders

- understand of design as a start-to-finish process

subtitle: Special Subject - Mathematics(Topic Chemistry)
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the science history and the chemical foundations necessary for science and engineering.
(2) learn how to apply attitude and chemistry knowledge to science and engineering.
(3) establish a style of study using a preview and review approach.
(4) develop an autonomous and consecutive self-directed study ability.
advice:
This is a course in chemical foundations. We will cover the following:

1. Periodic Table of Elements.
2.Theory of Atoms and Molecules, Atomic Structure,
3. Combustion of Substances.
4. Haber-Bosch process, Rate of chemical reactions. Chemical Equilibrium.
5.Organic chemistry (Functional Group, Isomer).

(1) The class will be conducted following this syllabus.
(2) Students are expected to do the homework, previews, and reviews for every class.
(3) Students are expected to ask the teacher questions and use the Math. and Science Education Research Center.
(4) Students are expected not to be late, as the accumulation of learning is important.
(5) Students are expected to approach exams and quizzes with sufficient preparation.
※ Some details of the course may be changed as the course progresses.
books:
Textbooks：Isaac Asimov  “A Short History of Chemistry” (Doubleday and Co. Inc. New York)
Reference books：Trevor H. Levere “A History of Chemistry from Alchemy to the Buckyball” (The John Hopkins Univ.Press)
　　　　　　　  William H. Brock “The Fontana History of Chemistry”  (Fontana Press)
requiredKnowledge:
(1) Students prefer to study chemistry in high school prefer. However, students will need to work hard in the course and make sufficient effort to master.
(2) Students are expected to read the textbook, complete the homework, and engage in the previews and reviews.

Understand the contents of the course and be able to complete the required tasks by the announced deadlines.

educationalGoal: What makes machines interesting and atracting is that they work. In this class, by making a crane that lifts objects out of many mechanisms, students understand its motion principle, and build an actual model with the aim of understanding the basics of mechanical engineering, the basics of design, the principle of machine motion.

courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal: Psychology is the study of how the human mind works, primarily through the use of scientific methods.This class is intended for students who do not specialize in psychology, and introduces the concept of scientific psychology, research subjects, and representative findings obtained through research to date. The purpose of this course is to provide students with knowledge and perspectives to better understand the mind, which we all possess.
advice:
In this class, we will introduce the basic concepts of psychology, research subjects, and scientific approaches to them, as well as findings from various areas of psychology.
The human mind is thought to be a difficult subject for scientific study because it is only subjectively experienced. On the other hand, it is also of interest to many people, and therefore, there is a lot of information circulating in the world that may not be valid from a scientific point of view.
In this class, we will begin with an overview of general ideas in psychology, followed by a discussion of representative findings in various fields of psychology.
Through the various topics introduced in this class, students will learn about the scientific research methods and ways of thinking about the human mind that psychology has been striving to develop, and will come to understand the human mind and behavior in a more scientifically reliable way.
Students are expected to try to understand the various findings introduced in class by relating them to various phenomena experienced in their own daily lives.
Note that the schedule and details of the topics are subject to change.

title: 生涯学習特別科目（ＮＧＯ論）
subtitle: Special Subject - Lifelong Learning(Theory of NGO)
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal: In this course, studnets will learn about history, social backgound of NGO, wide knowledge on society and politics, solving social problems, engaging and willing to support others, utilizing those knowledges, skill and attitudes in their daily life (in future). Upon completing this course, students will be able to think by themselves how to contribute to civil society.
advice:
(Outline of the course)
   Students will gain knowledge about NGO as well as other related actors such as civil society and volunteers in Japan and outside of Japan, public sector and private sectors' role in social activities. Students are expected to become knowledgeable and to be able to take actions by themselves after graduated.
   Students will learn about various actions in civil society (NGO), public sector, private sector. By the end of the course, students will learn K (Kindness of Heart), I (Intellectual Curiosity), T (Team Sprits), So that they can acquire skills and knowledges that they can practice in future.

(Advice and comments)
1)Students will learn to open up their eyes to watch the world, to take interests in social issues, and keep their minds on such issues.
2)The international and social issues which will be discussed in these classes will be the issues that students may have to tackle in future.
3)The program of the course may change dependingon the number of students and circumstances of classes.
4)A lecturer of one class will be a person from NGOs, so there may be some changes in the program.
5)The lecturer of this course used to work for JBIC and JICA, as well as served as a JOCV, and as a director of an NGO.
books:
1) JANIC, 2022, NGO Databook, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (in Japanese):https://www.janic.org/blog/2022/04/22/ngodatabook2022/
2) Worldwatch, various year, State of the World, Island press,
3) Edwards, M. and Hulme, D., 1997, Making a difference, Earthscan
4) Hulme, D, and Edwards, M. 1997, NGOs, States and Donors, Save the Children
requiredKnowledge: No specific requirements to take this course. It is desirable that students have interests in daily international issues. Some English materials will be used.

activityGoals.body: Understand and explain the expected role of NGO in society.
Argue and discuss the roles and needs of NGO in Japan.
Argue and discuss the roles of NGO in international society.
Comprehend the roles of public sectors, private sector, and civil society (NGO) in international cooperation.
Explain and plan his/her own role in future how to support NGOs.
Acquire some senses of advocacy as one of the most important role in NGO.

              1.International Cooperation

3.Gobal South
4.Poverty
5.Mutual Support

              Recently, there are variety of approaches for international cooperation, even in people's daily life. In this course, students will learn that people are able to participate in supporting developing countries and the poor in many ways. Students are expected to understand such current situation. Upon completing this course, students will be able to think by themselves how to contribute to international cooperation.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              (Outline of the course)
   Students will learn activities of development assistance cooperation, international organizations, or NGO to support other people living inside and outside of their countries through learning international affairs. The goal of the students is to achieve the basic knowledge of international cooperation and its background so that they can practice such activities in their future.
   Students will learn the concept of international/global development/cooperation and its practice. By the end of the course, students will learn K (Kindness of Heart), I (Intellectual Curiosity), T (Team Sprits), So that they can acquire skills and knowledges that they can practice in future.
(Advice and comments)
1)Students will learn to open up their eyes to watch the world, to take interests in social issues, and keep their minds on such issues.
2)The international and social issues which will be discussed in these classes will be the issues that students may have to tackle in future.
3)The program of the course may change depending on the number of students and circumstances of classes.
4)A lecturer of one class will be a guest lecturer from outside, so there may be some changes in the program.
5)The lecturer of this course used to work for JBIC and JICA, as well as served as a JOCV, and as a director of an NGO.

title: 数理特別科目（教養のための量子力学基礎）
subtitle: Special Subject - Mathematics(Basic Topics of Quantum Mechanics for Liberal Arts)
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal:
Quantum mechanics is at the root of the latest modern technology, and quantum mechanics continues to make strong advances, including applications to quantum computers and quantum information. Even if you are not fully familiar with the mathematical aspects of modern education, it will be essential in the future to acquire the basic knowledge of quantum theory.
In this lecture, we will explain the basic content of quantum mechanics in a way that even second-year students can underst.
advice:
In this lecture, we will explain the structure of quantum mechanics and learn about its differences from classical physics. The use of mathematical formulas will be kept to a minimum, but in order to explain the structure, a minimum number of mathematical formulas will be presented, and the focus will be on explaining their physical meaning without delving into the treatment of mathematical formulas.
① Explain how quantum mechanics is constructed from classical mechanics through a procedure called "quantization." At this time, we will also explain the very basics of analytical mechanics necessary for quantization. ② Present the Schroedinger equation and explain its origin and interpretation, especially the fact that Schroedinger himself was unable to correctly interpret the equation he developed ③ Briefly explain the range of applications of quantum mechanics and explain the uncertainty principle I will explain about it. ④In addition to explaining quantum entanglement such as EPR correlation, we will also explain paradoxes such as Schroedinger's cat. ⑤Explain the interpretation of quantum mechanics. Specifically, I will explain the Copenhagen interpretation, the many-worlds interpretation, etc. Note that there are no serious textbooks that contain mathematical formulas that correspond to this lecture, so references will be introduced as appropriate.
books:
Do not use textbooks.
References will be given as appropriate in class.
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable to have basic knowledge of high school physics (especially mechanics) and basic knowledge of first-year mathematics calculus, but even if you have some gaps, you can listen to the lectures with concentration and improve your knowledge. You can take the course if you are willing to proactively research the parts you are lacking in and work on the tasks to make up for it. Even if you have a lot of prior knowledge, it will be difficult to complete the course if you are unable to maintain concentration during lectures.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the differences between classical mechanics and quantum mechanics and the "quantization"
Be able to explain the origin and interpretation of the Schroedinger equation.
Be able to explain the simple application range and uncertainty principle of quantum mechanics.
Be able to explain quantum entanglement such as EPR correlation and paradoxes such as Schroedinger's cat.
Be able to explain the interpretation of quantum mechanics.
Be able to attend every class, work on assigned assignments, and strive to understand the lesson content.

              Quantum mechanics is at the root of the latest modern technology, and quantum mechanics continues to make strong advances, including applications to quantum computers and quantum information. Even if you are not fully familiar with the mathematical aspects of modern education, it will be essential in the future to acquire the basic knowledge of quantum theory.
In this lecture, we will explain the basic content of quantum mechanics in a way that even second-year students can underst.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this lecture, we will explain the structure of quantum mechanics and learn about its differences from classical physics. The use of mathematical formulas will be kept to a minimum, but in order to explain the structure, a minimum number of mathematical formulas will be presented, and the focus will be on explaining their physical meaning without delving into the treatment of mathematical formulas.
① Explain how quantum mechanics is constructed from classical mechanics through a procedure called "quantization." At this time, we will also explain the very basics of analytical mechanics necessary for quantization. ② Present the Schroedinger equation and explain its origin and interpretation, especially the fact that Schroedinger himself was unable to correctly interpret the equation he developed ③ Briefly explain the range of applications of quantum mechanics and explain the uncertainty principle I will explain about it. ④In addition to explaining quantum entanglement such as EPR correlation, we will also explain paradoxes such as Schroedinger's cat. ⑤Explain the interpretation of quantum mechanics. Specifically, I will explain the Copenhagen interpretation, the many-worlds interpretation, etc. Note that there are no serious textbooks that contain mathematical formulas that correspond to this lecture, so references will be introduced as appropriate.

              Do not use textbooks.
References will be given as appropriate in class.

You can take the course if you are willing to proactively research the parts you are lacking in and work on the tasks to make up for it. Even if you have a lot of prior knowledge, it will be difficult to complete the course if you are unable to maintain concentration during lectures.

educationalGoal: The term marketing is often used in a narrow sense, such as advertising, publicity, and sales promotion activities. ○ Students will be expected to pay attention to the latest market information and express their own opinions and interpretations of market trends. When doing so, students will be required to provide objective evidence as to why they think that way.

              The term marketing is often used in a narrow sense, such as advertising, publicity, and sales promotion activities. Still, it has a broader meaning, such as "activities to come up with products and services that are beneficial to consumers, realize them, and increase mutual satisfaction and results ." The main purpose of this course is to acquire the basics of management that engineers need to understand in this broad sense, conduct research and analysis of actual company data, and participate in marketing activities.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              [Class Outline (Procedure)]
○ Each class will have a lecture on a variety of marketing-related themes.
○ PowerPoint materials will be used in class. Important keywords and points will be raised, and students will deepen their understanding of the theory through group research and discussion of case studies.
[Advice]
○ Students are expected to have their own opinions, rather than simply memorizing knowledge.
○ Students will be expected to pay attention to the latest market information and express their own opinions and interpretations of market trends. When doing so, students will be required to provide objective evidence as to why they think that way.

educationalGoal:
In this course, students will learn how to demonstrate your creativity and design
skills, after having done some rudimentary exercises to hone your sensibilities. T
hey will work on practical skills such as clay work and drawing. Students will als
o learn about creation systematically in lectures and study the transition of desi
gn. They will learn how to apply and utilize their skills to their own field of ex
pertise.
advice:
The objectives of this course are for students to understand;
- Understand their own biases and be able to look at things from a bird's eye view.
- Cultivate one's eyesight for understanding the essence of matter.
- Learn how to create their own answers.
- Enjoy and actively engage in class.

title: サステナブルイノベーション
subtitle: Sustainable Innovation
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal:
In this course, students will learn methods to transform society through specializ
ed study of the SDGs.
In addition, by developing SDG gamification materials, students will deepen their
understanding of the SDGs, experience the process of developing their own products
 and making them better, and acquire the thinking necessary to explore ways of soc
ial change in the process.
advice:
Since 2016, activities have been taking place around the world to achieve the SDGs, which are common goals for a
ll UN member states.
In this class, students will learn an overview of the SDGs and how they can actually create their own actions an
d involve others.
In particular, the second half of the class will focus on the development and utilization of gamification materi
als and social implementation, deepening students' understanding of how to create activities that improve societ
y while having fun at the same time.

title: 科学技術と人・社会
subtitle: Science,Technology and Human Society
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
keywords: Science and technology and industry, nation, and policy
educationalGoal: In the 18th and 19th centuries, scientific activity was institutionalized and professionalized, becoming "science." In this course, we will review the relationship between science and technology, and between science-technology and human society. Interactions among science, technology, and human society led to the social and environmental issues being experienced now. Upon completing this course, students will be able to establish their own viewpoints as engineers and/or scientists who support society.
advice:
Course description:
1. How science and technology work: Science and technology studies
2. Historical overviews on science and technology: institutionalization and professionalization of
   science, the relationship between science and technology
3. Interactions between science and technology and human society:
   nations, economic development, and changing values
4. Social issues caused by science and technology:
   from environmental, information, and bioethics viewpoints
5. What is required for engineers and/or scientists in today's society?

title: プロジェクトデザイン特別科目（ＡＩ活用実践）（春期集中講義）
subtitle: Special Subject - Design Project(AI Application and Implementation)
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal: In this class, students will prototype and verify systems that use AI technology to solve problems on campus. During prototyping and verification, students will utilize generative AI and learn about the system development process. Students will understand AI technology and how to apply generative AI. Students will also improve their skills in effective communication of information through project planning, progress management, and documentation.
advice:
In this class, students will verify the effectiveness of AI technology by creating a prototype of a system to solve a problem on campus for the purpose of problem solving through PBL. In addition, students will acquire skills in the system development process (design → development → verification), as well as document creation and system development using AI.

Main contents of the class
1. Acquisition of skills for each process in system development
Learn what needs to be considered in each process (basic design, system design, functional design, etc.) and create the necessary documents by using the generated AI.
2. Prototyping a system that embodies the solution
Prototype a system that embodies the solution using AI based on the created documents.
3. Verify the effectiveness of the developed system
Evaluate the performance of the system and verify its effectiveness in solving the problem.
4. Presentation
Demonstration and presentation of the prototype system will be conducted as a summary of the class.
books: None
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge and experience learned and acquired by the time of the course.

To be able to demonstrate a willingness to objectively evaluate one's own abilities

title: 専門教養特別科目（基礎化学工学）
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal:
The learning objectives of this course are to acquire the following knowledge and skills as a foundation for chemical engineering:
1. Unit Conversions
2. Creating and Using Stoichiometric Equations
3. Calculating Mass Balances
4. Calculating Energy Balances
advice:
It is essential in chemistry to express the necessary amounts of substances and energy numerically. Understanding elementary arithmetic, especially the concept of ratios, is indispensable for these calculations. Those who have not made an effort to understand the concept of speed in arithmetic, but have merely memorized the calculation procedure, will not be able to understand math after middle school, let alone chemistry problems.
In this course, we will re-understand the concept of ratio from the basics and learn basic calculation methods for chemistry and chemical engineering using the concept of ratio. Understanding the concept of ratio requires effort, and there is no easy path to understanding it.
Memorizing the answers will not improve the learner's ability. It is important to think through and solve the exercises on your own.
1.Unit Conversions
2.Creating Stoichiometric Equations
3.Calculating Mass Balances
4.Calculating Energy Balances

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              It is essential in chemistry to express the necessary amounts of substances and energy numerically. Understanding elementary arithmetic, especially the concept of ratios, is indispensable for these calculations. Those who have not made an effort to understand the concept of speed in arithmetic, but have merely memorized the calculation procedure, will not be able to understand math after middle school, let alone chemistry problems.
In this course, we will re-understand the concept of ratio from the basics and learn basic calculation methods for chemistry and chemical engineering using the concept of ratio. Understanding the concept of ratio requires effort, and there is no easy path to understanding it.
Memorizing the answers will not improve the learner's ability. It is important to think through and solve the exercises on your own.

educationalGoal:
Through aiming to enhance artistic problem-solving skills with intuitive and intuitive thinking accompanied by execution capabilities:
-be able to learn based dialogue on museum exhibition (exhibits/spaces) .

advice: In the era of V.U.C.A. (Volatility, Uncertainty, Complexity and Ambiguity), not only is scientific problem-solving emphasized, which relies on logical and rational thinking, but also artistic problem-solving, which depends on intuitive and sensory thinking, is required. In this course, we combine project-based learning focusing on the cultivation of cultural literacy within our living communities with museum learning involving visits to multiple museums from the region. To aim for the improvement of artistic  problem-solving skills through the combination of these two modes of learning in liberal arts education. The traditional museum learnings often focus on humanities fields such as art museums and historical museums, but what distinguishes liberal arts education at technical universities is the inclusion of museums in the field of technology. As one means to achieve the theme of the project, we incorporate the planning and implementation of liberal arts open lecture as a learning task.

educationalGoal: Research in tissue engineering/regenerative medicine (TERM) aims to restore or enhance organ functions lost through disease or injury. Bioengineered tissues such as skin are already in clinical use. To advance this field, integration of medicine and engineering is essential. This course introduces beginner students from any background to the fundamentals of TERM, with the goal of understanding its significance, core methods, and the need for interdisciplinary integration and social implementation.

This course primarily teaches the fundamental knowledge of tissue engineering and regenerative medicine through lectures.

title: 専門教養特別科目（プロダクトデザイン（スタイリング理論））
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal: This course aims to cultivate design engineers with a solid foundation in engineering skills and acquired design competencies. Students will be able to design novel product appearances and add value to product exteriors without altering technical performance, while integrating problem-solving across functional components, exterior elements, and their intersections.
advice:
Course Overview

This course classifies the styling process into key elements and explains each through representative examples using photographs and illustrations.

Course Content

Key topics include the objectives and evaluation of product styling; essential styling elements such as visual themes, silhouette, proportion, form, lines, volume, surface, color, and materials; practical design exercises; and a written report to confirm learning outcomes.

Study Guidance

Students are encouraged to observe industrial products critically, analyze their visual characteristics, and reflect on the messages conveyed by their forms in order to deepen their understanding of industrial design and develop design sensibility and skills.
books: Textbook: Peter Dabbs. 2023. Introduction to product design styling. BNN Inc.
requiredKnowledge:
1.No prior knowledge is required; the course is open to students interested in design and design engineering.
	2.Design exercises allow flexible methods of expression, including hand drawing, digital drawing software, and CAD.
	3.Software exercises focus on creating 2D digital data for cutting machines used in mock-up production.

activityGoals.body: To Understand the purpose of product styling schemes
To be prepared to make novel design proposals.
To understand the type of key elements in product styling.
To be able to identify the type of key elements in product styling on product exterior.
To be able to carry out styling plans with the key elements in product styling.
To be able to visually communicate the intent of planned design to a third party.

advice:
Course Overview
Students will acquire fundamental knowledge related to three-dimensional form development in industrial product exteriors, as well as CAD techniques for creating and shaping forms.The course focuses primarily on forms composed of curved surfaces, assuming future development work involving mobility devices and handheld controller-type equipment.

Course Content
1.Knowledge of Three-Dimensional Form Development
2.CAD  Techniques
　Learning CAD operations by creating replica shapes of existing products.
1)Sub-D modeling
　Intuitive modeling method for idea generation.
2)Surface modeling
　Dimensionally defined modeling method with 3D wireframes.
3.Rendering
　Converting 3D models into 2D images by setting surface texture.
books: None

1.No prior knowledge is required; the course is open to students interested in design and design engineering.
2.Will use 3D modeling software RHINOCEROS.

Be able to use analysis tools to adjust the geometry.
Be able to visually express the overall shape and the design of the subject to a third party.

              1.Design engineering

              This course aims to cultivate design engineers with a solid foundation in engineering skills and acquired design competencies.
Students will acquire CAD techniques for exterior styling of devices, aiming to promote and improve the efficiency of practical prototyping through 3D data.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Course Overview
Students will acquire fundamental knowledge related to three-dimensional form development in industrial product exteriors, as well as CAD techniques for creating and shaping forms.The course focuses primarily on forms composed of curved surfaces, assuming future development work involving mobility devices and handheld controller-type equipment.

Course Content
1.Knowledge of Three-Dimensional Form Development
2.CAD  Techniques
　Learning CAD operations by creating replica shapes of existing products.
1)Sub-D modeling
　Intuitive modeling method for idea generation.
2)Surface modeling
　Dimensionally defined modeling method with 3D wireframes.
3.Rendering
　Converting 3D models into 2D images by setting surface texture.

2.Will use 3D modeling software RHINOCEROS.

title: 職業指導
subtitle: Career Guidance
educationalGoal: Now in the situation of education, vocational guidance (career guidance) is changing to foster in students a zest for life. In this course, we understand the history of vocational guidance, the current situation around the school, and the trends in educational reformation. Then we will consider how students will select and determine their own way of life, and the way of vocational guidance (career guidance) that allows them to achieve self-actualization.

  3. Curriculum and vocational guidance(career guidance)
  4. The basic theory of vocational guidance
  5. The current situation of vocational guidance(career guidance)

Part 2: Practical consideration
  1. The concept and practice of vocational guidance(career guidance)
  2. The educational evaluation of vocational guidance(career guidance)
  3. The collaborative design of vocational guidance(career guidance)
  4. Exercise: making an annual guidance plan

title: 教育原理（春期集中講義）
subtitle: Principles of Education
educationalGoal: The goal of this course is to have one's own view of education through a fundamental study of education. To that end, based on educational theory, clarify the actual issues of school education, home education, and social education, and cultivate the basic ability to think about future education.
advice:
This course covers the items as below.

1. What is “Education”?
 The significance and goal of education, “Learning” and “Teaching”, The structure of school education, The significance of “Pedagogy”
2. Philosophy of Education and the history of school education
 Nature and education, The thought of new education movement, The method and Philosophy of education, The thought of national education
3. The history of school education
 The establishment of modern school, The issues of school education
4. Lifelong education
 The significance of lifelong education, Home education and social education
5. The issues of the current education
 Education in cooperation with community, The future education
books: Kyouiku to Manabi no Genri: Hendo suru Syakai to Mukiau tame ni, (The University of Nagoya Press.(The Principle of Education and Learning: For the moment of facing a changing society.)
requiredKnowledge: This course is for those who are serious about becoming a teacher.

title: 教育心理学（夏期集中講義）
subtitle: Educational Psychology
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to understand the basic knowledge of educational psychology which is necessary for effective educational practice in high school. In particular, we will learn about development, learning, adjustment, and educational evaluation. As a specific topic, students will consider each developmental stage until adolescence, and support for developmental disorder.
advice:
This course covers knowledge of educational psychology which is necessary for effective educational practice in high school.
  1. Development: 1)definition of development, 2) principles and characteristics of development, 3)developmental theories, 4)infancy and early childhood, 5)school age, 6) adolescence
  2. Maladjustment
  3. Learning: 1)definition of learning, 2)learning theories, 3) application of learning theories to education
  4. Motivation
  5. Educational evaluation
  6. Developmental disorder: 1)basic knowledge of developmental disorder, 2)support for students with developmental disorder
books: Junichi Nishimura & Sumie Nishimura(eds.) (2010) Essentials of Educational Psychology(2nd ed.). Nakanishiya Shuppan.
requiredKnowledge:
●To be interested in psychology, or to have taken “Introduction to Teacher Certification Course”.
●Aim to obtain a Japanese teacher's license.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the significance of development, explain it in text.
Be able to answer the question about the basics of educational psychology.
Be able to explain the feature of adolescence and psychological maladjustment in text.
Be able to state an opinion on the support for students with developmental disorder.
Be able to engage in this course and self-evaluate objectives of this course to be achieved.

title: 学習・発達論
subtitle: Learning and Development
educationalGoal: Learning Psychology and Developmental Psychology help us to practice effective education. In this course, students will understand learning theory, developmental theory and developmental disorder. After understanding them, students will acquire practical skills and perspectives.
advice:
This course aims to acquire basics of Leaning Psychology and Developmental Psychology for junior and senior high school teachers. They include the following materials:

 1. Development: cognitive development, personality development, development of sociality, developmental disorder
 2. Lerning: lerning theory, motivation, teaching-learning theory

Students will take lectures and discuss their significance with other students.
Students are required to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to be interested in the current state of school.
Students are expected to apply theories to educational practice.
Students are expected to build their own view of education.
books: Essentials of Educational Psychology(2nd ed.), Nakanishiya Shuppan
requiredKnowledge: To have taken the course of “Educational Psyhology”

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain basic developmental theories.
Be able to answer the space filling and descriptive questions about developmental theories.
Be able to answer the space filling and descriptive questions about learning theories.
Be able to understand developmental disorder students and describe the views how to support them.
Be able to describe ideas about effective education from the perspective of learning.
Engage in this course and self-evaluate objectives of this course to be achieved.

 1. Development: cognitive development, personality development, development of sociality, developmental disorder
 2. Lerning: lerning theory, motivation, teaching-learning theory

Students will take lectures and discuss their significance with other students.
Students are required to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to be interested in the current state of school.
Students are expected to apply theories to educational practice.

title: 工業科教育法
subtitle: Educational Methods for Engineering
educationalGoal: The objectives of industrial education are to acquire basic and practical skill, to understand the significance of industry in the current society, to solve problems of industrial technologies taking environment into account. In this course, students who aim to be an industry teacher design and practice an industrial lesson to achieve the above objectives.
advice:
This course can be divided into the following two parts.

Part 1:
  (1) The history and the current state of industrial education
(2) The course of study and the overview of the subject “Industry”
(3) Instructional design for the subject “Industry”
(4) To make a scenario of a lesson in group activities

Part 2:
  (5) To make a scenario of a lesson in personal activities
  (6) To make lesson practice, and discuss about it
  (7) To reflect on the lesson demonstration and improve the lesson

Nakamura, T. et al. (2019) Atarashi Kanten to Jissen ni Motoduku Kougyouka-Kyouiku-hou no Kenkyu (Revised edition). Jikkyou-Shuppan.(A Study on Educational Methids for "Industry" Based on a New Perspective and Practice.)

              The objectives of industrial education are to acquire basic and practical skill, to understand the significance of industry in the current society, to solve problems of industrial technologies taking environment into account. In this course, students who aim to be an industry teacher design and practice an industrial lesson to achieve the above objectives.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course can be divided into the following two parts.

Part 1:
  (1) The history and the current state of industrial education

(3) Instructional design for the subject “Industry”
(4) To make a scenario of a lesson in group activities

Part 2:
  (5) To make a scenario of a lesson in personal activities
  (6) To make lesson practice, and discuss about it
  (7) To reflect on the lesson demonstration and improve the lesson

title: 数学科教育法Ⅰ
subtitle: Educational Methods for Mathematics I
educationalGoal: In this course, students will acquire basic knowledge necessary for taking mathematics class in secondary education. This course covers the history, current status, and objective of mathematics education, the course of study “Mathematics”, and the content, materials, teaching methods and evaluation of mathematics.
advice:
In this course, students will learn basic knowledge necessary for taking mathematics class in secondary education as bellow.

 1. Mathematical education: history, PISA, objective, and evaluation
 2. Course of study “Mathematics”
 3. Overview of each area of mathematics, instruction, materials, and evaluation: set and logic, algebra, geometry, mathematical analysis, probability and statistics
 4. ICT for mathematics education
 5. Connection between junior high school and senior high school in mathematics

Students will take lectures and discuss their significance with each other.

title: 道徳教育の理論と実践
subtitle: Principles and Practices in Moral Education
educationalGoal: Students will learn the theory and practice of moral education and think about methods of future moral education. Students will clarify the relation between “moral education to be carried out through all instructional activities of the school” and “moral education to be performed during morality class”, and develop the basic abilities, knowledge, and instruction methods necessary for morality (i.e., “that I think and discuss”).
advice:
Students will learn about the theory of moral education and morality in the future while connecting theories of moral education with actual practice. Students will also argue for an appointed theme in groups and summarize the content in a worksheet:
  1. Moral education and problems in the morality department
  2. Moral education theory
    ① Historic process of moral education
    ② Theories about moral education
    ③ Moral education management
    ④ Moral education and “Special subject: Morality”
  3. Morality class theory
    ① Morality for thought and discussion
    ② Teaching materials
  4. Transmission of values and critical thought
  5. Moral education for future society
books: Textbooks：Middle School Curriculum - Commentary - “Special subject: Morality” (Higashiyama Publishing) 〈Tyugakkou-Gakusyuusidou-Youryou Kaisetu “Tokubetsu-no-Kyouka-Doutoku〉 Morality for Thought and Discussion - Making Classes with Active Moral Learning- 〈Kangae, Gironnsuru-Doutokujugyou- Active Moral Learning- no-Jugyouzukuri〉
requiredKnowledge:
●Applicants for a junior high school teacher's license must take this class.
●Applicants for a high school teacher's license should take this class.
●Students should have a strong desire to enter the teaching profession.
●Students should want to improve their understanding of moral education continuously.
●Students must participate in practice, mock classes, and positive discussions.

activityGoals.body: Can explain the social background of “Special subject: Morality”.
Can explain the theory and practice of moral education using specific examples.
Can understand the purpose of morality education, develop teaching plans and materials, and conduct classes.
Learn with a sincere attitude and self-evaluate their action targets.

title: 特別活動の指導法（夏期集中講義）
subtitle: Teaching Methods for Special Activities
educationalGoal: Problem behaviors of students are increasing now. In response to this situation, the expectation for extracurricular activity is growing. “Desirable group activity” is a keyword in extracurricular activity, classroom activities are especially important. In this course, students study historical change and theory of extracurricular activity. In addition, teacher's practical teaching skill for club activity and classroom activity is considered.
advice:
This course covers the items as below:
 (1) The objectives and contents of extracurricular activity found in the course of study
 (2) The historical change of postwar extracurricular activity
 (3) The students’ situation and teacher’s practical teaching skill
 (4) The guidance of club activities
 (5) The practice of extracurricular activity focusing on classroom activities
books: Eriko Harada, Tomomi Takahashi, & Ken-ichi Moriyama(2019) Saishin Tokubetu-Katsudou-Ron(revised edition), Daigaku-Kyouiku Shuppan.
requiredKnowledge:
●It is important to remember the experience in secondary education for understanding and considering extracurricular activities.
●Aiming to obtain Japanese teacher's license.

Be able to state an opinion about the better extracurricular activities suitable for traits of puberty.
Be able to explain the educational significance of club activities.
Be able to make a plan of classroom activities with understanding the function of classroom.
Be able to engage in this course and self-evaluate objectives of this course to be achieved.

4.Club Activity

              Problem behaviors of students are increasing now. In response to this situation, the expectation for extracurricular activity is growing. “Desirable group activity” is a keyword in extracurricular activity, classroom activities are especially important. In this course, students study historical change and theory of extracurricular activity. In addition, teacher's practical teaching skill for club activity and classroom activity is considered.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course covers the items as below:
 (1) The objectives and contents of extracurricular activity found in the course of study
 (2) The historical change of postwar extracurricular activity
 (3) The students’ situation and teacher’s practical teaching skill
 (4) The guidance of club activities
 (5) The practice of extracurricular activity focusing on classroom activities

title: 教育方法・技術論（情報通信技術の活用を含む）
subtitle: Educational Methods and Techniques
educationalGoal: A good lesson is understood as a Teaching-Learning Process. To make and carry out a lesson as a teaching-learning process, a teacher is needed to have ability to analyze teaching materials and to make a lesson plan. In addition using ICT, teaching materials, making a plan for educational evaluation and improving a lesson are also important. The objective of this course is to acquire methods and techniques for a good lesson.
advice:
This course covers the knowledge and technique which are needed for design and practice of a good lesson as below.
 1. The knowledge which is needed for design and practice of a good lesson.
   1) Teaching: Teaching-Learning process, Teaching theories, corroborative learning.
   2) The elements and requirements which constitute a lesson.
   3) The significance of educational evaluation
 2. The techniques which are needed for design and practice of a good lesson.
   1) how to make a unit
   2) how to make a lesson
   3) how to create a lesson plan
   4) How to use ITC and media
   5) how to make teaching materials
   6) how to make a plan for educational evaluation
books: Ryou Okada, Motoyuki Nakatani, Takamichi Itou, & Shuichi Tsukano(2016) Mizukara Kangaeru Kodomo wo Sodateru Kyouiku no Houhou to Gijutsu. Kitaoji-Shobou.
requiredKnowledge:
●To have taken “Education”, “Educational Psychology” and “Theory of Curriculum”.
●Aiming toobtain Japanese teacher's license.

activityGoals.body: Be able to design a lesson plan with basic knowledge of teacher-learning process.
Be able to create a lesson scenario and explain the significance of the lesson scenario.
Be able to explain how to use ICT and Media effectively in a lesson.
Be able to make a plan for educational evaluation and explain the significance of the plan.
Be able to engage in this course and self-evaluate objectives of this course to be achieved.

title: 生徒・進路指導論
subtitle: Guidance and Career Education
educationalGoal: Students learn a principle of student instruction and the vocational counseling that accorded with education reform of our country and think about the purpose and significance, especially in junior high schools and high schools.
advice:
Students learn the basics of practical leadership of the student instruction and the vocational counseling.
1. Student instruction
①Significance and purpose of the student instruction
②A domain and contents of the student instruction
③Problem of the student instruction
④Student instruction and other instructional activities
⑤Method of the student instruction－Collective instruction, Individual instruction
2. Vocational counseling
①Significance and purpose of the vocational counseling
②A theory and method of the vocational counseling－The history of the vocational counseling, Connection with the career education, Occupational development theory
After having learned the content mentioned above, students investigate a contemporary problem about the student instruction and the vocational counseling and consider the way of the desirable student instruction and vocational counseling. They search the desirable instruction method or the way of the correspondence for the student and acquire a practical instruction technology and skill.

title: 教育相談（夏期集中講義）
subtitle: School Counseling
educationalGoal: This course covers psychological problems in secondary school(relationship between students and parents, truant, bullying, school maladjustment, developmental disorder, and so on). Students will discuss psychological features in adolescence, relationship between teachers and students, and relationship between teachers and parents, and aim to acquire the correct view and skill for students with school maladjustment.
advice:
This course includes the following materials:
(1) To consider the current issues of school maladjustment in secondary education(truant, bullying, and school maladjustment)
(2) To understand psychological features and psychological problems in adolescence, and the support system for students with school maladjustment
(3) To understand basic theories of school counseling and psychological support for students with school maladjustment.

Students are expected to consider what is necessary for secondary school students.
books: Toshiyuki Kasugai & Minako Itoh(2011) Yoku Wakaru Kyouiku-Soudan, Mineruva-Shobou.
requiredKnowledge: To understand basic knowledge of educational psychology.

activityGoals.body: Be able to answer the space filling and descriptive questions about truant, bullying, and school maladjustment.
Be able to explain how to understand secondary school students with psychological problems.
Be able to explain the correct psychological support for secondary school students.
Be able to engage in this course and self-evaluate objectives of this course to be achieved.

4.Developmental Counseling
5.Cooperation between School and Community

              This course covers psychological problems in secondary school(relationship between students and parents, truant, bullying, school maladjustment, developmental disorder, and so on). Students will discuss psychological features in adolescence, relationship between teachers and students, and relationship between teachers and parents, and aim to acquire the correct view and skill for students with school maladjustment.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course includes the following materials:
(1) To consider the current issues of school maladjustment in secondary education(truant, bullying, and school maladjustment)
(2) To understand psychological features and psychological problems in adolescence, and the support system for students with school maladjustment
(3) To understand basic theories of school counseling and psychological support for students with school maladjustment.

Students are expected to consider what is necessary for secondary school students.

              Toshiyuki Kasugai & Minako Itoh(2011) Yoku Wakaru Kyouiku-Soudan, Mineruva-Shobou.

title: 教育実習（事前・事後指導）
subtitle: Student Teaching
educationalGoal: The objectives of Teacher Practice are working at a school experientially,  determining own aptitude as a teacher, and clarifying the ideal teacher . To achieve the objectives, It is needed to understand teacher job and responsibilities and define the goals of teaching practice as preparation. After teaching practice, it is important to reflect on teaching practice and check the achievement status of the goals. This course is significant for considering the own aptitude as a teacher.
advice:
This course consists of two parts. One is Pre-guidance for final preparation of Teaching Practice, and the other is Post-guidance for reflection on Teaching Practice.
1. Pre-guidance
It includes lectures by experienced teachers in secondary school. Students will make a concrete image of you during Teaching Practice, survey the training school and teachers’ job in school, and make a lesson plan.
2. Post-guidance
It includes check the achievement status of the goals, and discussion about each experience during Teaching Practice.
books: Perfect Guide for Student Teaching, The Mook of Educational Technology, Shogakukan Co. (Kyouiku-Jisshu Kanpeki Guide (Kyouiku-Gijutsu Mook), Shogakukan Co.)

Reflect on the teaching practice and to be able understand the job of teachers in school.

5.The Course of Study

              The teacher in charge of “industry” is required to have basic knowledge of each area of industry. This course covers the overview of each area of industry, the acquisition of basic knowledge of each area of industry, the significance of industry in current society, environmental problems, and energy problems. Finally students will be required to have the foundation of practice to resolve proactively, rationally and ethically.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course will take mechanical engineering, mechatronics, information engineering, architecture, civil engineering, and industrial chemistry. In each area, students understand basic knowledge and the relationship between each area and society.

educationalGoal: To get a teacher's license, five days of nursing care experience at social welfare facilities and two days of nursing care at special needs schools are required. This course consists of three parts. One is Pre-guidance for final preparation of the experience of nursing care, second is experience of nursing care, and the last is Post-guidance for reflection on the experience of nursing care. In Pre-guidance, students will acquire.
advice:
1. Pre-guidance
Students will understand the significance of the experience of nursing care, and acquire basic knowledge of social welfare, special needs education, handicapped people, and elderly people.

2. The experience of nursing care
Students will participate in five days of nursing care experience at social welfare facilities and two days of nursing care at special needs schools

3. Post-guidance
For reflection on the experience of nursing care, students will discuss each experience and build the view of education and human based on the discussion.
